author: claude[bot]
body:
Closes #711.

## The window

`Plugin.start()` hashed the plugin binary through one `os.Open` of its path, and
`launch` then handed that path to `exec.Command`, which opens it again. Two
lookups of a mutable name with a window between them. An atomic rename landing in
that window — an in-place upgrade is exactly that, no attacker required — records
a digest of bytes the kernel never ran.

Everything downstream then preserves the wrong answer faithfully:
`ResolvedPlugin.distribution_digest` pins runs to it, `CheckPluginsAvailable`
admits or refuses workers by comparing against it, the relaunch refusal
(`ErrDistribution`) compares two digests each taken with the same race, and
`flow plugins` reports it as "the digest of the executable currently serving".
A digest that can describe a process that never existed is worse than no digest:
it is a wrong answer wearing the appearance of a checked one.

## What closes it

The executable is opened once, and the digest and the exec are both taken from
that one open file description (`pkg/flowstate/v1/plugin/image.go`).

On Linux the child is exec'd as `/proc/self/fd/N` — the descriptor's own name —
after the host verifies with `os.SameFile` that the magic link resolves to the
inode it just hashed. `execve` opens its path argument before it closes
close-on-exec descriptors, so the forked child can name a descriptor that does
not survive into the program it becomes; the plugin therefore inherits no
readable handle on its own image, and the launch works even when the path has
been renamed over and only this descriptor keeps the inode alive.

Two details that are load-bearing rather than decorative:

- The descriptor is moved to number ≥ 16 first (`execFDFloor`). `os/exec`
  rebuilds the child's low descriptors with `dup2` — stdin, stdout, stderr, then
  each `ExtraFiles` entry — in the forked child, *before* `execve`. A descriptor
  of ours inside that range would be overwritten there, and `/proc/self/fd/N`
  would name a pipe at the moment exec resolves it.
- The handle is closed only after `Start()` returns, which is after the child's
  `execve` has been attempted: the parent waits on a pipe the successful exec
  closes.

`argv[0]` is unchanged — still the installed path, which is what the catalog,
the logs and an operator call the plugin. Only `cmd.Path` differs.

## Portability, stated rather than implied

`execveat(fd, "", AT_EMPTY_PATH)` says the same thing without `/proc` and is not
used: `os/exec` owns everything between fork and exec (process group, pipes,
environment, cancellation) and offers no seam to substitute the final syscall.
Reimplementing that to avoid one `/proc` lookup would trade a lot of subtle code
for nothing, so the lookup is verified instead.

Where a descriptor cannot be named — no `/proc`, and every non-Linux platform
(`image_other.go`) — the plugin still launches by path with the digest it always
had, and the host logs one line per launch saying the recorded digest describes
what the path held at launch rather than proving what ran. `DistributionDigest`'s
godoc and the "Worker to plugin" section of `THREAT_MODEL.md` now say which
guarantee is which; nothing silently offers the weaker one as the stronger.

## The test forces the race, it does not wait for it

`Config.beforeExec` is an unexported, nil-by-default seam that runs after the
digest is taken and before the process is started. The test replaces the binary
there, so the window is open on every run rather than on an unlucky one — a
sleep-based version would prove nothing on a loaded machine and would pass on a
fast one whether or not the defect was fixed.

The oracle is a fake plugin (`self-digest`) that reports the digest of its own
`/proc/self/exe`: the running inode, not a path lookup, so it is the truth about
which bytes served. The test asserts that against what the host recorded.

- `TestTheDigestIsOfTheImageThatRanWhenTheBinaryIsSwappedAtExec` — with
  `cmd.Path` reverted to `found.Path`, it fails every run: *"the plugin process
  is running sha256:850c93… and the host recorded sha256:97ef7d…; a run pinned to
  the recorded digest would be pinned to bytes that never served it"*.
- `TestExecImagePointsAtTheDescriptorRatherThanThePath` — the primitive directly:
  after the path is rebound, the digest is unchanged and the exec path still
  resolves to the opened inode.
- `TestExecImageRefusesWhatIsNotARegularFile` — the check runs on the descriptor,
  because hashing a fifo is a read with no end on a path a worker's startup waits
  on.

Both new tests are `//go:build linux`, since the guarantee is.

## Group-writable, in the same pass

`checkWritableByOthers` refused `0o002` only. "Any member of group staff chooses
what this worker executes" is the world-writable sentence with one word changed,
and a group is a list this process does not curate, so the mask is now `0o022`
and the message names who can write.

Swept the tree for the same predicate: `cmd/flow/acme.go` masks `0o077` and
`cmd/flow/keys.go` requires exactly `0600`, both of which already cover group.
This was the only gap. The `--allow-insecure-plugin-dir` help text already said
"other users", so no reference regeneration was needed for it.

The negative direction is tested in both directions: group-writable directory and
group-writable binary are refused (and `AllowInsecureSearchPath` still accepts
them), and a 0755 binary in a 0755 directory is still discovered — a refusal that
over-reached would break every legitimate deployment. Reverting the mask to
`0o002` fails the two refusal subtests.

Note for deployments: an installer that leaves a plugin directory 0775 will now be
refused. That is the intent, and the named escape hatch is unchanged.

## Verification

`go run ./tools/gate` PASS (5 legs run, 3 skipped, appearance NOT VERIFIED
locally — vhs absent, CI's appearance job owns it; this change alters a plugin
discovery error string, which no recorded tape covers). Also run in full:
`GOMEMLIMIT=1GiB go test -race ./pkg/flowstate/v1/plugin/... ./cmd/flow/...`,
`make test-plugins`, and `staticcheck` over the touched packages.

author: reloru
body:
## Summary
Adds `.github/workflows/claude.yml` — `anthropics/claude-code-action@v1`, triggered by mentioning `@claude` in an issue, issue comment, PR review, or PR review comment. Claude gets the thread as context and does what it was asked, either replying in-thread or pushing a branch and opening a PR.

Auth is the `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` repo secret (referenced via `secrets.`, never embedded). Separate credential from `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`; grants nothing on Cloudflare.

Deliberately unconstrained **on tools**: bare `Bash` (any shell command), no `--max-turns` cap, no `--disallowedTools`.

> **Note:** an earlier revision of this PR set `allowed_bots: "*"` and argued it was safe here. That was wrong and has been corrected — see "Who can trigger it" below. The rationale in this description reflects the final state.

## Who can trigger it — `allowed_bots` is unset, on purpose

Settled empirically on #185 rather than assumed. A comment posted from a Claude Code cloud session reports as:

| field | value |
|---|---|
| `user.login` | `reloru` |
| `user.type` | `User` |
| `author_association` | `OWNER` |
| `performed_via_github_app` | `claude` |

The GitHub **UI** renders `performed_via_github_app` as an app badge, so these comments *display* as bot-authored — but the **actor** the action's permission check evaluates is `reloru`, a User with write access. So cloud-session comments already trigger through the ordinary human path and need no bot entry.

Leaving `allowed_bots` unset does three jobs at once:
1. Owner and cloud sessions trigger it (write access).
2. **Loop guard.** The action ships no documented self-trigger prevention, and `GITHUB_TOKEN` recursion prevention is *not* a backstop — the action resolves `steps.run.outputs.github_token || inputs.github_token || github.token`, and the Claude App token is not `GITHUB_TOKEN`, so it *does* create new runs. Naming the identity this workflow posts under is exactly how a comment loop would start.
3. Avoids `"*"`, which would be actively unsafe on a public repo: per the action's `docs/security.md`, *"A bot that matches an entry does not need to be installed on your repository or have write access."*

## Changes
- **`.github/workflows/claude.yml`** (new) — the assistant workflow.
  - `additional_permissions: actions: read` (paired with `actions: read` in `permissions:`) so Claude can read CI status and download job logs.
  - `claude_args: --allowedTools "Bash,Read,Write,Edit,NotebookEdit,Glob,Grep,WebFetch,WebSearch,TodoWrite,Task"`.
  - `github_token` intentionally unset — it's optional, and only required for `allowed_non_write_users`, which this workflow doesn't use.
- **`docs/ops/ci-cd.md`** — documents the workflow (required by the repo's same-PR docs rule for cross-cutting operational config).
- **`CLAUDE.md`** — one bullet noting the second workflow and why `allowed_bots` must stay unset.

## No `if:` trigger-phrase guard, on purpose
The usual pattern gates on `contains(github.event.comment.body, '@claude')`, but GitHub expressions have no `toLower()` and `contains()` is case-sensitive — that guard silently drops `@Claude`, the spelling most likely typed at the start of a sentence, and a dropped trigger is indistinguishable from a broken workflow. The action does its own case-insensitive detection. Cost is a runner that starts and exits early on unrelated comments.

## Scope
`contents: write` lets Claude push a branch and open a PR. It still cannot push to `main`, which `new-relo-main-ruleset` protects (PR mandatory, linear history, both required checks) — the ruleset is the backstop on production, not the token scope.

## Verification
- Every input name checked against the action's live `action.yml` before use, not from memory.
- `claude_args` passthrough flags confirmed against the action's `docs/configuration.md`.
- `github_token` precedence read directly from the action source: `steps.run.outputs.github_token || inputs.github_token || github.token`.
- The `allowed_bots` exposure claim checked against the action's `docs/security.md` — which is what caught the original error.
- Comment-author identity measured live on #185 (created and closed for this purpose).
- Both workflow files parse as valid YAML (`yaml.safe_load`); asserted `allowed_bots` is absent from the final config.
- Confirmed the OAuth token appears only as `${{ secrets.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN }}` with no literal value committed.
- No `src/` changes, so `Syntax check` / `Build check (dry-run)` are unaffected.

author: stringhijocimar-cyber
body:
A tela Conferir mentia por omissão.

Ela abria com um formulário vazio pedindo o número do concurso e as quinze
dezenas à mão — enquanto o app **já** tinha o concurso guardado e **já** havia
conferido todos os jogos contra ele, sozinho, na abertura. Um jogo com 14
acertos na Lotofácil ficava invisível ali: para descobrir, era preciso ir até
Meus jogos e procurar.

Pedir para digitar um resultado que o app conhece não é só trabalho repetido —
é dizer que não sabe.

## Antes e depois

| Antes | Depois |
|---|---|
| Formulário vazio: concurso, data, 15 dezenas | Painel com o último sorteio: número, data, dezenas, ganhadores |
| Botão "Conferir 3 jogos salvos" (como se nada tivesse sido conferido) | "3 jogos conferidos · melhor **14 acertos** · **1 em faixa de prêmio**" |
| Os acertos só apareciam em Meus jogos | Cada jogo com os acertos marcados, do melhor para o pior |
| Dois botões de busca com efeitos parecidos | Um botão de atualizar, com três respostas distintas |

O formulário à mão continua abaixo — é a via que não depende de rede — agora
apresentado como o que é: para um concurso que a busca não trouxe.

## As três travas de honestidade

**Quem manda é `conferencias`, nunca uma recontagem no painel.** Ela é
preenchida por `conferenciaAutomatica()`, que respeita a regra de que um jogo só
vale para concursos a partir da data em que foi salvo. Recontar no painel
produziria acertos em sorteios anteriores ao dia em que o jogo existiu — o
número mais fácil de exibir e o mais desonesto.

O teste que cobre isso usa um jogo salvo **depois** do sorteio e com dezenas
**idênticas** às sorteadas. Se o painel recontasse, ele apareceria com 15
acertos e faixa de prêmio:

```
ok   o jogo salvo DEPOIS do sorteio não aparece como acerto
ok   ele aparece explicando por que ficou de fora — jogo salvo em 2026-08-20, depois do sorteio
```

**Jogo não coberto diz por que ficou de fora**, em vez de sumir da lista ou
aparecer com zero. Zero é uma afirmação; ausência de conferência é outra coisa.
Vale para teimosinha fora da faixa declarada também (`terminou no 3301`,
`começa no 3500`).

**O painel diz o que o app guardou, não o que existe no mundo.** O texto admite,
com essas palavras, que pode haver concurso mais novo que ninguém buscou.

## O botão de atualizar

Três desfechos, cada um com resposta própria — um botão que responde sempre a
mesma coisa ensina a pessoa a não ler o que ele diz:

| situação | resposta |
|---|---|
| concurso novo | "Concurso 3402 é novo por aqui. 1 conferência feita." |
| já conhecido | "Já estava atualizado: 3402 continua sendo o último." |
| sem rede | "Nenhuma fonte respondeu (…). Dá para digitar o resultado à mão abaixo." |

Os três são testados no navegador, com `buscarNaCaixa` trocada por uma função de
teste — depender da Caixa responder tornaria a seção um gerador de falha
intermitente. Também é testado que buscar duas vezes não duplica a conferência,
e que o recado não persegue a pessoa por outras telas nem vaza para outra
modalidade.

## Dois defeitos que o painel empurrou para debaixo do olho

- **"Conferir 1 jogo salvos"** — o plural caía só no substantivo e o adjetivo
  ficava fixo. Defeito antigo, visível só no caso de quem está começando. Agora
  há teste varrendo o painel inteiro atrás de `1 jogos`, `1 acertos`, `seus 1`.
- **"buscar o último concurso"** no formulário virou duplicata do painel. Saiu,
  junto com o parâmetro `qual` de `preencher()`, que ficou sem chamador. Um teste
  guarda a ausência para a duplicata não voltar por distração.

## Validação

| bateria | resultado |
|---|---|
| motor | 575 passaram, 0 falharam (+29) |
| interface | 52 passaram, 0 falharam (+7, estável em 3 execuções) |
| ícones | 34 conferências, nenhum problema |
| XML do Android | 11 arquivos, bem-formados |
| referência dourada | idêntica |
| `index.html` vs `www/index.html` | idênticos |

Largura conferida em **360, 390 e 412 px**, nos três estados do painel (com
jogos, sem jogos, sem concurso guardado) — sem estouro horizontal em nenhum.

Nada do motor adaptativo, das travas de honestidade do laboratório ou das outras
telas foi tocado.

author: heshipstech
body:
## The table

Five columns, units in the header rather than repeated on every cell, right-aligned mono figures, about five rows visible then scrolling with the header staying put.

| When (s) | Closed for (ms) | Amplitude (mm) | Speed (mm/s) | A/V (ms) |

A blink under **1.5 mm** of amplitude is **greyed rather than hidden**. The export keeps that row, so the panel must not disagree with the file. The threshold comes from measured sessions where real blinks ran 2.2 to 6.9 mm and the phantoms sat under 1 mm.

`formatBlinkEvent` is deleted rather than left behind.

## The modal

The question used to sit inside the Session card, and the export waits on its answer. A card that can run past the fold plus a question that gave no sign of itself produced a report that Export CSV was broken when it was only waiting.

**Deliberately not closable by the backdrop or Escape.** Every way out records an answer, Skip included. A dismissal that recorded nothing would leave a file that cannot say whether the question was declined or never asked.

## What the old panel was carrying

After answering, it stayed on screen showing your answer, because that answer goes into the exported file and being able to see what you said is part of trusting the data.

A modal cannot keep that promise by staying open, since staying open blocks the page. **The record moved into the Session card** and the dialog closes on every path out.

## What the suite found

**Seven specs broke at once.** A dialog that cannot be scrolled past cannot be clicked past either, and each of them started a camera and then clicked something. They answer it first now, exactly as a person does. The shared helper tolerates its absence, because a run that fails before a session starts never asks.

`"answer the question below"` lost its last word. Nothing is below a modal.

Two lines are sentences rather than label-and-value rows, the score headline and the dialog prompt, and the hidden colon rendered them as `Alertness scoremeasuring...`.

## Gates

lint, typecheck, 603 unit, coverage 98.68%, 22 e2e across two engines, format:check, build, bundle budget 219.8 kB of 240, ruff, 97 Python.

- `auth.js` registra **login, logout, PIN errado, bloqueio e acesso negado** (categorias `acesso` e `seguranca`). Negativas GET de API são ignoradas para não afogar a auditoria com polling; telas e mutações são registradas.

- `cont_route.js`: quem tem `contagem.ajustar` aplica direto; quem só tem `contagem.contar` deixa o ajuste **PENDENTE** em `contagem_pendente`. O estoque só muda na aprovação, registrada na auditoria com **quem contou e quem aprovou**.

author: sos-pc
body:
Found while looking at something else: a **25 MB FLAC sitting in `/staging` since 7 August** — nine days — plus an empty job directory from the same day. I had seen both twice tonight and dismissed them as "not mine".

## What actually happened, not what I first assumed

`/staging` is shared with the engine container: the engine writes each download into `/staging/<uuid4 hex>/`, the Go side moves the file out and removes the directory. That removal is a **deferred `RemoveAll` on the success path**, and nothing else ever looked at the volume.

My first hypothesis was a client-side HTTP timeout leaving an orphan. The evidence says otherwise:

| checked | result |
|---|---|
| is the track in the library? | **yes**, FLAC and cover both present |
| does it have a `library_files` row? | **no** — a `tracks` row, nothing else |

So the ingestion *succeeded*. What did not happen is the deferred cleanup **and** the catalog write. That pairing is the signature of the process dying between the atomic write and the end of the job — a deferred call does not run when you are killed — not of a failed download.

## The sweep

`reclaimStagingLoop`: 10 minutes after startup, then every 6 hours. Same shape as `cleanupLoop` and `verifyLibraryLoop`, panic recovery included.

Two rules keep it from deleting a live download, and **both** are needed:

- **Only directories the engine would have created** — `uuid4().hex`, 32 lowercase hex characters. Anything else on that volume came from something that is not a download, and age alone would eventually find it.
- **Staleness is the newest write anywhere inside the directory**, not the directory's own mtime. A directory's mtime changes when an entry is created or removed, *not* while a file inside it grows — so a long download looks as old as the moment its file appeared. Verified against a mutant using the directory mtime: it deletes an in-flight job.

**Six hours, not six minutes**, because the engine is a *separate* container and can still be writing into a directory this process gave up on: the Go client's timeout is 10 minutes, after which it returns an error while the engine carries on.

`engineStagingDir` is exported as `EngineStagingDir` so the jobs package can ask where the volume is — matching its already-exported neighbour `EngineBaseURL`.

## A test that was wrong before it was right

The first version created two directories differing only in case. On Windows those are **the same directory**, so the pair collapsed into one and the assertions passed while testing nothing — and it would have passed on Linux CI too, for a different and equally uninformative reason. The uppercase rule belongs to `isJobDirName` and is tested there, on the function, where the filesystem cannot interfere.

## After merge

The two stranded directories go on their own, 10 minutes after the app restarts. No manual cleanup needed — and worth watching for the log line:

```
[Staging] Removed abandoned job directory path=... bytes=... idle_for=...
```

## Not fixed here

The missing `library_files` row for that 7 August track. The file is in the library and the catalog does not know it — which the library rebuild in Maintenance is exactly what exists to reconcile. Separate action, separate decision.

author: rickyr19631
body:
## Summary
- Root-caused the "images look morphed/displaced on phone" report: `.item-art` (the product photo area on every menu card), `.case-item` (hero showcase icons), and `.map-art` (the location map) each had an `<svg width:100%; height:100%>` child living inside a parent sized with CSS `aspect-ratio`. That combination creates a circular sizing dependency, and the browser resolves it by silently forcing the parent to the svg's own intrinsic ratio (1:1, from its square viewBox) instead of the intended ratio. In practice this meant the intended 4:3 product image area was rendering as a large, off-center square on every one of the 18 menu items, with the icon artwork sitting oddly inside it.
- Fixed by making the icon `position: absolute` with an explicit `inset` and explicit `width`/`height`, which takes it out of the layout pass that was causing the circular dependency, so the parent's `aspect-ratio` resolves correctly and the icon centers cleanly inside it.
- While in there, redrew the croissant and cinnamon roll icons — both were hard to read as their intended pastry even before this bug.

## Test plan
- [x] Verified via computed layout: `.item-art` now measures the correct 4:3 box (333 × 249.75px at a 375px viewport) instead of the previous 333 × 333px square
- [x] Screenshotted every menu category (Breads, Cakes, Cookies, Pastries, Pies) at 375px width — all icons render centered and undistorted

author: chelsealong
body:
## What does this PR do?

`_get_mcp_servers()` in `hermes_cli/mcp_config.py` only read the native
`mcp_servers` config block, so every `hermes mcp` subcommand
(`add`/`remove`/`list`/`test`/`login`/`reauth`/`configure`) was blind to
a portable Agent Plugin's MCP server. The plugin loads fine and its
skills work at runtime — `tools/mcp_tool.py` already bridges native +
portable there — but the CLI/dashboard name resolution never did, so a
portable server that needs OAuth had no route to a token and was
permanently unauthenticatable.

This merges `PluginManager.get_portable_mcp_servers()` into
`_get_mcp_servers()`'s result, with native entries winning on name
collision — the same precedence already used by the runtime tool
layer in `tools/mcp_tool.py:5132`. Portable entries surface under
their existing namespaced key.

Several follow-on write paths needed a guard once portable names became
visible in the merged dict, or they would have behaved incorrectly:
- `hermes mcp remove <portable-name>` would delete nothing (not in
  native config) while still printing "Removed" — now reports that
  the server is plugin-owned and can't be removed this way.
- `hermes mcp configure <portable-name>` would have written a
  connection-less native stub entry (just a `tools` filter, no
  `url`/`command`) that then shadows the working portable one under
  the new native-wins precedence — now reports the same thing.
- `tui_gateway/methods_tools.py`'s `mcp.servers.set_api_key` RPC (used
  by the TUI/gateway to store credentials) reads the same merged
  `_get_mcp_servers()` and only checked `name not in servers` before
  unconditionally writing `cfg["mcp_servers"][name] = entry` with a
  real bearer token in it. Once portable names became visible, this
  path would succeed for a portable-only name and write a
  credential-bearing native shadow entry — worse than the pre-fix
  state, where the RPC correctly 404'd. This was caught in review
  (missed in the initial diff, which only audited `mcp_config.py`'s
  own call sites) and is now guarded the same way as `cmd_mcp_configure`.

## Related Issue

Fixes #87253

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/mcp_config.py`: `_get_mcp_servers()` now merges in
  `get_portable_mcp_servers()` (native wins on collision); guarded
  `cmd_mcp_remove` and `cmd_mcp_configure` against portable-only names.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_mcp_config.py`: added
  `test_portable_plugin_mcp_servers_are_visible` and
  `test_native_server_wins_name_collision_with_portable`.
- `tui_gateway/methods_tools.py`: guarded the `mcp.servers.set_api_key`
  RPC handler against portable-only names, matching the
  `cmd_mcp_configure` guard.
- `tests/tui_gateway/test_mcp_profile_rpcs.py`: added
  `test_set_api_key_rejects_portable_only_name`.

## How to Test

1. Install a portable Agent Plugin whose `mcp.json` declares a remote
   OAuth MCP server.
2. `hermes mcp list` now shows it; `hermes mcp login <name>` can find
   it and run the OAuth flow.
3. Automated:
   `pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_mcp_config.py tests/tui_gateway/test_mcp_profile_rpcs.py`

### Test output

```
tests/hermes_cli/test_mcp_config.py .................................... [ 81%]
tests/tui_gateway/test_mcp_profile_rpcs.py .........                      [100%]
49 passed in 3.51s
```

Verified the new tests fail without their corresponding source fix:
- `test_portable_plugin_mcp_servers_are_visible`: reverted
  `hermes_cli/mcp_config.py` to `HEAD~1` → fails with
  `AssertionError: assert '...' in {}` (old `_get_mcp_servers()` never
  looked at portable servers). Restored → passes alongside the rest.
- `test_set_api_key_rejects_portable_only_name`: reverted the guard
  just added to `tui_gateway/methods_tools.py`'s `set_api_key` handler
  → the RPC returns `{'ok': True, ...}` and would write a
  credential-bearing native shadow entry for the portable-only name,
  reproducing the exact regression a reviewer caught before merge.
  Restored the guard → the RPC 4064s and no `config.yaml`/`.env` write
  happens.

- [x] My PR contains only changes related to this fix (no unrelated commits)

### Documentation & Housekeeping

description reviewed before pushing.

author: muramatsu-kohei
body:
## 背景

起動バナー `Opus 5 · Claude Max · <組織名>` は 2 系統の寄せ集めで、プラン名は `.credentials.json` から即座に反映されるのに対し、組織名は `~/.claude.json` の **24 時間キャッシュ**から読まれる。`swap` は `.credentials.json` しか書かないため、切り替え直後は「プランだけ新しく、組織名は前のアカウントのまま」という食い違いが最大 1 日続く。

2026-08-16 に無編集の実測で確定した。個人 (Max) アカウントで動かしているのに、TTL が切れるまでバナーは組織アカウント名を出し続け、TTL 切れ後の起動でようやく `organizationType` が `claude_team` → `claude_max` に変わった。

つまりバナーはアカウントの取り違え検出に使えない。むしろ Team のつもりで個人枠を溶かす事故をそれらしい表示で後押しする。

## 変更

### 1. アカウントスロットの表示

```
claude @max | Opus5 hi | ctx 41k | $0.32 +12/-3 | 5h 26% 05:50 | 7d 7% Sat 09:00
```

- `readAccountSlot()` が `~/.claude/accounts/.current` を読み、先頭グループに `@<スロット名>`(マゼンタ)を出す
- `@` を付けるのは、色を落とす端末でディレクトリ名の一部に見えないようにするため
- **「無い」と「読めない」を区別する。** ファイルが無いとき(未導入、まだ一度も swap していない、`swap` が来歴を消した)だけ無表示。読めない・壊れている・ホームが解決できないときは `@?` を出す。畳むと「読めていないだけ」が「未導入」と同じ見た目になり、この表示が防ごうとしている“取り違えに気づけない状態”を自分で作ることになる
- 許す字種は account-guard の `NAME_RE` と同一。長さは弾かず 16 文字で切り詰める(弾くと、長い名前を付けた利用者にだけ表示が消える)
- ホームの解決順は `credentials.js` の `usableHome()` に合わせる(`USERPROFILE` > `HOME` > `os.homedir()`、空白のみは不採用)
- 限界も明記した。`.current` は「前回このツールが切り替えた先」の来歴であって現在のログインの証明ではなく、`swap` を通さず `/login` すると古いまま残る

`docs/account-separation.md` は「バナーのほうが正確」を理由にこの案を却下していた。前提が誤りだったので、§4.6 として方針転換の経緯ごと記録した。

### 2. ctx はトークン数を主に出す

色の閾値は既に絶対量 (150k / 250k) で決まっており、`%` は「なぜ黄色いのか」の説明にしかなっていなかった。1M 窓では 250k 使っても 25% にしかならず、運用上も確認しているのは常に何 k かのほうだった。

| 状態 | 変更前 | 変更後 |
|---|---|---|
| 通常 | `ctx 4% 41k` | `ctx 41k` |
| 85% | `ctx 85% 41k` | `ctx 41k 85%` |
| トークン数が取れない | `ctx 85%` | `ctx 85%`(据え置き) |

`%` を添えるのは窓そのものを使い切りそうなとき (70% 以上) だけ。そこでは自動 compact が近いという別種の情報になるため、このファイルの「既定から外れたときだけ出す」方針に合流させた。

### 3. 利用枠が別建てのモデルは色を変える

`5h` / `7d` は入力に来た枠をそのまま出しているだけで、どのモデルの枠かは区別しない。Fable は枠が別建てなので、切り替えたことに気づかないまま残量を読むと見込みを外す。モデル名の色で切り分ける。

- 判定は `ALT_MODEL_RE`(既定 `/fable/i`)。モデル ID と表示名の両方に当てるのは、表示名の付け方が変わりうるため
- 色は明るい青。警告色(黄/赤)を避けたのは、危険ではなく「別勘定」だという区別を色で表すため

### 4. `no fields` 診断がスロット表示で潰れないようにする

スロットは stdin ではなくローカルのファイル由来なので、入力の形が変わって全項目を落としても `@max` の 1 項目が残り、`parts.length === 0` が成立しなくなっていた(このブランチで作り込んだ退行)。異常が「項目の少ない正常な行」に化け、ファイル冒頭の「異常時も必ず1行出す」という不変条件が、まさにそれが守るべき場面で働かない。スロット由来の 1 項目を判定から外した。

## 検証

`claude-statusline` には自動テストが無いため、サンプル入力を加工して手で確認した(下表は最終コミット時点の実際の出力)。

| ケース | 結果 |
|---|---|
| `.current` あり | `demo @max` |
| `.current` 無し(未導入相当) | `@` ごと出ない。他の項目は不変 |
| `.current` に制御文字 | `demo @?` |
| `.current` が読めない(EISDIR) | `demo @?` |
| ホームが解決できない(空白のみ) | `demo @?` |
| 26 文字のスロット名 | `demo @personal-max-ac~` |
| 入力が `{}` (スロットあり) | `(statusline: no fields)` |
| 入力が `cwd` のみ | `demo @max` |
| 入力が `model` のみ | `@max \| Opus5` |
| ctx 4% | `ctx 41k`(緑) |
| ctx 85% | `ctx 41k 85%`(黄) |
| `total_input_tokens` 欠損 | `ctx 85%` にフォールバック |
| model = Opus 5 | 従来どおり dim |
| model = Fable 5 | 明るい青 |

`~/.claude/statusline.js` への配備後、`usage.jsonl` への追記が継続していることも確認した(usage-tracker フックの解決を壊していない)。

author: claymore666
body:
Refs #549

Addresses finding **2** in #549 — which I think is the more important half of that issue, and is independent of the orphan-lease flake that surfaced it.

## The detector has been blind on two of three modes since #527

The macvlan/ipvlan fixture's parent link (`dh-itest-host`) is brought up with **no address at all**. Only the DHCP-server end of the veth pair is addressed.

A host answers an ARP request only if it can route a reply back to the sender, so the conflict probe needs a source on the leased subnet. With none available it falls back to a link-local source, and since #524 that correctly yields *undetermined* rather than clean. So every `192.168.99.x` probe reported "could not run".

The bridge fixture was unaffected, because there the parent **is** the addressed bridge — which is exactly why runs showed one verdict and two failures:

```
CONFLICT PROBE: 1 probe(s) reached a verdict and found no conflict, but 2 could
  not run at all.
```

That line has been printing since #527 merged, and **nothing failed on it**. At the suite level "nothing checked" and "nothing found" read the same — the precise failure #524 exists to prevent, one level up. `ConflictProbeLine` is what made it visible; the instrument was working, the gate was missing.

To be clear about severity: this is a **fixture** gap, not a plugin bug. In production a macvlan parent is a real NIC that carries an address, so the probe works there. What was broken is our ability to *prove* it works.

## The fix

`HostVethAddr = 192.168.99.2/24`, applied to the parent.

- **`.2`** — outside `[DHCPPoolStart, DHCPPoolEnd]` so dnsmasq can never hand it to a container (which would manufacture a genuine conflict), not the server's `.1`, and not `StaticTestIP`.
- **Applied after the server's address**, deliberately. Both ends of the pair now hold an address in `192.168.99.0/24`, so the host has two connected routes with equal metric and Linux breaks that tie by insertion order. Installing the server's first leaves every existing non-source-pinned path selecting the interface it selected before this change. The probe is insensitive to the order either way — it installs a `/32` link-scope route for the address under test, more specific than either `/24`.

## Verified

- Measured the two-addresses-on-one-subnet case in an unprivileged netns: two connected routes appear as expected, and source-pinned traffic between the ends works.
- `TestHostVethAddr_MakesTheConflictProbeUsable` passes — pins that the constant stays on-subnet, out of the pool, and off both the server and the static reservation.
- `go vet`, harness package tests, license headers.

## Not verified until CI runs

Whether adding a second address on that subnet disturbs any of the ~30 tests sharing this fixture. That is exactly what the integration suites answer, and I would rather they answer it than reason about it further.

**The check to watch in this run** is the conflict-probe census line: it should go from `1 reached a verdict, 2 could not run` to all probes reaching a verdict, with the only remaining failure being the one `TestAddressConflict_BareParentIsUndetermined` causes on purpose.

## Deliberately not in this PR

Making the census **fail** rather than report. It is the obvious "postmortem ends in an executable check" move, and I want it — but it is not as simple as it looks:

- `TestAddressConflict_BareParentIsUndetermined` (#541) increments `conflict_probe_failures` on purpose, so a blanket failure on `>0` breaks a correct test;
- the floor runs per shard, and a shard that creates no endpoints legitimately has zero probes, so failing on `probes == 0` would red the suite spuriously.

Filing that separately rather than rushing a gate into the release that fails for the wrong reasons.

author: mherschberg
body:
The adoption half of #134. Both rules are stated directly here rather than left to the template comment, since this is the path that actually points at someone's production repo.

## CI is never installed

`templates/ci/code-repo-ci.yml` is the gate for a repo the method **creates**, and it is failing-until-configured by design. Dropped into a running system it either replaces the workflow that gates their merges or fails every build until someone deletes it.

Adopted repos already have CI. The recon map's **Tests & CI** section recorded what each one runs, and session `1.12` writes that up — so the information is captured without touching anything. Moving a repo onto the standard gate stays a decision its owners make later.

## The notice follows the README decision, not the repo

If the `Role in <project>` section from #133 was **accepted**, that section is BSD-3-Clause scaffold material and the repo is owed its notice — placed with `scripts/apply-project-license.sh --notice-only <repo-path>` (#134), so no project `LICENSE` is written and nothing is claimed about the repo's own code.

Running the helper **without** the flag is called out explicitly as wrong: it refuses, and correctly, since it would otherwise assert the project's license over code the method never authored.

If the addition was **declined**, nothing Throughstone-authored is in the repo, so nothing is owed. Placing a notice for absent material would only mislead a later reader.

## Verified

- Full maintainer suite 14/14.
- Fresh adoption fixture from a `git archive` of this branch: `check.sh` 0 fail / 0 warn, `links.sh` 0 fail.
- Three assertions pin the parts that fail silently: the CI prohibition, the exact `--notice-only` invocation, and the declined-means-nothing-owed branch (the one an agent is most likely to "helpfully" fill in).

## Depends on

`--notice-only` lands in #134 on the base line. Nothing here breaks before that forward-merges — the instruction names a mode that doesn't exist yet on this branch, exactly as earlier adoption work named the base rules it rides.

author: juliantellez
body:
**What.** A dispatch node declares what will show it worked, and the crew checks it. `expect: { file: package.json }` is a path that must be in the run's thread after the turn, read from the working directory the crew keeps. `expect: { contains: "all green" }` is a string the reply must carry. An expectation that does not hold stops the run, naming the node and what was not there.

**Why.** The first flow run against a real crew finished at `done` with four transitions and read back as a success, and none of the work happened. The repository was not in the run's thread, every turn said so, and the run took the success edge because the only signal a `choice` had was `result.failed`. That says the model did not error. It says nothing about whether anything was achieved, and a capable model answers plausibly rather than stopping.

The run stops rather than branching: the crew knows the work did not happen and does not know why, and a run that halts is read correctly while a run that finishes is believed. The thread is left alone rather than archived, because that is where the evidence is. An expectation nothing could check stops the run too. A graph that declares nothing behaves exactly as it did.

**Left out on purpose.** A command the crew runs and requires to exit zero, which is the obvious third form the issue names. It turns an imported graph into a way to run arbitrary commands through the control plane, and that is a decision to take on its own rather than in passing. The file check covers the case that was found. Say the word and it is a small change on top.

The file check is a Go interface the engine holds, not a new call on the service, for the same reason.

Closes https://github.com/atlantic-blue/quay-crew/issues/263

**Tests.** Nine cases in `internal/flow/expect_test.go` (the reducer stopping, the reducer carrying on, both directions of the reply check, an expectation nobody can check, and four refusals at import). Three cases in `internal/controlplane/threadholds_test.go` for the file check itself, including a crew with nowhere to look. Three scenarios in `features/flows.feature`: a run stops when the file is not there, carries on when a turn actually wrote it, and stops when the reply does not carry what it said. Watched failing in both directions: with the check disabled the two stopping scenarios go red, and with the file lookup broken the carrying on scenario goes red.

**Stacked.** Merge order: https://github.com/atlantic-blue/quay-crew/pull/326 first, then https://github.com/atlantic-blue/quay-crew/pull/328, then this one. You are here: 3 of 3. This branch is based on the 264 branch, not on `main`.

body:
## Merge order

1. **This PR first** (`#479`, text-only draft sync)
2. Then desktop `#483` (images/files on the same draft)
3. iOS `#6` pairs with this PR (needs these endpoints)
4. iOS `#7` stacks on iOS `#6` and pairs with `#483`

`#483` includes this commit. Merge this on its own; do not squash `#483` first.

---

Unsent composer text is localStorage-only today, so a sentence typed on desktop is gone on the phone (and the other way around).

This persists the visible composer string for a **persisted** conversation and syncs it last-write-wins, same origin+revision pattern as `tabs://changed`.

## Security
- Authenticated `get_composer_draft` / `put_composer_draft` only.
- Only real conversation ids (`get_by_id`). New-tab `draft:` keys stay local.
- 256 KiB UTF-8 cap. Origin is 1-64 `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`.
- The WS notify is **ids only** (`conversation_id`, `revision`, `origin`, `cleared`). The body is never on the firehose, so a WS/log dump cannot leak what the user is typing.
- Empty text is a tombstone so a clear on one device wipes the other.
- No logging of draft text.

## Clients
Desktop/web: after the existing 300ms local draft save, PUT the visible text. On open / reconnect / notify, GET and apply if the revision is newer and `origin` is not this browser.

iOS native follow-up is `#6` on `codeg-ios`. A phone using the web UI is covered by this PR alone.

## Tests
- Origin / size / missing-conversation / put-get-clear in `conversation_composer_draft_service`.
- WS payload has no `text` field.
- `composer-draft-sync.test.ts` for key parsing and echo suppression.

No secrets. One concern.

## Summary

- Full audit of OwnerControlCenter and overlapping Projects Hub, Digest, Approvals, Activity, System Health, Ventures, Marketing, CRM, Finance, Tasks, and development-status surfaces.
- Defines canonical business attention signals, freshness/state semantics, source precedence, and unsupported gaps.
- Proposes read-only OwnerAttentionItem and OwnerDevelopmentStatus projection contracts.
- Recommends live business computation plus a generated development artifact, without creating a competing source of truth.
- Defines a bounded OC-A through OC-F implementation sequence.

Documentation and architecture planning only. No production UI, backend, API, schema, Airtable, runtime, routing, navigation, business logic, or projection JSON changes.

author: pablonyx
body:
## Scope

Adds two new flows to the `renderer.flow.*` diagnostics family
(`lib/infra/diagnostics/renderer-flow-timing.ts`), closing the R12/T4
perceived-latency instrumentation debt. **Measurement only** — no behavior
changes, no new UI, no new thresholds (both budgets stay `thresholdMs: null`,
matching the existing four flows).

1. **Composer submit → first visible token** (`composer_submit`): begins at
   prompt-submit dispatch for the existing-session send path (keyed by
   `sessionId`; new-session sends are out of scope since no `sessionId`
   exists yet at submit time), finishes when the latest transcript turn
   gains its first renderable assistant content in
   `session-stream-flush-apply.ts` (the cheapest truthful proxy available —
   there's no paint hook at this layer).
2. **Mode switch input → paint** (`mode_switch`): begins when a mode config
   change is enqueued (keyed by `intentId`, which PRO-261's tail-coalescing
   keeps stable across a rapid burst of switches — re-begin on each pick
   restarts the clock to the latest input), finishes when
   `dispatchConfigIntent` commits the mode change.
3. **Pane/session switch**: already covered by the existing `session_open`
   flow family (`session-open-flow-marks.ts` + `use-session-history-hydration.ts`).
   Not duplicated, per the existing flow's own instrumentation.

Both new flows are two-point (begin/finish only — no `shell_committed` /
`data_ready` midpoints), so their `content_stable` records omit
`intent_to_shell_ms` / `shell_to_data_ms` and carry timing solely via
`intent_to_stable_ms`. **Field semantics (post-review):** `data_to_stable_ms`
is Honeycomb's "last-mile paint stage" field (time from `data_ready` to
`content_stable`); it is only emitted when `data_ready` was actually reached,
for every flow kind, not just the two new ones. composer_submit/mode_switch
never emit it — their budget metric points at
`renderer.flow.<kind>.intent_to_stable_ms` instead, the field they actually
produce.

## Review round 2 (REQUEST CHANGES → addressed)

- **FINDING 1 (HIGH):** the composer_submit finish check ran on every
  applied stream batch, including reconnect/gap-fill batches, and looked at
  "whatever is `turnOrder`'s last entry" rather than the specific submitted
  turn. A gap-fill batch completing an OLDER turn that was still
  `turnOrder`'s last entry (because the newly submitted turn hadn't started
  yet) would satisfy the check and finish the flow on stale content — a
  bogus duration recorded, and the real completion silently swallowed
  (finish is one-shot). Fixed by binding the flow to the actual turn id the
  submit creates
  (`session-stream-flush-composer-submit-turn.ts`): the first turn id that
  appears in a batch which wasn't present in the prior `turnsById` map is,
  structurally, the submitted turn (a session has at most one
  `composer_submit` in flight — the composer blocks a second concurrent
  send). Dedup is by turn id against the full prior `turnsById` map, not by
  `turnOrder` position, so a gap-fill batch that merely reorders an
  existing turn can't be mistaken for a new one.
- **FINDING 2 (MEDIUM):** removed the `data_to_stable_ms` alias described
  above; see "Field semantics" note in Scope.

## Salvage

A prior agent attempt died mid-work leaving uncommitted changes in a
separate worktree (`/Users/pablohansen/proliferate-worktrees/ux-latency-r13`,
based on a merge of `origin/main` rather than `r1-instrumentation`). Its diff
was sound and applied cleanly against this branch's base with no
adjustment; every line above is that salvaged content, re-verified here.
Nothing was discarded.

## Testing

- Full `@proliferate/product-client` vitest suite (after rebuilding dist,

author: tya5
body:
**[architect]** — part of #4876. #4879 の続きですが、**別の hazard** です。#4879 は正規表現の欠陥（偽の違反数）を記録しました。これは**その 1 つ手前の段**です。

## 何が起きたか

```
① reviewing session が #4852 の body から prefix を grep → 見つからず
   → 14 セッションに broadcast「著者は名乗り出てください」
② 私が引き取り、★自分で grep → 同じく空
   → 「omission がどれくらい一般的か」を 200 PR の census で調査
   → 「200 中 60 件が rule 2 違反」と報告、gate を提案
③ 真実: prefix は最初から body の 571 字目に在った
   `[a-z-]+` が `e2e-coder` の数字を除外していた
```

②の各ステップは**独立した実測**です。それでも全部間違っていました。

## #4879 が届かない理由

**私は「著者は特定できるのか」を一度も訊いていません。** 受け取った問い —「なぜ特定できないのか」— が既に答えを主張していたので、**body を開くことが、私が立てたどの計画にも step として現れませんでした。** 原因を探し、もっともらしいものを見つけ、その上に構造的診断を積みました。

2 セッションの誤りは同じ正規表現に見えて、**同じ失敗ではありません**: 1 人目は測定を誤った。2 人目は**結論を出発条件として採用し**、その下流に本物の労力を注いだ。**問い自体を手渡されているとき、独立した測定は独立ではありません。**

## 既存の節との違い

§17・§20・§21 は、いずれも**著者が下手に構成した検索**の話です。ここでは検索は*結果*でした — よく出来た query が、誰も引き直さなかった前提に照準されていた。むしろ **§2 の self-sealing false prohibition の同型**です（偽の「X はできない」が、それを反証する使用を禁じて生き延びる）。違いは、封をしているのが主張の内容ではなく**問いの文法**であることです。

## 検出手法（節に書いたもの）

- **why-question は主張を運ぶ。問いに答える前に主張を検査する。** 「なぜ著者が特定できないのか」は 1 コマンドで反証できる — body を印字するだけ。**前提が自分の観測でなく他人から来たときは、毎回それを先に。**
- **推論した観測に印をつけるのと同じように、受け取った前提にも印をつける**（§23）。事実が既に述べられた状態でタスクが来たら、その事実は**自分が観測するまで未観測**です。「下流は全部測った」はその witness になりません。
- **兆候は「失敗し得る step が 1 つも無い計画」。** X の原因を探す検索には、X が偽と判明する分岐が在りません。

## Test plan

- [x] `mkdocs build --strict -f .mkdocs/mkdocs.yml` → built in 23.67s
- [x] `python scripts/check_doc_anchors.py` → `no dangling anchors into published pages`
- [x] `python scripts/check_retired_config_keys_denylist.py` → `OK: 0 hits (25 retired top-level key(s) checked)`
- [x] (skipped — `src/` / `tests/` 無変更のため ruff / tier audit / pytest は対象なし)
- [x] lead-coder に broker で「merge 後に follow-up で足すか、不要なら足さない、判断はお任せ」と伝えた上で起票。**不要と判断されたら close してください** — 保留のまま置くと、それ自体が silent な第 3 状態になるため、先に出しています。

Passe « champ libre » : le trio qui rend le site le plus attractif à cet endroit précis — le partage sur WhatsApp, la preuve sociale des ventes, et une vraie carte de l'île.

## Partage WhatsApp (le canal de Saint-Barth)
- Bouton **« Partager »** sur la fiche annonce et la fiche restaurant : feuille de partage native sur mobile (`navigator.share`), lien WhatsApp direct sur desktop.
- **Aperçus riches** : chaque annonce et chaque restaurant a désormais une image de partage générée à la volée (`opengraph-image`). Un lien collé dans un groupe WhatsApp affiche la photo de l'annonce, son titre et son prix — ou la carte typographique du restaurant (nom, cuisine, quartier, prix moyen) aux couleurs Food. Si la donnée est indisponible, une carte générique de marque prend le relais plutôt qu'un aperçu cassé.

## Annonces vendues (migration `0014_vendu_public.sql`)
- Une annonce marquée « vendu » **reste visible 7 jours** avec sa pastille dorée « Vendu », puis sort naturellement — au lieu de disparaître brutalement. C'est la meilleure preuve que le site fonctionne.
- `sold_at` posé par trigger en base (impossible à oublier ou antidater), fenêtre de 7 jours appliquée par la RLS elle-même.
- Fiche : bandeau « Cette annonce a trouvé preneur », barre de contact neutralisée. « À la une » n'affiche que du disponible. L'admin peut désormais ouvrir n'importe quelle fiche (utile pour juger un signalement).

## Carte St Barth Food (migration `0015_carte_restaurants.sql`)
- Les positions GPS des 54 fiches, reprises de l'export OpenStreetMap d'origine (elles avaient servi aux quartiers mais n'avaient pas été stockées) — correspondance sur le couple unique (nom, quartier).
- Bouton **« ◈ Carte »** dans les filtres de l'accueil Food : carte Leaflet de l'île, épingles dorées (grisées quand l'établissement est fermé en ce moment), popup avec nom, cuisine, note et lien vers la fiche. Les filtres actifs s'appliquent à la carte. Leaflet est chargé à la demande, jamais au premier affichage.

## Micro-finitions
- Transition d'entrée de page douce (`template.tsx`), rejouée à chaque navigation, respectueuse de `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- Retour tactile sur les cartes (léger enfoncement sous le doigt).

- `next build` passe (20 pages) ; tests Playwright avec données simulées : pastille et bandeau « Vendu », bouton Partager, 2 épingles + popup + mention « sans position » sur la carte ; les deux routes `opengraph-image` répondent en `image/png`.

author: saknopp
body:
This PR fixes an issue where autonomous agents (or external MCP runtimes) attempting to observe terminal output through `runTerminalCommand` would frequently receive empty strings or garbled text instead of the actual command `stdout`.

**The Problem:**
1. **Login Shells:** The implementation previously invoked `bash -l` (login shell). In non-TTY background execution contexts, user `.bash_profile` or `.bashrc` scripts often hang, execute interactive terminal-only utilities (like `tmux`), or prematurely `exit`, causing the node `child_process` to capture no output.
2. **ANSI Color Pollution:** `getColorEnv()` previously forced `FORCE_COLOR=1` and `TERM=xterm-256color`. While this looks great in the UI, agents expecting machine-readable text struggle to parse ANSI-polluted streams, and some CLI tools alter their output buffering behavior when they detect forced color sequences in a non-TTY pipe.

**The Solution:**
- Replaced the login shell flag `-l` with a standard `/bin/bash -c` execution to bypass user-specific interactive profile quirks.
- Modified `getColorEnv()` to explicitly request a plaintext environment (`NO_COLOR="1"`, `TERM="dumb"`), ensuring that the output returned to the agent is clean and strictly decodable.

**Testing:**
Verified locally that terminal execution commands reliably return their stdout streams to external LLM runtimes without hangs or formatting corruption.

author: saadings
body:
feat(ci): a screen taller than the screen gets photographed twice

`dashboard-390` ended on the `What came in` heading with the chart entirely
below the fold, and looked finished -- because a viewport shot always does.
The Dashboard is the first screen here one viewport cannot hold, and it is
the one Nauman asked for by name.

Any screen measured taller than the viewport now gets a second picture,
scrolled to the bottom: `dashboard-390-lower.png` beside `dashboard-390.png`.
Eleven of thirty-nine turned out not to fit. Screens that fit keep one.

Still two viewport captures rather than one `fullPage`. Full page distorts
anything sticky -- it put the day sheet's footer in the middle of its own
form -- and it photographs the Dashboard's chart blank, because resizing the
viewport makes recharts re-measure and the shot lands mid-remeasure. Each
capture here is a true viewport; only the scroll differs.

## Three things the first lower halves found

**A scroll that was dispatched and not waited for.** `mouse.wheel` returns
when the event is sent, not when the page has moved, so the position read
straight afterwards was zero on a page about to scroll -- a different screen
each run, which is what a race looks like. It now waits for the thing that
has to be true: the screen's own top going negative.

**My own pointer in the picture.** The wheel needs a pointer over the
content, and after scrolling it sat on the Dashboard's chart, which opened a
hover tooltip over its own bars and photographed it. The instrument was
changing what it measured. The pointer is taken back to a corner before the
shot.

**A column running off the right edge of `The houses` at 390.** `11,798,452`
then `9,3`, clipped. Not mine, and already fixed by #100 -- this branch
forked one merge before it, so the picture was a true statement about a
commit that is no longer the answer. Rebased onto `b3d0f46`, and
`dashboard-390-lower.png` now shows `9,310,000` and `12,840,000` whole.

Worth recording that **two instruments found it, on the same day, and
neither could have been the other.** const-2's column measurement found it
by asking every list where its cells sit. These pictures found it by
looking, below the fold, at a place no picture had ever reached -- the
Dashboard is the first screen here one viewport cannot hold, so before this
change there was nowhere for a still to find it.

## A count that cannot agree with itself

The first version counted pictures as it took them. Planting "never take the
lower half" then passed: the taking and the counting were one decision, so
removing it removed both, and the run reported thirty-nine pictures and a
cheerful `0 of them too tall`. That is exactly the defect the per-screen
count was added to prevent, arriving inside the fix for it.

Now the measurement writes down which lower halves are owed, before any is
taken, and the check asks the disk. Two facts rather than one: this screen
did not fit, and a picture of it exists.

## A screen that drew nothing is not a screen that fits

Both return "not taller than the viewport". The marker wait proves one
string is visible; it does not prove a screen has body. So a height under
200px is reported as a screen that did not draw. The shortest real screen
here is `How it looks` at 344px on a phone.

## Checked

Five defects planted. Four caught by the thing that names them: the lower
half decided and never written (`11 screens did not fit and have no lower
half`), a lower half written for a screen nothing measured as tall (`Wrote 78
pictures, expected 50`), the scroll dispatched and not waited for (`did not
scroll (its top is at 0)`), and a screen drawing its marker and nothing else
(`24px tall. That is not a short screen, it is a screen that did not draw`).

The fifth proved nothing and is recorded as proving nothing: setting the
height floor to a value nothing could fall under passes, because no screen
in the run was short. A plant whose condition never occurs is not a test of
the guard.

author: tradersamwise
body:
Switching symbol or interval left the native chart ignoring every drag, often for many seconds.

#1416 fixed one cause of this — a dropped `isLoading` edge — but the symptom survived, because the static projection that swallows drags is latched by **seven** independent conditions and that fixed one of them.

## Finding

Instrumenting all seven on device named the survivor in every repro:

```
holdingSnapshot true -> false
isLoading true -> false          <- #1416's latch, clearing correctly
barsContextMismatch true -> false
dataLoadRenderBlocked false -> true
pendingDataLoadViewport false -> true    <- never comes back
projection STILL pinned 2030ms | PF_XBTUSD@15 | set: dataLoadRenderBlocked, pendingDataLoadViewport
projection STILL pinned 4035ms ...
projection STILL pinned 6051ms ...
```

## Cause

`pendingDataLoadViewport` is a `useMemo` over `[dataKey, interval, viewportBars]` that reads the pending view-scale capture out of a **ref**. The layout effect that applies the capture clears that ref — but clearing a ref cannot invalidate a memo, so the derived viewport stayed non-null after it had already been consumed.

`dataLoadRenderBlocked` stayed true, the renderer stayed on a static projection, and the chart only recovered when the next bars array happened to change identity and re-ran the memo. On a quiet market that is an arbitrary wait, which is why it read as intermittent.

## Fix

The capture is state, so applying it invalidates the value derived from it.

## Measurement

iPhone 16 Pro simulator, harness that switches, waits 1.6s, then drags, using the time axis as the oracle:

| | drags ignored |
|---|---|
| before | 3 / 10 |
| after | 0 / 16 |

Suite is 2232/2233; the one failure is a pre-existing timeout in `ChartTopBar.test.ts`'s drawing-toolbar block that also fails on `master` and varies run to run.

No regression test: this is hook wiring with no pure seam, and the package has no `renderHook` infrastructure to build on.

body:
## Summary
- stop Cascade progression from fetching the server every 750ms
- reconcile server progression on startup / return-to-page and on a five-minute visible-tab cadence, while sampling local changes without network traffic
- accept both deployed Cascade progression response shapes
- add exponential retry backoff so Cloudflare quota failures cannot turn into a one-second retry storm
- preserve the two-visit anonymous-progress ownership boundary using a per-visit sessionStorage marker
- reduce global challenge-alert fallback polling from 5s to 60s while keeping immediate event-driven refresh opportunities
- reduce Cascade telemetry heartbeat from 30s to 5min and suppress periodic heartbeats for hidden/idle tabs
- prevent stale-device hydration from racing the local publisher into a redundant server write
- add browser/static request-budget regression coverage

## Why
Production metrics showed request amplification rather than CPU or memory pressure. The largest issue in this stabilization layer was `cascade-progression-sync.js`: every visible Cascade page performed `/api/me/progression` every 750ms. The global alert controller separately polled `/api/me/feed` every 5s.

This is stabilization stage 1. #327 is the stacked follow-up that makes the player-platform path event-driven and removes remaining read-side write amplification.

## Request budget after this change
- Cascade progression: startup/return reconciliation plus a five-minute visible-tab server cadence instead of 750ms polling
- alert fallback: at most once/minute while visible instead of once/5s
- telemetry heartbeat: at most once/5min while active and visible instead of once/30s
- unchanged local progression produces no network write
- failed progression requests back off from 15s exponentially to a 5min ceiling

## Validation
Fresh PR validation is running against the final head. Cascade coverage includes stale-device hydration with zero redundant writes and an idle-tab request budget. RPG scope is classified out on the final diff because this PR changes no RPG files.

No deployment change is included.

author: sauce-git
body:
Resolves two authority seams in `agents/pm.md`. Both are rewordings of authority text in the same document, so they land together — two PRs on this file would collide.

Closes #29
Closes #32

## What changed

### #29 — the PM and documentation (`:17`, `:52`)

`:13` granted the PM authority to "maintain the project's documentation" while `:45` forbade "editing source yourself", in a repository where the documentation **is** the product. Implements the middle path the owner recorded on the issue, as a new third paragraph under Authority:

> Mechanical documentation fixes are yours to write, on your own branch: typo, broken link, formatting, an index synced to files that already changed. Anything that changes a rule, a published claim, or what a passage means goes to a worker, exactly as code does; conventions alone stay yours. Nobody but you reviews that PR — a known, accepted gap, and why the list is exhaustive.

- **Boundary is closed, not a judgement call.** The mechanical class is an exhaustive enumeration ("why the list is exhaustive"); everything else is defined by the contrasting test — does the edit change a rule, a published claim, or what a passage means.
- **Self-review gap named.** "Nobody but you reviews that PR — a known, accepted gap" states it as accepted, and ties it to why the list is kept closed.
- **`:15` stands unchanged.** Never a direct push to the default branch; "on your own branch" plus "that PR" keeps the PM inside it.
- **Conventions carve-out.** Without `; conventions alone stay yours`, "anything that changes a rule → worker" would contradict the Conventions section (`:74`, "You maintain the conventions day to day; workers may not"), since conventions are rules. This is the one place where a meaning-changing edit stays with the PM, and it is now stated where the rule is.

**Reconciling `:13` / `:15` / `:45`** — note `:45` was rewritten by #34, so this addresses the current text at `:52`, not the text quoted in the issue:

| Line | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `:13` | "maintain the project's documentation and conventions" | unchanged — now defined by `:17` |
| `:15` | "Everything lands via pull request, documentation included" | unchanged, as the issue requires |
| `:52` | "not by **editing source yourself**" — reads as an absolute ban | "not by writing it yourself; **only the edits named under Authority are yours**" |

`:52` now points at the single place the boundary is stated instead of restating a competing one.

### #32 — review state vs marked comment (`:40`)

Before: `Submit a formal review state where the host permits one; otherwise post the verdict marked as the decision, never an unmarked comment.`

After: `Reviewing under the author's own account, post the verdict as a comment marked as the decision, never an unmarked one. Where the accounts differ, submit the formal review state.`

- Keyed on **identity**, not host capability.
- The marked-comment branch is stated **first and as a plain conditional** — not as a fallback, an exception, or an "otherwise". In the default setup it is the branch that always runs.
- "never an unmarked one" retained as the named failure.
- The forge error and the reasoning are **not** restated; only the decision rule, per the owner's instruction.
- No README change — dropped from scope by the owner.

## Rule inventory (before → after)

The hard constraint forbade growth, so the two additions are paid for by consolidating restatements elsewhere. **No rule was dropped.** Three were *relocated* to their single canonical statement rather than repeated:

| # | Rule | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Single merge authority framing | kept, reworded (`a single merge authority is what keeps` → `that single authority keeps`) |
| 2 | Project conventions binding, outrank this definition | verbatim |
| 3 | Reviews/merges PRs, manages issues, maintains docs + conventions | verbatim |
| 4 | Deletes merged/stale branches; owns worker lifecycle | verbatim |
| 5 | No source modification unless the user instructs | verbatim |
| 6 | No push to default branch; everything via PR, docs included | verbatim |
| **7** | **Mechanical doc fixes are the PM's; meaning changes go to a worker; conventions excepted; self-review gap accepted** | **ADDED (#29)** |
| 8 | Deciding table, all six rows | verbatim |
| 9 | Decide alone = decide + report; escalate = options + recommendation | verbatim |
| 10 | Never review from memory; read governing conventions first | verbatim |
| 11 | Review standard is the project's; find via same entry point | kept; dropped `and apply it as written` (duplicates "is the project's, not yours") |
| 12 | Four fallback checks (Scope/Conventions/Verification/Depth) | verbatim |
| 13 | Report a result per check; mark the unverified | kept, tightened |
| 14 | Cite `rule §section` + `file:line`; uncitable = preference | verbatim |
| **15** | **Verdict channel keyed on shared vs different account** | **REWORDED (#32)** |
| 16 | Approve/merge only when checks pass, none unverified | kept; stopped re-listing the four checks |
| 17 | Request changes with a fix direction; re-review the delta | verbatim |
| 18 | Reject when the approach is wrong: explain, close, open an issue | verbatim |
| 19 | Named failure: approving to be agreeable / clear the queue | verbatim |

author: ifeelrobbed
body:
## Summary
- Every metric in this repo so far reflects the cluster's own view of itself - nothing checks that the site is actually reachable (DNS/TLS/200) from outside. Deploys `prometheus-blackbox-exporter` (same pattern as `cert-manager`/`ingress-nginx`: a plain Helm-chart `Application`) and a `Probe` CRD targeting `https://robertjcameron.com` with the chart's default `http_2xx` module.
- `http_2xx` against an `https://` target also reports `probe_ssl_earliest_cert_expiry` for free, covering cert-expiry visibility as a side effect - no extra config needed.
- Adds `probeSelectorNilUsesHelmValues: false` + `probeNamespaceSelector: {}` to `kube-prometheus-stack`'s values pre-emptively. The same cluster-wide-discovery gap that left resume-site's own `ServiceMonitor` unscraped for days (#8) applies identically to `Probe` CRDs, so this closes it before it bites twice.

## Test plan

author: empressstella
body:
Clepsydre is a new binding that wraps around GNOME's libecal and leaves behind the Rust structs. All day was reading as a  timestamp starting at midnight UTC regardless of trying to apply the local system's detected timezone offset. Chrono was still causing all-day events to register in that UTC midnight stamp, shifting backward by midnight UTC minus local timezone.

Here, I changed chrono from using chrono::Local to chrono::Utc to preserve the iso8601 string for all-day events. Time slot events maintain chrono::Local for proper conversion to the local timezone.

author: rodboev
body:
## Thinking Path

- Refresh Models crosses three independent caches: the server catalog, the server live-model cache, and the browser live-model cache. The refresh transaction now invalidates the relevant provider and profile state, forces current discovery, and publishes only results from the active generation.
- A failed Agent lookup is one stage of discovery. The existing custom and named OpenAI-compatible `/v1/models` fallbacks still run before a refreshed request returns `live_models_unavailable`.
- Failed refresh responses stay uncached and clear the failed refresh marker, so a later ordinary lookup can recover. Provider key and self-hosted mutations invalidate server and browser live-model state.
- Browser cache, generation, and pending-request state are keyed by the active profile and provider. Stale completions cannot publish old models or leave a pending marker behind.
- Required refresh failures now use locale-owned provider-refresh messages, so the provider toast remains truthful and user-facing without raw helper literals.

## What Changed

- `api/routes.py`: preserve all live discovery fallbacks after primary lookup failures, bound failed-refresh recovery, and invalidate live-model state after provider key and self-hosted mutations.
- `static/ui.js`: scope live-model cache, generation, and pending state by profile and provider, with stale-completion cleanup; route required non-OK and empty-catalog errors through provider-refresh translation keys.
- `static/panels.js`: invalidate browser live-model state after self-hosted provider setup while preserving the existing dropdown rebuild sequence.
- `static/i18n.js`: add provider-refresh messages to every configured locale block so locale parity and active-locale selection remain intact.
- `tests/test_issue6919_live_model_refresh.py`: cover fallback routing, failed-refresh recovery, server provider mutation invalidation, stale completion cleanup, profile isolation, provider-key aliases, and both localized required-refresh failures.

## Why It Matters

Refresh Models now reaches the provider's current discovery path and updates the picker without a page reload. Failed refreshes remain truthful and give user-facing guidance from the active locale.

## Verification

The three new localization regressions fail on the previous head because the raw English messages bypass the translation function, then pass on the current head with the expected translation keys and active-locale values. The locale-parity files pass `63` tests. The focused issue regression passes `21` tests. The TTL, refresh-route, and provider-removal coverage add `5`, `6`, and `12` passing tests, for `107` focused tests total. Runtime JavaScript validation, the invariant enumeration gate, and the diff check pass.

## Screenshots

Before: the Providers panel shows the raw transport error in the refresh toast.

![Before, raw Refresh Models error toast](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rodboev/hermes-webui/screenshots/webui-6919-before.png)

After: the same Providers panel shows the user-facing provider-refresh guidance.

![After, localized Refresh Models error toast](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rodboev/hermes-webui/screenshots/webui-6919-after.png)

## Risks / Follow-ups

- The real-provider re-read and refreshed picker result remain deployment-level evidence that this repository cannot reproduce without the reporter's endpoint and credential.
- Forced discovery remains tied to the authenticated refresh generation. Failed refreshed discovery returns an explicit error without caching; a later ordinary lookup can use normal discovery or the static fallback.
- All configured locale bundles carry the two provider-refresh messages under the repository parity contract; future locale additions must preserve the same key set.
- Provider discovery changes no credential persistence or response shape. The existing provider-scoped-key guard remains in place.
- The catalog and disk-cache owners remain unchanged outside this live-model refresh path.

## Scope

- **Task type:** bug fix, live-model refresh and fallback contract.
- **Touched areas:** server live-model routing and provider mutation invalidation; browser live-model cache ownership; provider-change orchestration; provider locale entries; required-refresh error presentation; focused regression coverage.
- **Relevant public docs:** `docs/CONTRACTS.md`, `docs/GUIDELINES.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`.
- **Scope boundaries:** no new endpoint, no change to the `/api/models/refresh` response shape, no change to the `/api/models/live` request contract, no credential flow change, and no catalog or disk-cache TTL change.
- **Evidence needed before claiming done:** a credentialed provider re-read remains an external follow-up; repository-level cache, fallback, recovery, race, and required-refresh error regressions are green, and the Providers toast pair is captured above.

## Upstream

Closes #6919.

## Model Used

GPT-5 via Codex CLI; current-source inspection and adversarial cross-layer review shaped the design.

author: miutaku
body:
## Summary
`live-rke2-preflight` on PR #53 (and now #56/#57) has been stuck `queued` for over an hour. Root-caused via live investigation on the OKE cluster (controller logs, ArgoCD status, upstream issue search) — not related to RKE2 itself.

## Root cause
1. The pinned runner image `ghcr.io/actions/actions-runner:2.334.0` fell below GitHub's currently-enforced minimum self-hosted runner version. New registrations from it are rejected as deprecated (exit code 7).
2. ARC's controller treats a deprecated runner as "outdated" and tears down the `AutoscalingRunnerSet` (listener, `EphemeralRunnerSet`, and the GitHub-side runner-scale-set registration) to recreate it.
3. `gha-runner-scale-set-controller` 0.14.2 (current latest — there is no newer chart release) has two known, still-open upstream bugs that combine here:
   - [actions/actions-runner-controller#4600](https://github.com/actions/actions-runner-controller/issues/4600): the `DeleteRunnerScaleSet` call made during that teardown has no request deadline / unbounded reconcile context. If it ever hangs, the single `AutoscalingRunnerSet` reconcile worker wedges permanently.
   - [actions/actions-runner-controller#4595](https://github.com/actions/actions-runner-controller/issues/4595): once `status.phase` is persisted as `Outdated` with cleanup already completed, the controller never logs or reconciles that resource again — restarting the controller pod just re-enters and re-hangs on the same delete call, since phase is stored in status and its only exit path is a *successful* full cleanup+recreate.
4. This matches what was observed exactly: `oci-arc-systems-gha-rs-controller` pod stayed `Ready` throughout, zero further log output for `oke-rke2-admin`, `kubectl get autoscalinglisteners` empty, 0 runners, unaffected by controller pod restarts, a GitHub PAT rotation, or recreating the `AutoscalingRunnerSet` object itself (which briefly got further — created a runner, immediately re-marked it outdated because it's still the same deprecated image — before wedging again).

## Fix
Bump the pinned runner image to `ghcr.io/actions/actions-runner:2.336.0` (current `actions/runner` latest), which is above GitHub's deprecation cutoff, so the controller has no reason to mark it outdated and re-enter the teardown path that can wedge.

## Scope note
Unrelated to the RKE2 v1.35.7 patch upgrade itself (PR #53) — split out per the same "focused PR" pattern as #56/#57, since this is a pre-existing infra issue blocking the live-preflight validation gate rather than something introduced by the version bump.

## Verification plan
Once merged, ArgoCD (`selfHeal: true`) will sync the new pod template onto the already-wedged `AutoscalingRunnerSet`, which changes its spec hash and should trigger one more outdated→recreate cycle — this time landing on a non-deprecated image so it should stabilize with a running listener instead of wedging again. Will confirm live: `autoscalinglisteners` gets created, `live-rke2-preflight` moves off `queued`.

| `errata-pending/stage0-the-bundle-was-invisible.md` | **E275** |
| `errata-pending/release-entitlements-drop.md` | **E276** |
| `rulings-pending/copy-and-the-apple-button.md` | **R74** |
| `rulings-pending/session-restore-on-reinstall.md` | **R75** |
| `rulings-pending/city-data-distribution.md` | **R76** |

Order follows the rounds' own dependency chain, so an entry that cites an
earlier one cites a lower number — the #158 sequence (step 3 → step 4 → wiring →
reinstall → step 5 → copy round) reads forward. R74/R75 are rulings 1–4/6 and
ruling 5 of the same 2026-08-14 owner round, kept adjacent.

## Citations rewritten

**In code (2).** Both were the `<errata-pending/species-map-string-kind>`
placeholder that E274's own staging note named for splice-time rewrite, now
`ERRATA E274`:

- `Tools/build_seed.py:1136`
- `Tools/test_seed_species_map.py:9`

Worth knowing: `PendingCitationGuardTests` scans `Cypress`, `CypressTests`,
`CypressUITests` only, so it never saw these two. `Tools/` is outside its sweep.

**In the spliced prose (12).** E268 ×2, E270 ×4, E271 ×4, E272 ×1, R75 ×1 —
each pending filename replaced by the assigned number.

**Sweep method.** Two patterns, each calibrated against a planted citation
before an empty result was trusted. The directory-prefixed pattern
(`errata-pending|rulings-pending`) alone **misses bare-basename citations**, and
seven of the twelve prose citations were exactly that shape. The second pattern
greps the fifteen pending stems. Union of the two, over all tracked files.

Left alone deliberately, having been read: `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/pull_request_template.md`
and `docs/investigations/repeat-failures-postmortem.md` describe the staging
practice; `.github/workflows/testflight.yml:181` and `docs/ERRATA.md:19264` are
historical narrative about past merges; `CityDownloadsPresentation.swift:60` and
`BundledCityTests.swift:5` cite the design proposal by its own path, which is the
self-describing shape that must not be rewritten.

## Cross-references honored

- **PR #89's request.** `docs/ERRATA.md` E240's "export performs the one and only
  signing pass" now carries a note pointing at **E276**: `-exportArchive` never
  reads the project and builds the final entitlements from the archived app's
  existing signature, so an unsigned archive requests nothing and every declared
  entitlement was dropped — TestFlight 34 and 35.
- **E270 §5** flagged a citation to fix at splice time (the `AccountLinkRequest`
  reflection pin, said to name `AccountAskTests.swift`). Checked: E266 already
  names `CypressTests/AccountAskSheetTests.swift`, the correct file, and both
  files exist. No change needed — verified rather than assumed.
- **E274's** staging note named its own two code citations. Done, above.

## Content preservation

Each entry was diffed against its origin/main source, non-heading line by
non-heading line. Every difference is a rewritten staging preamble or a rewritten
citation; E265 and E267 are byte-identical in body. Nothing else moved — this
change numbers and places, it does not edit substance.

## One thing not decided

`docs/design-proposals/2026-08-14-city-data-distribution.md:38` says the
rulings-pending entry from that round is "unnumbered until the orchestrator
splices it". That is now false — it is **R76**. Left as-is, because it is a dated
design document and E275 §3 (spliced in this PR) establishes that convention in
as many words for this very file. Flagging rather than deciding.

## CI — this merge SHIPS, and that is worth a decision before merging

My PR body first claimed this would take the prose-only path. **That is wrong, and
`unit` + `ui` running on this PR is the tell.** I re-ran `plan`'s own predicate
against this diff, calibrated against known answers first:

```
DOC_ONLY='docs/|graphify-out/|[^/]*\.md$'
NO_ARCHIVE=".github/|CypressTests/|CypressUITests/|Tools/ui-test-shards.txt$|$DOC_ONLY"

buildable = Tools/build_seed.py, Tools/test_seed_species_map.py   ->  ships=TRUE
```

`Tools/` is deliberately **not** exempt — the workflow comment says why in as many
words: `Tools/build_seed.py` builds the seed that ships inside the app, so
exempting `Tools/` broadly would be unsafe. The exemption is the single file
`Tools/ui-test-shards.txt`, and #31 is its receipt.

So on merge this consumes the next build number and, at the expire step, expires
the current testable build — **for two doc-comment lines that change no shipped
byte.** The seed is a checked-in resource; the archive never runs `build_seed.py`.
That is the build-16 shape the workflow's own comment records: a merge shipping an
app byte-identical to its predecessor, every tester handed an update notification
for nothing.

Nothing here is broken and I am not routing around it. Two ways to land, and the
choice is the orchestrator's:

1. **Merge as-is** and accept one no-op build. Cheapest, and harmless if a
   TestFlight build is wanted around now anyway — note E276's own fix PR expects
   its merge to be the proving run.
2. **Split**: drop the two `Tools/` citation rewrites from this PR so it becomes
   genuinely prose-only (`ships=false`), and carry them on the next change that
   ships for its own reasons. Costs a follow-up, and leaves two citations naming a
   pending filename in the meantime, which CLAUDE.md forbids — so this is a trade
   between a stale citation and a wasted build, not a free win.

`release` is gated on `github.event_name != 'pull_request'`, so **this PR itself
consumes nothing.** The decision only bites at merge.
