Closes #237, part of #164. Stacked on #239; merge the stack in order, then retarget to main.

Memory call sites dominate the generated source: 433,438 load/store calls on merman whose method names alone take 4.1 MB.
Every load/store unit is renamed to `[iuf][bhwd][ls][bhwd]?[oa]?`: sign-or-float, value width (b/h/w/d = 8/16/32/64), load/store, memory width for narrow ops, then the static-offset `o` or wrapping-add `a` suffix.
`i32_load` becomes `iwl`, `i32_load8_u` becomes `uwlb`, `i64_store32` becomes `idsw`, `i32_loado` becomes `iwlo`.
The full mapping table and rejected alternatives are in decision 79; decisions 75 and 78 keep their suffix rules and forward-link the spelling change.
The name codes live in one shared table (`load_code`/`store_code` in `dewasm-backend`) so Ruby and Python cannot drift; Go, Java, and Perl keep `load_method` and are out of scope.
`copy`/`fill`/`init`/`grow`/`read_string` stay named: three orders of magnitude fewer sites, and `read_string` is user-facing host glue.

Measured (before = #239):

| metric | sqlite3-shell | merman |
| --- | --- | --- |
| source bytes | 7,732,176 → 7,295,696 (−5.6%) | 47,707,217 → 45,315,890 (−5.0%) |
| load/store name bytes | — | 4,073,915 → 1,683,020 |
| ISeq instructions | unchanged (measured, not assumed) | — |

Verified with `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test`, and `--features slow_test` for both backends (each: spec 257/257, wasi 72/72); zero old-style names remain in units, backends, docs, or converted output.
Docs and the Rails example glue are updated, with a one-line decoding comment where the codes appear.

author: logosrx
body:
## Summary

WCAG 2.1 AA audit + fixes across the shared component layer (`apps/web/src/components/**` + `globals.css` tokens), plus real pending-state feedback for every command form. Scope honors the parallel `app/ops/**` sweep — **zero page edits**; everything lands through the shared components.

## Part 1 — Accessibility audit (component-by-component)

### Fixed

| Component | Issue | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `ui/field.tsx` (`Field`) | Labels rendered next to controls with no `for`/`id`; help text unassociated; `required` only visual | `Field` now auto-associates via `useId`: single `Input`/`Select`/`Textarea` child is cloned with `id`, `aria-describedby` → help text, `aria-required` (skipped when the control is natively `required` or the call site set its own). Composite children (checkbox/radio groups with inner labels) become `role="group"` + `aria-labelledby` instead of an invalid nested label. Required `*` is `aria-hidden`. Explicit `htmlFor`/`id` pairs pass through untouched. |
| `ui/data.tsx` (`TH`) | No `scope` on header cells | `scope="col"` by default; `scope="row"` opt-in prop |
| `ui/card.tsx` (`LinkCard`) | `focus-visible:outline-none` with no replacement — invisible keyboard focus | Visible `--ring`-token outline on `:focus-visible` |
| `shell/sidebar-nav.tsx` | Collapsed rail = icon-only links with `aria-hidden` icons → nameless links; toggle lacked expanded state | `sr-only` label span when collapsed; `aria-expanded` on the collapse toggle (it already had an `aria-label`) |
| `shell/command-palette.tsx` | Focus lost to `<body>` when the dialog closes | Focus returns to the trigger button on close |
| `ops/action-form.tsx` | No pending feedback (see Part 2) | See Part 2 |
| `ops/stage-timeline.tsx` | No accessible current-step; active step number 3.9:1 on its tint | `aria-label="Workflow stage"` on the list, `aria-current="step"` on the active item, active number moved to `text-tone-brand` (AA-passing text tone) |
| `ops/queue-row.tsx` | `hover:text-brand` link text fails 4.5:1 on card surface (dark) | `hover:text-tone-brand` |
| `auth/*` (sign-in, accept-invite, webauthn-register) | Inputs suppressed outline with border-only focus; error text not announced | `focus:ring-2 focus:ring-ring/40` added; errors are `role="alert"` + `text-tone-danger` |
| `portal/*` (sign-in, setup, profile, change-password, shell) | Same input/error issues; success messages silent; nav lacked landmarks | Same ring + `role="alert"` treatment; success messages `role="status"`; `nav aria-label="Portal"` + `aria-current="page"` |
| `globals.css` | Contrast failures (table below); animations ignore `prefers-reduced-motion` | Token adjustments + reduced-motion block (below) |

### Audited — already compliant

- **`ui/toast.tsx` / `ops/flash.tsx`** — correct live regions (out of scope, verified only)
- **`ui/button.tsx`** — visible `:focus-visible` ring via `--ring`; disabled styling
- **`ui/icon.tsx`** — decorative by default (`aria-hidden`)
- **`shell/theme-toggle.tsx`**, dismiss buttons, pagination arrows — `aria-label` already present on all icon-only buttons found by sweep
- **`shell/command-palette.tsx`** keyboard handling — arrow/Enter/Escape + focus containment already correct; verified, not rewritten
- **Tone badge combinations** — all `tone-*` text-on-tint pairs computed ≥4.5:1 in both themes
- **`--muted` text** — passes on every surface in both themes (worst case 5.34:1)

## Contrast changes (WCAG ratios, before → after)

| Token | Theme | Before | After | Worst-case surface ratio |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--subtle` | dark | `#687287` | `#828da6` | 3.25 → **4.71** (surface-3); canvas 4.07 → 5.91 |
| `--subtle` | light | `#8a93a8` | `#657089` | 2.82 → **4.55** (surface-2); white 3.08 → 4.96 (subtle text never sits on light surface-3) |
| `--brand` (under white button text) | dark | `#6b66f1` (4.38) | `#615aee` | **4.99** |
| `--brand-hover` (under white button text) | dark | `#7e7af4` (3.51) | `#5750e8` | **5.65** |

Light-theme brand tokens already passed (5.76 / 7.32). Changes are minimal hue-preserving nudges; the `brand/12` and `brand/15` tints are visually unchanged.

### prefers-reduced-motion

Added a `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block collapsing `animation-duration`, `animation-delay`, `transition-duration`, `transition-delay`, and `animation-iteration-count`. Zeroing the **delay** matters: `.stagger-children` uses `both` fill with per-child delays, so duration-only reduction would leave content invisible for up to 240ms. Iteration-count 1 also ends the skeleton shimmer and pulse-dot loops.

## Part 2 — Command pending states

Commands post natively (full-page POST → redirect + flash), so `useFormStatus` never observes the in-flight window. `ActionForm` therefore tracks it itself:

- `onSubmit` flips a `pending` context flag (after the optional `confirm` gate)
- every `SubmitButton` inside consumes the context: **disables + shows an inline SVG spinner** (`animate-spin`, `aria-hidden`) while keeping its visible accessible name
- the form gets **`aria-busy`** while pending
- **double-submit blocked** two ways: disabled buttons + an `onSubmit` guard for Enter-key resubmits from text controls
- a `pageshow` listener resets `pending` on bfcache restores, so back-navigating to a submitted form doesn't leave it disabled forever

Wired inside `ActionForm`/`SubmitButton` themselves — every existing command surface (30+ ops pages) gets it with zero page edits.

## Tests + gates

- New `ui/field.test.ts` — 7 tests pinning the label/help/required association invariants (for/id pairing, `aria-describedby`, no clobbering call-site ARIA, native-`required` dedupe, labelled-group path)
- `pnpm typecheck` ✅ · `pnpm test` ✅ 455 files / 5397 tests · eslint ✅ · prettier ✅
- No new dependencies, no prisma/lockfile changes, toast files untouched, no `app/ops/**` edits

Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com)

author: pretinhuu1-boop
body:
## Divisão, sem sobreposição

| Check | Cobre |
|---|---|
| `seo-marketing-meta` (já existia) | **metadados**: title, og:image, JSON-LD, noindex, existência de robots/sitemap |
| `seo-foundation` (novo) | **fundação**: conteúdo do robots, canonical, 404 real, normalização de host, `llms.txt` |

O check novo **não** reverifica a existência de robots/sitemap — verifica o **conteúdo** deles.

## O erro mais caro, e por que é `high`

Bloquear CSS e JS no `robots.txt` "para economizar crawl". O Google **renderiza a página como um navegador**: sem folha de estilo e sem script ele vê um site quebrado, e avalia como tal. `Disallow: /_next` é o caso mais comum.

## Três coisas que o arquivo nunca prova

Ficam no playbook, para quando o site está no ar:

**Soft 404** — página de erro devolvendo `200`. O buscador indexa milhares de páginas de erro como se fossem conteúdo, e nada no repositório denuncia isso.

**Sitemap é uma declaração**: "estas são minhas páginas boas". URL que redireciona, que dá 404 ou que está `noindex` não pode estar lá — e sitemap gerado automaticamente a partir de rotas inclui exatamente essas.

**`hreflang` sem autorreferência** é ignorado, e o erro passa despercebido porque nada quebra visivelmente.

## `llms.txt`

Novo e ainda raro, o que o torna barato e diferenciador: markdown na raiz com o que um assistente precisa para responder sobre o negócio sem adivinhar pelo HTML. Entra como `low` justamente por ser recente.

## Ordem de implementação quando falta tudo

1. Desbloquear CSS/JS no robots — sem isso nada mais é avaliado corretamente
2. Canonical
3. Normalização de host e barra final (301)
4. 404 com status real
5. Sitemap saneado
6. `llms.txt`

## Verificação

`check-selftest`: **74/74 gate-áveis (100%), 0 regressões**.

author: elonsg
body:
## The problem with the unit as it was

`never_required_modules` reported **30 live modules as dead on every run** —
`core/restart/{transitions,marker_fields,liveness_signal_producers}/*.lua`, which `devloop_wiring.lua`
loads via `load_entries(...)` by a **computed** name that no literal-require scan can see.

The unit's docstring described that trap accurately and did nothing about it. So its output was a
permanent 30-entry block a reader must ignore — and a unit nobody can read is not a unit. Advisory
output that is always wrong in the same way trains you to skip it, which is worse than not having it.

## The fix

A computed require does leave static evidence behind: the sibling `index.lua` that **names** the
module (`{ module = "blocked", key = "blocked" }`). This unit now reads it.

**30 -> 0**, with no real signal lost.

## Verified in both directions

A unit that only ever prints 0 proves nothing, so both sides were probed with a temporary fixture:

| fixture | reported |
|---|---|
| orphan module in a directory with **no** index | **yes** — and it was the only entry |
| same module, with an `index.lua` naming it | **no** |

Worth recording how nearly this went wrong: both probes were first run against
`packages/idle-detector/core/`, a directory that **does not exist** (that package has `core.lua`, not
a `core/` tree). Both printed 0, and the second would have read as "registry resolution works".
Asserting the fixture exists before measuring is what caught it — and re-running probe A then
surfaced that a cleanup `git checkout -- .` from the failed attempt had silently reverted the code
change under test.

## Verification

`scripts/run.sh check`: `OK`. Survey on `dev` after the change:

```
exported library functions with no consumer: 0
declared-but-unused lib_deps: 0
ambient devloop exports with no real reader: 0
source files >= 900 lines: 0
leaf functions > 150 lines (informational; repo has no function-length rule): 22
modules no require reaches and no index registers: 0
```

Advisory only, as before: not referenced by `scripts/run.sh` or `ci.yml`, never fails a build.
Targets `dev` per the supervise-does-not-execute exception.

author: krymszuch-stack
body:
## Kontekst

Audyt parserów, systemu logowania i warstwy wizualnej. Kod kompilował się czysto (`tsc`, `vite build`, testy — wszystko zielone), więc zgłaszane „dużo błędów" okazało się problemem **runtime i semantyki**, nie kompilacji.

Dwa commity: naprawa parserów, potem warstwa wizualna.

---

## 1. Parsery zwracały wymyślone dane

**`cvUniversalParser.ts`**
- `pdfjs-dist` był zależnością, ale **nigdy nie był importowany** — sprawdzenie `window.pdfjsLib` zawsze zawodziło, więc każdy PDF trafiał na fallback czytający binarne bajty jako tekst. Ładowany teraz dynamicznie (osobny chunk, działa też w testach).
- Certyfikaty i wykształcenie były generowane **zawsze**, niezależnie od treści CV (`'Certyfikat Zawodowy - …'`, `'Uczelnia / Szkoła Techniczna'`, twarde daty 2017–2021). Doświadczenie miało zastępczy wpis `'Przedsiębiorstwo Operacyjne'`, a umiejętności miękkie były stałą tablicą czterech stringów.
- Wprowadzona detekcja sekcji — gdy sekcji brak, pole zostaje **puste**.

**Oferty pracy**
- `JobMatcher.handleMatchUrl` fabrykował ofertę dla każdego URL-a (`'Stanowisko z Linku URL'`, `'Firma Partnerska'`), mimo że działający endpoint już istniał. Podpięty realny przepływ `fetch-jd-url` + `parse-jd`.
- `fetch-jd-url` podstawiał zastępczy HTML przy nieudanym pobraniu — teraz zwraca uczciwy błąd i rozpoznaje blokady portali (403).
- Zakładka „Agregator Live" filtrowała wbudowaną listę 5 stałych ofert, sugerując wyszukiwanie na żywo.

**`DiffView`** — przycisk „Zastosuj" ignorował wybór użytkownika i zawsze scalał; strategie przekazywane są teraz per sekcja. Dodana brakująca sekcja Wykształcenia.

**Usunięte:** `linkedinParser.ts` (267 linii generatora fikcyjnych profili, zero importerów), `JDParserModal.tsx` (martwy i niezgodny z API), `INITIAL_SAMPLE_VAULT`.

---

## 2. Kontrast łamał WCAG w trybie ciemnym

Najpoważniejsze znalezisko wizualne: `text-white` na wypełnieniu brandowym w **41 miejscach**. W trybie ciemnym `brand-600` to jasna lawenda `#8b93e8`, więc biały tekst dawał **~2,8:1** — poniżej progu AA — w przycisku primary, wszystkich zaznaczonych pigułkach, logo, plakietce Pro i dymkach czatu.

Dodany token `--on-brand` (biel w jasnym, near-black w ciemnym). Zmierzone po zmianie na wszystkich punktach gradientu:

| motyw | vs brand-600 | vs violet |
|---|---|---|
| ciemny | 6,73:1 | 6,98:1 |
| jasny | 4,70:1 | 5,70:1 |

Gradient w jasnym motywie kończy się teraz na violet-600 — biel na violet-500 dawała 4,23:1, tuż poniżej progu.

---

## 3. Spójność wizualna z prototypem

Fundament był zgodny (tokeny, aurora, easing `[0.19,1,0.22,1]` użyty konsekwentnie 40×). Rozjechało się wykończenie:

- `--brand-grad` (kanoniczny gradient 120°) był zdefiniowany, ale **nigdy nieużywany** — zamiast niego cztery ręczne kopie pod kątem 45°/90°. Udostępniony jako utility i zastosowany w logo, przycisku primary, plakietce Pro i liczbie hero.
- **Ciemny motyw domyślny** + skrypt w `index.html` eliminujący mignięcie jasnym tłem. `ThemeToggle` trzymał własny stan i pisał do tego samego klucza `localStorage` co `ThemeProvider` — teraz jedno źródło prawdy.
- Nowe komponenty wg prototypu: `PremiumBadge`, `LockCover` (dwie intensywności rozmycia), `TrustChip`. Wszystkie **podpięte**, nie zostawione jako martwy kod.
- `PricingCard` dociągnięty do wzorca: gradientowa plakietka, kwota mono 38px, prefiks waluty, nota o rozliczeniu.

## 4. Zamiast `alert()`

11 wywołań przeglądarkowego `alert()` zastąpionych systemem toastów (zero nowych zależności). Reset hasła nie twierdzi już, że wysłał link — bo nie wysyła.

## 5. Dostępność i sprzątanie

- `@media prefers-reduced-motion` — hook `useReducedMotion` istniał, ale nie miał **ani jednego konsumenta**, a aurora i shimmer chodziły bez przerwy.
- `aria-label` na akcjach wierszy trackera i 7 przyciskach paska edytora.
- **Usunięte 1175 linii martwego UI** (`Header`, `AutocompleteInput`, `UiSandboxModal` i in.) — siedziała w nich większość naruszeń tokenów.
- Bug: `Slider` odwoływał się do nieistniejącej zmiennej `--border-line`.

---

## Weryfikacja

- `tsc --noEmit` — czysto · `vite build` — przechodzi · `vitest` — **16/16** (3 nowe testy regresyjne pilnujące, że parser nie wstawia zmyślonych danych)
- Aplikacja uruchomiona i sprawdzona wizualnie w obu motywach; kontrast zmierzony w przeglądarce (tabela wyżej)

## Poza zakresem tego PR

Zgodnie z ustaleniami: migracja na Supabase (baza, realne logowanie), integracja Stripe i serwerowe uprawnienia. Obecna warstwa auth nadal działa w całości w przeglądarce, a status subskrypcji jest zapisywalny po stronie klienta — plan przewiduje to w kolejnych fazach.

author: belisiasv
body:
## Summary

Follow-up fixes on top of the previous cycle-editing round:

1. **Active cycle's start date/length was still blocked once a next cycle was queued.** The coach's actual need is to always be able to move the active cycle's start date, with anything already queued after it shifting forward automatically — not to be locked out. `edit_active_cycle` now rebuilds the active cycle and cascades the new end date through every cycle queued after it (each still starting the day after the previous one ends), instead of raising an error. Verified live: shifting the active cycle's start date by a week moved the already-queued "Competitie" cycle's start/end by the same week automatically. Settings no longer disables or shows a "ligt vast" warning on these fields.

2. **"Network Error" saving a queued cycle.** Root cause: Starlette sends an unhandled exception's default 500 via `ServerErrorMiddleware`, which sits *outside* `CORSMiddleware` — so that response never carries CORS headers, the browser blocks it outright, and axios can't tell it apart from a dropped connection, so it just says "Network Error" with no readable detail. (A `@app.exception_handler(Exception)` doesn't fix this either — Starlette special-cases the base `Exception` handler straight to that same outer middleware; verified empirically.) Fixed with ordinary HTTP middleware registered *before* `CORSMiddleware` is added, so it sits inside CORS and any future unhandled exception now comes back as a normal, readable error instead of an opaque network failure — this is a systemic fix, not specific to one endpoint, so it also gives us a real error message if this particular case recurs.

3. **Training composition builder**: added a "✕" per block to remove it from a proposed session entirely (distinct from the existing skip-to-0, which keeps the block but excludes it) — for rebuilding a session from scratch when the auto-proposal isn't right. Verified the existing bouts→duration sync (e.g. adjusting bouts to 3 correctly updates the display to "3x 5.5' (rust 2.5')") already works correctly in the current code.

4. **Recent sessions**: added a delete action per row and in the session detail modal (new `DELETE /api/training-sessions/{id}` — nothing else has a foreign key to a session, so it's a plain, safe delete).

5. Fixed a real bug the delete-block feature would otherwise have shipped with: composition table rows were keyed by array index, so an uncontrolled reps `<input>` kept a **stale value** from whatever block used to sit at that index after an earlier block was removed. Rows are now keyed by vorm+occurrence, stable across insertions/removals.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest` (backend) passes
- [x] `npm run build` (frontend) succeeds
- [x] Playwright: edited the active cycle's start date with a cycle already queued — save succeeds, DB confirms the queued cycle's start/end shifted by the same delta
- [x] Playwright: empirically confirmed the CORS-on-500 bug and its fix using a forced exception + `TestClient` (headers present after fix, absent before)
- [x] Playwright: composition builder — deleted a block, confirmed no other block's displayed reps/duration became mismatched (this is the stale-key bug caught and fixed)
- [x] Playwright: finalized a session, deleted it from "Recente sessies", confirmed it's gone

author: alex-s-gardner
body:
Correct the ambient reanalysis air temperature to on-glacier conditions with the Shaw et al. (2025) decoupling factor `k` from `GEMB_ClimateForcing`, weighted by the fraction of the cell ERA5-Land does *not* already treat as ice:

```
k_eff = 1 - (1 - k) * (1 - glm)
```

`k` corrects an *ambient* (off-glacier) temperature, so it only applies to the part of the cell whose land-surface scheme has no glacier boundary layer. The formula is the full correction where the cell carries no glacier (`glm = 0`) and the identity where it is entirely glacier (`glm = 1`).

Where no `k` is found the forcing is left ambient rather than the run failing: RGI regions 05 (Greenland periphery) and 19 (Antarctic) are absent from the Shaw et al. dataset entirely, and a positional lookup can find nothing within `max_distance`. A cell with no `:glm` column, or a `missing`/`NaN` value, is treated as `glm = 0` — the uncorrected reanalysis assumption, hence the full correction.

## Changes

- **`cell_decoupling_factor(row)`** — new exported lookup. Matches by nearest glacier centroid, wrapping the cell's native 0–359.9°E longitude, and returns `nothing` when the table has no match.
- **`forcing_at_elevation`** gained `decoupling_factor`, applied *after* the elevation adjustment — the order `climate_adjust_for_glacier` requires, since `k` scales an ambient temperature already at the glacier's elevation.
- **`gemb_glacier_cell`** gained `glacier_decoupling = true`, resolved once per cell (`k` is a property of the glacier, not of the bin or perturbation). `false` skips the lookup; a `Real` prescribes `k` directly, bypassing the `glm` weighting. An all-glacier cell weights to exactly 1.0 and skips the adjustment rather than running a no-op pass over the whole forcing record.

## Provenance

The effective `k` is retained in its own right, the way `forcing_elevation` is — the run-parameters dict alone is compared numerically on restart and so cannot distinguish a cell left on ambient forcing from one corrected by exactly 1.0.

- **`GlacierCellRun.decoupling_factor`** — a scalar field, since `k` is a property of the cell rather than of the perturbation grid.
- The NetCDF writer emits it as a **scalar variable** alongside `forcing_elevation`, using the fill value when no correction was applied. The global attribute of the same name keeps recording `1.0` instead, because a fill would never compare equal to itself on restart; the variable's comment says so.
- **`on_output`** now passes `decoupling_factor` to the hook, so a callback can label a figure without reaching back for the cell.
- **`decoupling_factor_label(k)`** formats it concisely for a plot header: `"k=0.774"`, or `""` when no correction was applied. Empty rather than `"k=1.0"` — a factor on every figure of an uncorrected sweep is noise, and its absence is what distinguishes ambient forcing from a cell the correction happened to leave alone. `era5_example.jl`'s verbose plotter appends it to the title only when non-empty.

The branch also carries work that was already uncommitted in these files: `age` joining `PROFILE_VARIABLES` (the column's only clock) with a guard for files predating it, and the `on_output` hook that gives `era5_example.jl` per-simulation plotting.

## Testing

188 tests pass locally (`julia --project=. test/runtests.jl`). New coverage: the weighting is exact at both `glm` endpoints and linear between, absent/`missing`/`NaN` `glm` all fall back to the full correction, both longitude conventions resolve to the same glacier, uncovered regions and open ocean return `nothing`, and `max_distance` bounds the match. The keyword resolution, the scalar-variable round-trip (including fill for ambient), and the header label are pinned separately. All offline — the Shaw et al. table is vendored in `GEMB_ClimateForcing`.

Note: `Pkg.test()` cannot run in this repo — `Project.toml` pins `GEMB = "1.0.0"` while the manifest resolves GEMB 2.0.0, so the test sandbox refuses to re-resolve. Pre-existing and unrelated to this change; worth fixing the compat bound separately.

author: yannelli
body:
<!-- CURSOR_AGENT_PR_BODY_BEGIN -->
## Problem

Per the attached root cause report, Yard 0.1.0 conflates capability *origin* (standalone / plugin / builtin) with capability *type*. This causes two classes of bugs:

1. **Doctor false positives.** Hook and MCP probes don't resolve plugin-root variables or relative paths against the contributing plugin, so working scripts/servers get reported as broken. Contribution discovery misses several supported shapes (Codex `apps`, Cursor external/sibling `mcp.json`, Claude nested marketplace `source.path`, Claude `lspServers`/monitors), so 15 non-empty plugins get flagged `plugin-empty`. 31 stale links under Codex's own disabled/parking directory are reported as 31 separate warnings instead of one hygiene finding.
2. **Web UI false success.** Actions post only `{client, kind, name, desired state}` to the backend, which loses whether the item is plugin-owned, user-owned, or built-in. The backend applies a generic mutation (e.g. `skillOverrides`, project `.mcp.json`) that the target client doesn't actually consult for that item, then reports `changed: true` / HTTP 200 even though nothing the client reads was touched.

This PR implements the report's five-part resolution design.

## Changes

**1. Source-aware action plans (`src/env/actions.ts`, `src/http.ts`, `src/env-api.ts`)**
- Every inventory item now has a stable `id` (client + scope + qualified name). The HTTP layer and `ActionTarget` accept an optional `id` for unambiguous resolution instead of guessing from a bare name.
- Added `resolveEntry` to look up the exact item by id (or disambiguate by name when no id is given) before any mutation is attempted.
- Extracted pure, testable predicates — `skillActionBlocked`, `pluginActionBlocked`, `mcpActionBlocked` — that encode the client/origin action matrix from the report (e.g. Claude plugin skills can't use `skillOverrides`; Cursor has no skill enable switch; Codex plugin MCPs aren't `config.toml` entries) and are now shared between the backend, `context.ts` remedies, and the frontend.

**2. Client/origin action matrix**
- **Claude:** `setMcpEnabled` now branches on origin — plugin/user/local-scoped servers write `disabledMcpServers` in `~/.claude.json` (what Claude actually reads for plugin MCPs) instead of the project `.mcp.json` key. `skillOverrides` is no longer applied to (or written for) plugin skills, matching Claude's own docs that the setting is inert there.
- **Codex:** plugin-contributed MCPs and skills are refused with plugin-lifecycle guidance instead of suggesting `codex mcp remove`, which doesn't apply to them.
- **Cursor:** skill visibility/enable toggles are refused consistently (Cursor has no skill switch at all), and this is now enforced identically in both the Inventory and Context tabs.

**3. Postcondition verification**
- Added `verifySkillVisibility`, `verifySkillEnabled`, `verifyPluginEnabled`, `verifyMcpEnabled`, which rescan the environment after a write and assert the stable item actually changed state. A write that lands in a file but is shadowed by a higher-precedence setting (or simply isn't read by the client) now returns an explicit error instead of a false `changed: true`.

**4. Probe context and error capture (`src/env/probe.ts`, `src/env/doctor.ts`, new `src/env/shell-words.ts`)**
- New `shell-words.ts` provides quote-aware shell tokenizing (`splitShellWords`) and variable expansion (`expandVariables`) shared by Doctor's hook-path resolution and the probe's MCP launch resolution.
- `doctor.ts`'s hook check now expands `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` etc. before splitting into a script path, instead of naively regex-slicing the raw command string (this is exactly acceptance test #1 in the report).
- `probe.ts` now resolves `command`, `args`, `cwd`, and `env` against the contributing plugin/project root, expanding known variables first. `cwd: "."` (or any relative `cwd`) now resolves against the plugin root instead of Yard's own process directory — this was a regression risk I caught with a dedicated test (acceptance test #2).
- Stderr capture now prioritizes the first actionable `Error:`/module-not-found line instead of blindly keeping only the last 5 lines, so failures actually explain themselves.

**5. Contribution discovery and noise reduction**
- Codex: counts `apps` (`.app.json`) contributions so app-only plugins aren't `plugin-empty`.
- Cursor: `mcpServers` can now be an external path, inline object, an array of either, or auto-discovered from a sibling `mcp.json` — all counted as contributions.
- Claude: resolves the nested plugin root for `git-subdir` marketplace sources (fixes `atomic-agents`-style checkouts), and counts `lspServers`/`experimental.monitors` as contributions.
- Doctor aggregates all disabled/parking-directory link warnings into a single informational finding instead of one warning per stale link.

**Frontend (`web/src/lib/api.ts`, `inventory-tab.tsx`, `context-tab.tsx`)**
- Mirrors the blocking predicates so the Inventory tab greys out unsupported controls up front with an explanatory tooltip, rather than letting the user click something that silently no-ops.
- `ContextLine` gained `remedyActionable`; the Context tab now only renders a clickable remedy button when Yard can actually execute the fix, otherwise it shows the remedy as informational text (fixing the Inventory/Context inconsistency called out for the Cursor `canvas` skill in the report).
- Both tabs now send the item's stable `id` with every action request.

## Screenshots

Inventory tab, filtered to a plugin ("toolkit"): plugin-owned skill/MCP controls are disabled with tooltips explaining why, while Claude's own plugin-enable switch and its `disabledMcpServers`-backed MCP switch remain interactive.

![Inventory tab showing blocked plugin controls with explanatory tooltips](https://cursor.com/artifacts/c/art-5dfc0d70-951b-43d5-84b0-7d1db9ded3fa)

Context tab, "what it is spent on": a mix of actionable remedy buttons and informational (non-actionable) remedy text in the same table.

![Context tab showing actionable buttons alongside informational remedy text](https://cursor.com/artifacts/c/art-d8e1b45a-6ca3-4255-a0b5-6a7f80d4d578)

## Testing

- `npm test`: 239/239 passing (added `src/env/actions.test.ts` covering the full predicate matrix, id resolution/disambiguation, per-client end-to-end action calls, postcondition-mismatch detection, and dry-run behavior; extended `doctor.test.ts`, `codex.test.ts`, `cursor.test.ts`, `claude.test.ts`, `context.test.ts`, `probe.test.ts`).
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean for both the server package and `web/`.
- `npm run validate` (bundle build + sanity checks) passes; rebuilt and committed `plugins/yard/dist/cli.js` and `plugins/yard/public/` so installed copies of the plugin actually ship these fixes.
- Manually built the web UI against a fixture environment mirroring the report's client/scope/origin matrix and drove it with a `computerUse` session to capture the screenshots above.

## Scope notes

- Linting: this repo has no root `lint` script and `eslint` isn't installed as a dependency; the web app's `npm run lint` has pre-existing errors in unmodified shadcn-generated files (`badge.tsx`, `button.tsx`, `tabs.tsx`), confirmed via `git stash` to predate this change. Left as out of scope.
- Investigated but could not reproduce as a distinct bug: the report's Cursor `canvas` skill Inventory/Context inconsistency was actually already consistent under `skillActionBlocked`; the real gap was Context rendering a button for *any* remedy text regardless of actionability, which is fixed generally here (item 3 above), not just for `canvas`.
- Not changed: the "monitor" contribution type is counted generically alongside `lspServers` since Claude's docs don't fully specify its manifest shape; flagging here per the report's request to document ambiguous-but-handled items.
- Known follow-up: several remedy strings still suggest a bare `yard ...` command, which per the report isn't

author: sagarsuperuser
body:
> "how did events get ingested for no valid customers in earlier tests?"

They didn't. That question exposed a real bug **and** a bad verification.

## First: the API was never wrong

Every earlier run used a pre-populated database whose bench fixtures were already correct:

| database | fixtures | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| `velox` (all earlier runs) | **50 customers, 6 meters, all `livemode=false`** | 201, rows land — genuinely valid |
| a fresh one | `livemode=true` | 422, correctly rejected |

`customer "bench-customer" not found` is **mode isolation working**: the key was test-mode, the fixtures had been stamped live-mode, so the customer genuinely did not exist in the authenticated partition. No event was ever accepted for a customer that didn't exist.

## The real bug: the previous fix was inert

`postgres.WithLivemode(ctx, false)` is read **only by `TxTenant`**. The `TxBypass` branch of `BeginTx` sets `app.bypass_rls` and nothing else — so on the bootstrap path the context value is silently ignored, and the `BEFORE INSERT set_livemode` trigger stamps the GUC's default, which is LIVE.

The fix is the pattern `internal/tenant/bootstrap_run.go` **already uses for exactly this reason**:

```go
// "TxBypass doesn't set it, so pin it per insert"
tx.ExecContext(ctx, `SELECT set_config('app.livemode', 'off', true)`)
```

So the product was right; the bench tool had deviated from an established house pattern.

## And a bad verification, which is the more useful lesson

I reported the earlier fix as verified. It wasn't.

**The trigger is INSERT-only.** So `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET livemode = false` writes the correct value, and a **second** run against the same database repairs the fixtures and makes every check pass. The re-run that "confirmed" the fix took that path — the intervening `DROP DATABASE` had silently failed because the server still held connections.

Re-verified properly by asserting freshness instead of assuming it:

```
tables before bringup: 0   (must be 0)
HTTP 201 and the row landed (0 -> 1)
customer livemode=false / meter livemode=false / apikey livemode=false
```

`MANUAL_TEST.md` now says to assert the database is empty before seeding, and why.

## Summary

Implements Issue #216's accepted candidate-independent validation contract for the second selected `LexicalDeclaration` qualification slice.

This PR remains validation-only. It does not change the production parser, selected static semantics, aggregate qualification integration, public APIs, dependencies, crates/workspace structure, serialization, async/concurrency, or unsafe Rust.

## Scope

- add validation-only focused rule evidence for co-trigger ownership and supporting authored ranges;
- add candidate-independent whole-source gold for selected `const`, multi-binding, R02/R03, EE-04 preservation, normalization, and initializer boundaries;
- correct the frozen `EE-15-R03` Q7 dependency metadata to retain `IsConstantDeclaration`;
- map R02/R03 and multi-binding EE-36 fixtures into the frozen rule inventory;
- add consistency tests that prevent rule inventory coverage from outrunning focused rule ownership evidence;
- preserve the existing #208 R01 / Script-duplicate gold while allowing additional independently owned mappings;
- add candidate-independent rule-local precedence witnesses that reject family-global traversal inconsistent with #215 Completion Record v2;
- preserve `ExpectedQualification` / `ImplementationCoverage` separation and the fail-closed aggregate completeness gate.

## Validation authority split

```text
GoldFixture
  -> whole-standard expected meaning

RULE_UNITS
  -> frozen normative coverage universe

FocusedRuleEvidence
  -> coverage-sensitive rule ownership / co-trigger relation
     for the new R02/R03 claims

RulePrecedenceFixture
  -> candidate-independent project-local ordering witnesses
     without creating new global rule-coverage claims
```

The precedence witnesses extend the pre-existing rule-local validation authority. They do not import production parser/static-semantic result types and do not expand whole-standard gold or the rule inventory merely to encode diagnostic ordering policy.

## Key evidence boundaries

```text
let x, x;
  primary selected evidence: EE-15-R02
  co-trigger: EE-36-R01

const x;
  primary selected evidence: EE-15-R03
  missing Initializer receives no fabricated authored range

const x = foo;
  Initializer present
  whole-standard valid
  not EE-15-R03

const x = ;
  whole-standard SyntaxRejected
  not EE-15-R03
```

Project-local selected evidence precedence remains:

```text
for declarations in source order:
  R01
  -> R02
  -> R03

then:
  EE-36-R01
```

This ordering is Frontend Analysis evidence policy, not a claim about ECMA-262 diagnostic ordering.

The final candidate-independent precedence matrix additionally pins:

```text
const x; let let;
  -> earlier declaration R03 precedes later declaration R01

let let, let;
  -> R01 precedes R02; EE-36 also co-triggers

let x; let x; let let;
  -> declaration-local R01 precedes Script EE-36
```

Together with the existing focused witnesses (`const let;`, `let x, x;`, `const x = 1, x;`), these cases reject family-global traversal that would violate the accepted declaration-source-order policy.

## Changed files

```text
crates/frontend-analysis-core/src/ecmascript/qualification_static_semantics_validation_tests.rs
crates/frontend-analysis-core/src/ecmascript/qualification_validation_tests/focused.rs
crates/frontend-analysis-core/src/ecmascript/qualification_validation_tests/gold.rs
crates/frontend-analysis-core/src/ecmascript/qualification_validation_tests/inventory.rs
crates/frontend-analysis-core/src/ecmascript/qualification_validation_tests/mod.rs
```

All five files are validation/test authority. No production ECMAScript parser/static-semantics/aggregate implementation file is changed.

## Exact repository identity

```text
base main
09802e8cdcb7c87a94b828d7d3c04eaf53f90b0f

merge base
09802e8cdcb7c87a94b828d7d3c04eaf53f90b0f

PR head
fea6af4a7971b1882c79f1db8b249375bc25ea53

PR head tree
147ad9b55ad6365231dc4f325c5cfd9aaa20cd48

GitHub synthetic PR merge tested by final CI
fe2c50b5f318f51199aca5986d21982cdec9d603

branch relation
ahead 9 / behind 0
```

The branch is ahead-only from the accepted base and no shared-history rewrite was used.

## Final executable validation

### Rust Core Run #222 — PASS

Run ID: `31935260337`

GitHub Actions validated the current PR through its synthetic merge commit for head `fea6af4a...` against base `09802e8c...`.

```text
accepted Rust toolchain 1.97.1                         PASS
production workspace policy                            PASS
cargo fmt --all -- --check                             PASS
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features  PASS
cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features    PASS
cargo metadata --offline --format-version 1 --locked   PASS
clean validation result                                PASS
```

Do not describe this run as an exact PR-head commit checkout: `actions/checkout` validates GitHub's synthetic merge for the current head/base pair.

## CI correction history

The final head was reached without shared-history rewrite.

Relevant diagnostic runs during the precedence-blocker fix:

1. Run #220 exposed only a Rust closure-signature error in the new `SourceText::anchor(...).unwrap_or_else(...)` assertions. The closure was corrected to accept the `Result` error parameter.
2. Run #221 then exposed only rustfmt layout differences in those assertions. The exact rustfmt layout was applied.
3. Run #222 passed workspace policy, formatting, Clippy, tests, locked metadata, and clean-tree validation.

These corrections did not change the intended precedence evidence semantics.

## Independent adversarial review

The first independent review intentionally rejected the earlier head because same-declaration witnesses alone did not exclude a family-global traversal that could violate declaration source order.

That blocking finding was repaired with the three rule-local precedence witnesses above.

Exact-head adversarial re-review of current head:

```text

```

Re-reviewed boundaries:

whole-standard meaning vs coverage          PASS

No blocking contradiction remains on the current head.

## Risk

Primary risk is accidentally allowing a co-triggering whole-source rejection to masquerade as focused R02 coverage. The validation-only focused evidence and bidirectional R02/R03 inventory consistency tests fail closed on that condition.

A second risk is silently implementing project-local evidence precedence by rule family instead of declaration source order. The final rule-local precedence witnesses now explicitly reject that class of traversal.

Another risk is conflating unsupported selected initializer coverage with normative initializer absence. Dedicated whole-standard fixtures keep those meanings separate.

author: rumankazi
body:
## The one that matters

`DECISIONS.md` D20 says a scanned repository cannot restructure a report about
itself. **It could.** `escapeMarkdown` escaped pipes but not backslashes:

```
input   "name\|INJECTED|more"
escaped "name\\|INJECTED\|more"
row     | `rule` | pass | 100 | 3 | name\\|INJECTED\|more |
cells   6   (the header row has 5)
```

`\\` renders as one literal backslash, which frees the pipe after it to end the cell.
Any repository that can name a ruleset could add a column — the exact injection D20
was written to prevent. CodeQL's `js/incomplete-sanitization` found it, on the code
written to stop it.

Backslashes are now escaped **first**; that ordering is the entire fix. The new test
counts cell boundaries in every row and compares to the header, rather than asserting
on the escaped string — and it **fails against the old implementation**, which is the
only reason to trust it.

## The other three highs on `main`

| Alert | Where | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `js/polynomial-redos` | `resolveApiBaseUrl` | `/\/+$/` backtracks polynomially on a mostly-slashes value. Trimmed by scanning — linear, and plainer to read. |
| `js/insecure-temporary-file` ×2 | CLI tests | Predictable paths in the shared temp dir are a symlink-swap target. `mkdtemp` instead. |
| `js/regex/missing-regexp-anchor` ×2 | badge tests | Replaced with extracting every URL and asserting each host is `www.w3.org` — what the assertion actually meant. |

## Note on PR #31

Its CodeQL failure was **not** js-yaml v5. It was this same
`js/incomplete-sanitization` alert resurfacing because the bundle got rebuilt on that
branch and the line moved. This PR removes the cause; #31 should go green once
rebased.

## Score impact

None.

author: illume
body:
## Summary

- add a validated registry for desktop OAuth callback providers
- route startup, second-instance, and macOS protocol callbacks to registered providers
- keep unmatched product protocol URLs on the existing deep-link path
- cover registration, ownership, dispatch, and failure behavior with focused unit and Electron process tests

## Provenance

- Direct source: [Azure/aks-desktop#823](https://github.com/Azure/aks-desktop/pull/823), patch `0018-headlamp-upstream-oauth-provider-registry.patch`
- Retained patch commit: `2e4c7e7d95a8a0fcba47961e9a4e79616739b38c`, authored by Thomas Gamble on 2026-07-31
- Original OAuth callback flow: [Azure/aks-desktop#260](https://github.com/Azure/aks-desktop/pull/260), commit [`5b78e600bbb2666969c649043bd89610f407bebf`](https://github.com/Azure/aks-desktop/commit/5b78e600bbb2666969c649043bd89610f407bebf)
- Related branded protocol correction: [Azure/aks-desktop#457](https://github.com/Azure/aks-desktop/pull/457), commit [`d9b4def25efc00ad66f4f2af23d2d89f9c6c0f86`](https://github.com/Azure/aks-desktop/commit/d9b4def25efc00ad66f4f2af23d2d89f9c6c0f86)
- Prerequisite protocol support: [kubernetes-sigs/headlamp#7252](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/headlamp/pull/7252), now merged into `main`

The implementation commit preserves Thomas Gamble as author and the original author date, with Rene Dudfield as co-author.

## Improvements over the existing changes

- Put focused unit and Electron process tests before the implementation commit so reviewers can see the intended behavior and regression boundaries independently of the production change.
- Raise focused registry branch coverage from the retained tests to 100%, with an enforced 80% threshold, so validation, cleanup, dispatch, and error paths cannot regress without failing the focused check.
- Document exported interfaces, fields, callbacks, parameters, and return values with TSDoc so downstream provider implementations have an explicit contract instead of relying on implementation details.
- Reject callback paths containing traversal segments so registrations cannot claim ambiguous or path-normalized routes that differ from the exact callback URL being dispatched.
- Verify case-normalized callback ownership, stale cleanup safety, and synchronous and asynchronous provider failures so route ownership remains deterministic and one failing provider cannot disrupt protocol handling.
- Exercise provider registration and callback dispatch in a real Electron main process without requiring Kubernetes so the process boundary is tested quickly and reliably in CI.
- Buffer macOS launch callbacks until providers and the application window are ready because Electron can emit `open-url` before `ready`; without buffering, a cold-start OAuth callback can be lost.
- Keep protocol listeners, startup arguments, window focus, validation, dialog errors, and renderer fallback out of `main.ts` so the Electron entry point remains wiring-focused and the protocol lifecycle can be tested as one encapsulated unit.
- Release buffered callbacks after either a successful renderer load or a main-frame load failure, with a diagnostic, so a broken initial page cannot leave OAuth callbacks queued forever.
- Focus and restore the application window when a buffered callback is finally dispatched, so cold-start `open-url` handling matches second-instance behavior.
- Document query parameters as untrusted and require providers to validate OAuth state, authorization codes, and PKCE values rather than treating route matching as security validation.
- Surface synchronous and asynchronous provider failures through a translated desktop error dialog while retaining route ownership, so users get a recoverable failure instead of a silent hang or unsafe deep-link fallback.
- Run protocol routing from a temporary app root and invoke the parent app's Electron/esbuild binaries explicitly, avoiding tracked manifest mutation and accidental nested dependency resolution.
- Ignore benign Electron stderr unless the fixture exits before producing its callback, reducing Linux CI flakes from GPU, Fontconfig, or DBus warnings.

## Testing

- `npm --prefix app run i18n-check`
- frontend i18next parser with `--fail-on-update`
- `npm --prefix app run test:oauth-coverage` (40 tests, 100% branches with an enforced 80% threshold)
- `npm --prefix app/e2e-tests run test-app -- tests/protocolScheme.spec.ts tests/oauthProvider.spec.ts --workers=1` (4 tests)
- `npm --prefix app run tsc`
- `npm --prefix app run compile-electron -- --dev`
- `git diff --check upstream/main..HEAD`

## Screenshots

Not applicable. This change adds main-process callback infrastructure with no visual difference.

Assisted by copilot.

author: shaelsrv
body:
The ChatGPT installer interview was too long — **13 one-question-at-a-time steps** before the user got any value. Now the installer asks **depth first** and branches, with an estimated time on each.

## The three depths
| Depth | Time | What it asks |
|---|---|---|
| **Simple** | ~2 min | **Just your location.** Everything else uses labeled sensible defaults — all-level monitoring, broad interests, Starter briefings, standard schedule. |
| **Advanced** | ~5–7 min | **~70% of the interview** — the 7 choices that matter: interests, ranking, official sources, secondary sources, scope, install mode. Fine print defaulted. |
| **Full control** | ~12–15 min | **Every option** — extra jurisdiction bodies, timezone, excluded sources, language, briefing depth, all 17 task types, per-task scheduling. |

You can start Simple and deepen any setting later.

## How it works
- A depth question runs right after the consent step; the choice is recorded as `interview depth`.
- Each of the 13 interview steps is tagged `[A]` (advanced+full), `[full only]`, or `[all depths]`, so a single flow serves all three depths — Simple asks nothing past location, Advanced runs the `[A]` steps, Full runs everything.
- A **Simple-defaults** block fills every skipped question with a concrete, non-sensitive default.

## Consent is preserved at every depth
A shorter interview means fewer **questions**, not less **control**:
- The profile summary now lists **every field**, with anything defaulted marked `(default)`, and invites the user to change any line before continuing — this is the consent surface a short interview leans on.
- The **Review → Explain → Confirm → Apply** gate and the **privacy warning** for the sensitive tasks (5, 15) **always fire**, regardless of depth. Simple/Advanced never add a private task on their own.
- Defaults only ever cover non-sensitive setup (scope, interests, cadence) — never a private task, never invented sensitive data.

`INSTALL.md` documents the three depths and their times up front (~2 min minimum, down from "5–10 minutes").

author: dyike
body:
## What

Turns the session log modu_code already writes into something you can read: a turn-aware event ledger with per-record timing, status, and token accounting.

- **`/trajectory`** — prints the ledger in the terminal: turns, approximate model steps, per-tool call counts and timing, failures, token usage, prompt changes.
- **`/trajectory html [path]`** — a self-contained interactive page (no external requests): a three-lane horizontal timeline, a turn rail, foldable turn/step groups, and a tabbed detail panel.
- **`get_trajectory`** — the same projection exposed to the model, so it can answer "which tools did I run, which failed, where did that turn spend its time" from facts rather than from what happens to still be in context.

Modelled on [`@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-trajectory`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/tree/master/packages/client/ui-trajectory).

## Two things the log did not record, and now does

Both were missing from the write path entirely — no amount of projection could recover them.

**A model call's own clock.** The agent now stamps request start, first content event, and completion onto the reply. That gives real time-to-first-token, decode time, and throughput. Sessions written before this keep working: their model calls fall back to a start derived from the previous event, and every record carries whether its timing was `measured` or `derived`, so an inferred number is never read as a measurement.

**The system prompt and tool catalog.** Persisted as a sidecar entry, written *only when they change* — a system prompt plus every tool's schema dwarfs the conversation it explains, so per-turn writes were never an option. Change-triggered writes turn out to be the better record anyway: each entry marks a point where the model's instructions actually moved, and the viewer diffs it against the previous one.

Snapshots taken before a session's first message belong to no turn, so records may now sit in turn 0, rendered as a "Between turns" section rather than forced into turn 1.

## Reporting choices

- `input` tokens are billed input, restated in full on every request, so summing them gives the bill and not the context size — reported separately.
- A session resumed across weeks spans far more wall clock than it worked, so stats carry both `durationMs` (span) and `activeMs` (summed per-turn). On a real 613-line session: 26d22h vs 9m44s.
- `timeToFirstTokenMs` was renamed `firstResponseMs`; the old name claimed a measurement that did not exist before this PR. Real TTFT is now a separate field, present only where it was recorded.

## Viewer

Three timeline projections — `sequence` (equal width), `compressed` (real durations, idle gaps removed), `actual` (real wall clock). Drag to focus the ledger, wheel to zoom, right-drag to pan, right-click to clear, 500 ms hover for exact clock and duration. Turns and steps fold. Details are tabbed per record kind. Search covers tool inputs, outputs, and prompt text, not just the summary line. Bilingual, following the browser, with `?lang=en` / `?lang=zh` to pin.

## Testing

`go test ./pkg/... ./cmd/...` green. Projection package at 88.7% coverage.

- **Projection**: turn/step boundaries, tool pairing, failures, unfinished calls, sidecar exclusion, abandoned branches, both detail levels, CJK truncation, malformed lines, recorded-vs-derived timing, prompt snapshot merge order.
- **Write path**: proven end-to-end that timing and prompt snapshots reach disk, and that an *unchanged* prompt is not written again.
- **Viewer**: 17 tests driving the real page in **headless Chrome** — projections, drag-to-focus, zoom/pan/reset, folding, deep search, tabs per kind, prompt diff, Between turns, throughput reporting, language switching. They skip when no browser is installed.

Bugs the browser tests caught: `#inspector { display: flex }` outranked the UA `[hidden]` rule so the panel could never close; a missing 3px drag threshold meant a click's pixel of drift registered as a drag, killing right-click-to-clear; and `setPointerCapture` sitting first in the handler aborted the whole gesture wherever capture was refused.

## Known limitations

- **Subagent internals stay invisible.** A subagent runs in its own session file; the parent only sees one `subagent` tool call. Projecting into it would need the parent to record the child's session id.
- **No virtualization.** Measured (headless Chrome, best of 3, minus a 1758 ms blank baseline): 388 records ≈ 560 ms / 536 KB, 3104 ≈ 940 ms / 3.7 MB, 10088 ≈ 2030 ms / **12 MB**. Fine into the thousands; a very long cron session would want paging.
- Cancellation-frozen record states and per-request sampling options are still not persisted.

- Base: `66359f959338e29212d20f090236271cb20d608e` (`origin/main`)
- Head: `89d3af8` (`codex/s12-semantic-import-tests`)

## Structural-to-semantic mapping

| Structural assertion removed | Exact semantic replacement | Command proving it | Why equivalent |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `workflowSource` contains `retries: { limit: 3, delay: "2 seconds", backoff: "exponential" }` | `import-media-workflow.test.ts` asserts the exported `AcquisitionTaskStepConfig`, derives Cloudflare retry bounds, and runs retryable failures through a virtual clock. | `pnpm --filter @meal-planner/api exec vitest run src/features/imports/import-media-workflow.test.ts src/features/imports/import-recipe-recovery.workflow.test.ts --config vitest.config.ts` | Validates the public configuration and observable retry behavior, rather than a source spelling. |
| `workflowSource` contains `MaximumNestedAcquisitionAttempts = 9` | The production-bounds semantic test asserts the exported nested-attempt ceiling is 9. | Same focused import command. | Validates the consumed exported value, not its declaration text. |
| `workflowSource` contains `MaximumScheduledWorkflowSeconds = 2985` | The production-bounds semantic test derives and asserts the exported scheduled-workflow ceiling is 2985. | Same focused import command. | Validates the derived runtime budget, not its declaration text. |
| `workflowSource` contains `MaximumAbsoluteWorkflowSeconds = 3066` | The production-bounds semantic test derives and asserts the exported absolute-workflow ceiling is 3066. | Same focused import command. | Validates the derived runtime budget, not its declaration text. |
| `import-media.model.ts` matches the generation interpolation source string | `import-media-workflow.test.ts` calls public evidence-key helpers and asserts exact immutable generation-scoped R2 object and manifest keys. | Same focused import command. | Proves the externally consumed key values, including the generation segment, rather than the template source. |

## Retained structural contracts

All other structural checks remain because there is no one-to-one local semantic replacement: static deployment identity/configuration, D1 migration allowlists and snapshot parity, exact Workflow/Queue/R2/D1 bindings and budgets, least-privilege/secret-redaction/privacy policy, non-destructive acquisition and replay guards, container supply-chain constraints, and operator/documentation safety policy.

author: pirapira
body:
Closes #12460.

`scripts/sweep_one.py:205` read `return 1 if fa else 0` — the sweep exited non-zero **only** on a false accept, and any number of false rejects passed silently.

⛔ **Under the project-wide iff standard a false reject is a bug**, not a frontier signal. The header comment at `:20-21` described the code accurately, so it was not stale prose — the behaviour itself encoded the retired policy.

## Change

- exit non-zero on **`fa or fr`**
- FR fixture listing block, mirroring the existing FA block
- header wording corrected: **both `FA=0` and `FR=0` are required**; the only exemption is an input outside the stated envelope (small block number, small timestamp, bounded gas), which is a **statement precondition, not a gate**

## ⭐ Why this is cheap and safe

**`sweep_one.py` gates nothing.** It appears in exactly two tracked files — itself and `docs/eest-stateless-testing.md`. No workflow, shell script or Makefile invokes it; its exit status is consumed only by whoever runs it by hand. ⇒ **No pipeline turns red.**

⚠️ **I originally told the maintainer the opposite** — that gating on FR would turn every corpus sweep red overnight and block work that was green. **That was wrong**: I inferred CI consequences from an exit code without checking the call sites.

## ⚠️ Expected on first use

The corpus FR count has historically been non-zero, so **the first honest run after this will exit 1.** That is the intended signal, not a regression. ⛔ The old `364/26,104` figure is stale and must not be quoted — record a fresh count with its ELF sha.

**No corpus sweep was run for this PR**, so no new FR count is claimed. Python compile and `git diff --check` pass; script-only, no Lean, no image change.

body:
## What changed

- New `src/pause.ts`: a `<beckettDir>/pause.json` hold — existence IS the flag, chosen over a
  config key because the brake must be instant, revocable, readable by both the daemon and
  short-lived CLI subprocesses, and removable without editing a boot-validated config
  (overhaul B-P9).
- While held: `task deploy`/`task start` refuse before filing a run, `quick` dispatch and
  browser `exec`/outward dispatch refuse, and the supervisor's `spawnGuarded` declines to staff
  any run still in state `queued` (live runs finish untouched; the existing watchdog staffs the
  queued run once the hold lifts).
- The concierge gets a per-turn SYSTEM hold note (declines in one honest sentence instead of a
  surprise CLI error) plus a "When you're on hold" doctrine subsection in `concierge.md`.
  `beckett status` always prints whether a hold is set.
- Review fix: wired `pauseFilePath: paths.pauseFile` into the daemon's `createRunSupervisor` call
  in `src/shell/main.ts` — without it the supervisor's partial-config fallback ignores
  `BECKETT_DIR`, so on any install that sets it (e.g. `beckett-dev.service`) the daemon would read
  a different `pause.json` than the one the CLI writes and the brake would fail off silently.
- Review fix: `readPause` no longer throws if the file is deleted between its `existsSync` guard
  and the subsequent read/stat (a genuine race with `beckett resume`) — degrades to "not paused"
  instead of escaping uncaught into the concierge's per-turn check, `spawnGuarded`, or the status
  provider.
- Review nit: wired the same `pause` dep into `dream-cli.ts`'s proposal-accept `deployRun` call
  site, matching the two sites already covered in `core.ts`.

## How it was tested

- `bun x tsc --noEmit`: clean.
- `bun run test`: 3237 pass / 0 fail / 2 skip (fast lane, ~46s).
- Manual scratch-`BECKETT_DIR` proof: `beckett pause --reason "hands off tonight"` →
  `beckett task deploy --prompt x` exits 1 with a `paused:` stderr line and writes no run row;
  `beckett resume` lifts it; a subsequent `--dry` deploy succeeds.
- Snapshot diff is exactly the new help-line occurrences plus two new CLI cases.

## Left undone (flagged by reviewer, not applied)

- Reviewer's suggested new pause.test.ts case for the exact existsSync→readFileSync race window
  was not added: reproducing it deterministically needs mocking `node:fs`'s ESM bindings, which
  is brittle relative to the value here. The fix itself (guarding the catch block with a second
  `existsSync` check and falling back to "now" if `statSync` also races) is applied and covered
  indirectly by the existing corrupt-file and absent-file tests exercising the same code paths.

body:
## Summary

- add exact AAC packet decoding and contiguous half-open sample-range reads
- preserve and apply priming, end padding, signed track offsets, and ordered MP4 edit mappings, including empty edits as silence
- drive native and Web Audio output adapters from a monotonic audio clock, skip expired audio deadlines, and always request the exact clock-selected video frame
- cancel queued work on seek, reset both streams, preroll audio, and resume under a new scheduling generation

## Root cause

The portable core had exact video reads and synchronized writes, but no decoded-audio input path or playback state machine. There was therefore no shared place to apply gapless/edit metadata, translate the audio master clock back to a frame index, or invalidate queued work across seeks.

## User impact

Frame-indexed audio reads now return exact contiguous ranges without duplicated or missing samples. Native and browser playback backends share the same clock, scheduling, cancellation, and exact-frame contract; late presentation can be skipped without substituting a different `get(n)` result.

## Changelog

- Added an entry under `CHANGELOG.md` ? `Unreleased`.

body:
🚨 Severity: HIGH
💡 Vulnerability: The blog component renders HTML directly using dangerouslySetInnerHTML without sanitization, which creates a Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability if malicious content is introduced.
🎯 Impact: An attacker could execute arbitrary JavaScript in the context of the user's session if they can inject malicious code into a blog post's content, potentially leading to unauthorized actions or data theft.
🔧 Fix: Added isomorphic-dompurify to sanitize the HTML content before it is passed to dangerouslySetInnerHTML, neutralizing any potential malicious script tags while preserving safe HTML.
✅ Verification: The application builds successfully and the tests pass, confirming the fix didn't introduce syntax errors. The HTML rendering logic was manually verified to include the DOMPurify.sanitize call.

author: cbcoutinho
body:
## What

Two marketing-site changes:

**1. "Sign in" points at the production portal.** The button in the marketing
header is built from `NEXT_PUBLIC_PORTAL_URL`, inlined at build time into the
static export. It was still set to the dev portal, so every visitor who clicked
Sign in landed on `app.dev.astrolabecloud.com`. The Pages workflow now bakes
`https://app.astrolabecloud.com`.

**2. Pricing page reflects the current pricing model.** It previously described
an invite-only "contact us" page with no model at all. It now explains the
metering dimensions:

- a flat monthly platform fee per Nextcloud (the whole bill for MCP-only use);
- indexed content metered per month on retained chunks (chunk-months, so
  mid-month load/purge is pro-rated), semantic and keyword-only metered
  separately, quoted in pages since that's what a prospect can count up front;
- OCR billed once per scanned page, so born-digital corpora don't subsidise
  scanned ones;
- no volume tiers, no per-seat charge, keyword ingestion free.

Rates are deliberately **not** published on the page — they live in the Stripe
catalog, and a statically exported page would go stale the first time they move.
The page describes the shape and routes to a quote.

**3. New self-hosting offer.** A third card offering paid help deploying and
supporting Astrolabe on the customer's own hardware (sizing the vector index and
OCR pipeline, standing it up next to their Nextcloud, optional ongoing support),
quoted per engagement, with its own mailto CTA.

## Test coverage

No API surface changes — this is marketing-site copy plus one build-time env
var, so the e2e/contract gate in `CLAUDE.md` doesn't apply. `npm run build` in
`website/` is green (its TypeScript pass included). Note that `npm run lint`
there is broken independently of this change: the script calls `next lint`,
which the pinned Next version no longer ships.

- Conclusion: the migration logic itself is correct and minimal; the real gap is automated coverage (OFFLINE-INTEGRATION-001 Finding 5), not correctness.

**3. Migration test strategy proposal** — Option A (hand-rolled fixture test against the real `onUpgrade`, using the exact historical schemas recovered in the audit) vs Option B (Drift's official schema-export/`SchemaVerifier` tooling). author: takayan0908
body:
緩和ではなく**決定の記録**。次にこれを見つけた人（私かもしれない）が「対応漏れ」と読んで、検討済みだと知らずに"直す"ことがないように。

## 受容した内容

デプロイエージェントは sgadmin として動く。書き込みはカーネルが封じているが、**読みは sgadmin の届く範囲すべて**に及ぶ（Claude OAuth トークン / postgres スーパーユーザパスワード / magickit の Google OAuth 秘密 / GitHub PAT / prismind の OAuth 資格情報 / conclair の DB URL）。外向き通信は API 呼び出しに必須なので開いている。

∴ 連鎖は実在する: **`origin/main` のテキストは、repo を読んで判断するのが仕事のエージェントにとって入力**であり、main に載せられる主体にはループも含まれる。

## 受容の論拠（そのまま記録）

**main に何かを載せられる時点で守るべきものはほぼ突破されている。** main のコードはそのサービス*として*動くので、その秘密はどのみち手に入る。エージェント経由で 1 手早く読まれても大差ない。

## 受容していない部分（例外も記録）

リストのうち **1 つを除いて**その論拠は成立する。**Claude の OAuth トークンはどのサービスも保持していない。** conclair として動く悪意あるコードでも手に入らず、被害範囲がこのホストの外に出る。

この構成の正確な description は「デプロイエージェントは各サービスの権限を**横断して集約**している」であって、「main が破られたら同じ」は per-service には正しいが aggregate には正しくない。**分かったうえで受容**しており、それは分からずに受容しているのとは別のこと。

## 再判断の条件（4 つ）

main のレビュー水準が異なる repo が対象に入る / Claude 資格情報が単一ユーザのものでなくなる / main への書き込み主体が増える / 対象 repo が増えて横断して読める秘密が増える。

## 安価な非緩和策（未実施、選択肢として記載）

境界にはならないが、試みが `permission_denials` として監査に残る。

author: antoncl
body:
The **#76 provider-layer tail** — the last five complexity findings the [ADR-0058](https://github.com/antoncl/local-writing-app/blob/master/docs/design/adr/0058-a-provider-is-a-class-registered-once.md) reshape (#1047) left behind. The reshape dissolved the *dispatch* complexity; these five are *decomposition* — a method doing several steps that hadn't been named. After this, the provider layer (`providers.py`, `profiles/*`, `call_resolver.py`) reports **0** of the four `#76` rules.

### What changed

**1. Parameter Object at the public boundary** (clears `chat`/`chat_stream` PLR0913 = 10/11)

The arg count was a **data clump at the seam**, not an un-decomposed body: the router `resolve_call_params(...)` → `ResolvedCall`, unbundled it into ~10 loose kwargs, and `chat()` re-bundled them into a `ChatCall`. Now:

- `chat(call: ChatCall, *, provider_name, settings, policy)` and the same shape for `chat_stream` — the request is one object, the routing is three keywords.
- New `ResolvedCall.to_call(system_prompt, messages, system_blocks?, session_id?)` bridge builds the `ChatCall` once. The four call sites (`routers/ai.py` chat + both `chat_stream`, `services/ai/chat.py` `run_chat_turn`) drop the unbundle→rebundle.

**2. Anthropic `chat_stream` decomposition** (clears C901 = 15 / PLR0912 = 14)

- `_message_kwargs(call)` — the model/tokens/messages/temperature/system kwargs, now **shared with `chat`** (kills a duplicated block).
- `_apply_thinking(kwargs, call)` — the streaming thinking budget + `temperature=1` rule.
- `_stream_text_events(event)` — per-event text/thinking delta routing; `chat_stream` becomes `for event in stream: yield from self._stream_text_events(event)`.

**3. `ThinkTagSplitter.feed` decomposition** (clears C901 = 11)

Two mirror-image branches (scan `</think>` → thinking; scan `<think>` → content) collapse into one parameterized `_scan(delim, event_cls)` generator whose return value tells `feed` whether to flip state and loop.

### Behaviour preserved (byte-identical)

Same wire kwargs, same delta/thinking/usage handling, same splitter output. The splitter tests, anthropic/openrouter caching tests, and the streaming/cost tests are the oracle and stay green.

### New coverage (where the refactor added seams)

- **`to_call` unit test** — field-by-field wiring (a swap would send the wrong model or silently drop thinking).
- **Direct `AnthropicProfile.chat_stream` test** — drives the real body through a faked `anthropic` SDK (text vs thinking delta routing; thinking budget + `temperature=1`). The endpoint/cost tests mocked the whole stream away, so this path had **zero** direct coverage before. Both new helpers **mutation-verified** (misroute thinking → red; wrong thinking temperature → red).

### `#76` scope note

The remaining findings are in **other files** — `helpers.py`, `preview.py`, `entry_ref.py`, `streaming.py` — and are the next `#76` slice (the long tail across the rest of the AI service), kept out of this byte-identical provider-layer move.

`main` has been red since #357 and it was not the advisory ruff noise: the same job carries a **blocking** S110 ratchet at baseline 0, and a `try/except/pass` in `_pdf_tables_enabled`'s fitz probe tripped it. The red X was misread as style debt for a day — by me included.

- **New fence** `tests/test_no_silent_handlers_in_app.py`: states the rule as a test (where it can't be mistaken for lint noise), implemented with `ast` so it needs no ruff install and runs on every CI leg. ## Summary

- make `MPOTensor.IsSourceSimple` source-faithful to CPSV16's standing active
  canonical-block convention (lines 217–246) and Definition 4.7 (lines 815–822):
  MPDO positivity, a nonzero closed MPO at some positive length, and an
  existential positive blocking with a CPSV basis of normal tensors whose
  doubled physical-trace transfers are nonnilpotent
- exclude the identically zero family without requiring nonvanishing at every
  positive length; dormant extra candidates remain possible under the paper's
  raw BNT definition and are not ruled out by this predicate
- keep the all-positive-length condition in the explicitly named
  `MPOTensor.IsNonvanishingSourceSimple` refinement
- prove `IsSimple.isSourceSimple` unconditionally: a line-246 unit-weight sector,
  a non-eventually-zero power-sum coefficient, eventual linear independence,
  gauge transport, and physical unblocking produce a nonzero closed MPO
- preserve positive-real scaling invariance for both interfaces and record the
  dimer's stronger all-length nonvanishing status
- add the sign-flip tensor with
  $\rho_N(M)=(1+(-1)^N)I$: it is nonzero at $N=2$, vanishes at $N=1$, and proves
  `IsSimple M ∧ IsSourceSimple M ∧ ¬ IsNonvanishingSourceSimple M`
- synchronize generated imports, Blueprint, glossary, paper-gap notes, and
  CPSV16 audits

The sign-flip witness is not a counterexample to Definition 4.7. It separates
source simplicity (nontrivial somewhere) from the project's all-length
nonvanishing refinement. No RFP or BNT coefficient-rigidity claim is made.

Closes #6501.

author: joestump
body:
## What

Adds a `TestMain` to `internal/backend` that redirects the global Crush config lookups at a throwaway temp tree before `m.Run`, plus a `TestGlobalConfigIsolated` guard. Applies the same fix as #263 did for `internal/agent`.

## Why

`internal/backend`'s tests call `config.Init(...)` with no isolation of their own:

- `internal/backend/channels_test.go` — `insertChannelWorkspace`
- `internal/agent/agenttest/coordinator.go` — `NewCoordinator`, reached from `accepted_run_integration_test.go` under `t.Parallel()`

`config.Init` always merges the user-level config locations on top of the working dir, so on a developer machine these load the real `~/.config/crush/crush.json`.

Measured on a live machine with a throwaway probe test in the package, a bare `config.Init` here pulled in:

- **13 MCP servers** and **7 LSP servers** from the host config
- **authenticated model-discovery HTTP requests** to the provider endpoints that config names — `litellm 401`, `gemini 404`, `openai 401`

After the fix the same probe reports `0` MCP, `0` LSP, skills dir inside the temp tree, and a single `WARN No providers configured` with no network calls.

Nothing asserts on exact counts today, so this is **latent rather than failing** — but it is the same trap that made `TestSidekickDashboardSubscribeDeliversToolPushes` report `129` tools where it expects `1`, fixed in #263.

## Notes on the specific env vars

- **`CRUSH_SKILLS_DIR` is not optional.** The default skills search path reaches `~/.agents/skills` and `~/.claude/skills` via `home.Dir()`, which caches `os.UserHomeDir()` in a **package var at init** (`internal/home/home.go:11`). Redirecting `HOME` cannot reach it — the pre-existing `xdgIsolated` helper's `t.Setenv("HOME", ...)` never actually isolated those paths.
- **`XDG_DATA_HOME` is deliberately left alone.** `config.cachePathFor` resolves the Catwalk provider catalog cache under it (`internal/config/provider.go:37`); redirecting it would send every `config.Init` back to the network for a provider list.
- **It has to be `TestMain`, not per-test.** Most tests in this package use `t.Parallel()`, which forbids `t.Setenv`.

## Test

`TestGlobalConfigIsolated` guards the arrangement. It was mutation-checked rather than assumed:

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| `cleanup := func() {}` (isolation removed) | fails — `TestMain must set CRUSH_GLOBAL_CONFIG` |
| `CRUSH_GLOBAL_CONFIG` pointed back at `$HOME/.config/crush` | fails — `host MCP servers leaked into the test config`, listing all 13 |
| unmutated | passes |

## Verification

```
go test -race ./internal/backend/ -count=1                        # ok, green
gofumpt -l internal/backend/                                      # clean
golangci-lint run --config=.golangci.yml ./internal/backend/...   # 0 issues
./scripts/check_log_capitalization.sh                             # clean
```

## On the expected runtime drop — it did not materialize

The issue anticipated the backend test runtime dropping from ~7.0s. **It doesn't.** Measured 3 runs each, warm:

| | baseline | isolated |
|---|---|---|
| `go test` | 5.2–6.3s | 5.1–5.6s |
| `go test -race` | 8.1–8.3s | 8.5–8.8s |

Wall clock is flat (marginally *up* under `-race`, since this adds one more test). These tests run in parallel, so the wall clock is bounded by the deliberate timing waits in `TestPathDedupe_FullCreate`, `TestHoldExpiry_RaceWithAttach` and friends — not by config loading.

What *does* drop is aggregate per-test time, **10.57s → 7.18s (-32%)**, spread across parallel workers and absorbed by the wall clock. Every config-loading test got individually faster — e.g. `TestMCPReconnect_ReloadsConfigFromDisk` 0.16s → 0.06s, `TestPathDedupe_FullCreate` 1.15s → 0.84s, `TestFirstWinsMismatch_LogsOnFlagDifferences` 0.82s → 0.53s.

Run-to-run variance also tightens (baseline had 6.3s / 10.8s / 16.7s outliers; isolated stays 5.1–5.6s) because no run reaches the network anymore. The earlier 7.0s observation was most likely one of those cold, network-bound runs.

**The justification for this change is hermeticity, not speed.** Tests should not read the developer's config or talk to their LLM endpoints.

## Not included

I considered dropping the `XDG_DATA_HOME` line from the existing `xdgIsolated` helper, since `GlobalConfigData` now consults `CRUSH_GLOBAL_DATA` first and that line only blocks the catalog cache. I measured it: **no benefit**, and it makes those tests read a real host path. Reverted — not in this PR.

Also noting for a separate change: this repo has no `Makefile`, so `make test` / `make lint` don't exist; it uses `Taskfile.yaml` (`task test`, `task lint`), which is the upstream convention. Adding a Makefile wrapper would create merge friction on every `charmbracelet/crush` sync, so I left it alone rather than bundling it here.

author: rezabaita12
body:
Stage 4 of #151, on top of #160. The MCP column becomes real.

Closes #155

## What changed

All 42 tool declarations swap `access.site: 'editor'` for `access.permission: 'entries:delete'`, matching the REST route that does the same thing — **literally the same string on both sides now**, so `auth.md`'s rule that a tool whose gate is looser than its route is a hole stops being a judgement call and becomes something you can read off two lines.

`ToolAccess.permission` takes a list for the merged tools: `write_collection` creates *or* updates depending on what it finds, and a caller cannot promise which half it will use, so it asks for both.

## The column, not the person

`ctx.sitePermissions` is the **mcp** column of the approving user's role, resolved per request the way the destructive grant is. A site admin whose role delegates everything except the delete deletes entries all day over REST, and nothing acting as them can — one edit, on one role, holding for every client they ever approve.

That is deliberately a different shape from the #145/#149 grant, and the two compose:

| | Decided by | Scope of the decision |
|---|---|---|
| Token scopes | the client, at consent | this consent |
| Destructive grant | the operator, at consent | this client |
| **`role.mcp`** | the operator, on a role | every client, every time |

Effective authority is `role.mcp ∩ token scopes ∩ destructive grant`, narrowest wins, all three checked.

## One deviation from the issue, on purpose

#155's checklist asked for the mcp column to **hide** tools from `tools/list` the way a missing scope does. It does not, and should not: a scope and the grant are fixed for the life of the consent, but a permission is part of a role and a role can change under a live token. This server reports `tools.listChanged: false`, so a list narrowed by something mutable is a list the client has no reason to refetch — it would cache a surface that is wrong the moment somebody edits a role. That is the existing invariant in `registry.ts` and `auth.md` ("role failures are never hidden"), and the refusal instead arrives at call time naming the permission, which an operator can act on.

The behaviour the checklist was after — the same client doing two different things for two different people — is pinned by test, at dispatch.

## Also here

`update_site_config` and `PATCH /sites/:slug/config` lose the hand-rolled `roleAtLeast(role, 'admin')` that #154 missed because it never called `requireSiteRole`. Both are `collections:update` now: what they write is the per-entry custom field definitions and the metadata defaults every entry inherits — the shape of the site's content, which is what that permission means everywhere else.

## Verified

`bun run lint`, `typecheck`, `test --isolate` (829 pass, 0 fail), `build`. `schema-compact.test.ts`'s payload budget still passes — the access declaration is not part of the wire schema.

Three new tests in `mcp.test.ts`: the asymmetry (site column allows the delete, mcp column does not, REST is unaffected), one client answering differently for two approvers with no per-client configuration, and `tools/list` staying whole under a narrowed column. The existing 41 are unchanged apart from the refusal messages, which now name a permission instead of a rank.
