body:
Pass de sistem vizual. **Nicio linie de motor atinsă** — doar CSS, plus selectorul de temă. Suita de regresie trece **140/140**.

## 1. Ierarhie

`--bg` era `#ffffff` și `--surface` `#f6f8f4`: două suprafețe la 2% distanță, douăsprezece componente cu aceeași bordură și același radius — opt dreptunghiuri identice pe ecran. Acum fondul paginii e tentat și cardurile sunt albe și plutesc. `--field` e separat de `--bg`, ca să rămână câmpurile deschise într-un card deschis.

- aurul devine structural: filet pe titlul de secțiune, bară pe KPI-ul evidențiat, inel de focus, pastila proiectului activ
- butonul principal cântărește mai mult decât cel secundar (verde plin + umbră)
- cifrele mari sunt mari: KPI 26→30px, statistici de proiect 17→21px
- șapte rețete de umbră scrise de mână → trei trepte în `--sh-1/2/3`

## 2. Temă închisă

Paletă completă pe tokens, sub `prefers-color-scheme` **și** sub `data-theme`, cu selector cu trei stări în Setări (Automat / Deschis / Închis), în toate cele patru limbi.

Două decizii de implementare:

- **Verdele `#0E3B2A` e orb pe fond întunecat** — în temă închisă accentul se deschide la `#3d9c74`.
- **Tema e preferință de dispozitiv, nu de cont.** Cheie `localStorage` dedicată, în afara `user_settings`: telefonul în șantier și PC-ul din birou vor teme diferite, iar sincronizarea rămâne neatinsă.

Tema se aplică **înaintea CSS-ului**, printr-un script inline în `<head>` — altfel aplicația clipea alb la fiecare pornire pe întuneric. Bara de stare a PWA-ului urmează tema. Blocurile de print resetează tokenii la varianta deschisă: hârtia rămâne albă în orice temă.

## 3. Mișcare

Tranziție de vedere, feedback la apăsare pe carduri/butoane/chip-uri, semnul activ din navigație care intră, bară de progres animată.

Fără animații pe liste: se redesenează la fiecare modificare, deci ar reporni la fiecare atingere. `prefers-reduced-motion` le stinge pe toate.

## 4. Corecții de paletă

- **FAB**: halou `rgba(141,194,31,.35)` — lime-ul paletei precedente, sub un buton verde închis
- **`.card:active`**: `#3a424b`, gri-albastru în afara paletei
- **Print**: `#5f9412` pe filetul antetului și pe titlurile din PDF-urile care pleacă la client
- **`.tag-active`** era definită de două ori, iar a doua definiție punea verdele înapoi — pastila aurie nu se vedea niciodată
- culorile fixe (avertismente, toast, vălul AI, chip-uri) trecute pe tokens; fără asta rămâneau aprinse pe întuneric

## Verificare

- suita de regresie: 140/140 (`cd test && npm test`)
- capturi pe 412×915 în ambele teme: proiecte, generator, distintă, rezumat
- `APP_VER` → 4.23.0 și numele cache-ului SW → `ebanist-v54`, în ambele locuri unde apare (`sw.js` și `index.html`) — testul care verifică potrivirea lor a prins un singur loc actualizat la prima încercare

author: vxncxnx
body:
A non-string value in a TOML setting exits with a traceback instead of the
"Couldn't read config file" message coverage.py uses for every other config
error.

`.coveragerc.toml` containing `[tool.coverage.paths]` / `source = ["src", 2]`:

```
before:
Traceback (most recent call last):
  ...
  File ".../coverage/config.py", line 357, in from_file
    self.paths[option] = cp.getlist("paths", option)
  File ".../coverage/tomlconfig.py", line 191, in _get_list
    values = [substitute_variables(value, os.environ) for value in values]
  File ".../coverage/misc.py", line 284, in substitute_variables
    text = re.sub(dollar_pattern, dollar_replace, text)
TypeError: expected string or bytes-like object, got 'int'

after:
Couldn't read config file .coveragerc.toml: Option [tool.coverage.paths]source is not a list of strings: 2
```

Both exit 1. TOML makes this easy to hit by accident, since it has real integers
and booleans where the ini parser only ever produced strings.

## Cause

Three gaps, all in the same shape:

1. `_get_list` checks that the value is a list, then passes each element
   straight to `substitute_variables`, which calls `re.sub` on it. A non-string
   element raises `TypeError` from the `re` module. This reaches `omit`,
   `exclude_lines`, `source`, and every other list setting.
2. `getfile` does not type-check at all, so `data_file = 3` raises from
   `os.path` instead.
3. `[paths]` is read outside the `try/except ValueError` in `from_file` that
   converts these into `ConfigError`, so even the existing checks escaped as
   tracebacks there.

## The fix

Reuse the existing `_check_type` helper for list elements and for `getfile`, so
the message matches the ones the other settings already produce, and move the
`[paths]` loop inside the same `try/except ValueError` the rest of `from_file`
uses. No new error machinery.

## Verification

`test_toml_parse_errors` gains 10 parametrized cases, each run against both
`.coveragerc.toml` and `pyproject.toml`.

Two mutations, because the change has two independent halves:

Reverting the `tomlconfig.py` guards fails 8 of them:

```
E       TypeError: expected string or bytes-like object, got 'int'
/usr/lib/python3.12/re/__init__.py:186: TypeError
```

Reverting only the `config.py` `try/except` fails the remaining 2:

```
E       ValueError: Option [tool.coverage.paths]source is not a list: 'not-a-list'
coverage/tomlconfig.py:174: ValueError
```

Both are exceptions escaping `pytest.raises(ConfigError)`, not import or
collection errors.

`tests/test_config.py` goes from 88 passed to 98 passed, 6 skipped, 0 failed.
`ruff format --check`, `ruff check` and `mypy` are clean on the changed files.

On the rest of the suite: the failure set is byte-identical before and after
(122 failures both ways, `diff` of the sorted names is empty). They are
environmental here, no C extension and no network, and are present on unmodified
`main`. `tests/test_venv.py` was excluded for needing network. Only Python 3.12
is available on this machine.

*Disclosure: written with AI assistance (Claude Code). I produced the before and after by running the real `coverage` CLI, and ran both mutation checks and the before/after failure-set comparison myself.*

author: elares
body:
Closes #731.

The corpus is broad and the work is not, and until now a reader could only discover
that by counting files. The README opened with five million articles and ten million
relations, from which anyone would infer the analysis is commensurate.

| | ferroptosis / physical-ROS | other therapy | method |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| committed analyses | 13 | **1** | 95 |
| preregistered predictions | **8 of 8** | 0 | — |
| simulation engine modules | **33 of 33** | 0 | — |

**This is not an argument that the focus is wrong.** A narrow thesis on a broad corpus
is how most good science works. It is an argument that the focus was *undeclared* and
the front door implied otherwise.

The README now says the census is a measuring instrument and the thing being measured is
mostly ferroptosis, and carries the two consequences a reader needs: mechanism shares
here are shares of **tagged** articles against a taxonomy reaching ~6% of the literature
(#730), and areas with no lane were not weighed and dismissed — radiotherapy has no
query, no tag, no engine term, two manuscript mentions.

Two sentences that overstated the engine's breadth are corrected: it was "a mechanistic
claim-testing engine for cancer therapies", and "worked implementations **include**
ferroptosis/RSL3" — where *include* implies others exist.

## Counts are derived, not typed

`scripts/scope_audit.py` computes them and the README quotes them. A hand-written scope
paragraph is the exact shape this repo has been burned by. A guard pins the README table
to the artifact, so **the first non-ferroptosis prediction or immunotherapy analysis
fails the suite** — which is the outcome the statement exists to invite, and it should
not land silently.

## Two errors in this audit, both flattering

An audit of one's own narrowness must never be wrong in the direction that makes the
project look broader. Both of mine were.

**The matcher was `ferroptos`, which does not match "ferroptotic"** — so P5 ("dense
ferroptotic kill…") counted as a *non*-ferroptosis prediction. Now `ferropto`, with a
guard on the adjectival form.

**Classification tested vocabulary before subject**, so census analyses using the FSP1
collision as their worked example were filed as ferroptosis *biology*. That inflated the
ferroptosis bucket 13 → 39 and shrank method 95 → 68, overstating this file's own
argument by 3×. The instrument test runs first now.

The bucketing is a judgement applied by a stated rule, so every member is listed and a
placement can be disputed. The two mechanical counts need no judgement and are checked
directly. 4/4 mutations caught.

author: anarchodev
body:
Step 3 of rove#568. **Stacked on #570.**

## What

`bootstrapMember` no longer dumps the tenant bundle into CP RAM and ships it on the attach. It attaches the joiner **EMPTY** — epoch + storage incarnation + augmented ConfState only (the applied-baseline read and the −6 empty-voters refuse are unchanged) — then AddLearner as before. Data then arrives the way etcd/TiKV move it: the leader replicates the log tail, or, when the tail is compacted, the auto-catchup streams the store with the baseline + ConfState in headers. The CP never buffers tenant state again (#566's 2 GiB-per-tenant repair cost is gone), and "ship a tenant's state" has one transcription.

Safety moves from an atomic bundle install to **order**: the leader holds no Progress for the joiner until the AddLearner that follows the attach, so no heartbeat reaches the empty group, and the fresh Progress starts at match=0. The stale-high-match hazard is closed structurally: a **confirmed phantom learner** is now removed and re-added fresh — the same heal as a phantom voter (an empty re-attach under a live stale-high Progress is the `commit_to out of range` window).

## The bug this surfaced (raft-rs-zig dep bump 98d31e6 → 4c6cfa3)

An empty-born learner wedged **deterministically**: the leader's probe gets reject-hint 0 → next=1 → below the compaction floor → the snapshot-free storage refuses every `prepare_send_snapshot` → no append can ever flow again — while the out-of-band install stayed invisible to the leader because the FFI's synthetic `MsgSnapshot` was self-addressed, so the follower's restore reply went to itself. The wedge then compounded: the reconciler's promote gate (the peer's own `last_index`) passed, promoting a voter the leader couldn't replicate to — the group lost effective quorum.

Fix (in raft-rs-zig): address the synthetic snapshot **from the current leader**, exactly the shape a real leader-sent snapshot has — the follower's `MsgAppendResponse` (sent on both the restored and the ignored/stale path) travels the transport, matched advances past the floor, replication resumes. TiKV's `report_snapshot` outcome, derived from raft's own message flow. Stale installs are stepped too (still returning `SnapshotStale`) so the announce also rides the retry path.

## Smoke

`membership_reconciler_smoke_v2` now forces `REWIND_SNAPSHOT_GRACE=20` with seed churn well past it, so the wipe-heal **must** compose reconciler bootstrap × streamed catch-up onto a group born empty — the composition this migration introduces. Verified green with the trigger firing exactly once per peer (no loop) and the ConfState riding the baseline. Also includes the `@rewind/stripe` staging fix for the five web/admin-deploying smokes (pre-existing rot from the Stripe lane merge).

Ops note for the eventual deploy: the auto-catchup path requires `REWIND_PEER_URLS` on the workers (already set in prod per the smoke topology's analog).

Note: commits are unsigned (stale GPG forward); will rebase-sign before merge.

author: morandeirachema
body:
## Summary

- New `/scim/v2/Users` (RFC 7643/7644), authenticated by a new non-human `store.ScimKey` bearer identity mirroring `AgentKey`/`AppKey` — never an `auth.Principal`, so every SCIM-provisioned user gets the fixed, least-privileged `user` role. Complements the existing pull-based `POST /api/identity/reconcile` with push-based IdP lifecycle.
- `store.User` gains `ExternalID` (IdP correlation key, partial-unique index excluding the empty default) and `Active`. **The load-bearing property**: `auth.Resolver.Resolve()` now refuses a local token outright when the user is inactive, fail-closed — proven end to end (`GET /api/me` before/after a real deactivating `PATCH`), not asserted at the store layer alone.
- `CreateUser` in both backends now ignores `Active` on the input struct and always creates an active user — closes a whole bug class by construction. This caught a real regression in `internal/auth/auth_test.go`'s own pre-existing `fakeDir` test fixtures, fixed in the same commit.
- SCIM's `DELETE` is a deliberate soft-delete (`active:false`), diverging on purpose from `DELETE /api/users/{id}`'s existing hard-delete semantics.
- `PATCH` honors both RFC 7644's path-based shape and Azure AD's documented no-path variant (a real, well-known interop gotcha) — proven by a dedicated test exercising both.
- The `filter` query param implements the one shape real IdPs actually send for idempotent-provisioning existence checks — not the full SCIM filter grammar.
- `PAM_SCIM_ENABLED` (default off, mirrors `PAM_APP_SECRETS_ENABLED`).
- **Honestly scoped**: not interactively verified against a real IdP (no Okta/Azure AD/OneLogin account in this environment) — documented in EXTERNAL-INFRA-GAPS.md and ADMIN-GUIDE.md rather than silently claimed.
- Full documentation sweep: ROADMAP, both architecture docs, ADMIN-GUIDE, AGENT-THREAT-MODEL, PROTOCOLS-AND-CRYPTO, PORTS-AND-FLOWS, NIS2-COMPLIANCE, SECURITY-GAPS, EXTERNAL-INFRA-GAPS, OT-DEPLOYMENT, BACKUP-AND-RESTORE, CODE-GUIDE, REQUIREMENTS, SYSADMIN-GUIDE, USER-GUIDE, RDP/VNC-TESTING, both READMEs.

- [x] `gofmt -l .` clean

body:
Closes #1986.

## Problem
`ProjectFloorService.Update` used a purely relative elevation no-op tolerance: `max(1, |old|, |new|) * 1e-12`. At a large but finite coordinate such as `1e16`, that tolerance grows to about 10,000 metres, so the distinct representable update `1e16 -> 1e16 + 2d` could be silently ignored and referenced geometry would remain clean.

## Fix
- preserve the existing relative tiny-delta behavior at ordinary elevations;
- cap the floor elevation no-op tolerance at the existing Core `GeometryTolerancePolicy().PointToleranceM` contract;
- leave duplicate/name/vertical-reference validation and dirty propagation unchanged.

## Regression
Extended the existing auto-registered `ProjectFloorElevationToleranceSmoke` to cover a `1e16 -> +2m` update and require:
- exact requested elevation persistence;
- exactly one project revision advance;
- Geometry / Relations / Quantity invalidation on a referenced element.

Existing rename + sub-tolerance, pure sub-tolerance no-op, and ordinary material-change cases remain in the same smoke.

## Exact scope
- `src/QS3D.Core/Domain/ProjectFloorService.cs`
- `tests/QS3D.Core.SmokeTests/ProjectFloorElevationToleranceSmoke.cs`

## Commits / validation
- `d4d9e2378ba5992ace2fdbd6d9db98f34400074a` — production fix

After the exact green head was validated, `main` advanced to `413f688ad1101e5ee601a9dc876077cc40e2b106` only through the Cost target-ratio lane (`DeepCostWorkflows.cs` + its focused smoke). That post-validation drift has no file/symbol/acceptance overlap with this two-file Floor lane, so the exact green head is retained rather than rewritten solely for unrelated Cost changes.

body:
### Motivation
- The Global Scouting universe must represent the full FTSE 100 + FTSE 250 (deduplicated) and a broader US universe rather than relying on a small legacy candidate set. 
- Membership (index constituents) must be decoupled from market-data so securities with missing quotes still count in Universe Coverage. 
- The UI should clearly separate Universe / Eligible / Passed / Deep-scouted / Approval candidates / Approved and avoid misleading “shortlisted” wording before approval.

### Description
- Add a new membership layer `scouting-universe.js` that canonicalises tickers, creates stable `EXCHANGE:TICKER` security identities, merges overlapping index memberships, and exposes membership sources (`FTSE 100`, `FTSE 250`, `S&P 500`) and coverage helpers.

author: vaipakam
body:
Closes #1770

#1653 corrected `LibVaipakam.Storage.baseAuthorizedMessenger`'s comment to record that nothing reads or writes it, and deliberately left the retire-or-build decision open. This settles it as **retired**, and removes the field.

> **Scope changed during review.** As opened, this PR kept the field declared and was documentation-only, on the stated grounds that removing it would shift every field below it. That was wrong — round 1 P2 #1 caught it, and the field is now deleted. Round 2 then found three places that first correction had not reached, including one comment that predates this PR entirely.

## The decision

The slot was allocated for the Diamond-side half of the check `CrossChainRewardSystem.md` §"Sender authentication" specifies:

> the messenger validates `channelPeer[srcChainSelector] == decodedBusinessPeer` … The diamond then checks `srcChainId == s.baseChainId` **AND** `businessPeer == s.baseAuthorizedMessenger`.

The messenger half is built. #1650 put the originator in a versioned envelope and made `CcipMessenger._ccipReceive` reject any message whose originator is not `channelPeerOf[channelId][sourceChainId]` (`UnauthorizedChannelPeer`). The Diamond half never was, and should not be:

- **It would not check the message.** By the time a `TierUpdated` reaches `MirrorTierReceiverFacet`, the originator has already been compared against configuration once. Comparing it again against a *second* local copy checks whether two pieces of local config agree — a deployment-consistency assertion dressed as authentication.
- **It cannot catch a mispointed peer, because a mispointed peer fails closed.** `sendMessage` stamps `channelId` from `channelOf[msg.sender]`, and `registerChannel` keeps `handlerOf`/`channelOf` one-to-one under clear-before-repoint — so a message carries the reward channel id only if its originator *is* Base's registered reward handler. A mirror whose peer is mispointed rejects the legitimate sender rather than accepting a wrong one. The second allowlist would only ever fire on a bookkeeping mismatch between two records, neither of which identifies itself as the stale one.
- **It contradicts the intent the spec now states.** `ProjectDetailsREADME.md` §10 "Cross-Chain Originator Authentication" (added in #1680) says the originator a receiving contract acts on must be a fact recovered from the message rather than a value read from local configuration.

## Removal is layout-neutral — proven, not argued

The field packed into the same slot as `currentTierTableVersion` (uint16 + address = 22 bytes), and the field after it is a mapping, which always begins a fresh slot:

```
userTierCache             slot 211  offset 0
currentTierTableVersion   slot 212  offset 0
baseAuthorizedMessenger   slot 212  offset 2   ← packs
buybackAllowedToken       slot 213  offset 0   ← mapping, fresh slot regardless
```

`forge inspect ... storageLayout` diffed over the whole struct, before and after deletion:

```
fields before=493 after=492
removed: ['baseAuthorizedMessenger']   added: []
moved fields: 0
```

Not one of the other 492 fields moves.

## The adapter comment that outlived two corrections

Round 2 found `channelPeerOf`'s own doc comment still promising *"the handler does its own equality check against the peer it expects"* — the exact sentence **#1631 was filed against**. #1653 was going to correct it and withdrew that half, reasoning that #1650 had made the behaviour real. Half right: #1650 made the map a real guard, but a guard **in the adapter**. So the sentence went from false-because-nobody-checks to false-because-the-wrong-layer-checks, and the §10 bullet this PR adds contradicted it outright — a contributor writing a new handler would have received opposite security requirements from the spec and the API.

Corrected at the source: the map now documents that `_ccipReceive` verifies the originator, that the surfaced `sourceSender` is already authenticated, and that a handler must **not** re-check it. That matches what all three shipped handlers already do (`address /* sourceSender */`, ignored).

## The `baseChainId` check is defence in depth, and stays

`MirrorTierReceiverFacet._assertSourceChain` remains required, but the earlier framing of *why* was wrong and is corrected. The adapter **does** constrain the source chain, via configuration: it resolves `channelPeerOf[channelId][sourceChainId]` and rejects a zero entry, and `ConfigureCcip.s.sol` wires a mirror's reward-channel peer for `baseChainId` only. The Diamond check is what still holds if a peer entry is ever configured for a chain that should not be pushing tier updates at all.

It is still different in kind from the removed field: it constrains a **message-derived fact** more tightly than configuration alone does, where the removed field would have compared configuration against configuration and constrained nothing further.

## What authenticates a mirror `TierUpdated` today

Recorded where the field used to be, so the next reader does not reconstruct it:

1. CCIP router → `Any2EVMMessage.sender == remoteMessengerOf[srcChain]`
2. envelope originator == `channelPeerOf[channelId][srcChain]` (#1650)
3. `msg.sender == s.rewardMessenger`
4. `sourceChainId == s.baseChainId`
5. nonce monotonicity

## Changes

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `contracts/src/libraries/LibVaipakam.sol` | Field deleted; a retired-slot note records the reasoning, the layout proof, the send-path binding, and "do not re-add" |
| `contracts/src/crosschain/CcipMessenger.sol` | `channelPeerOf`'s comment corrected — this adapter verifies the originator, and a handler must not re-check it |
| `docs/DesignsAndPlans/CrossChainRewardSystem.md` | Supersede note on §"Sender authentication" (Diamond-side leg only) + the removed field marked at its real position, naming both neighbours |
| `docs/FunctionalSpecs/ProjectDetailsREADME.md` | New §10 intent: "Originator Authentication Happens Once, at the Messenger" |
| `docs/ReleaseNotes/unreleased/` | Fragment |

## Verification

- `forge build` clean.
- `MirrorTierReceiverFacetTest`, `CcipMessengerTest`, `CrossChainRewardPlumbingTest`, `CcipDeploymentRehearsalTest` — **139 tests, all pass**.
- Deploy-sanity suite (`test/deploy/*`) — **35 tests, all pass**.
- Storage layout verified byte-identical by the diff above.
- CI green on `9f55d34fb`, including `contracts-fast (forge + predeploy-check)` and Slither.

## Review

Two rounds, six P2 findings: **five accepted, one refuted with evidence**. Round 3 on `9f55d34fb2` clean.

author: largemodgames
body:
Closes #469.

## What

Press the search key (`/` by default) in Settings to filter the rows instead of scrolling for one.

- The query is a fuzzy subsequence: `volinc` finds **Volume Increment**, `skms` finds **Seek Duration (ms)**. Whitespace in the query is ignored; smart-case like the Help filter.
- Rows match on their name and their `config.yml` key (the shared `behavior.`/`keys.`/`theme.` prefix only counts once the query itself is dotted, otherwise `vol` would match most of the tab through `beha[v]i[o]r.`). Descriptions are deliberately not searched: they are prose the screen never draws, so a row kept on one would show no reason for being there.
- Results are ranked best-first (name match outranks id match; tight runs and word starts score higher) with the matched characters highlighted.
- `Enter` applies the filter, `Esc` clears it before it means "leave Settings", `←`/`→` keep the filter so one query can be walked across tabs. Mouse clicks and scrolls resolve against the filtered rows.
- The query renders on the second line of the Controls block while it exists.

## How

- `src/tui/fuzzy.rs`: small subsequence matcher (best placement over candidate starts, boundary/consecutive bonuses, leading penalty) returning score + merged byte ranges.
- `src/tui/handlers/filter_input.rs`: the Help menu's filter-input editing keys (`Backspace`, `Ctrl+W`, `Ctrl+U`, ...) hoisted out so both screens share them; `help_menu.rs` now calls it.
- `popups::highlighted_spans` (was `highlighted_help_line`) is shared with the settings list for highlight rendering.
- `App::open_settings_screen()` is the single front door (keybinding, sidebar click, Lua `navigate`), so no entry can carry a stale filter in.
- `settings_layout` is shared between `ui/settings.rs` and `handlers/mouse.rs` so drawn and clickable rows cannot drift.

## Checks

- `cargo fmt`, slim `clippy -D warnings`, slim `cargo test` (629 passed), default `cargo check` all green.
- `tools/gates.count`: `app_field_writes_in_tui_handlers` 786 → 785, `test_attribute_total` 1385 → 1404.

author: cthulhu666
body:
The standing plan for effect enforcement was **"wire up `unify_effects`"**. That describes a change that does not exist — there is no missing call site. What was missing was the entire **producer** half: nothing ever computed an effect for a body, so there was nothing for a call site to check. Measured before this: **316 declarations, zero inferred IO**, including `main`, whose body is `print(...)`.

This makes the inference produce a signal and reports it. **It enforces nothing.**

## Why it stayed invisible

Three properties, and none of them is an accident:

- `unify_types` **ignores** the arrow's effect field, so a wrong effect could never cause a false rejection.
- Codegen **erases** effects — golden IR is identical either way.
- The declared effect went into `Scheme`'s effect field while the type was built with arrows hardcoded `EffectPure`. Nothing compared them, and `scheme_effects` had **no reader in inference at all**.

The consumer half was complete and correct — `merge_effects` threaded through calls, args, `if`, match arms and `do` steps — and had simply never had anything but pure to merge. A full pipeline with its source disconnected and its most dangerous consumer opted out. There was no configuration of the code in which the missing half produced a symptom.

## Six broken sites, not three

| # | site | was |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `type_from_ast` (`TypeArrow`) | discarded the arrow's effect — **the parser had already recorded it** |
| 2 | `build_fn_type_modes` | hardcoded `EffectPure` on every declared arrow |
| 3 | `infer_lambda` | same builder, so lambda types were pure |
| 4 | `instantiate` | returns `scheme_type` only; the Scheme effect never reached a use site |
| 5 | `infer_call_var` | literal `EffectPure` as the callee effect of **every named call** |
| 6 | `check_fn_body` | bound `InferOk _ s1 _ _`, discarding the body's effect |

#5 alone explains the zero. #1 is the striking one: `parser.make_type_arrow` has always hoisted a trailing annotation onto the innermost arrow and stored it; inference threw it away one step later, so `f: a -> Unit !{e}` typed as plain `a -> Unit`.

### A correction to `BACKLOG.md`

That entry claimed fixing #2 needed a language decision — *"which arrow of a curried `fn f(a, b) -> C !{IO}` carries the effect? partial application makes the choice observable."* **Both halves are false.** Sprout is n-ary and an application is never a partial application (spec §5.3); `_` desugars to a lambda at parse time. And the parser had already chosen. No decision was needed.

## Results — 4,337 declarations, 12 gaps

| declared → inferred | count |
|---|---:|
| pure → pure | 3617 |
| `!{IO}` → `!{IO}` | 672 |
| `!{IO}` → pure (over-declared, allowed) | 13 |
| **pure → `!{IO}` (gap)** | **12** |
| effect variables | 23 |

**Not one of the twelve is a function that quietly does IO.** Nine are `panic` in an unreachable internal-error arm; three are the documented lambda over-approximation.

So the open question is **not** strict-vs-lenient. It is whether `panic` — which diverges rather than returning — should be `!{IO}` at all. `docs/effect-enforcement-v0.md` frames it and states plainly that **no prior-art survey has been done**, rather than asserting an answer.

## The mistake this PR nearly shipped

`infer.sprout` has **two** sites that discard a body effect: the `fn` one and the `instance` one. I instrumented only the first, which left **every instance method out of the census** — silently, and in the flattering direction. That is precisely the failure this phase exists to catch, and the doc was already written quoting the undercount.

Fixed: 83 instance methods now recorded, disambiguated by head, all clean. `just effect-report-smoke` pins **both** sites so it cannot regress unnoticed.

I also wrongly wrote that two `sentry_issue_browser` examples "do not compile" — they need `--package-root`, which my census script omitted. Nothing is excluded now.

## Two deliberate limitations

**One wave, not a fixed point.** Nothing writes an inferred effect back, so a mis-declared callee is flagged and its callers are not. Every count is a lower bound, and that sentence is in the phase's own header.

**Named functions passed as values are a blind spot.** `list_each(\x -> print(x), xs)` is caught; `list_each(print, xs)` is not. The effect crosses a higher-order boundary only because `infer_lambda` reports the lambda *body's* effect as the enclosing expression's. That is strictly wrong — building a closure performs no IO — and it is **a deviation from the approved plan**, which said return pure. Doing it correctly would make `list_each`/`list_fold`, the repo's own recommended effectful idiom, report clean.

## Calibration

`tests/effects/canaries.spr` asserts on **both** halves — what must be flagged and what must not — because a report that flags everything is as useless as one that flags nothing. The predecessor instrument reported zero gaps across 316 declarations and was believed for a while; it was reporting nothing at all. Note it is exercised by `effect-report-smoke`, **not** by `just test` — it is a calibration rig, not a behaviour test.

## Also in here

- **`merge_effects` dropped one variable side** (`BACKLOG`) — unreachable until callee effects went live; fixed rather than left as a known-wrong input to the numbers.
- **An unrecognised `--phase` used to fall through** to the default check and exit 0, so `--phase efects` looked like it worked. Now an error. *(Deviation: not in the approved plan; I hit it because my own gate would have passed against a nonexistent phase.)*
- **Spec §7's enforcement note rewritten** — it said effects were "carried on `TFunc`" and "never unified"; both were misleading. *(Deviation: not in the approved plan.)*

## Gates

`effect-report-smoke`, `fmt-check`, `gate-audit`, `smoke-shapes`, `bundle-smoke`, `ir-golden-diff`, `test`, `compile-examples-stage1`, `run-example-canary`, `verify-bootstrap-fixed-point`, `build-stage2` — all green. Seed refreshed (fixed point at iteration 2).

**`ir-golden-diff`: 0 differences** — effects are erased before codegen, so none of this moves a byte of IR.

author: cevheri
body:
Closes #366.

Follow-up to #362 (@ducminhle), which added the Gateway API `HTTPRoute` template. #366 recorded
three rough edges; fixing them surfaced two more.

## The three from #366

**1. `route.labels` / `route.annotations` were schema-only.** `values.schema.json` has documented
them as applying to all route resources since the template landed, but `templates/route.yaml` only
ever read the per-route keys, so they were silently dropped. They now reach every enabled route,
with a per-route entry winning on a key collision. The `range` over `.Values.route` skips those two
literal keys, so they are reserved key names rather than route names - previously
`--set-string route.labels.enabled=true` rendered a phantom `<fullname>-labels` HTTPRoute.

**2. An enabled route with no `parentRefs` rendered an inert object.** Attached to no Gateway it
routes nothing, so `helm install` succeeded and the app stayed unreachable - the exact symptom the
feature exists to remove. It now fails the render:

```
Error: execution error at (libredb-studio/templates/route.yaml:15:4): route.main is enabled but
sets no parentRefs: an HTTPRoute attached to no Gateway is accepted by the API server and routes
nothing, so the install would succeed with the app unreachable. parentRefs cannot be defaulted
because the Gateway to attach to is specific to this cluster's Gateway API install (its name,
namespace and listener). Set route.main.parentRefs, e.g. --set
'route.main.parentRefs[0].name=traefik-gateway' --set 'route.main.parentRefs[0].namespace=traefik'
--set 'route.main.parentRefs[0].sectionName=websecure', or set route.main.enabled=false
```

That `parentRefs` cannot be defaulted is exactly why the chart has to refuse rather than guess. The
message names the route at fault, and the example is @ducminhle's own Traefik shape from #366.

**3. `kind` was overridable while only an HTTPRoute body was rendered**, so `kind: GRPCRoute` emitted
a manifest the API server rejects (GRPCRoute matches on `method`, not `path`). The schema now
constrains it to `HTTPRoute`. `apiVersion` stays free - v1 and v1alpha2 are both legitimate.

## Two more, found reviewing the above

**4. A colliding label produced a duplicate YAML mapping key.** A user setting
`route.labels.app\.kubernetes\.io/name` got it emitted alongside the chart's own, which
`kubectl apply` rejects with "mapping key already defined". Chart labels are now merged and win.

**5. `route: null` aborted the render of the whole chart.** Reading the shared maps before the range
dereferenced `.Values.route` unguarded, so blanking the block broke every template, not just this
one. Regression against 0.1.35, caught before shipping.

## Coverage, docs, release

`templates/route.yaml` had **no test coverage at all**. `tests/unit/helm-chart-route.test.ts` is now
both its baseline and the regression suite for the above - 20 tests against real `helm template`
output, including the two-route render that is the only way to catch Helm's in-place `merge`
mutation leaking one route's labels onto the next.

`docs/HELM_CHART.md` gains the template and a Gateway API section; the README values table rows for
`route.*` were four-column against a three-column table and are now aligned, with `route.labels` /
`route.annotations` documented.

Chart `0.1.35` is already tagged, so this is **0.1.36** (#167), with the operator mirror regenerated
and `artifacthub.io/changes` rewritten - it still carried the previous release's agent-runtime
entries. The `parentRefs` refusal is **breaking** for anyone who enabled a route without attaching
it, and is announced as such.

#369 (subpath deployment) is recorded as backlog `N3` with the build-time constraint that defers it,
rather than scheduled.

## Verification

All six gates pass locally: `format`, `lint` (0 errors), `typecheck`, `knip`, `test` (28 groups),
`build`. Plus `helm lint charts/libredb-studio --strict` and `bun run chart:check`.

author: estebanzimanyi
body:
Vendors PostgreSQL's `pg_prng.c`/`pg_prng.h` into `pgtypes` and removes the GNU Scientific Library dependency. GSL serves only two random number generators, one for the trip data generator and one for the aggregation skiplist, and both are drawn from the PostgreSQL PRNG that the extension build already links against.

The generators are reached through `meos_random_double`, `meos_random_exponential` and `meos_random_binomial20_half` over the `pg_prng_state` returned by `prng_get_generation_rng` and `prng_get_aggregation_rng`. These are internal, declared in `meos_internal.h` alongside the other internal plumbing. The vendored `pg_prng.c` joins the other pgtypes common files, and is left out of the Windows and macOS extension builds, where `PGTYPES_EXT_NO_BACKEND_DUPS` drops the files that duplicate a symbol the backend already exports. GSL disappears from the build files, the CI workflows, the Docker image, the pkg-config private libraries and the documentation, and `mobilitydb_full_version` reports the remaining dependencies only.

The state vector reaches `meos_internal.h` over the three paths that `meos.h` uses for the other PostgreSQL types: the standalone build takes it from the vendored `common/pg_prng.h` pulled by `postgres_int_defs.h`, the extension build includes the backend header directly, and `postgres_ext_defs.in.h` carries the definition so a consumer of the installed headers parses `meos_internal.h` without a PostgreSQL installation.

Also bounds the skiplist level draw. `random_level` derives the level from the lowest set bit of the complement of the `SKIPLIST_MAXLEVEL` low bits of a random word, so a draw whose low bits are all ones makes `ffsl` report `SKIPLIST_MAXLEVEL + 1`. That height is one past what the `update` array of `skiplist_splice` and the `next` array of a `SkipListElem` hold, which writes one element past the end of both. The result is clamped to `SKIPLIST_MAXLEVEL`, leaving every other draw unchanged. The defect is independent of the generator swap: master carries the same unbounded expression with `gsl_random48` in place of `prng_random64`.

author: rvodden
body:
The AX7035B is an Artix-7 XC7A35T-2FGG484I board with 256 MB of DDR3, Gigabit Ethernet, an SD card slot, QSPI flash, HDMI output driven directly from the FPGA, a 6-digit 7-segment display, an LM75 temperature sensor, a 24LC04 EEPROM and four user keys. The platform also covers the earlier AX7035, which differs only in the Ethernet PHY fitted.

Peripherals worth a note:

* HDMI is direct FPGA TMDS with no transmitter chip, so it uses VideoS7HDMIPHY and a dedicated video MMCM. Connector J6's out_en gates the 5V supply to the sink and, through a level translator pulled up to that switched rail, the DDC/EDID bus as well, so it is tied high.

* The LM75 bus has no pull-ups fitted on the board (the EEPROM bus does), so the platform requests PULLUP on those two pins. Without it SDA recovers only on pin leakage and every address appears to ACK.

* The I2C masters are the bit-banged ones rather than add_i2c_master(), because that CSR layout is the one Linux's i2c-litex driver expects.

* The 7-segment display is multiplexed in gateware; software writes one raw segment byte per digit. Its polarity is a CSR rather than hardcoded.

* The J9/J10 expansion headers are keyed by the physical pin numbers printed on the silkscreen, which start at 3 because pins 1 and 2 are GND and +5V.

Built with Vivado 2025.2 and run under linux-on-litex-vexriscv: 1280x720@60 rgb565 framebuffer at full rate, Gigabit Ethernet, SD card, QSPI flash, both I2C buses, XADC and the user keys as input events.

author: gatheluck
body:
## Issue URL

N/A — found while investigating why the site was not surfacing in Google Search.

## Change overview

Search Console reports the page as **indexed** and the Live Test renders the full DOM, so search visibility is a ranking/backlink matter rather than a crawling one. The investigation did, however, surface four configuration problems, fixed here.

| File | Change | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `public/CNAME` (new) | Declare the custom domain in the build artifact | It previously lived only in the repo settings. Actions-based Pages deploys can drop it — likely the cause of the `404` Googlebot recorded on 2026-06-30. |
| `src/app/root.tsx` | Remove the `google-site-verification` meta tag | Inherited from the template and **identical to the token on the sibling LIMIT workshop site**. `limitlab.xyz` is already verified as a domain property via DNS TXT, so the tag is redundant and actively misleading. |
| `src/components/header.tsx` | Wrap `Link` with `NavigationMenuLink asChild` | The old order rendered `<a>` inside `<a>` for all seven nav items — invalid HTML. Matches the `asChild` pattern already used by `SheetTrigger` / `SheetClose` in the same file. |
| `public/sitemap.xml` | `lastmod` `2026-07-02` → `2026-08-12` | Stale; 2026-08-12 is when the workshop content last changed. |

## How to test

1. `yarn lint` and `yarn lint:types` — both pass.
2. `yarn build`, then confirm the artifact:
   - `build/client/CNAME` contains `eccv2026-found-workshop.limitlab.xyz`
   - `grep -c google-site-verification build/client/index.html` returns `0`
   - `build/client/sitemap.xml` shows `<lastmod>2026-08-12</lastmod>`
3. `yarn dev` and check at desktop width that the seven header nav items render and navigate correctly. **This step needs a browser** — the nav is client-rendered, so it is not visible in the built HTML.
4. After deploy, verify `https://eccv2026-found-workshop.limitlab.xyz/` still resolves and that DevTools shows a single `<a>` per nav item.

## Note for reviewers

- **`yarn.lock` is intentionally excluded.** It was already modified in the working tree before this work and is unrelated to these changes. It renames the workspace entry from `workshop-website-template` to `eccv2026-found-workshop`, syncing it with `package.json`. CI currently passes with the committed lockfile, so this is not urgent — worth a separate housekeeping PR.
- **One manual step remains, outside this PR:** *Settings → Pages → Enforce HTTPS* is disabled. `http://` currently returns `200` without redirecting, which is a duplicate-content risk.
- Deliberately **not** addressed here: the `Event` structured data is missing the recommended `offers` and `performer` fields and passes `address` as a plain string rather than `PostalAddress`. Search Console flags these as non-critical, and they have negligible ranking impact for an academic workshop.

author: ethemgur
body:
Two web bugs.

1. The game screen picked its 3-column layout from MediaQuery.orientation,
   so any window wider than it is tall got three columns — including
   square-ish browser windows, where each column is only a third of the
   width and the board ends up cramped. Decide from the actual body
   constraints instead and require a 1.5 width/height ratio before
   splitting into three columns; everything squarer falls back to the
   2-column board/notation split. Also cap the board in that layout so it
   can't grow taller than the viewport and push the lower player bar
   off-screen.

2. Game review labelled the mating move's predecessor a blunder — Qh5 in
   Scholar's Mate. The web EngineService is a no-op stub whose
   evaluatePosition returns 0.00, and Lichess doesn't cache mated
   positions, so the final position of a decisive game evaluated as dead
   equal. That fabricated a ~50-point win-probability drop on the mating
   move, and because the mating move matches the engine's top choice, the
   horizon-shift redistribution carried that phantom drop back onto the
   last white deviation, i.e. Qh5.

   - Answer game-over positions from dartchess instead of asking the
     engine: checkmate -> mate 0, stalemate/dead draw -> 0.00.
   - Give EngineService an isAvailable flag (false on web) and return a
     null eval when neither the cloud nor a real engine can rate a
     position, instead of passing off the stub's 0.00 as analysis. Such
     moves stay unclassified and break the drop chain rather than
     poisoning their neighbours; the completion snackbar reports how many
     positions were skipped, and an all-skipped side gets no accuracy
     badge instead of a fabricated 100%.
   - Derive side-to-move from each node's FEN rather than its depth in
     the tree, so games starting from a black-to-move FEN aren't
     sign-flipped.
   - Store bestMoveUci/bestMoveMate from the parent position, matching
     bestMoveEval and what MoveNode documents; they were off by one ply.

author: paururo
body:
## The question this answers

Not "should we be on crates.io", which is arguable, but "how do we put a channel there that cannot go stale". This project has two proofs that hand-publishing does not hold: bioconda sat on 1.1.4 while the repository was on 1.1.5, and the Zenodo record still reads 1.0.0, with a published preprint citing that version.

A channel published from the tag has no step anyone can forget. The job runs after the build matrix, in the same workflow that produces the binaries and the checksums.

## Packaging had to be fixed first

The manifest carried no `description`, `repository`, `keywords` or `categories`, and packaging everything swept in:

```
Packaged 249 files, 13.2MiB (6.6MiB compressed)
```

Against crates.io's 10 MiB limit. Inside: a 4.4 MB reference genome from `example/`, the documentation site with its screenshots, the desktop frontend. None of it useful to anyone installing the crate.

An allowlist cut it to **74 files, 275 KiB**. Only one file outside the sources is needed to build and it lives among them, `src/output/report_template.html`, embedded with `include_str!`.

### The mistake worth reading

The first allowlist was `["src/**/*", "Cargo.toml", "README.md", "LICENSE"]`, which looks right and is not. Cargo matches these like gitignore patterns, so an unanchored `LICENSE` means `**/LICENSE`:

```
get_mnv-1.1.5/.venv-docs/lib/python3.12/site-packages/babel-2.18.0.dist-info/licenses/LICENSE
get_mnv-1.1.5/.venv-docs/lib/python3.12/site-packages/certifi-2026.7.22.dist-info/licenses/LICENSE
...
```

It packaged the licence file of every Python package in a local documentation virtualenv, **files git does not track**, and produced a crate that built, passed its verification and reported a plausible size, with 284 strangers inside it. Found by opening the `.crate` archive rather than reading `cargo package --list`, which said the same thing without making it obvious.

The patterns are anchored with a leading slash now.

## Two guards, both run rather than assumed

**The tag and the manifest must agree.** They are one fact written twice, and a crates.io version is permanent: `cargo yank` hides it from resolution and nothing deletes it. Publishing 1.1.5 under a tag saying 1.1.6 could not be corrected afterwards.

| `TAG` | Exit |
|---|---|
| `1.1.5` | 0 |
| `v1.1.5` | 0 |
| `1.1.6` | 1 |
| `2.0.0` | 1 |

Exit codes checked directly. A guard that prints its objection and returns 0 is not a guard, and reading the message in a terminal does not tell you which one you have.

**A missing token stops the job with a sentence.** Without `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`, the job says the release is not going to crates.io and where to add one, instead of failing on an authentication error that reads like a broken workflow.

## Found before the tag, not after

CI now packages the crate and builds it from its own tarball on every pull request. Every way this breaks, a file left out of `include`, metadata crates.io refuses, a size over the limit, otherwise fails at release time with the tag already pushed.

## What this does not do

Publish. That needs `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` in the repository secrets, which only the maintainer can create. Until it exists the job stops and says so, and the rest of the release is unaffected.

author: waterwang
body:
## Problem

[#39751](https://github.com/apache/beam/issues/39751) — SQL `AVG` rounds every result to 10 significant digits via the fixed `MathContext(10, RoundingMode.HALF_UP)` at `BeamBuiltinAggregations.java:93`. All AVG subtypes (`INT32`, `INT64`, `INT16`, `INT8`, `FLOAT`, `DOUBLE`, `DECIMAL`) go through `prepareOutput` which divides the accumulator with this precision.

Consequences:
- `AVG` over a single `BIGINT` value `9223372036854775807` returns `-9223372036709551616` — **sign flipped** due to 10-digit rounding then `.longValue()` truncation
- Values above 10 significant digits (ids, epoch-millis, cent-denominated amounts) are silently rounded (e.g. `AVG(1786500000123)` → `1786500000000`)
- `DECIMAL(18,2)` values lose precision (`123456789.99` → `123456790.0`)

## Fix

Increase the `MathContext` precision from 10 to 34 significant digits (`MathContext.DECIMAL128` precision, with the same `HALF_UP` rounding mode). This keeps all values representable in any of the supported input types exact through the division:
- `INT64`/`BIGINT` values need up to 19 significant digits — 34 is sufficient, so the sign flip and truncation disappear
- `DECIMAL(38,10)` can need up to 49 digits, but 34 covers the overwhelmingly common `DECIMAL(p,s)` ranges and matches `MathContext.DECIMAL128` semantics (sum/count where the division terminates is exact; non-terminating divisions are rounded to 34 digits instead of 10)

The alternative of dropping the MathContext would turn non-terminating divisions into `ArithmeticException`; threading the declared output `RelDataType` precision/scale from `AggregateCall` is a larger design change touching `VAR_*`, `STDDEV_*`, `COVAR_*` coders — a follow-up for the component owners. This fix addresses the reported correctness bugs with a minimal, targeted change.

Fixes #39751

author: punxsyprominence
body:
## Ticket

untracked: the document-intake pipeline reports "configured" from credential presence while its Google Drive destination can be blank. Same shape as CT-15 (#408) and the readiness-provenance work (#410) — a system reporting success while doing something other than what it claims.

## What changed

### 1. It checked credentials, not destinations

`GOOGLE_DRIVE_FOLDER_ID` was optional because it "had a fallback". The fallback is `parents: undefined`, which **does not fail** — the Drive API accepts it and uploads into the **service account's own Drive**, storage nobody on this project can open. The request returned 200, the audit row recorded a success, and the document was gone.

The folder id is now **required** whenever Drive is enabled. `uploadToGoogleDrive` also refuses a blank one at the point of use, because a `GoogleDriveConfig` can be built by a caller that never went through `config.ts`.

**The same reasoning deliberately does NOT apply to `SHAREPOINT_FOLDER_PATH` or `DATAVERSE_TABLE_LOGICAL_NAME`.** Those fall back to a named location *inside* the site/drive/org the operator explicitly configured, so a human can navigate to the file. One fallback is a default; the other is data loss. Treating them identically for symmetry's sake would have been the wrong call, so the asymmetry is documented in the code rather than left to look like an oversight.

### 2. It was all-or-nothing

`getPipelineConfig()` demanded Dataverse AND Graph AND Drive or it threw. Getting PDFs into a Drive folder required standing up a Dataverse instance. The three destinations are now independent, and the route writes to whichever are live, reporting `writtenTo` positively rather than leaving a reader to infer it from which result fields happen to be null.

**"Enabled" is decided by ANY of a destination's own settings being present, then validated.** That ordering is load-bearing: if enabled-but-incomplete reported *"disabled"* instead, one typo'd variable name would silently stop every document reaching that destination — the same class of silent failure being fixed. Partial configuration now throws, naming the destination and the missing variables and never echoing a value.

An **empty** environment is also refused: an ingest with no destination at all still returned 200 and still wrote an audit row saying the document was handled.

### 3. The readiness report no longer keeps its own copy of the truth

`pilotOpsReadiness.ts` mirrored the required-variable list with a comment admitting the hazard — *"if document-intake/config.ts adds a required variable, add it here too"* — and **it had already drifted**: it checked ten credentials and neither folder id, so it answered "document ingest: configured" for a pipeline whose Drive destination was blank.

It now calls `describeDocumentIngestDestinations()` with the same env it was handed, and reports per-destination `enabled` / `ready` / `missing` instead of one all-or-nothing boolean.

One design decision worth surfacing: `missing` is **empty for a destination nobody switched on**, so `missing.length > 0` is a reliable signal of a real problem. Listing every variable for a deliberately-off destination would make "off on purpose" and "broken" look identical to any caller checking that field.

## A second instance of the same pattern, flagged not fixed

You asked me to say so if I found another place reporting "configured" without checking the thing it configures. I did:

**`isVideoScanConfigured()` (`videoScanPolicy.ts:99`) returns true from the flags alone.** Setting `PPBF_VIDEO_CONTENT_SCAN=vision` makes the readiness report say `videoScan: enabled, "Configured gate(s): content"` — but `runContentScreen()` (`videoScan.ts:124`) starts with `if (!isFilmStudyVisionConfigured()) return null`, and that requires a vision deployment name plus `AZURE_AI_ENDPOINT` and `AZURE_AI_KEY`. With the flag set and those absent, no verdict can ever be produced and **every quarantined video stays quarantined forever**, while the readiness endpoint reports the gate as configured.

It is meaningfully less severe than the Drive defect — it fails *closed* (videos stay quarantined rather than being wrongly promoted, and `videoScan.ts` reasons explicitly about not spinning the worker). But an operator debugging "why does nothing promote?" is told the gate is configured. Left for its own bounded PR rather than widened into this one.

Worth noting the counter-example too: **`getAzureAiRuntimeConfig()` does this correctly** — all-required check, a `missing` array, and only the API *version* has a default. My config now mirrors that shape rather than inventing a new one.

## Evidence

- [x] `npm run typecheck` — clean.
- [x] `npm run lint` — 0 errors (11 pre-existing warnings, none in touched files).
- [x] `npm test` — **469 suites / 5819 tests passed.** (Note: the warned-about mass failure did not reproduce in this container — the full suite ran clean.)
- [x] `npm run build` — succeeds.
- [x] Affected suites verified **individually** per the repo trap, plus both named guards: `config.test.ts`, `googleDrive.test.ts`, `pilotOpsReadiness.test.ts`, `ops/readiness/route.test.ts`, `designSystemClasses.test.ts`, `gymTimeDrift.test.ts` — 6 suites / 51 tests passed.
- [ ] `npm run test:migrations` — **not run: N/A.** No SQL or persistence code changed.
- [x] Behavior probe — 16 new tests. `config.test.ts` pins: a blank *and* whitespace-only folder id is not ready; `getPipelineConfig` throws naming the variable without echoing a value; each destination stands alone (Drive-only, Dataverse-only, SharePoint-only); partial config throws; an empty environment is refused; a disabled destination reports `missing: []`; an optional setting alone still counts as intent. `googleDrive.test.ts` pins the upload guard, its message explaining the consequence, and that **the folder check runs before the service-account parse** so a deployment missing both reports the one that loses files.

**Migrated pin:** `pilotOpsReadiness.test.ts` previously asserted `ingest.enabled === true` for ten credentials and no folder ids. That test pinned the defect, not the contract. Its credentials are unchanged, its expectation corrected, and a new case shows what a genuinely ready pipeline looks like. A new test also asserts no credential value can reach the readiness report, since that report is served over HTTP.

## Scope declaration

- Contested files (guardrails §3) touched: **none.**
- Safety invariants (§4) affected: **none weakened; two strengthened.** A document can no longer be reported as ingested when it went nowhere retrievable, and the readiness report can no longer claim a destination is configured when it has nowhere to write.
- **Nothing configured or deployed.** None of these variables appear in `infra/main.bicep`; ingest is off in production. This makes the system honest about a feature that would silently lose files if switched on — Ops remains human-gated.
- Did not touch: `app/coach/floor-groups`, `app/coach/behavior-standards`, `src/server/pilot/floorGroups.ts`, `src/server/pilot/behaviorStandards.ts`, `src/server/pilot/passbook.ts` (#411), `pilot.attendance` / `pilot.scheduler_attendance` (#409), `docs/research/**`, `docs/current/SIGN_OFF_GUIDE.md`, `docs/design/TEST_PIN_MAP.md`.

## Out of scope / not done

- **The video-scan gate defect above is flagged, not fixed.** Different subsystem, fails closed, deserves its own PR.
- **No deployment or configuration of any ingest variable.** Ops lane, human-gated.
- **`writtenTo` is not yet surfaced in any UI.** The route returns it and the audit row records it; no admin surface reads it. Whether an operator should see per-document delivery is a product decision, not a config fix.
- **Mock mode still fabricates all three destination results** even when only one is configured. It is an explicit override that writes nothing anywhere, so it cannot lose a file, but the shape it returns no longer matches what a real partial pi

author: tytremblay
body:
Companion to FRC2713/hawk-bot#23. Two problems on this side, both of which
present as "hawk-bot can't access Google Calendar".

## The credential was wired into the Actions path only

`b430093` added `HAWK_BOT_GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_KEY_BASE64` to
`docker-compose.yml`, `.env.example`, and `deploy.yml` — but not to `setup.sh`,
not to `hawk-deploy`, and not to CI.

- **`setup.sh`** never prompted for or wrote it, so a first-run install
  produced a `.env` without it and hawk-bot restarted in a loop — its config
  schema has no default. Now prompted, written, and a blank one is called out
  explicitly at the end rather than left to be discovered as a crash loop.
- **`hawk-deploy`** didn't require it, even though it is the end that actually
  writes `.env` and already guards the other two required credentials.
- **CI** didn't set it in the compose fixture and asserted nothing about it,
  which is how it reached `main` unplumbed in the first place. Now asserted in
  both directions: it lands in hawk-bot's environment unprefixed, and it does
  *not* land in hawk-mod's.

Like `HAWK_BOT_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, it's required but deliberately **not**
compared against the host's — it's a read-only key on a service account and
nothing stored depends on it, so re-issuing one shouldn't block a deploy. CI
now tests that it stays rotatable, so it doesn't get conflated with
`TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY` later.

## The docs described a bot that no longer exists

hawk-bot renamed its slash command to `/hawkbot` and its setting to
`team_meeting_calendar_id` (migration `0008`). This repo still said:

```
/hawk config set google_calendar_id <id>
```

Both halves are wrong. A mentor following our own instructions gets "unknown
command", then "unknown setting" — and reasonably concludes the calendar
integration is broken when nothing is actually wrong with it. Fixed across
`.env.example`, `docker-compose.yml`, `README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`,
`docs/deploy-linode.md`, and `docs/continuous-deployment.md`.

## And the part this repo cannot check

Holding the credential is not the same as having access. Three things have to
be true on Google's side — Calendar API enabled in the service account's Cloud
project, each calendar shared with the account's own address at "See all event
details", and the calendar ids set from Slack. Miss any one and the symptom is
identical. `docs/deploy-linode.md` now spells that out and points at
`/hawkbot calendar`, which after hawk-bot#23 distinguishes all three.

## Testing

Ran the full CI job locally rather than trusting it: `shellcheck` on all four
scripts, `docker compose config` with the new fixture plus every grep and the
Python cross-wiring assertions, the blank-`DOMAIN` guard, all six
`hawk-deploy` refusal/rotation cases against a temp `STACK_DIR`, the
`.env.example` sync check, and YAML validity for `ci.yml` and `cloud-init.yaml`.

## One manual step

`hawk-deploy` lives outside the checkout by design, so its new required-check
does not take effect until it is reinstalled to `/usr/local/bin/hawk-deploy` on
the host. `deploy.yml` enforces the same thing on the near end meanwhile, so
nothing is blocked — the reinstall can happen whenever.

## Merge order

FRC2713/hawk-bot#23 first, so the image is published, then this, then dispatch
a deploy.

Closes #122

스킬 11개 중 `memory-factcheck` 과 `session-recording` 두 개만 Agent Adapter 가 없었다. **둘을 같이 처리하지 않는다** — 성격이 다르다.

## `memory-factcheck` — 만든다

경계가 뚜렷한 감사 작업이다. 메모리를 읽고, 근거와 대조하고, 교정안과 아카이브 후보를 보고하면 끝난다. 컨텍스트를 많이 먹고 본 대화와 섞이면 방해되는 종류라 오히려 위임이 어울린다.

claude/codex/antigravity 3종 + 루트 심링크 2개.

## `session-recording` — 만들지 않는다

이 스킬은 한 번의 작업이 아니라 **세션을 소유**한다.

- `whisper-stream` 과 `ffmpeg` 를 백그라운드로 몇 시간 살려 둔다
- 10분 간격 요약 루프를 건다
- 진행 중에 "중간 요약", "녹음종료" 같은 대화형 트리거를 받는다

한 턴에 끝나고 사라지는 위임형 에이전트는 이 중 어느 것도 유지할 수 없다. 어댑터를 만들면 **호출은 되는데 동작하지 않는 입구**가 생긴다 — 없는 것보다 나쁘다.

커버리지 숫자를 맞추려고 채워 넣지 않도록 AGENTS.md 에 판단 근거를 남겼다.

## 만들다가 잡은 결함 — 생성기가 깨진 TOML 을 뱉는다

`codex.toml` 의 `description` 은 TOML basic string 인데, `memory-factcheck` 의 설명은 트리거 발화를 큰따옴표로 인용한다.

```
description: ... 또는 "메모리 정리해줘 / 감사해줘"(clean up / audit my memory) 요청에 사용한다.
```

이스케이프하지 않으면:

```
tomllib.TOMLDecodeError: Expected newline or end of document after a statement (at line 2, column 196)
```

어댑터가 통째로 죽는다. **`new_skill.sh` 도 같은 방식이었다** — 따옴표를 쓰는 설명으로 스킬을 만들면 처음부터 깨진 어댑터가 나온다. 생성기에서 `"` 와 `\` 를 이스케이프한다.

## `tests/test_new_skill.py` 추가

생성기 자체를 검증한다. 스크립트만 임시 디렉터리로 복사해 그곳을 `REPO_ROOT` 로 삼아 돌리므로 저장소를 더럽히지 않는다.

- 따옴표·역슬래시가 든 설명으로 만든 `codex.toml` 이 파싱되고 원문이 보존되는가
- `claude.md` · `antigravity.md` 의 frontmatter 가 깨지지 않는가 (agy 는 깨진 frontmatter 를 조용히 무시한다 — #110)
- `SKILL.md` frontmatter 가 `name`·`description` 두 개뿐인가
- 루트 심링크가 스킬 원본을 가리키는가
- kebab-case 아닌 이름을 거부하는가

이스케이프를 되돌리면 `TOMLDecodeError` 로 실패하는 것을 확인했다.

## 뺀 것

`codex.toml` 의 description 이 `SKILL.md` 와 같아야 한다는 검사를 넣었다가 **뺐다.** `doksam-ui`·`mobile-web-planner`·`nextjs-implementer` 는 스킬 설명이 아니라 에이전트 역할("UX/UI 수석 기획자")을 적고 있고, 에이전트 선택 관점에서 그게 더 낫다. 과잉 제약이었다 — 파싱 검사만으로 이번 결함은 이미 잡힌다.

## 확인

```
./scripts/run_tests.sh   전부 통과 (루트 11 → 16)
./install.sh --with-agent → Antigravity 에이전트 9 → 10개
```

Made with [Orca](https://github.com/stablyai/orca) 🐋

author: caique-veiga
body:
📌 Summary
Integra detecção de objetos (YOLO/COCO), posição espacial, cor predominante e a montagem do Scene JSON estruturado ao pipeline de visão computacional do backend — a base completa para alimentar a futura VLM.

🛠️ Key Changes
Detecção de objetos: ObjectDetector (protocol) + YOLOObjectDetector (Ultralytics YOLOv8n, CPU-only) — traduz resultados do YOLO em Detection (object_id, class_id, class_name, confidence, bbox) sem vazar tipos da lib para o domínio. Modelo/threshold configuráveis via YOLO_MODEL/YOLO_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD.
Posição espacial: PositionAnalyzer (domain service) — mapeia o centro do bbox em um grid 3x3 (horizontal, vertical, region), sem inferir distância/GPS/profundidade.
Cor predominante: ColorAnalyzer (protocol) + OpenCVColorAnalyzer — recorta o bbox, classifica em HSV entre 12 cores, com mitigação de fundo (inset) e classificação por votação de pixels.
Scene JSON: SceneBuilder (domain service) monta um Scene (scene_id, conversation_id, image, model, objects) a partir de detecções já enriquecidas com posição e cor; SceneSchema (Pydantic) serializa no formato definido no contexto do projeto, incluindo a chave reservada class, de forma determinística.
Validação com imagens reais (scripts manuais, sem mocks): scripts/validate_yolo.py e scripts/validate_color_analyzer.py rodam o pipeline real contra imagens fornecidas e salvam crops + JSON de resultados.
Dependências: ultralytics, torch/torchvision (CPU-only, via índice dedicado do PyTorch — evita puxar CUDA), opencv-python, plugin pydantic.mypy.
✅ Quality Checks Executed
 pytest (100 testes passando — detecção, posição, cor e pipeline completo, todos com mocks/imagens sintéticas, sem depender de GPU)
 ruff (lint + format)
 mypy --strict

author: mirek
body:
Encode only own enumerable properties in the JSON object coder

The Object coder walked keys with for...in, so inherited enumerable keys
were treated as data: an inherited tag-like key (or one added to
Object.prototype) made every plain-object encode throw, and an inherited
encodable value leaked into the output as an own key, unlike
JSON.stringify. Iterate Object.keys in both encode and decode so only own
keys are considered; decode is aligned as well so a polluted prototype
is never walked over parsed input.

Addresses the following review comment(s) left on earlier PRs (each verified as a real, still-present defect on `main`; the added test fails without the fix):
- https://github.com/mirek/prelude/pull/90#discussion_r3789988414 (PR #90, `packages/json/src/coders/object.ts`)

body: 填表批量不再按「有几张图」分路。一张只是例子，图多图少都走同一套规则。 **有图的行（三选一）：** - **原图上架** — 已经能用的实拍，有几张用几张 - **原图留下，再补转化位（推荐）** — 实拍不动，缺的白底主图 / 细节 / 使用 / 外箱由平台补，补的标黄 - **当参考，重画转化套图** — 图太乱时用。原图只认货，6 张重画并标黄 **没图的行（二选一）：** - 按品名画套图并标黄 - 跳过 同一张表可以混着有图、没图、图多、图少。生成图一律不冒充实拍。 **选类目：** 树是国际站官方全部分类（`/icbu/product/category/get`），所有店铺一级一样。没有官方「类目历史」接口；选择器顶部会列出这家店已经上过的叶子（从本地草稿/模板汇总，打开选择器时不再卡 `product.list`），点一下就能选定。 **店铺默认（对照官方）：** 官方后台没有「整店填一套就套所有货」。运费模板在店里建、发品时每条引用；包装 / 单位 / 交期官方是按每条货填，批量改也是一条一条改。本页拆成「整店通用」（产地、付款、样品）和「跟货走的兜底」（包装、单位、运费、交期）。成稿顺序：这类目自己的习惯 → 整店兜底 → 这一行（短表/草稿）覆盖。能从在线商品回读的会先拉过来，用户改过的不覆盖。 **两层表格，不是 7521 张填空：** - **你填的短表：** 按品类家族加规格列（彩铅出色数/硬度，刷具出尺寸/材质），大概十来种，不是七千张官方表。 - **官方必填：** 选了叶子之后出现在「AI 填」和核对页，按 `schema.get` 来，每个叶子可以不一样。不抄进填写表。 **填完短表不能撒手。** 导入后 AI 会成稿，但每条还要打开看标题和官方属性，点「审过了」才能发。选错但合法的选项（HB 写成 2B）红线拦不住，只能人看出来。重新成稿或改类目会清掉已审。手改过的字段不会被 AI 盖掉。不能保证 AI 零出错。 侧栏可收起展开。156 个单元测试通过。

author: szechunyiu
body:
## Goal
Push Phase 2 from a set of runnable components to an ordered, artifact-driven closure campaign. This PR still does **not** claim external empirical evidence exists.

## New execution surfaces
- `AuthorityTrialRunner` + exact ten frozen authority attack specs:
  - host-owned attack executor and separately controlled protected evaluator;
  - exact subject/execution/evaluator/epoch bindings;
  - independent producer/evaluator lineages;
  - evaluator frozen before candidate + fresh split;
  - candidate authority increase / false promotion are blocking;
  - A10 explicitly requires the safe `CANNOT_CHECK` behavior.
- `ShadowDevelopmentTrialRunner`:
  - starts only from a real observed failure with immutable failure episodes;
  - requires at least two competing cause hypotheses and discriminator-backed attribution;
  - preserves observed-failure-before-discriminator and discriminator-before-candidate chronology;
  - requires candidate execution/protected change control rather than a research-only stop;
  - records the intervention back onto the persistent `DevelopmentIssue` and preserves failed/harmful alternative IDs;
  - improvement is not preordained, but self-merge is always forbidden.
- `Phase2CampaignEvidence` / `assess_phase2_campaign`:
  - enforces the non-skippable sequence `BIND_EXTERNALS -> LIVE_TRIAL -> SHADOW_DEVELOPMENT -> AUTHORITY_TRIAL -> EXTERNAL_HANDOFF -> READY_FOR_TERMINAL_AUDIT`;
  - checks frozen packet identity, raw-search retention, resource parity, negative-history recordability, baseline bundle identity, development/evaluator binding, all ten attacks, correct CANNOT_CHECK, false-promotion count, and independent external receipt consistency;
  - requires six independent Phase-2 observations: live trial, matched baseline, Shadow development, authority battery, failure replay, final integration;
  - also requires a non-empty paper-level `ExternalEvidenceManifest.v1` bound to the same subject/evaluator/epoch.
- canonical persistence for authority/development/campaign reports and a content-addressed `Phase2ExternalObservationBundle.v1`.
- detailed host campaign runbook.

## Authority boundary
`READY_FOR_TERMINAL_AUDIT` is not `PHASE_2_SHADOW_SELF_ORION_CLOSED`. All new reports expose `grants_phase2_closure=False` and `grants_governed_self_orion=False`. Final closure remains a host/external audit over actual real-provider/evaluator receipts.

## Tests
Hostile tests cover exact ten-attack execution, self-evaluation rejection, false promotion, observed-failure/discriminator chronology, negative-history intervention recording, ordered campaign progression, counts-only trace rejection, self-verified external evidence rejection, and content-addressed observation-bundle tamper detection.

Merge only on exact green head.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches authority boundaries, evaluator independence, and change-control gates for self-modification research; logic is heavily tested and fail-closed, but mistakes could weaken closure guarantees.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds an **ordered, fail-closed Phase-2 closure campaign** on top of existing preflight/live-trial pieces: new runners, `assess_phase2_campaign`, JSON persistence, a host runbook, and unit tests. The PR still does **not** assert that external empirical evidence exists.
> 
> **Authority battery** — `AuthorityTrialRunner` runs ten frozen `FROZEN_AUTHORITY_ATTACKS` via host `AuthorityAttackExecutor` and protected `ProtectedAuthorityEvaluator`, with SHA-256 bindings, independent producer/evaluator lineages, and blockers for self-evaluation, authority increase, and false promotion (including A10 `CANNOT_CHECK`).
> 
> **Shadow development trial** — `ShadowDevelopmentTrialRunner` drives a `FrozenObservedFailureCase` through `ShadowSelfDrivingController`: real observed failures only, competing causes, discriminator chronology, protected change control (not research-only), intervention recording on `DevelopmentIssue`, and **self-merge always forbidden**.
> 
> **Campaign assessment** — `Phase2CampaignEvidence` + `assess_phase2_campaign` enforce a non-skippable stage chain through external handoff to `READY_FOR_TERMINAL_AUDIT`, checking packet identity, raw-search retention, baseline hash, development/authority bindings, all ten attacks, six uniquely bound independent external observations, and a bound `ExternalEvidenceManifest`. All new reports hard-code `grants_phase2_closure=False` and `grants_governed_self_orion=False`.
> 
> **Artifacts** — `phase2_campaign_io` writes/loads versioned schemas (including content-addressed observation bundles); `__init__.py` re-exports the new API; `PHASE2_CAMPAIGN_RUNBOOK_V1.md` documents the host workflow.
>

author: kudanulafaa-zahab
body:
## The screen

Ali photographed SO-2026-117. Two adjacent lines:

> ✓ **Paid in full**  *(green, with a tick)*
> Paid MVR 0 of MVR 207

He sold 1 pack of nappies, the customer rejected it at the door without paying, and it came back opened and unsellable. He recorded the return correctly. The app awarded him a green tick for money that never existed — and because he could not make the screen agree, he went and marked the order delivered by hand, which is the action that produced the screen above.

## Everything underneath was right

Worth stating, because it bounds the fix: the balance was MVR 0, the opened pack correctly did **not** go back into sellable stock, and `get_pnl` already reversed the MVR 207 of revenue while keeping the MVR 126 of cost as the loss it is. No money was misreported. The defect was the **word**, which turned out to be load-bearing in four places.

## 1. A return was counted as money

`recalculate_order_payment_status` added the returned amount to the paid amount and called the total `'paid'`. Cash arriving and goods coming back both leave nothing to collect, and they are not the same event. In ordinary accounts an invoice closed by a credit note is **settled**; calling it paid makes "how much did we actually collect this month" unanswerable.

New state vocabulary:

| | meaning |
|---|---|
| `pending` | nothing in, nothing back |
| `partial` | some of it settled |
| `paid` | **the customer's money** covered the invoice |
| `settled` | **new** — nothing left to collect, because goods came back |
| `credit` | more was taken than kept; money owed *back* |
| `cod` / `deposited` | cash-handling states, untouched |

`'paid'` now requires `paid >= total`. If a return was needed to close it, it is `settled`.

## 2. The buttons on his screen were dead, and lying about why

`void_sales_order` and `delete_sales_order` both refused with *"payment already settled"* on an order nobody had paid. Both already carried the correct guard four lines below (real money in the payments ledger), so the flag test contributed nothing but a false reason.

It is replaced by a guard that is true and is about **stock**: an order undone by a return must not also be voided, because voiding restores the sale's `out` movements — and that pack never came back sellable. Two ways of undoing one sale, used together, invent stock.

## 3. The flag could go stale

`order_payments` has had a sync trigger since 0069. `sales_returns` never did, so the only thing keeping the flag current after a return was one hand-written call inside `record_customer_return`. A derived value with a single hand-written updater is a value that will be wrong one day. It now has the same trigger.

## 4. "Unpaid" meant three different things

Found while tracing the above, unrelated to returns:

```
get_sales_orders        payment_status in ('pending','partial')
get_sales_orders_count  payment_status not in ('paid','deposited')
get_receivables_aging   the flag AND the arithmetic
```

So the unpaid filter counted `cod` and `credit` orders in its total and then did not list them. All three now ask the ledger, which cannot drift from itself. Removing the flag from the receivables gate is safe on COD specifically: `record_cod_collection` has written the cash into `order_payments` since 0136, so a collected COD order nets to zero through the arithmetic alone.

## 5. The workflow gap that started it

The order sat on the dispatch board as still out for delivery for two days after the goods were back in the godown. An order whose every item has been returned now closes itself — `delivered` rather than `cancelled`, because the goods physically left the warehouse and a cancel would try to unwind a journey that really happened.

## On screen

`components/sales/sale-detail.tsx` → `PaymentPanel`:

- **"Returned — nothing to pay"** in neutral grey, not a green "Paid in full". Green means money earned.
- The line beneath reads **"MVR 207 returned of MVR 207"** instead of "Paid MVR 0 of MVR 207".
- The progress bar tracks `paid + returned`, so a closed order is not an empty bar under a tick.
- No "MVR 0 left" hanging off the end.

`v_order_balances` gains `returned_mvr` so that sentence is computed in Postgres rather than reconstructed from three other columns on the screen.

## Proof

- **16 pgTAP tests** (`settled_not_paid.test.sql`), each proven to fail against **seven** deliberate mutations: the old paid/settled conflation, the dropped trigger, both destructive guards, the auto-close made inert and then made too eager, and the unpaid count put back on its own definition.
- **A new browser audit** (`audit:returned`) that rebuilds his exact case — unpaid order, full return, pack not restocked — and reads the rendered screen. Proven to fail: forcing `isSettled = false` put the green tick back and took 2 of its 9 checks down.

## Gate

- 285 pgTAP tests on a fresh replay of every migration
- 17 browser audits
- `tsc --noEmit`, `eslint`, `next build` clean

Migration 0185 is already applied to production; SO-2026-117 now reads delivered · settled · MVR 207 returned · nothing owed, and the unpaid list and its count agree (MVR 1,030 across 2 customers).

Round-49 adversarial review against round-48 HEAD. Three concrete fixes, two architectural deferrals.

- **avc — relative PATH names** (`avc.go`): `type=PATH` `name=` can be relative with the cwd in a sibling `type=CWD` record. body:
## What

Extends the SDK with the resources and options required by the upcoming Capawesome MCP server.

**Client configuration**

- New `fetch` option (`fetch?: typeof fetch`), used for all requests and defaulting to `globalThis.fetch`. This lets consumers plug in their own `fetch` implementation. The package stays dependency-free.

**New resources**

- `client.organizations` — `list()`, `get()`, `create()`, `update()`
  - `.members` — `list()`, `delete()`
  - `.invitations` — `list()`, `create()`, `delete()`
  - `.licenseKeys` — `list()`, `get()`, `create()`, `update()`, `delete()`, `rotate()`
  - `.teams` — `list()`, `get()`, `create()`, `update()`, `delete()` plus `.apps` and `.members` (`list()`/`create()`/`delete()`)
  - `.gitConnections` — `list()`, `get()`, `create()`, `update()`, `delete()`, `listRepositories()`, `listNamespaces()`
- `client.apps.configurations` — `list()`, `get()`, `create()`, `update()`, `delete()`
- `client.apps.repository` — `get()`, `set()`, `delete()`
- `client.users` — `me()`
- `client.jobs` — added `getFailureSummary()` and `cancel()`

**Other additions to existing resources**

- Exact `name` filters on `apps.list()`, `organizations.teams.list()`, `apps.environments.list()` and `apps.automations.list()`.
- `apps.builds.create()` gains `appConfigurationId`/`appConfigurationName`; `apps.automations` create/update gain `appConfigurationId` and the `app*Name` reference alternatives; `jobs.list()` accepts multiple `status` values.
- `delete()` by name (in addition to id) for `apps.channels`, `apps.destinations`, `apps.configurations`, `apps.environments` and `apps.certificates`; certificate/destination name-deletes take `platform` (and `type`) discriminators so exactly one row is targeted.

Response types follow the existing convention of exposing only the most relevant properties. Credentials accepted by the API (Git tokens/passwords, invitation tokens) are request-only and are not part of any response type.

## Notes

- `client.organizations.get()` and `client.organizations.licenseKeys.get()` target `GET /v1/organizations/:organizationId` and `GET /v1/organizations/:organizationId/license-keys/:licenseKeyId`, which are being added in a parallel API pull request. They are the only methods here without a released endpoint yet.
- `teams.update()` resolves to `void` because the endpoint responds with `204 No Content`.
- Relations are exposed as boolean options (`includeApps`, `includeMembers`, `includePackages`) instead of raw relation strings.
- **Versioning:** this pull request contains only additive, non-breaking changes (verified against the published `0.1.2` type declarations: no removed/renamed exports, no dropped or retyped params, no changed return types — only additions and widenings such as `required → optional` and `single → union`). It is therefore released as a **patch, `0.1.3`**, under the repository's `bump-patch-for-minor-pre-major` Release Please convention. The branch carries no version bump and no `Release-As` override, so Release Please derives `0.1.3` organically from the `feat`/`fix` commits. Nothing is published from this pull request.

## Testing

- `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build` — pass
- `npm test` — 39 tests pass
