author: mirek
body:
Give wrapped iterators %IteratorPrototype% so iterator helpers keep working

Wrap plain iterators without Proxy invariants and keep them closed

`generator` proxied the source iterator itself, so for a frozen iterator
or one with a non-configurable `next` the Proxy `get` invariant rejected
the bound method and `[...gen]` threw. The synthesized `return`/`throw`
also reported `done` without remembering it, so a later `next()` kept
yielding source values. Replace the Proxy with a plain wrapper object
that forwards `next`/`return`/`throw`, and track a closed flag so that
after `return()`/`throw()` (synthesized or forwarded and done) `next()`
returns `{ done: true, value: undefined }` like a real generator.

Addresses the following review comment(s) left on earlier PRs (each verified as a real, still-present defect on `main`; the added test fails without the fix):
- https://github.com/mirek/prelude/pull/20#discussion_r3789391737 (PR #20, `packages/generator/src/generator.ts`)
- https://github.com/mirek/prelude/pull/111#discussion_r3790168958 (PR #111, `packages/generator/src/generator.ts`)

Refs #68 — closes the last four implementable stories.

## Summary
Audit goes to **108 checks**: desktop **105 pass / 0 fail / 3 skip**, mobile **93 pass / 0 fail / 5 skip**.

The four remaining stories were all blocked on the same thing: verifying them honestly meant doing something to the live server, the shared agent, or the machine's Tailscale config that an audit has no business doing. Isolated dependencies unblock all four without touching any of it.

## `startIsolatedServer()`
A throwaway server with its own database, port and scripted agent. It imports the built server directly rather than shelling out to the CLI, because **the CLI hard-codes `~/.argusde/argusde.sqlite`** — an isolated instance must never touch the real database.

| Story | How it's now verified |
|---|---|
| **US-4.6** | The fixture asks for permission **and echoes the outcome back**, so this proves the *chosen option reached the agent* — not merely that the prompt disappeared. Prompt, both options, a11y scan, and resolution all asserted. |
| **US-7.3** | An agent-driven `current_mode_update` lands live (`default -> plan`), no refresh. The one mode path `AcpSession` can't synthesize, since it isn't answering a client request. |
| **US-4.3** | An agent that dies mid-turn is reflected in the connection banner, rather than leaving the user waiting on a reply that will never come. Own server, since killing the agent ends that server's usefulness. |
| **US-11.1** | QR code and MagicDNS URL verified against a **stub `tailscale` on PATH** answering the three queries `cli.ts` makes. |

## Why a stub for US-11.1, not the real thing
The machine's tailnet already has a mapping on the live port, so the server correctly takes its skip-to-avoid-overwriting branch — the real path is unreachable without mutating your `tailscale serve` config. The stub exercises **ArgusDE's own output logic**, which is the part under test.

Verified afterwards that nothing real changed: all three pre-existing mappings intact, live server still reachable over Tailscale (200), `command -v tailscale` → `/usr/bin/tailscale`.

The QR assertion checks for half-block glyphs, not just the URL — that's what makes it *scannable* rather than the address echoed twice.

## Supporting changes
- `fake-agent-cli.mjs` gains `permission-request`, `autonomous-mode-change` and `exit` steps.
- `spawnAgentProcessTransport` accepts `env`, so a fixture agent can be scripted per session — documented as *replacing* rather than extending the environment, since that's how `spawn` treats it.

## The three remaining skips
Not gaps: each has a dedicated unit test asserting the same thing more directly — US-2.8 and US-5.6 (`ws-server.test.ts`), US-1.5 (`electron-connect-screen.test.ts`). Re-driving them through a browser would cost a live agent session or a flaky race for no added signal.

## Test plan
- [x] **TDD, red first** — the `env` passthrough test timed out before the change
- [x] `pnpm run typecheck`, `pnpm run build` — clean
- [x] **`xvfb-run -a pnpm run test` — 288 passed, 26/26 files**
- [x] Audit desktop **105 pass / 0 fail / 3 skip**, mobile **93 pass / 0 fail / 5 skip**
- [x] Live server untouched: project count 5 → 5, zero stray `/tmp` fixtures, Tailscale config verified unchanged

author: rubenvdlinde
body:
> Corrects a false equivalence I asserted and then relied on. Answers "did we
> properly document setting up Euro-Office?" — **no. We documented ONLYOFFICE and
> called it Euro-Office. Then we actually installed Euro-Office.**

## What happened

The portability work ran `onlyoffice/documentserver` and labelled it
**"Euro-Office / ONLYOFFICE"** throughout the setup doc, the compose file, the specs
and the PR text. **At that point Euro-Office had never been installed, started or
probed.**

The justification I wrote for the substitution was:

> *"Euro-Office is the ONLYOFFICE fork … It is **API-compatible** with ONLYOFFICE
> Document Server, which is what the overlay runs — the upstream image is public,
> **the consortium build is not separately published for local development**."*

The first half came from **ADR-087 — which I wrote in this same programme the day
before.** The second half I wrote here, from nothing: there is no source for
"API-compatible" and none for "not separately published". It exists to bridge the gap
between what was asked for and what I could pull, and it reads exactly like a fact.

So the shape of the error is worth naming: **a claim was introduced in an ADR, then
cited as the authority for a substitution the same programme was making.** Nobody
checked, because it looked already checked.

## Corrected

The second half of "not separately published" turned out to be checkable, and false.
`ghcr.io/euro-office/documentserver` exists, so the substitution was never necessary —
the suite was pulled, started and verified on its own image, with its own connector
app and its own container.

| Suite | Sidecar | Status |
|---|---|---|
| ONLYOFFICE | `docudesk-onlyoffice` :8092 | installed, configured, **verified end to end** |
| **Euro-Office** | `docudesk-eurooffice` :8093 | **installed, configured, verified on its own image** — anchor round-trip and chart fidelity NOT repeated here |
| Collabora Online | `docudesk-collabora` :9980 | installed, configured, **verified end to end** |
| LibreOffice | `docudesk-libreoffice` :8094 | **converter only** — no WOPI, no editor; verified as a converter |

- One page per suite under `docs/office-suites/`, each recording its own run. Nothing
  on one page is evidence for another.
- **The WOPI-disabled finding is re-attributed** to the image it was measured on. It
  was a real measurement *of ONLYOFFICE* credited to Euro-Office. Euro-Office's own
  `wopi.enable: false` default was then measured separately, on Euro-Office.
- **A new requirement makes the rule explicit**: a suite may be a portability *target*
  freely, but may not be called supported until that product has been run; a
  measurement is attributed to the suite it was taken on; and *a document may not
  serve as its own evidence*.
- `occ docudesk:office:probe` — the verification command the setup guide already told
  operators to run, and which **did not exist** — now exists, probes each suite
  separately, and prints one line per suite so no suite's result can be read off
  another's.

### What is still NOT verified on Euro-Office

Anchor stability across a Euro-Office save, and chart-rendering fidelity. Both were
measured on ONLYOFFICE only and do not transfer. Recorded as such in
`docs/office-suites/eurooffice.md` and in the spec.

## What survives unchanged

The **format-independence** claim. ODF/OOXML editing happens in-package with no suite
in the call path, and that is tested by `SuiteIndependenceTest`. It was never a claim
that a second suite had been exercised — that part was my labelling, not the
architecture.

## Note on this description

An earlier revision of this PR body said Euro-Office was "not installed, not
configured, not verified" and quoted a status table that two later commits had already
replaced. **The description had become the thing it was written to correct**: text
reporting something other than what was run. It is corrected here rather than left,
and the spec paragraph that still read "never installed or run" is corrected with it.

## Three PR-owned reds, cleared

1. **`info.xml` failed Nextcloud schema validation.** `info.xsd` fixes child order and
   `<commands>` was written after `<navigations>`. The misplaced element is the one
   registering `docudesk:office:probe` — the change that finally shipped the promised
   verification step shipped it in a position that stopped the app validating.
2. **Coverage ratchet: −5.05 %, +56 statements.** The ratchet was right: 56 statements
   were added with nothing reaching them. 15 real tests now cover them (probe
   discovery: served / unnamed app / 404 / 200-login-page / no-actions / transport
   failure / unconfigured; the command: registered name, per-suite absent-and-why,
   available, second path tried, `--suite`, and — the one that matters — ONLYOFFICE
   answering leaving `eurooffice` absent). Reproduced locally against the same merge
   base: the same +56, 42/99 → 98/99, and the pre-fix clover still fails the guard.
3. **gate-16:** `configure()` and `execute()` now carry `@spec` tags pointing at
   requirements that exist; checked against gate-46, which was first shown to reject an
   invented anchor.

The **E2E red was inherited**, not PR-owned: the branch predated #633, whose batch-state
persistence fix is what turns the `batch/{id}/extract` 404 into a 200.
`origin/development` is merged in rather than the job rerun.

1468 tests, 0 failures locally on the merged tree. phpcs 0 errors, phpmd 0, psalm 0
errors, phpstan `[OK]` over 244 files.

author: gfx
body:
A malformed template string says what is wrong with it, and the shape template
expansion emits is named in one place per fact rather than spelled out on both
sides of the pipeline.

## Diagnostics

A format specifier is a closed grammar, parsed by `format_spec`:

```text
SPEC := [[fill] align] ['+'] ['#'] ['0'] [width] ['.' precision] [kind]
kind := 'b' | 'o' | 'x' | 'X' | 'e' | 'E' | 'f' | '?'
```

Anything outside it is a syntax error pointing at the offending character, so
`${n:zz}`, `${n:%}`, `${n:5:8}` and the printf-ism `${n:08d}` name their
problem instead of formatting as a bare `${n}`. `f` is fixed-point — the same
rendering as a bare precision, so `${x:.2f}` reads as a float format — and is
now in the WEP's table alongside the rest. Whitespace around the specifier is
trimmed as it already is around the expression, so `${ x : 5 }` reads as
`${x:5}`.

A malformed escape inside a template names itself, as it does in a plain
string: string, char and template literals share one escape scanner, which
stops at the first character that cannot belong to the escape rather than
consuming past the literal's closing delimiter.

The empty-specifier and empty-interpolation errors span the text they blame —
the offending character and the `${` respectively.

Interpolating a type that has no `Display` reports:

```
error: type `P` does not implement trait `Display`;
       use `${x:?}` for debug output, or add an `impl Display`
```

The suggestion in that message is written in Wado's interpolation syntax, so
typing it works.

## The `__tmpl` contract

`synthesis::template` emits a labeled block that `optimize::tmpl_hoist` matches
back apart, which is why `optimize::const_branch_prune` holds that block
un-flattened until the fixpoint ends. Every name the two sides share is
single-sourced:

- the label, through `name::is_template_block`. A label cannot start with `__`
  in source, so a synthesised block is the only thing wearing one.
- the stdlib symbols, through `CompilerItem` — including a new
  `string_with_capacity` item.
- `String`'s fields through `SeqField`, `Formatter`'s through a new
  `FormatterField` whose order is checked against the Wado declaration at
  startup. Its two sentinels are the one thing repeated in Rust, and the e2e
  fixture `template_formatter_sentinels.wado` renders through the path that
  uses them.

Template expansion walks TIR through `TirOptVisitor`, whose walk is exhaustive
over `TirExprKind`, so a template under any node is expanded — reaching
`lower::translate` unexpanded is an `unreachable!`, not a diagnostic.

## Structure

`format_spec` owns the grammar, the parsed `TemplateFormatSpec`, and its
rendering back to source. `FormatKind` and `Align` replace the raw `type_char`
/ `align` characters, which turns the trait selection in synthesis into one
table lookup and lets the `Formatter` literal be built from `FormatterField`'s
order rather than hand-written field indices. Reify asserts the escape-decoding
invariant its eligibility gate already guarantees.

body:
## Ticket
FEAT-001a

## Summary
- Solución completa desde cero: backend .NET 8 por capas (Domain/Application/Infrastructure/Api) + frontend Angular 18 (NgModules) + SQL Server dockerizado con TDE
- Endpoint `POST /api/organizadores/registro`: valida CUIT (dígito verificador), teléfono, password (política de Identity), mail (unicidad); rate limiting 5 req/min/IP
- Formulario reactivo con validación cliente espejo + manejo de error por campo, coexistiendo con interceptor HTTP genérico
- Stack completo containerizado — `docker-compose up --build` deja todo operable para pruebas manuales

## Changes
- **Bloque 1** — Scaffolding backend (solución 4 proyectos, SQL Server dockerizado, Identity, migración inicial)
- **Bloque 2** — Dominio: entidad `Organizador` + validadores puros de CUIT/teléfono (100% coverage)
- **Bloque 3** — Aplicación: puerto `IIdentityGateway` + `OrganizadorService` (100% coverage)
- **Bloque 4** — API: controller, middleware de excepciones, rate limiting por IP
- **Bloque 5** — Scaffolding frontend (Angular 18, Tailwind, Material MD3 vía API Sass)
- **Bloque 6** — Formulario de registro + E2E con Playwright .NET
- **Bloque 7** — Containerización completa (Dockerfiles + docker-compose)
- Corrective loop post-VERIFY: TDE real (cifrado at-rest) + cobertura de branches del frontend a 100%
- `ADR-001`: riesgo aceptado documentado para 2 CVEs sin parche en Angular 18.x (`tar`, `@angular/core`), con ticket de seguimiento pendiente para evaluar la migración de Angular

## Tests
- Tests run: 61 passed, 61 total (43 .NET + 18 Angular)
- Coverage: backend ~97% líneas/~92% ramas (código de negocio, excluyendo migraciones); frontend 100% en las 4 métricas

## Security
- SAST: PASSED (2026-08-16) — 2 CVEs High de .NET corregidas; 2 riesgos npm (1 Critical, 1 High) aceptados formalmente vía ADR-001, sin ruta de explotación verificada en el código actual

## Attribution
AI-assisted: implementación delegada a subagentes por bloque con revisión en dos etapas (cumplimiento de spec + arquitectura) en cada uno, decisiones de diseño y de riesgo aprobadas explícitamente por el usuario en cada punto de bifurcación.

body:
Treat ask timeouts above the timer limit as no timeout

setTimeout clamps delays above 2_147_483_647ms to 1ms (with a
TimeoutOverflowWarning), so a finite ask/call timeout above that limit
rejected almost immediately. Actor.ask, RemoteActor.ask and the JSON-RPC
Client.call now only arm the timer when the timeout is finite and within
the limit; larger values mean "no timeout", as documented on the options.

Addresses the following review comment(s) left on earlier PRs (each verified as a real, still-present defect on `main`; the added test fails without the fix):
- https://github.com/mirek/prelude/pull/79#discussion_r3789897732 (PR #79, `packages/actor/src/actor.ts`)

body:
## Outcome

Make the canonical v26.9.1 crown fail closed on live release-graph and standing-evidence verification, bind black-box Crown tests to the exact checked-out subject rather than GitHub's synthetic PR merge ref, and keep the cold-cache admission gate dependency-acyclic.

## Exact subject

- Base: `c2bae4b65fc281d19cc6514fd226215126b4dbe7`
- Head: `d9537ee5db53ef788c65542b5507a5c4c6d64642`
- Branch: `agent/crown-release-evidence-gates`
- PR: #21 (draft)

## Changed files

Three authored files:

- `scripts/crown.sh`
- `apps/ecosystem-cli/tests/cli.rs`
- `scripts/cold-cache.sh`

Generated projections: none.

## Changes

- `scripts/crown.sh` executes `python3 scripts/verify_release.py --check-refs` and `python3 scripts/verify_standing_evidence.py` before Rust/build gates; `python3` is explicit admission tooling; admission JSON names `release_graph` and `standing_evidence`.
- Black-box CLI subprocess tests remove ambient `GITHUB_SHA`; under `pull_request`, that variable names GitHub's synthetic merge commit even when Actions checks out the exact candidate head.
- `scripts/cold-cache.sh` now proves clean-target full behavior only. It no longer invokes `crown --verify` before the downstream Crown job has assembled `target/crown/admission.json`. This removes a cyclic verifier dependency without weakening final Crown verification.

## Observed predecessor falsifiers

At `1ad91675ddeea90bee849b4ec286dc1bdaf1a6ea`, Crown Admission run `31948688216` failed because child CLI processes inherited a synthetic PR merge `GITHUB_SHA` different from the exact checked-out candidate. That identity defect is closed at `92f22a82144fa8eddfa7b92537e039630ff25247`: run `31951925425` executed `cargo test --locked --workspace --all-features` successfully, including all four black-box CLI tests.

The same run then localized a second independent defect in `Cold-cache correctness`: after a successful clean-target full test execution, `scripts/cold-cache.sh` invoked `crown --verify`, which failed with `I/O at .../target/crown/admission.json: No such file or directory`. The workflow topology proves the admission artifact is intentionally constructed only in the downstream `CHATMAN ECOSYSTEM CROWN` job after `cold-cache` succeeds, so the predecessor cold-cache verifier was circular.

## Commands / exits observed

Exact predecessor head `92f22a82144fa8eddfa7b92537e039630ff25247`, Crown Admission run `31951925425`:

```bash
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                      # exit 0
cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings  # exit 0
cargo run --locked --quiet -p ecosystem-cli --bin ecosystem -- catalog validate      # exit 0
cargo run --locked --quiet -p ecosystem-cli --bin ecosystem -- architecture check    # exit 0
cargo run --locked --quiet -p ecosystem-cli --bin ecosystem -- projection check      # exit 0
cargo test --locked --workspace --all-features                  # exit 0
RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --locked --workspace --all-features --no-deps    # exit 0
cargo run --locked --quiet -p ecosystem-cli --bin ecosystem -- storage verify         # exit 0
cargo run --locked --quiet -p ecosystem-cli --bin ecosystem -- receipt verify-all     # exit 0
./scripts/cold-cache.sh                                         # tests exit 0; predecessor final crown --verify exit 1 because admission.json is not constructed until downstream crown job
```

Published exact head `d9537ee5db53ef788c65542b5507a5c4c6d64642` contains the dependency-acyclic cold-cache repair. No exact-head workflow run is visible yet, so no ALIVE promotion is claimed for the new head.

## Authority ceiling

Observation / verification / repository source repair only. This PR grants no component standing, planner/policy/role/agent authority, BRCE consequential DO, live Azure authority, release/tag authority, merge authority, or external production actuation.

## Receipts / replay

Replay:

```bash
python3 scripts/verify_release.py --check-refs
python3 scripts/verify_standing_evidence.py
cargo test --locked -p ecosystem-cli --test cli
cargo test --locked --workspace --all-features
./scripts/cold-cache.sh
./scripts/crown.sh
```

The workflow-level final Crown remains the authoritative composition court: after policy/test/cold-cache/GitHub-read gates succeed, it constructs exact-subject admission evidence and runs `ecosystem crown --json` followed by `ecosystem crown --verify` under `ECOSYSTEM_SUBJECT_SHA=${CANDIDATE_SHA}`.

## Falsifiers

- release graph live-ref verification fails
- standing-evidence verification fails
- child CLI resolves a subject different from the checked-out exact SHA
- cold-cache depends on an artifact constructed only after cold-cache succeeds
- Crown accepts missing or incomplete admission evidence
- malformed CLI command succeeds
- cold-cache execution diverges from warm execution
- receipt/projection/architecture/storage/GALL gates fail

## Rollback

Revert commits on `agent/crown-release-evidence-gates` or close the draft PR. `main` is unchanged.

body:
# Phase 01 · Sprint 03: Architecture and Module Boundaries

## Pull Request Description

### Summary of Changes
This pull request establishes the core technical architecture, modular boundaries, state ownership taxonomy, and error contracts for **ChessForge** as defined in `planning/sprints/P01-S03-architecture-and-module-boundaries.md`.

### Key Deliverables
1. **Authoritative Architecture Specification (`docs/architecture.md`):**
   - Decoupled unidirectional layered architecture: $\text{Presentation} \rightarrow \text{Application Service} \rightarrow \text{Pure Chess Domain} \rightarrow \text{Chess Adapter Port}$.
   - Stockfish WASM WebWorker isolation with tokenized asynchronous UCI protocol and thread/memory guardrails.
   - Tauri v2 Rust native desktop bridge with least-privilege scoped permissions.
   - State taxonomy establishing `GameSession` as single runtime source of truth, persistence as durable snapshots, engine as ephemeral advisor, and UI as transient projection.
   - Standardized `Result<T, AppError>` typed error propagation avoiding unhandled panics or stack trace leaks.
   - Comprehensive module directory tree for `src/` and `src-tauri/`.
   - Extensibility roadmap for future network/cloud chess adapters without domain refactoring.

2. **Architectural Decision Records (`docs/adr/`):**
   - **ADR-001:** Decoupled Pure Chess Domain & Adapter Pattern (rejected direct UI coupling & Rust domain).
   - **ADR-002:** Tauri v2 + React 19 + TypeScript Desktop Stack (rejected Electron, WPF, and pure PWA).
   - **ADR-003:** Stockfish WASM WebWorker Isolation & UCI Protocol (rejected spawned native binary & UI thread engine).
   - **ADR-004:** Local-First JSON Snapshot Persistence & Crash Recovery (rejected embedded SQLite & cloud databases).
   - **ADR-005:** Unified Typed Result and Error Models Across Boundaries (rejected thrown exceptions & untyped strings).

3. **SDET Architecture Verification Matrix (`docs/testing/test_cases_catalog_P01_S03.md`):**
   - 10 granular architectural verification test cases (TC-ARCH-01 to TC-ARCH-10) validating layer boundaries, dependency directions, invariant safety, engine invalidation, and schema validation.

---

### Verification & Quality Gates Summary
- **Scrum Master Gate:** Sprint planned and tracked in `task.md`.
- **SDET Gate:** Test Cases Catalog committed (`docs/testing/test_cases_catalog_P01_S03.md`).
- **Dev Technical Gate:** Full architecture and 5 ADRs authored and reviewed against coding standards.
- **Chess Domain Gate:** FIDE chess semantics isolation and invariant rules reviewed and approved.
- **Security Gate:** Tauri IPC capability scoping, WebWorker sandboxing, and error sanitization audited and approved.
- **Product Owner Gate:** All sprint acceptance criteria and DoD items verified.

---

### Acceptance Criteria Checklist
- [x] No circular dependency is required.
- [x] Chess domain is UI-independent.
- [x] Engine is isolated in dedicated WebWorker.
- [x] Native capabilities are isolated behind Tauri IPC bridges.
- [x] Future multiplayer does not force a rewrite of the domain.

author: marekgrzeska
body:
The second half of `modules-migrate-their-own-database`, held back from #99 on purpose so the agent went first and this one only follows a deployment that survived. It did: #99's smoke check got `health=200` from its own image on the first attempt, which — because the lifespan blocks until the migration finishes — is itself the proof that the new path ran.

## What this does

The same mechanism as the agent's, with one ordering that is specific to this module: the migration runs **before a single candle is written**, not merely before a request is served. `ingest.start()` sits far below it in the lifespan, and `test_nothing_is_collected_before_the_migration_finishes` asserts that rather than trusting it — a request served too early answers wrongly and can be retried, but a candle written into a schema the module does not know leaves a mark that cannot be taken back.

Two numbers differ from the agent's, both from the size of the tables here:

- **The lock wait is 25 minutes**, against the agent's 5. An index rebuilt over the candle table outlasts several ordinary starts, and a wait shorter than the migration ahead of it turns a slow migration into a restart loop that never finishes one.
- **25 and not 30**, because App Service caps `WEBSITES_CONTAINER_START_TIME_LIMIT` at 1800s. The module has to give up first and say why; the platform giving up first restarts the container and starts the same migration over, explaining nothing.

## Not in this diff

- `deploy-market-data.yml` is untouched. Its smoke check already reaches the process through `/ws/candles` — that property is exactly what #99 had to add for the agent, and this module has had it all along.
- `WEBSITES_CONTAINER_START_TIME_LIMIT=1800` is already applied (it went in with #99's `terraform apply`), and `scripts/grant-schema-ownership.sql` has already been run against the `market_data` database — check query returns zero rows. Merging this before that transfer would give a module that will not start.

body:
Follow-up to #223, which landed the six Arm B heads and their reports but no prose. Docs and one new report; **no code changes**.

## The stale claims this fixes

Three documents asserted the opposite of what is now true:

- `arch_training.md` §10 — "Nothing has been *trained* on anything but `fever_present`… an hour of GPU that has not been spent yet"
- `arch_encoder_training.md` §9 — "the six Arm B fine-tunes … have **not** been run"
- `architecture.md` §3.16 — "the six fine-tunes are an unspent GPU hour"

## The write-up

`reports/encoder_training/2026-08-16-plain-english.md`. Plain-English throughout rather than a translation of a separate technical document, because there is no separate technical document for this sweep — it sources directly from the six `<signal>.arm_b_finetune.json` files and says so in its header. It discharges the six obligations the reports README sets for a run write-up.

Every figure in it was checked against the JSON rather than transcribed.

## Three findings worth pulling out

**The 2026-08-09 fever result replicates across five more symptoms.** Arm B beat Arm A on `null_ambiguous` in every signal, p between 3e-05 and 2e-39. The frozen pooled representation was a constraint everywhere, not a quirk of fever.

| symptom | Arm B | Arm A | TF-IDF | `null→true` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| flank pain | 96.0% | 80.7% | 72.8% | 1.51% |
| dysuria | 94.9% | 82.4% | 70.5% | 3.49% |
| fever | 92.9% | 79.0% | 73.6% | 1.34% |
| haematuria | 91.5% | 82.8% | 74.7% | 2.33% |
| urinary frequency | 85.3% | 67.8% | 59.9% | 1.94% |
| nocturia | 83.0% | 70.4% | 64.9% | 4.04% |

**The errors are in the clear libraries, not the confounders written to be the hard part.** 39% to 87% of each signal's errors sit in `_true`/`_false`, while the confounder families mostly run 90–100%. `urinary_frequency_true` at 65.8% and `nocturia_true` at 71.1% are the worst libraries in the sweep. Half of flank pain's errors fall on **4 sentences out of 243**. That shape is a data problem with a nameable fix list, not a model problem — and the write-up quotes the failing sentences and groups them into five themes.

**Section 10's own cluster-tagging prediction did not hold, and the doc now records the verdict** rather than quietly dropping it. The plan predicted untagged signals would be flattered and fully-tagged `dysuria` penalised. `dysuria` came second of six; the two weakest signals are both fully untagged. The asymmetry is still real — an untagged interval is narrower than the truth — but it is swamped by differences in what the `_true` libraries contain.

## Also recorded

- **`null → true` runs 1.34% to 4.04%** — the cell that invents a symptom into a patient's pre-filled form. Noted in `architecture.md` alongside the fact that no head has been through a safety review and none is wired to anything.
- **`--base-model roberta-base` is mandatory on a comparable run.** `DEFAULT_BASE_MODEL` is `Bio_ClinicalBERT`, nine points worse; omitting the flag succeeds silently and produces numbers that can't be read beside the six committed reports.
- **`fever_present.arm_b_finetune.*` changed base model in the sweep.** Nothing unique was lost — the version it replaced was Bio_ClinicalBERT at 84.1%, exactly the Bio_ClinicalBERT arm still in `model_comparison` — but `2026-08-09.md` must now be read against `model_comparison`, not against the current file. The reports README says so.
- **`hedged` is the one confounder family still weak** (80.9–84.5% on three signals) and is the only confounder work on the next-steps list.

## Testing

Docs and markdown only, so nothing to typecheck. Ran the encoder-training and synthetic-recombination unit tests to confirm nothing regressed: 248 passed, 4 skipped (the `requirements-ml.txt` skips, as on CI).

author: duynhne
body:
## The problem this closes

`lint-version` is a **plain string input**. No Dependabot ecosystem reads a
workflow input value, so nothing has ever updated it. That is how the default sat
on `v2.6.0` while every local install had moved to `2.12.2` — CI's lint gate was
quietly weaker than the one developers run by hand, and **63 findings across the
fleet never reached CI**.

#109 raised the default. That fixed the symptom. This fixes the mechanism: the
same thing would happen again to `v2.12.2`.

## The change

A `tools/go.mod` using the Go 1.24 `tool` directive is a real module, so
Dependabot's `gomod` ecosystem bumps it — **per repository, in that repository's
own PR**, no fleet-wide flag day. Building the linter from that module is also
the command a developer runs locally, so CI and the workstation cannot drift.

```yaml
- name: Install golangci-lint
  run: |
    if [ -f tools/go.mod ]; then
      go -C tools build -o "$RUNNER_TEMP/golangci-lint" \
        github.com/golangci/golangci-lint/v2/cmd/golangci-lint
    else
      GOBIN="$RUNNER_TEMP" go install \
        github.com/golangci/golangci-lint/v2/cmd/golangci-lint@${{ inputs.lint-version }}
    fi
```

`lint-version` stays as the fallback, so migration is one repository at a time
and nothing breaks for callers that never adopt it. The Lint step now prints the
resolved version before running — a silent version gap is the exact failure this
job is meant to make impossible.

## Verified locally, not assumed

Tried on a real repository (`checkout-service`) before writing any of this:

```
$ go -C tools build -o ../.bin/golangci-lint …     # 4s
$ ./.bin/golangci-lint --version
golangci-lint has version 2.12.2 built with go1.26.5
$ ./.bin/golangci-lint run
10 issues: * goconst: 8  * gosec: 2
```

Identical to the system-installed 2.12.2 — same count, same findings. Note the
first attempt (`go -C tools tool golangci-lint run`) **does not work**: `-C`
moves the working directory into `tools/`, so the linter analyses the tools
module and reports "no go files to analyze". Building the binary and running it
from the repository root is the working shape, and it is what the docs describe.

Keep the tool in its **own module**, not the service `go.mod` — golangci-lint
pulls ~200 dependencies (measured), and they have no business in a service's
`go.sum` or its `govulncheck` results.

## Also in this PR

Docs record the **SHA-pin policy**, which was previously only implied — every
example said `@main` while all 12 consumers pin a SHA. This repository is
**deliberately not tagged**: for a reference pinned to a SHA that carries no tag,
Dependabot resolves the update to the latest commit on the default branch, and
the commit it proposes is itself untagged, so the arrangement sustains itself.
Callers track `main` while keeping an immutable, auditable pin.

The docs also now state plainly that the Lint job does **not** run on `push` —
so `main` is never linted, and a PR merged with Lint red leaves those findings
unreported. That is a real gap, but fixing it here would turn `main` red in 10
repositories immediately; it comes in a follow-up once the cleanup lands.

## Verification

- `actionlint` clean
- `yq` parses; `lint-version` default unchanged at `v2.12.2`
- the `tools/go.mod` path exercised end-to-end on a real repository (above)

body:
### Motivation
- Provide the shared primitives required by Phase 1: a single engr reference parser/canonicalizer, a workspace-level schema/version authority, and a reusable human-confirmation gate.
- Canonical, compact, human-friendly object references are required by the Phase 1 reference design without changing persisted identities.
- Preserve compatibility with legacy v0 workspaces while preventing accidental mutation of unknown/newer workspace versions.

### Description
- Add a shared reference primitive in `crate::reference` that parses standalone `engr:` and embedded forms, supports optional `:<section>` and `@<commit>` snapshot selectors, validates per-kind IDs, and implements the canonical 26-char lowercase Crockford Base32 UUID codec with fixed test vectors (`crates/engr/src/reference.rs`).
- Extract confirmation mechanics into `crate::confirmation` for challenge minting, response classification (exact / qualified / invalid), and a generic `ensure_fresh` helper to refuse stale prepared mutations (`crates/engr/src/confirmation.rs`).
- Make `.engr/format.json` the workspace schema/version authority and add detection of legacy v0 layouts, read-only behaviour for legacy workspaces, an explicit `engr migrate` path that updates incompatible representation (`Object.status` → `Object.state`) while preserving compatible legacy markers, and require the workspace to be current before mutation (`crates/engr/src/store.rs`, `crates/engr/src/main.rs`).
- Update the `Object` model to retain legacy markers where present, expose canonical `state` serialization for new objects, and keep compatibility when reading migrated objects (`crates/engr/src/model.rs`).
- Integrate the shared reference parsing into id resolution and `--ref` parsing so `engr:obj:<id>` and compact 26-char ids are accepted as object identifiers (`crates/engr/src/store.rs`, `crates/engr/src/main.rs`).
- Wire the new confirmation primitive into the gate so challenge minting and response handling are shared and the stale-check for `expected_rev` uses the gate helper (`crates/engr/src/gate.rs`).
- Update documentation and protocol artifacts to record the workspace authority, migration boundary, canonical compact UUID references, and embedded reference shape (`protocol/PROTOCOL.md`, `README.md`, `skill/SKILL.md`).
- Add unit and integration tests that exercise reference round-trips, legacy-workspace read/migrate/refuse semantics, confirmation behaviours, and the existing gate/verify invariants (`crates/engr/tests/*`).

### Testing
- Ran the full automated test suite with `cargo test --workspace`, including new unit tests and CLI tests, and all tests passed.
- Ran formatting checks with `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and linting with `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, both succeeded with no warnings.
- Verified the build and ran `cargo test` locally as part of CI iteration; no test failures were observed.

body:
Normalise vectors without magnitude under/overflow and a single pass

`magnitude` now divides components by the largest absolute component
before squaring, so vectors such as `[1e-200, 0]` or `[1e200, 0]` no

author: aniketp02
body:
## CF2 PR 2 of 2: tell the truth when things fail

Fixes **F-03 (CLI half), F-04, F-09 (rendering half), F-12, F-13** from the clean-room first-run report. Pairs with dorgu-ai/dorgu-operator#36.

### F-04: `dorgu health` reported health for a cluster it could not reach

Against an unreachable cluster it printed an empty node table, `Active Incidents: 0`, `"count": 0` in `--json`, and exited **0**. With four active criticals: also **0**.

- The command now probes the API server before assembling anything, reading `/version` (visible to any authenticated user, so a namespace-scoped role is not mistaken for an unreachable cluster) and failing with `cannot reach cluster; check your kubeconfig/context`, the kubectl detail, and context hints. Nothing is rendered from a failed call.
- New `--exit-code` for monitoring scripts. Exit codes, documented in `--help`: **0** read the cluster and found no criticals, **1** could not run the check, **2** active criticals, **3** health could not be judged. Without the flag the command still exits 0 whenever it read the cluster, so interactive use is unchanged.
- A failure listing `IncidentMemory` used to flatten to "0 incidents", making "the operator is not installed" indistinguishable from "nothing is wrong". It now reads `unknown` with the reason, and `--json` carries `unavailable` and `reason`.

Verified live: exit 1 against a kubeconfig pointing at a dead port, exit 2 with a critical incident, exit 3 with the CRD missing, exit 0 otherwise.

### F-12: unknown subcommands exited 0

Root cause is not what it looks like: setting `Args` is **not** enough. Cobra returns `flag.ErrHelp` for a command that is not `Runnable()` **before** it validates arguments, and `ExecuteC` turns that into "print help, exit 0". So a subcommand group could never reject anything. Each group now has a `RunE` that prints help when bare and rejects a stray argument otherwise:

```
$ dorgu remediation frobnicate
✗ unknown command "frobnicate" for "dorgu remediation"
Run 'dorgu remediation --help' for usage.
$ echo $?
1
$ dorgu remediation lst
✗ unknown command "lst" for "dorgu remediation"

Did you mean this?
	list
```

A test asserts every subcommand group rejects a stray argument, so a new group cannot regress this quietly.

### F-13: runtime errors buried under usage

`SilenceUsage` is set in the root's `PersistentPreRunE`, which cobra runs *after* flag parsing and argument validation. So argument mistakes keep their usage (as intended) while runtime failures print just the failure:

```
$ dorgu health --kubeconfig /nope/nothing.yaml
✗ kubeconfig file not found: /nope/nothing.yaml
```

### F-03 (CLI half): stop suggesting the command that fails

`remediation diff` printed `dorgu remediation approve ...` for plans with no auto-applicable step, and following it produced a `Failed` remediation and a 30-minute cooldown. An advisory plan now reads:

```
This plan is advisory: nothing in it can be applied for you.
Carry out the steps above yourself. Nothing changes in the cluster until you do.

Actions:
  dorgu remediation reject ra-web-imagepull -n apps --reason "..."
```

The manual steps are still printed: they are the value of the plan. `approve` on an advisory plan now reports "Approval recorded. This plan is advisory, so nothing was applied", matching the operator's new `Acknowledged` phase. Applicable plans are unchanged.

One existing test fixture used `Action.Type: "resource"`, which the CRD enum does not allow; it is now `persona-update`, so it exercises a plan that genuinely can be applied.

### F-09 (rendering half)

`CPU: n/a requests / allocatable ( / 3860m)` had an empty left operand. Every missing figure now reads `n/a` on both sides, and a real `0` on an idle cluster prints as `0` rather than being hidden. A test asserts no rendered saturation line can contain an empty operand. The other half of F-09 (the operator never computed these figures at all) is in the operator PR.

## Verification

```
make check                              # gofmt + go vet + all tests, matches CI
```

Live checks with the built binary: unknown subcommand and typo suggestion, bare group still prints help and exits 0, runtime error prints one line, argument error still shows usage, unreachable cluster exits 1, and the four `--exit-code` paths driven through a stub kubectl.

## Not merging

Left for review.

author: krishna-paulraj
body:
Adds a floating chat launcher on every page. A visitor writes, the thread is stored in Postgres, and replies land back in the same thread when they return. Conversations are read and answered from a private /inbox.

The scripted contact section on the homepage stays as it is; it now shares its accent with the live widget through a --chat-accent token.

Identity is a 256-bit token in an HttpOnly cookie, stored only as its SHA-256. The visitor endpoints never take a thread id from the client, so the thread is always resolved server-side and one visitor structurally cannot read another's conversation — there is no parameter to tamper with and no ownership check a later handler can forget to write.

The inbox is gated by ADMIN_SECRET, exchanged at a login route for an HMAC-signed session cookie. Kept separate from BOARD_SECRET on purpose: that key lives in localStorage and unlocks public board data, which is a survivable loss. These threads hold visitor emails and private messages, so the credential must be unreadable by any script on the page.

Delivery is polling, since there is no realtime transport here. It stops entirely on a hidden tab and stretches from 5s to 30s as a conversation goes quiet, and every write publishes its seq to Redis so an idle poll costs one GET and never reaches Postgres. Messages sort and page on that seq rather than a timestamp: same-millisecond rows would otherwise order nondeterministically, and the client only ever echoes back a number the server gave it.

Some decisions worth recording:

- Any new message reopens an archived thread, whoever sent it. Archiving means "done for now", not "mute" — leaving it filed away after someone writes in buries their message where the default view never shows it.
- A full thread refuses writes rather than dropping its oldest messages the way board comments do. Losing the start of a conversation is worse than being told it is full.
- No minimum-interval send guard. A read-then-insert check races under exactly the concurrent burst it would exist to stop; the per-IP send limit is tighter, and the per-thread cap still bounds things when Redis is unavailable and rate limiting fails open.
- Enforcement is per-route rather than in a proxy. Next's own guidance is that proxy checks are optimistic and cannot be the only line of defence, so the per-route check gets written either way.
- components/ui holds the registry components exactly as shipped. The one site-specific need — an accent for your own messages, since the palette is otherwise achromatic — is a className at the call site, so these can be reinstalled without losing anything.

Reuses the existing rate limiter, Prisma accessor, constant-time key comparison and control-character stripper. The contact route now shares lib/email.ts and the email validator instead of keeping its own.

author: ezzaldeen-albitar
body:
## What this changes

The Owner **resolved `P1-OD-025`**. This converts the gate that encoded it as OPEN into one that enforces the approved policy. It does not delete the gate.

`apps/web/tests/p1-28-reception-media.test.ts` proved three ABSENCES — that no SQL could create a document category, that the default storage provider refused every signing call, and that no version could leave `pending`. Those were correct while the decision was open. They are now the thing blocking the approved foundation: the private/versioned model seeds seven reception categories, so `no-document-category` fails on it.

Reproduced before this branch existed, on `remediation/p1-15-reception-document-foundation`:

```
FAIL tests/p1-28-reception-media.test.ts > `no-document-category`: the category table ships zero rows and nothing can add one
AssertionError: expected '-- P1-15 / P1-OD-025: operational, pr…' not to match /INSERT\s+INTO\s+shared\.document_cat…/i
```

## The five rules that replace the three absences

- evidence categories are never public, and always declare classification and retention
- the version lifecycle vocabulary is **closed** — a subset is a tree that has not grown the scan step; `auto_accepted` is a state that never has to earn acceptance
- acceptance is earned by a clean scan; a scanner failure never accepts
- a signature is finalized only against an ACCEPTED version
- the browser holds no storage credential and names no raw object key

Every rule is universally quantified over the repository, so each is also applied to a **planted violation it must reject** and to the **compliant form it must pass**. A new case guards the sweep itself — the three deleted cases could have read no file at all and still reported clean.

## Two things learned by running rather than reasoning

1. Judging *every* historical lifecycle definition condemns a migration series for having had a past: the migration that created `shared.document_versions` declared no `scanning`, because the state did not exist yet. Only the **effective** (last-applied, filename-ordered) definition can be judged.
2. Demanding **equality** with the approved set would fail this branch's own CI, since `develop` legitimately lacks `scanning` until the foundation lands. Hence a closed vocabulary rather than a fixed one.

## Verification

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Converted suite, **without** the foundation (this tree) | 26/26 |
| Converted suite, **with** the P1-15 foundation present | 26/26 |
| `tests/ci/p1-28-evidence-manifest.test.ts` | 96/96 |
| P1-27 + P1-28 evidence suites | 135/135 |
| Root unit tier | 2592 tests, **0 failed**, 99 files |
| Web tier | 2728 tests, **0 failed**, 98 files |
| `npm run verify:policies` | 0 problems |

## The seal

The conversion changes a path under `apps/**`, which this package computes as a product path, so the candidate was **re-frozen** rather than named as a successor. Carried through every field the gate checks: candidate and tree, an append-only `reFrozenFrom.history` entry, `successors` and `absorbedSuccessors` cleared, all **eleven** hosted bindings moved to `describesSupersededHead` with what supersedes them, five tier provenances moved to their pending twins, `pendingHostedBindings` rebuilt to equal the derived set plus its `awaits`, and both halves restated to name one candidate in full.

Every cited head was verified an ancestor with `git merge-base --is-ancestor` rather than assumed.

**The hosted bindings are PENDING, and that is correct.** Re-freezing moves the code the package describes; it cannot manufacture an observation of it. They close when CI runs at a head descending from this candidate — which is this pull request.

Local figures were recorded **as observed** at each step, including the transient seal failures while the package was mid-update, rather than the values they were expected to settle to.

## Why this must land before the foundation branches

`remediation/p1-15-reception-document-foundation` cannot be green until this merges: it seeds the categories, and it is forbidden by `check-phase-ownership.mjs` from touching `apps/web/**` to fix the test that goes red.

author: prabhat1308
body:
Closes #406.

## Issue

The unit-recycling accumulator added `unit_replacement_rate * layer_size` every step (scaled by the budget mode) but could pay one unit per step, so the default mode banked a warm-up debt that fired as a burst once units matured, and rates above `1/layer_size` accrued unbounded debt while producing bit-identical arms.

## New state

Budget accrues against the mature count (`rate * n_mature * rate_scale`) and the carried accumulator is capped at one pending replacement, matching the CBP fix in #371 and the reference scheduler. Selection, gates, budget modes, and `unit_replacement_counts` (which already reports the gated decision) are unchanged; the `unit_replacement_rate` docstring states the semantics.

Failing-test-first: `test_recycling_budget_does_not_accrue_while_every_unit_is_immature` and `test_recycling_budget_never_carries_more_than_one_pending_unit` fail on `main` and pass here; the existing gated / loss-pressure budget tests are unchanged.

|---|---|---|
| `ask.sh` | 「최종 Commit 스텝이 **줍는다**」 = 회수 경로를 이미 말함 | 회수 어휘에 「줍」 추가 |
| `merge_main.sh` | 라운드 소진 시 `die … 6`으로 죽음 = 판정 있음 | 사후 대조(`merge-base --is-ancestor`·`landed`)와 `die` 관용구를 판정으로 인정 |

킬테스트 = 조용한 스크립트를 심으면 차단, 복원 시 무경보.

## ③ 못 보는 축 ⓑ 호출부 삼킴 → **게이트 미신설이 옳다**

실물 4곳(`news-analyze` 2 · `news-ask` · `news-revise`의 `cardmake.sh` 호출)이 전부 이렇게 돼 있다.

```
|| echo "::warning::카드플랜 일부 실패(다이제스트는 보존됨)"
```

**무해 사유를 이미 적고 있다** = 정당한 fail-soft. 그대로 게이트를 세우면 위양성 4건이고, 「새로 삼키는 자리」는 ⓒ와 같은 축이라 별도 술어가 필요하다.

## ④ 못 보는 축 ⓒ 자리 바꿈 → 구조적 한계로 잔존

면책을 **파일별 개수가 아니라 자리 식별자**로 바꿔야 하는데, 그건 21개 표 전체의 문법 변경이라 별건이다.

## ⑤ 짝 게이트 위양성 봉합 (내 변경이 만든 것)

코얼레싱 짝 게이트가 git_land 호출줄을 **전부 코얼레싱으로 읽어**, 접두를 끈 채 부르는(`PAGES_COALESCE=0`) 제작·수집 축까지 라이브 서빙을 요구했다 = 위양성 2건. 스킵이 안 되므로 짝을 요구할 이유가 없다 → 접두 끄기 인정.

## 실측

- `check_refs` rc=0 — 124게이트, 워크플로 전수 파싱 통과
- **착지 침묵 0건 · 내용 소실 0건**(둘 다 면책표 비움)
- 부채 원장 188 → **183건**

author: miquelmatoses
body:
L'últim forat de seguretat que quedava obert de l'auditoria.

## El forat

El scope `auth_2fa` (10/min) estava configurat des de l'auditoria del maig del 2026 i **no s'aplicava enlloc**: és un limitador de DRF, i `dos_fa_verificar` és una vista de Django plana.

O siga que l'única pantalla del projecte que accepta **codis de recuperació d'un sol ús en bucle** era la que no tenia cap límit per a endevinar-los.

## El limitador

`comptes/ratelimit.py::excedeix_limit` — finestra fixa comptada al cache compartit, amb el ritme llegit del mateix `DEFAULT_THROTTLE_RATES` que fan servir els limitadors de DRF, perquè els números visquen en un sol lloc. Superar-lo torna **429** amb la mateixa pantalla i un missatge clar en lloc d'una pàgina d'error seca.

Dues decisions que val la pena que quedin explícites:

**La identitat és l'usuari, no la IP.** Qui arriba a esta pantalla ja ha passat la contrasenya, així que algú amb una galeta robada és *un* usuari per moltes IPs que rote. Comptar per IP seria comptar la cosa equivocada.

**Falla obert.** Si el cache peta, es deixa passar. La contrasenya continua sent necessària per a arribar ací, i una caiguda del cache no pot convertir-se en un bloqueig del compte de tothom. És una elecció, i per això està documentada — implica que el limitador és tan disponible com el cache.

## Proves

Quatre casos, cadascun verificat amb la seua mutació:

| Mutació | Prova que crida |
|---|---|
| Llevar el limitador (l'estat d'abans) | l'onzé intent ha de ser 429 |
| Comptar per IP en lloc de per usuari | una persona no pot bloquejar-ne una altra |
| Fallar tancat quan el cache peta | un cache mort no bloqueja ningú |

Més: mirar la pàgina (GET) no gasta intents, que si no una recàrrega o el botó d'arrere consumirien el pressupost de algú sense que haja escrit res.

body:
## Cause racine

`packages/capture-pgm-compat` (#231, `ee5cfb8a`) prouve qu'une source **figée** est
indiscernable d'une source saine sur l'axe spatial (`spatialStddevAvg` 50.986 vs
48.200) — seul l'axe temporel les sépare (0.002 vs 4.271). Cette suite est opt-in
(`PULSAR_LIVE_CAPTURE_COMPAT=1`) et **aucun job CI ne l'exécutait** : elle n'avait
tourné que sur la machine du porteur. Un drift silencieux sur l'axe temporel du
chemin de capture aurait donc atteint `main` sans être détecté.

Correction de cadrage vs #231 : pas de nouveau runner à créer — `offline-probes`
tourne déjà sur `windows-2022` contre un vrai `pulsar.exe` via l'artefact
`pulsar-rundir` produit par `build`.

## Fix

Nouveau job `capture-pgm-compat` (`needs: build`, `windows-2022`) :
- télécharge le même artefact `pulsar-rundir` qu'`offline-probes` — un vrai
  `pulsar.exe` avec CEF (obs-browser), pas de re-téléchargement des ~150 Mo de
  binaires via le postinstall de `pulsar-bundle-full`
  (`PULSAR_BUNDLE_SKIP_POSTINSTALL=1` + `PULSAR_BUNDLE_FULL_BINARIES_PATH`
  pointé sur le rundir de l'artefact) ;
- Node 20 + ffmpeg (`FedericoCarboni/setup-ffmpeg@v3`, même action que
  `live-broadcast`) ;
- build topologique des deps workspace (`pulsar-client`, `pgm-correlator`,
  `pulsar-bundle-full`) ;
- exécute la suite avec `PULSAR_LIVE_CAPTURE_COMPAT=1`.

**Oracle inchangé** — aucun seuil, aucun plancher de matérialité, aucun scénario
touché dans `packages/capture-pgm-compat/**`. Seul `pipeline.yml` est modifié.

## Preuve

CI de cette PR : voir le job `capture-pgm-compat (real CEF)`. Le log contient les
trois scénarios (`healthy`/`black`/`frozen`) avec `FRAME_HEALTH`,
`SPATIAL_MATERIAL_SEPARATION`/`TEMPORAL_MATERIAL_SEPARATION` et `PGM_EXTRACTOR`
réels du runner. Si CEF ne rend pas sur ce runner (pas de GPU, pas de session
bureau interactive), le job échouera pour une raison réelle — mesurée, pas
supposée — et sera documenté comme telle plutôt que contourné.

author: kazumadev619-dev
body:
## 概要

Stage 1 デプロイ計画の **Phase D（Task 15〜20）**。`k8s/` が GKE + クラスタ内 PostgreSQL 前提のまま実態と乖離していた問題（#105）を解消し、Raspberry Pi 5 上の k3s へデプロイできる状態にする。

namespace / Redis / cloudflared / RBAC は `fishing-infra` が所有するため、このリポジトリには **アプリのマニフェストだけ**を残す。

## 変更内容

### Task 15: 平坦化と `.gitignore`

- `k8s/base/` と `k8s/overlays/` を廃止し、`k8s/` 直下の本番一系統に
- 削除: `postgres.yaml` `redis.yaml` `namespace.yaml`（fishing-infra が所有）、`db-init-job.yaml` `secret.yaml`（作り直し）、`overlays/**`
- **`.gitignore` を `k8s/overlays/*/secret.yaml` → `k8s/**/secret.yaml` に変更**。平坦化した瞬間に平文 Secret の保護が外れるため、同一コミットで先に修正した

### Task 16: k3s + Traefik 向けに書き直し

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| namespace | `fishing-app` | `fishing` |
| Ingress | `nginx` / `fishing-app.local` | `traefik` / `fishing.kazuma-lab.com`（TLS は Cloudflare 終端） |
| `REDIS_URL` | `redis://redis:6379` | `redis://redis.fishing.svc.cluster.local:6379/0` |
| image | `fishing-app:latest` | `ghcr.io/kazumadev619-dev/fishing-app` |
| CPU limit | `500m` | **削除**（CFS quota による throttle が Stage 2 の p99 を支配するため） |
| securityContext | Pod レベルのみ | `readOnlyRootFilesystem` / `drop: ALL` / `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false` / `seccompProfile` / `automountServiceAccountToken: false` |
| probe | liveness + readiness | **startupProbe 追加**（5s × 30 = 最大 150s。arm64 の起動遅延で初回 CrashLoop するのを防ぐ） |

**readiness は `/readyz` のまま維持した。** 計画書の Task 16 は `/healthz` と書いているが、これは #125 より前に書かれた原稿で、そのまま適用すると「DB 未接続の Pod も Ready になる」状態に逆戻りする。

### `docker/Dockerfile`: runner の `HOME` を `/tmp` に

`readOnlyRootFilesystem: true` の実地検証中に発見。runner ステージだけ `HOME` 未設定で、既定の `/home/nextjs` を向いていた。今は誰も `$HOME` に書かないので EROFS は出ないが、ライブラリが書いた瞬間に本番で落ちる不発弾だった（migrator は元から `/tmp`）。

### Task 17: Secret を SOPS/age で暗号化

- `k8s/secret.enc.yaml` を追加（開発者 / CI / recovery の **3 鍵**）
- **`.sops.yaml` を `k8s/` からリポジトリルートへ移動。** sops は `.sops.yaml` を *カレントディレクトリ* から探すため、`k8s/` に置くとルートからの `sops -e k8s/secret.yaml` が `config file not found` で落ちる（計画書の手順そのものが動かなかった）
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` は含めない（build-arg で埋め込まれるため実行時に置いても効かない）

### Task 18: Job を db-migrate / db-seed に分離

| | `db-migrate` | `db-seed` |
|---|---|---|
| 実行 | 毎デプロイ（CI が適用） | 初回のみ手動 |
| kustomization | 含める | **含めない** |
| `backoffLimit` | `0` | `1` |
| 制限時間 | 240s | 1800s |

`backoffLimit: 0` は `kubectl wait --for=condition=complete` が Job の Failed を検知せず timeout まで待つ問題への対処。

`db-seed` は `DATABASE_URL` にも direct の値を入れる（`prisma/seed.ts` と `scripts/update-port-coordinates.ts` が Prisma CLI を通さず `process.env.DATABASE_URL` から自前で `pg.Pool` を作るため）。

### Task 19: kustomization 統合と CI 検証

- `k8s/kustomization.yaml` に一本化。**`secret.enc.yaml` は `resources` に入れない**（kustomize は SOPS を復号できず、暗号文のまま Secret を上書きして全 Pod が起動不能になる）
- CI に `manifests` ジョブを追加: `kustomize build` → `kubeconform -strict` → **Secret が描画されていないことの確認**

### Task 20: ドキュメント更新

`k8s/README.md` を全面書き直し（Minikube / EKS 前提を廃止）。`architecture.md` / `docker.md` / `development.md` の宙に浮いた参照も修正。

## 検証（すべて実際に実行した）

**`readOnlyRootFilesystem` の実地検証**（対照実験つき）

```
ルートFSに書けない（touch /app/xxx）        ✅ Read-only file system
/tmp と /app/.next/cache に書ける           ✅
/login /register を描画して EROFS           ✅ 出ない
HOME=/home/nextjs が書けない                ⚠️ → ENV HOME=/tmp で対処
```

**Neon 接続文字列の実地検証**

```
pooled  : current_user=fishing_app_rw / DDL は 42501 permission denied ✅ 最小権限
direct  : current_user=neondb_owner   / DDL 実行可 ✅
ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES: neondb_owner がテーブル(arwd)・シーケンス(rU)に登録済み
実地テスト: owner が作った直後のテーブルに app が INSERT/SELECT/UPDATE/DELETE 成功 ✅
```

**SOPS の往復検証**

```
ENC[AES256_GCM] 12個（8値 + コメント3 + mac）
平文の混入: neon.tech / postgresql:// / GOCSPX / .env.local の実値 → すべて 0 件 ✅
3 鍵すべてで復号成功、8 値すべて平文と一致 ✅
```

**migrator イメージの実地検証**（読み取り専用で起動）

```
$ prisma migrate status
Datasource "db": PostgreSQL "fishing_app" at "ep-...neon.tech"
4 migrations found in prisma/migrations
Following migrations have not yet been applied: ... ✅
tsx ローダ: node --import tsx/esm 動作確認 ✅
```

**マニフェスト検証**（kubeconform をローカルで実行）

```
kustomize build k8s/  → 5 resources: Valid 5, Invalid 0
k8s/job-db-seed.yaml  → 1 resource:  Valid 1, Invalid 0
kustomize edit set image → 2 イメージとも SHA タグに差し替わる ✅
kind: Secret の混入 → 0 件 ✅
```

## 関連Issue

refs #105

## テスト計画

- [x] `kustomize build` + `kubeconform -strict`（ローカル）
- [x] `readOnlyRootFilesystem` 実地検証
- [x] Neon pooled / direct の接続と権限検証
- [x] SOPS 3 鍵の暗号化・復号往復検証
- [x] migrator イメージで `prisma migrate status`
- [x] `node scripts/check-doc-links.mjs`（リンク切れなし）
- [ ] CI（Code Quality / Build / **Kubernetes Manifests**）

## 未検証として残ること

読み取り専用の検証に使った runner イメージは #125 より前のもので、**`/readyz` が入っていない**（404 だった）。readinessProbe が叩く先なので、**Task 21 のイメージビルド後に必ず確認する。**

author: 0xef6ae
body:
## ✅ PR 설명

BE 기수 공개 API 변경(2026-08-16 배포)을 반영하고, 그 위에서 막혀 있던 지원서 흐름을 복구합니다.
관련 이슈: #20

**1. 지원서 제출이 400으로 거절되던 문제 (핵심)**

프론트가 `email` `name` `essay` 같은 **고정 11개 키**로 answers를 보내고 있었습니다. 서버는 파트별 `applicationSchema.questions` 의 `key` 를 요구하는데, 어드민에서 key는 편집 불가이고 라벨을 slugify한 값이 자동 저장됩니다(한글 라벨 → 한글 key). **겹치는 키가 0개**라 4단계를 다 작성하고 제출하면 `400 INVALID_APPLICATION_ANSWERS` 로 거절되고 작성 내용이 유실됐습니다. 임시저장은 검증을 타지 않아 직전까지 정상으로 보였습니다.

→ 3단계를 파트별 질문으로 동적 렌더링하고, `answers` 를 질문 `key` 로 담습니다.

**2. 모집 파트를 못 불러오던 문제**

파트 칩 6개가 하드코딩이라 API 응답과 어긋나면 선택은 되는데 제출 단계에서 막혔습니다. → 활성 기수 응답에서 칩을 만듭니다.

**3. 모집 개폐 판정을 `status` → `ctaStatus` 로**

모집 기간까지 반영된 값이라 `status: "RECRUITING"` + `ctaStatus: "PRE_NOTIFICATION"` 조합이 존재합니다. **지금이 정확히 그 상태**이고, `status` 로 분기하면 지원 버튼이 잘못 열린 뒤 다음 화면에서 막힙니다. 활성 기수가 없을 때도 404가 아니라 `200 + hasActiveCohort:false` 로 오므로 `catch` 가 아닌 `hasActiveCohort` 로 분기합니다.

**4. 공개 응답 타입을 생성 스키마로 교체**

`GetActiveCohortResponse` 가 어드민 `CohortDto` 를 재사용하고 있었습니다. 공개 `parts[]` 에는 `applicationSchema` 가 없는데 `CohortDto` 기준으로는 필수라, `parts[0].applicationSchema.questions` 접근이 **타입 통과 후 런타임 TypeError** 가 되는 상태였습니다. `as unknown as` 캐스팅도 제거해 계약 위반이 빌드에서 잡히게 했습니다.

**그 외**
- 지원서 PDF 첨부 업로드 + 어드민 열람(만료형 서명 URL)
- 파트 질문 입력 유형(text/file) 설정
- 블로그·프로젝트 목록 페이지네이션, FAQ 문구 갱신
- apps/web ESLint가 설정 단계에서 죽어 있던 것 복구

<details>
<summary>커밋 4개 (각각 단독으로 타입체크 통과 — 어느 지점으로 되돌려도 빌드됨)</summary>

```
fc17ae5  feat(api,web): 기수 공개 API 계약 반영 + 지원서 파트별 동적 폼   (24 files)
bc540be  feat(admin): 지원서 첨부 열람 + 파트 질문 유형 설정              (7 files)
2211922  feat(web): 블로그·프로젝트 목록 페이지네이션 + FAQ 문구 갱신     (10 files)
f2e70f3  chore(lint): apps/web ESLint 설정 복구 + 가려져 있던 에러 수정    (5 files)
```
</details>

---

## 🧪 테스트 방법

- [x] 로컬 테스트 완료
- [x] 린트 및 빌드 통과

**자동 테스트** — 헤드리스 브라우저로 실제 클릭해 31개 항목 검증 (`fc17ae5` 범위)

| 구분 | 검증 내용 |
|---|---|
| 정상 흐름 (9) | 스텝바 3단계 · 칩이 API 응답과 일치(응답에 없는 칩 미노출 포함) · 질문 동적 렌더 · 필수 `*` 표시 · 빈 값 제출 차단 · PDF 업로드 · **제출 payload의 키·첨부 객체·생년월일 변환·전화 포맷** · 완료 화면 |
| 실패·경계 (7) | 조회 실패 → 다시 시도로 복구 · 실패해도 1단계는 입력 가능 · 열린 파트 0개 안내 · 파트 404 시 제출 잠김 · `hasActiveCohort:false` · `status=RECRUITING`+`cta=PRE_NOTIFICATION` |
| 라우트·애니메이션 (7) | `/` `/blog` `/project` `/recruit` `/recruit/apply` 콘솔 에러 0건 · 카운트업 재생 |
| 임시저장·파트전환 (8) | 질문 key로 저장/복원 · 파트 전환 시 이전 답변 미혼입 · 마감 파트 자동 해제 |

**검증 중 추가로 발견해 고친 버그 2건**
1. 파트를 바꾸고 새 질문 도착 전에 `다음` 을 누르면 이전 파트 질문이 그대로 보였고, 그 상태로 제출하면 `cohortPartId` 와 `answers` 키가 어긋나 **같은 400이 재발**
2. 임시저장 복원이 저장본의 `part` 로 덮어써서, 방금 고른 파트가 되돌아감

**수동 확인**
```
pnpm dev:web → /recruit/apply
현재는 모집 시작(08-29) 전이라 파트 상세가 404입니다.
"모집 중인 파트를 찾을 수 없습니다" + 제출 버튼 잠김이 정상 동작입니다.
```

**빌드·정적 검사**
```
@ddd/api tsc ✓   apps/web tsc ✓   apps/admin tsc ✓
pnpm lint 0 errors ✓   build:web ✓   build:admin ✓
```

## 🔍 체크리스트

**⚠️ 실데이터 검증은 아직입니다.** 위 테스트는 서버 응답을 모킹한 것입니다. 현재 6개 파트 전부 `404 COHORT_PART_NOT_FOUND` 라(모집 기간 밖) 실제 등록된 질문으로는 못 돌렸습니다. **08-29 모집 시작 후 또는 어드민에서 모집 시작일을 당긴 뒤 한 번 더 확인이 필요합니다.**

author: rasm105k
body:
## Linear
WOR-551 — 4.7.0 Conversations + Actions v1

## Goal
Complete the missing action-first primitives after PR #650 without introducing a parallel task/scheduler/chat platform.

## Current slice
- `CREATE_TASK` uses the persisted conversation action request itself as the durable task; no duplicate task domain.
- `REMIND_ME` uses the existing NotificationQueue `NextAttemptUtc` scheduler primitive; no client timers/new scheduler stack.
- `ASSIGN_SELF` is target-scoped and server-side: admin requests an eligible same-filial user; acceptance revalidates tenant/filial/current job state before assignment, and normal job access only applies after acceptance.
- existing deep links remain the V1 `OPEN_JOB` behavior.
- notification payloads now carry safe action metadata so an unassigned target can accept `ASSIGN_SELF` from Inbox without being granted conversation access first.

## Guardrails
- no new generic task table/service;
- no new notification provider or event bus;
- no loosened job/conversation ACL;
- action resolution remains idempotent and target-bound;
- future reminders must remain invisible to Inbox until due.

## Validation
Draft while backend compiler/gates, generated API client, focused tests, Postman and authenticated mobile Playwright are being completed.

## Summary

Field-caught in the jingun Phase-3 fanout canary (operator-approved): with the WS1 flag on and the updated host runner, the container's piri failed immediately with

```
Error: Failed to load extension "/opt/a2a-runner/piri-fanout-extension": Failed to load extension: Type is not defined
```

Root cause: the WS2 fork (#1841) dropped the example's `import { Type } from "typebox";` line while pruning the TUI/renderer imports (the original `examples/extensions/subagent/index.ts` line 30), but `index.js` still builds its tool schema with `Type.Object`/`Type.String`/`Type.Optional` → ReferenceError on every fanout load. Reproduced directly in the `v0.83.0-piri.2` image; the unit suite missed it because the baked-file tests assert content, not module resolution.

One-line fix: restore the import. No other change.

## Test plan

- Rebuilt-image smoke: `piri -p ... -e /opt/a2a-runner/piri-fanout-extension` loads and runs (verified after rebuild in the canary rerun — follow-up comment).

author: moka1980
body:
> «du kan kanskje legge til slett også, hvis de vil slette en policy, og ikke bare redigere»

## Hva som kan slettes, og hva som ikke kan

Det som kan slettes er et **utkast** — et forslag som ennå ikke binder noen. En policy som HAR styrt beslutninger fjernes ikke: da ville revisjonssporet pekt på noe som ikke finnes lenger. Derfor heter handlingen **«Forkast»**, ikke «Slett». Å avvikle en policy i kraft er en egen, styrt handling.

Databasen var alt klar — statusmaskinen i migrasjon 012 tillater `utkast → forkastet` og `validert → forkastet` og behandler `forkastet` som terminal. Det som manglet var tjenestefunksjon, rute og flate.

## Grensene som gjør det trygt

- Bare `utkast` og `validert`. Et **`godkjent`** utkast har fire øyne bak seg; å kaste den godkjenningen er en annen handling enn å rydde bort et forslag ingen har vurdert.
- **Aldri mens en runde er åpen eller klar.** Der er attestasjoner i omløp, og et forslag skal ikke kunne rives bort under godkjennerne mens de vurderer det. Knappen forsvinner, og tjenesten nekter uansett.
- Idempotensnøkkelen bindes til utkastversjonen, som ellers i modulen.
- Flaten krever bekreftelse — et irreversibelt valg skjer ikke på ett klikk — og bekreftelsen sier hvilket utkast det gjelder.

Scope er **`policy:write`**, ikke `policy:activate`: å forkaste et forslag endrer ingen fullmakt.

## Tester

**1111 python** (5 nye) + **221 node** (3 nye), begge kjørt to ganger.

| Kontroll (vakten reversert) | Rød test |
|---|---|
| åpen-runde-sjekken fjernet | runde-vakten |
| tilstandssjekken fjernet | «forkastet er terminalt» |
| bekreftelsesdialogen fjernet | «med bekreftelse først» |
| knappen vist også ved åpen runde | «finnes IKKE når en runde er åpen» |

## To ting testene fanget underveis

1. **Rutescope-registeret** (`test_pr008`) krevde at den nye ruten deklareres, og feilet til jeg gjorde det. Den kontrollen gjør nøyaktig jobben sin: en udeklarert rute er en rute uten scope-krav. Verdt å merke at den fanget det, ikke jeg.
2. **Flate-testen ventet på `.pa-kvittering` og fant `""`.** Kvitteringen fylles i en senere oppgave (live-området må rekke å bli registrert før teksten kommer — `4217a7f`), så den må vente på den FERDIGE boksen. Helperen `_ventKvittering` fantes allerede; jeg brukte den ikke først.

author: sdelmas
body:
## Summary

- Deletes `.github/workflows/sd-ai-command-pack-sync.yml`. The scheduled refresh has had nothing to do since the thin conversion: it ran `install.py "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" --force` against a tree whose pack payload now lives in the machine install, and `install.py <this repo> --check` reports `state: current`, so a forced run writes nothing. Keeping it meant a weekly job, a scoped `SD_AI_COMMAND_PACK_PR_TOKEN` secret, and a contract guarding both, all for a no-op. Refreshes are operator-initiated against the machine install from here on.
- Deletes the CI call to the PR-body scope guard for the same reason. The guard is not in this tree; the lane resolved it from an install a runner does not have and printed `skipped: no resolvable sd-ai-command-pack install` on every run. **The guard itself is untouched** — `.sd-ai-command-pack/pr-body-scope.json` and the prose that `tools/check_scope_heading_mirrors.py` validates remain the local authoring contract.

## Contract follow-through

Both deletions were pinned by `tools/check_ci_review_contract.py`, so removing the files alone would have failed CI:

- `REQUIRED_FILES` no longer names the workflow, and `_check_pack_sync` plus its five `test_pack_sync_*` tests are gone.
- The cross-workflow `actions/checkout` revision rule used the sync workflow as its second file; `codeql.yml` is the remaining peer and now plays that role in both the fixture and the mismatch test.
- The `("scheduled command-pack sync", ...)` docs needle is removed, along with the three PR-body-scope resolver needles.

`docs/DEVELOPMENT_CYCLE.md`, `.trellis/spec/amc/backend/testing-quality.md`, and `.trellis/spec/amc/backend/sd-review-kb-false-block.md` described the retired automation in the present tense and now say what is true. The last of those also claimed this repo vendors `scripts/*.py`, which stopped being true at the conversion. The dated `.trellis/audit/ledger.md` entry stays as the history it is.

Tooling/generated scope: `docs/repomix-map.md` is regenerated by `scripts/update_repomix`; it listed the deleted workflow.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/` — `2011 passed, 2 skipped in 249.65s`.
- [x] `pytest tests/test_ci_review_contract.py` — `85 passed`.
- [x] All four lightweight guards run clean: `check_ci_review_contract`, `check_copilot_instruction_contract`, `check_scope_heading_mirrors`, `check_guard_ci_coverage`.
- [x] `git grep` for `sd-ai-command-pack-sync`, `SD_AI_COMMAND_PACK_PR_TOKEN`, and `pack_sync` finds no live reference — only archived task records, journal entries, and the dated audit ledger, all of which are history.

author: heyong4725
body:
Closes the last open Phase-3 DoD row as **NOT MET at 2**, and with it Phase 3.

## Why this can be closed now rather than left pending

The verdict no longer depends on anything still open. PR #252's recovery can change the *count* but not the *outcome*, because its ceiling is 3:

| candidate | class | evalcard | under ADR-37's floor |
|---|---|---|---|
| `t2-scan-pose` | perception | 0.33 | refused (declares 0.0, measures 0.33) |
| `t2-scan-tsm` | decision | 0.0 | refused twice over |
| `ik-transfer-v2` | **motion** | **1.0** (min 0.75) | clears — a live candidate |

Even if #252's provenance confirms, its missing eval graphs are recovered, and `ik-transfer-v2` merges, the library reaches 3 against a DoD of ≥5. The row fails on arithmetic, independently of the provenance question — so leaving it open would only defer a conclusion already determined.

## What the number means, and what it does not

Stated in the report rather than left for a reader to infer, because "2 of 5" invites the wrong reading. It is **not** evidence that agents failed to produce reusable skills — they produced five, and H3 shows real cross-suite reuse (`s3-driver-v1` appears verbatim in a desk deliverable). Two things kept the library small, neither about agent capability:

1. **Retention** — three skills were authored in campaign worktrees the protocol never archived (#245). A library DoD counts artifacts that survive to review; the protocol did not make them survive.
2. **The tiers** — T2/T3 are unsolved at session budgets, so the skills authored against them scored 0.33 and 0.0. They are genuinely unproven, and ADR-37's floor refusing them is the floor working.

That reads consistently with H3's UNDECIDED verdict: **the ladder's difficulty spacing, not the library mechanism, is what this phase measured.**

## Also: I over-scoped my own earlier claim

The 2026-08-15 correction said the three sources were "gone", based on searching all 49 branches, the filesystem, and 51 dangling objects. That was exhaustive **for the operator checkout** and blind to other machines — and #252 has since staged source. Amended to the defensible statement: *not retrievable from the reviewed environment*, not *ceased to exist*.

## Smaller fix

The governance row still said two of three flags did not survive checking. #253 made it **all three** — corrected.

Docs only. ruff clean; `pytest -m unit` **1402 passed**; `env_hash` unmoved at `9b8d9080…`/73.

author: ayushkbhatia
body:
**GA4 has been recording nothing on the storefront.**

`(storefront)/layout.tsx` mounts `<GoogleAnalytics gaId={GA_MEASUREMENT_ID} />` and the measurement ID *is* configured in production — but the storefront Content-Security-Policy never listed `googletagmanager.com` on `script-src`, so the browser refuses `gtag/js` outright:

```
Loading the script 'https://www.googletagmanager.com/gtag/js?id=G-…'
violates the following Content Security Policy directive: "script-src
'self' 'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval' https://va.vercel-scripts.com …"
```

Observed live on https://indushydraulics.com/industries just now. The tag never loads: no pageview, no event, nothing.

**Why it went unnoticed.** The only symptom is a console violation. The site renders perfectly and the analytics dashboard is simply empty — which reads as "no traffic yet", not as a bug.

`connect-src` needed the collect endpoints too. Adding `script-src` alone loads the tag but then blocks every beacon it sends, which fails identically from the dashboard's point of view.

## Deliberately storefront-only

`ADMIN_CSP` still carries **no** third-party analytics origin, because admin URLs embed customer ids, RFQ codes and quote codes. `csp-analytics.test.ts` asserts **both** halves — that the storefront allows the tag, and that admin allows none of it — so a future "keep the two policies in sync" edit cannot quietly turn that into a data leak. It also asserts the parse didn't silently return an empty string, which would make every other assertion pass vacuously.

Verified by blanking the origin and confirming the test fails.

## Provenance

Pre-existing — not introduced by the design-v2 work. Found while verifying that #176 had deployed cleanly to production.

Gate: `typecheck` · `lint` (4 pre-existing warnings, 0 errors) · **591 tests**.
