author: alek7eeey
body:
# feat(acp): expose subagent activity via `_omp/agents/*` extension methods

Adds an ACP extension surface mirroring the Agent Hub roster, so clients of `omp acp` can query, live-track, and read subagent work:

- **`_omp/agents/list`** (request): current agent snapshot — main + subagents, advisors excluded — with `id`, `kind`, `parentId`, `status`, `sessionFile`, `activity` (one-line work gist while running), `resolvedModel`, and persisted usage `metrics` (tokens/requests/tools/cost/duration).
- **`_omp/agents/update`** (notification): debounced (100 ms) full-snapshot push after `initialize` and on every registry change (spawn, status transition, usage metadata, removal), so clients can render subagent lifecycle without polling.
- **`_omp/agents/progress`** (notification): live per-agent work stream — `lastIntent`, `currentTool`, `currentToolArgs`, recent output lines, and spend — mirrored from the task executor's `AgentProgress` on `tool_execution_update`, so clients render subagent work in real time.
- **`_omp/agents/messages`** (request): byte-offset paginated transcript read of a registered agent's session file (complete lines only), so clients can surface the subagent's own reasoning (thinking blocks) as it runs. Only files claimed by registered agents are readable — never arbitrary paths.
- **Wire hardening**: task tool-calls are tagged with `toolName` on the wire, and `tool_call` statuses stay terminal (late async progress cannot reopen a finished call).

All routes go through the existing `extMethod`/`extNotification` extension hooks and stay inert for clients that do not implement them. The registry subscription is released on `dispose()`; delivery failures are logged, never thrown.

## Why

The TUI Agent Hub, collab guests, and `history://` already expose subagent activity; ACP clients (e.g. editors, web frontends) had no equivalent. This closes that gap using the same `AgentRegistry` the other surfaces read, serialized as a wire snapshot documented in `docs/acp-agents.md`.

## Verification

- `bun test packages/coding-agent/test/acp-agent.test.ts` — 63 pass (roster + telemetry; debounced `_omp/agents/update` on spawn/status/dispose driven with fake timers; progress mirroring; transcript pagination/reset semantics).
- Full `bun test packages/coding-agent/test/acp-*` — 194 pass, stable across repeated runs.
- `tsgo -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` and `biome check` clean.
- End-to-end smoke against a real `omp acp` child: `initialize` → `_omp/agents/list` → initial `_omp/agents/update` notification, live `_omp/agents/progress` during a task-tool run, and `_omp/agents/messages` streaming thinking blocks — all observed on the wire, and consumed by an external chat frontend that renders subagent cards with live reasoning.

author: fmxexpress
body:
Follow-up to #571. That PR merged with only its **first** commit — the `/v1/responses` fix landed on the branch afterwards and never reached main, so this is a fresh branch off current main carrying it.

Confirmed against main: only two of the three session-keyed handlers set the key.

```
$ git show origin/main:...Gateway.Server.pas | grep -n 'SteeringKey :='
5757:  LoopCfg.SteeringKey   := ReqSessionId(ARequest);   HandleChat
7098:    LoopCfg.SteeringKey := ReqSession;               HandleChatCompletions
                                                          HandleResponses -- missing
```

## The gap

`/v1/responses` runs a session-keyed loop (`RunCheckpointedLoop` with `ReqSessionId`) but never set `SteeringKey`, so it had the identical failure #571 describes: a steer aimed at a running `/v1/responses` turn is accepted with `{"ok":true,"pending":1}`, **ignored by that turn**, and left on disk for whichever turn drains next.

**Verified in the relay on the current merged base** — not carried over from the earlier run: steer sent mid-turn, present in the running turn's system prompt at the next iteration, queue empty afterwards.

With this, every session-keyed loop in the gateway sets the key: `HandleChat`, `HandleChatCompletions`, `HandleResponses`.

## The rest of the audit (unchanged from the commit message)

Every production tool-loop invocation was checked, not just the endpoints originally examined.

- **`RunDesktopTurn`** — not a gap. Takes no session at all (`SystemPrompt`/`Prompt` only), so there is no key to steer with and no queue to leak from.
- **The seven channels** (Telegram, Discord, Email, IRC, LINE, Matrix, WhatsApp) — not the same bug. None reference steering, which the Steering unit header already documents as intended: channels get their own key *"when they wire concurrent polling (currently CLI-only)"*. They poll serially — the `TThread` is the poller, not a per-message worker — so a mid-turn message cannot reach a running channel loop; it waits at the transport. And since nothing drains a channel key, there is no leak vector. Wiring them is a feature, not a fix.
- **Heartbeat, Subagent, SubagentBg** — not applicable. Background and child loops; a subagent draining its parent's steering queue would be a bug in the other direction.

## Residual, recorded not fixed

`/v1/steer` accepts an arbitrary session string and queues unconditionally, so a steer for a session that never runs a turn sits on disk indefinitely. Unbounded but harmless, and separate from the reported symptom.

Full suite: **340 assertions, 0 failures.**

author: aiagencyos
body:
## The follow-up #200 promised

[#200](https://github.com/AiAgencyOs/AgencyOs/pull/200) closed the invoices DELETE surface and **deferred** the parallel one on `sales.proposals` / `projects.deliverables` / `projects.handovers` — its own change-log row said they "need the same care in a focused follow-up rather than a rushed guard — recorded, not rushed," pending validation of the `opportunities`/`projects` CASCADE-parent deletion semantics. **This validates them and closes all five** (`opportunities`, `projects`, `proposals`, `deliverables`, `handovers`).

## The hole

Each of the five carries the `ALL` write policy with **DELETE granted to `authenticated`**, so an end-user could **erase** the record and its §16 history / audit rather than closing it through the removal-terminal state every one already has:

| table | terminal state |
|---|---|
| `sales.opportunities` | `lost` |
| `projects.projects` | `cancelled` |
| `sales.proposals` | `superseded` / `rejected` / `lapsed` |
| `projects.deliverables` | `superseded` |
| `projects.handovers` | `cancelled` |

The application never `.delete()`s any of them.

## The cascade analysis #200 deferred — now settled

The only edges that **cascade-delete** into the five are:
- `core.organizations` → all five (identity-less teardown → **exempt**), and
- the intra-set `projects → {deliverables, handovers}` and `opportunities → proposals` — whose parents are **now guarded too**, so an end-user can't trigger them either.

The parents that *do* grant end-user DELETE — `crm.leads`, `core.client_accounts` — reach the five only by `SET NULL` / `RESTRICT` (`deltype=n`/`r`), **never cascade-delete**. So **no legitimate end-user cascade breaks** (verified: deleting a lead/client_account does not delete a guarded row).

## The fix

A shared `core.reject_end_user_delete()` `BEFORE DELETE` trigger (the #200 shape, generalized): refuses when `auth.uid()` is not null; the service role and the `ON DELETE CASCADE` from a deleted organization stay exempt.

## Proof

- **Red-proofed** live on all five: authenticated ops_admin DELETE refused, row survives.
- **Positive**: service-role delete + full `org → opportunity → proposal` / `org → project → deliverable + handover` teardown cascade both work.
- Live assertions added: `db:verify:deliverables` §6b, `db:verify:handover` §8, `db:verify:quotations` §9.
- `tests/records-are-closed-not-deleted.test.ts` (new) pins **all six** guards (these five + invoices) as `BEFORE DELETE`, so a regeneration cannot silently reopen the verb.
- All eleven verify scripts exercising these tables green, including `verify-requirement-proposal` run against the app on the verify DB (the §Q concurrent-runner section passed clean this run).

## Gates
typecheck · lint · secrets · **1,715 tests** · restore rehearsal green; fresh `db reset` applies all **114** migrations in order.

body:
## Summary

Release `dev` → `main`. This is the first production release since 2026-06-15 (PR #91) — 236 commits and 80 merged PRs, covering the whole feature train plus the design/a11y queue that was blocked behind a red CI gate for five weeks.

**Stacks liquidation health (the differentiator)**
- Arkadiko liquidation-health adapter, alongside the existing Zest + Granite adapters
- Cron worker delivering liquidation web-push alerts, with the sweep bounded against Cloudflare limits and made observable
- Supabase schema, auth, and web-push opt-in backing the alerts

**Stackr Wallet — native signer app**
- Expo + Tamagui + Privy app with onboarding, multi-chain HD signer core, and a backup & keys section with recovery-phrase reveal
- Stackr Link: end-to-end-encrypted pairing between the wallet and stackr.ie, relaying sign requests
- Tamagui design system for the native wallet

**Portfolio & assets**
- Gold and manual asset holdings, included in the dashboard total
- SUI as a fifth chain, incl. Slush wallet connect for address discovery
- NFTs & collectibles: normalized schema, Stacks SIP-9 adapter, media renderer, dedicated `/collectibles` route
- Markets page defaults to live data

**Security & platform**
- Same-origin proxies for Hiro, Alchemy, Helius, Etherscan and Alpha Vantage so no vendor key reaches the browser; fleet-wide proxy rate limiting + edge caching
- Tightened Content-Security-Policy; central address guard; route and global error boundaries
- Dependency bumps clearing the `pnpm audit --prod --audit-level high` gate (#193)

**Testing**
- Shared Gherkin BDD specs with a web Playwright runner and Maestro mobile flows
- Real end-to-end Stackr Link pairing test; MetaMask connect e2e revived behind a connector-level mock

**Design & accessibility**
- Chain colors, order book highlights and allocation bars all sourced from design tokens instead of drifted hex maps
- Themed `Select` replacing native selects across Add Wallet / Add Holding / Markets / Settings / Account
- Visible focus rings on holdings, activity and collectibles links; active-route indicator in header and mobile nav (incl. nested routes)
- Real error/failure states for the price chart, collectibles, portfolio total and liquidation health, replacing false empty states

## Linked issue

Refs #145 — unblocks the grant-readiness checklist item "stackr.ie deployed from main with the merged train".

## Verification

- All 80 PRs in this range merged green: `checks` (lint, typecheck, unit, `pnpm audit`), 3 Playwright shards, and the Cloudflare Workers build
- `dev` tip `ee70dfc` is the last of these merges; no open PRs remain against `dev`

## Note before merging

Merging this deploys to stackr.ie via the Cloudflare Git integration. It is the first deploy in 62 days, so worth a smoke pass on the live site afterwards — particularly the proxy routes (Hiro / Alchemy / Helius / Etherscan / Alpha Vantage), which need their production env vars present, and Supabase auth, which needs its production keys.

author: rankly-rgb
body:
Pièce 3, volet crons (étape 5, **partie code uniquement** — la suppression de `self-monitor` n'est pas dans cette PR, voir le dernier paragraphe).

Sentry surveille désormais l'exécution planifiée elle-même : le cron pointe au début et à la fin, et c'est **l'absence de pointage** à l'heure attendue qui déclenche l'alerte. C'est la différence de fond avec `self-monitor`, structurellement incapable de signaler quoi que ce soit quand il ne tournait pas lui-même — exactement ce qui s'est produit pendant cinq mois (issue #38).

## Contenu

| Fichier | Rôle |
|---|---|
| `_shared/sentry-cron.ts` | `startCronCheckin(slug)` → `finish('ok' \| 'error')` |
| `sync-stripe/index.ts` | monitor `nightly-sync` (jobid 38, `0 2 * * *`) |
| `calculate-scores/index.ts` | monitor `nightly-scoring` (jobid 39, `0 3 * * *`) |
| `supabase/tests/sentry-cron.test.ts` | 8 tests |

Les deux schedules ont été relus en base (`cron.job`), pas repris du guide.

## Points de conception

**Pas de nouveau secret.** L'URL de pointage est dérivée du `SENTRY_DSN` déjà configuré — un DSN porte déjà la clé publique, l'hôte et l'id de projet, qui sont exactement les trois composants de l'URL de check-in. Un secret de plus serait un secret de plus à garder synchronisé. Échappatoire si Sentry change ce format : `SENTRY_CRON_URL_<SLUG>` prime sur la dérivation.

**Le pointage terminal réutilise l'`id` du pointage initial.** Sans cet id, Sentry crée deux check-ins indépendants : le premier resterait `in_progress` et finirait marqué en timeout — une fausse alerte à chaque exécution pourtant réussie. C'est le piège principal de cette pièce.

**`buildCheckinUrl` retourne `null` plutôt qu'une URL approximative** quand le DSN manque ou ne parse pas. Ne pas pointer laisse le monitor signaler l'absence ; pointer dans le vide ferait croire que la surveillance est en place.

**Rien ne peut faire échouer un cron** : aucune fonction ne lève, timeout 5 s, et sans DSN tout le module est inerte.

**Pointage uniquement pour le run planifié**, reconnu à l'absence d'`organization_id` dans le body (les deux jobs postent `{}` — vérifié dans `cron.job.command`). Sans ce filtre, les ré-invocations par org de `sync-stripe` produiraient autant de pointages que d'orgs, et un rafraîchissement manuel depuis l'UI fabriquerait un pointage hors planning — le bruit qui ferait passer un run planifié manquant pour un run réussi.

**`cronOutcome` démarre à `'error'`** et n'est repassé à `'ok'` que sur la sortie de succès : un chemin d'échec oublié se traduit par une alerte, jamais par un silence rassurant. Les deux sorties d'échec en amont du `try/finally` (clé Stripe absente, verrou déjà tenu) clôturent explicitement en `'error'`. Un org en échec ou en timeout ne compte pas comme un run réussi, même quand la fonction répond 200 avec le détail.

## Vérifications

`npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm run test` (**1071 tests**, dont 8 nouveaux). Les 69 fichiers Edge reparsés sans erreur de syntaxe.

**Non vérifié ici — c'est la preuve de l'étape** : aucun pointage réel n'a atteint Sentry. Le code n'est pas déployé et les deux monitors n'existent pas encore côté Sentry.

## Pourquoi `self-monitor` n'est pas supprimé dans cette PR

En relisant son code avant de le supprimer : sur ses 7 blocs, 3 sont de l'alerte (croissance DLQ, scoring périmé, échecs de sync) — bien remplacés par Sentry, et mieux. Mais **3 autres sont des tâches de ménage que Sentry Crons ne fait pas** : auto-fail des `data_syncs` bloquées en `running` > 15 min, auto-fail des `playbook_executions` bloquées, purge DLQ > 30 jours. Une ligne restée `running` ne se résout jamais seule.

(Le 7ᵉ bloc, la libération des verrous cron expirés, est bien redondant : `acquireCronLock` purge déjà son propre verrou expiré avant d'insérer — un verrou périmé ne bloque donc jamais durablement un cron. Vérifié dans `_shared/cron-lock.ts`.)

Supprimer la fonction est une action de production, et cette découverte change ce qu'elle coûte. Consigné au parking lot, décision à Naima.

body:
…t it promised not to

Blueprint line 523 is one sentence with three clauses: deactivating a client with open tickets warns, blocks new tickets, and never hides the historical ones. The middle clause looked like the task and is the one part that cannot be built — POST /tickets has no controller, and B-028 already wrote both refusals into createTicket's contract description. What was outstanding was a hole in each of the other two.

The third clause was broken on S-15. TicketListPage's client filter read useListClients({ isActive: true }), so a deactivated client left the filter and every ticket they had ever raised became unreachable through the one control that reaches them — clause two breaking clause three, silently. The create form still sends the parameter and must: same operation, opposite answers, and the question that separates them is "new or historical", not "active or not". Now stated on the parameter in the contract.

The warning was on one of the two paths that deactivate a client. S-33's Status select reaches INACTIVE in two clicks and saved without a word, on a page that had already loaded openTicketCount. DeactivationWarningDialog moved out of ClientBulkStatusBar rather than being copied — one consequence described twice is how two descriptions start disagreeing. The bulk warning also read the current page, a limitation B-025 documented and left; this grid builds selections across pages on purpose, so a client ticked three pages ago went through unwarned. It now reads every row the grid has seen.

Both new-ticket gates now come from ticketEligibility.ts — B-028's primary contact and B-029's deactivation — failing closed on an absent field and reporting deactivation before a missing contact. It also backs a submit-time refusal, which getOptionDisabled structurally cannot: Save & Create Another keeps a clientId across many tickets, so a selection routinely outlives the deactivation that invalidated it. With no server behind POST /tickets, that module is the only enforcement in the system. Flagged for Stream C, along with the two edits in their files.

No backend production change and no migration. openTicketCounts, lastTicketDates and TicketListSpecs never looked at clients.status — correct by omission, which is what a later change removes without noticing. Three ITs now assert it through the deactivation: the same figures before and after, the ticket rows untouched, and all three readings of ?isActive= at once.

Two fixture findings. No ticket had ever belonged to a deactivated client (clientId: i % 3 === 0 ? null : i % 3 only yields 1 and 2, both ACTIVE), which is why S-15 went unnoticed for three tasks. And mulberry32 was seeded once at module load and never rewound, so each resetDb() continued the stream: adding one test made a C-016 assertion fail three tests later in another describe, both passing alone. Rewound in createDb() and flagged for Stream D.

author: florianriquelme
body:
Builds every ruling [#76](https://github.com/FlorianRiquelme/grind/issues/76) enumerates — the
twelve [#5](https://github.com/FlorianRiquelme/grind/issues/5) closed after the base — in one PR,
in the modules that already exist. Twenty-one units in dependency order, each an atomic commit
that left `just verify` green.

Plan: `docs/plans/2026-08-15-001-feat-leg-1-map-rulings-plan.md`.

## What changed

**Dispatch's preconditions.** The `Handoff SHA` row parses to a bare SHA by a hex-and-length scan,
so a Job writing parenthetical context stops firing a warning nobody reads. Dispatch then fetches
in the declared clone and asks one answerable question — *does this worktree contain the Handoff
SHA* — over `merge-base --is-ancestor` in **both** directions, which is what separates *behind*
from *diverged* and lets the refusal say *fast-forward and re-dispatch*. Run 2's worktree was
behind and fast-forwardable at second zero; the string comparison said the same thing there as it
says when everything is fine. A failed fetch is a note, never a refusal or a clean bill of health.
An Anchor artifact that is not on disk refuses — presence only, never shape.

**What Grind writes.** `QUEUE_LABEL` is gone. `ready-for-agent` is one of the five canonical triage
roles, so Dispatch was erasing a triage fact to record a queue fact (ADR-0012). Grind now writes
comments on the Job issue and nothing else, on any repo, and `tests/topology.rs` carries the
absence of every classifying flag.

**What the Run is told.** *No human present* becomes *unsupervised*; *this slice is transcription,
not design* goes, and *do not re-open decisions the Anchor records* survives it. The Handoff SHA
paragraph bounds output rather than reading. The prompt asks for a narrative by category and for
`Closes #<job>` with licence to decline — and nothing reads either back, asserted as an absence.
An optional `Intent` row interpolates only when present.

**The budget.** A **Wait** is an Attempt that did no work: it parsed, cost nothing and took at most
one turn. Derived, never persisted, and keyed on work done rather than cause — `parse_ok == false`
is never a Wait, which is what keeps a crash loop from being free. Waits spend no attempt budget
and a run of them is bounded by its own counter, read off the persisted list so a reboot cannot
reset it. The spend ceiling ADR-0010 withdrew is gone from the Job, the record, the conditions and
every invocation.

**A Blocker** stops a Run at once and leaves it resumable: the same denied invocation on two
consecutive working Attempts that both failed to advance, with an `Unobservable` progress reading
never firing it. It is a supervisor state and a policy stop, never a `Verdict` variant.

**Observing the Run rather than the repo.** The PR is found by head commit with the branch lookup
as a fallback; the rollup resolves against the PR that lookup found. Artifact listings are scoped
to the Run's own diff, so a fresh Run stops reading `planned` at dispatch on a repo where someone
else merged a plan. Base drift arrives as a count plus overlapping paths, three-valued. The fan-out
matcher accepts both tool names, and a transcript with tool calls and no recognised spawn reads
*could not observe* rather than `none`. Fan-out is recorded per Attempt as two integers. A rough
verify-coverage estimate names the changed paths no contracted step covers.

**The Handback** renders the fresh verdict in the top position and never the recorded state, from a
fact set `cli` and the supervisor both gather through one function. Count rows are gone, pointers
move to a trailing block, five things surface only when there is a surprise, and rows that could
not be observed group where the eye can see they are a different kind of row. A **second renderer**
over that same fact set posts a markdown comment on the Job issue at every terminal state —
appended, never edited, best-effort, and carrying each observation's mark and never its `Reason`.

**Surviving a reboot.** `supervisor.log` lands in the run directory. `grind resume --all` re-enters
every cut-off Run concurrently, one detached child each, skipping any whose worktree is dirty and
never touching a stopped one. A launchd plist and a systemd unit ship in `dist/`, both carrying the
machinery that keeps the spawned supervisors alive past the one-shot's own exit, and `grind doctor`
gains its first platform-branching check for whether the one-shot is **loaded**.

## What it does not do

Nothing gates. No verdict variant means rejected, blocked or failed; no summary boolean sits over
the fan-out counts, the drift, the coverage estimate or the verify contract. `tests/topology.rs`
and `tests/compile_fail.rs` pass unchanged and unrelaxed, no directory exists under `src/`, and the
twelve denial globs are byte-identical to `CLAUDE.md`'s.

## Worth a reviewer's attention

- **Three commits are unsigned** — `a413069`, `731d326`, `a4a2b2d`. Commit signing broke partway
  through and the work was committed rather than held. They want re-signing before merge.
- **`resume --all` is the first place Grind spawns Grind**, and a detached child that outlives its
  parent is the exact behaviour the sandbox had no scenario for until now.
- **The systemd process-group behaviour is the one piece of real machinery here**, and no test
  reaches a service manager. Getting it wrong kills every Run seconds after boot, silently.
- **The Blocker ships against a shape neither recorded Run exhibited.** #76's named Run 2 replay
  test does not survive its own evidence; the substitution is recorded in
  [#78](https://github.com/FlorianRiquelme/grind/issues/78).
- **Handback fidelity is not scored yet.** [#77](https://github.com/FlorianRiquelme/grind/issues/77)
  owns re-scoring it against the first Run dispatched after this lands.

body: A git knowledge base whose token expired (or whose repo moved) could only be removed and re-added, losing its config and - for SSH sources - the installed deploy key. The PATCH endpoint already accepted uri/ref/api_key/http_username with verified-invalidation and server-side re-check on enable (docs/API_CONTRACT.md line 317), so this is UI only: an Edit button on git rows opening a modal with name/URL/branch, the write-only token + username fields for HTTP sources (blank keeps the stored token), and the existing deploy public key re-shown for SSH sources (never regenerated). Saving immediately re-runs the connection check and shows the verdict; a disabled source can be enabled in place once it passes. Validated with a full app image build (tsc).

author: timurbazhirov
body:
## Summary

Two phases of the Job Designer UX update ([SOF-8023](https://mat3ra.atlassian.net/browse/SOF-8023), [plan](https://github.com/mat3ra/job-designer/blob/claude/jd-ui-ux-improvements-99w9fg/plan/review/2026-08-17-Job-Designer-Phase-2-Guided-Designer.md)), both in the compute form: **1.1** stops the form complaining before the reader has done anything, and **2.3** gives it a cluster choice worth making and says what the answer costs.

> 2.3 needs a `@mat3ra/cove` release carrying `SelectableCard`, `MetricTile`, `SegmentedMeter` and `NumericStepperInput` (mat3ra/cove#97). Merge order is cove → this.

## 1.1 Progressive validation

A new job opens the Compute tab on **four red "The field is required" errors** — complaints about things the reader has not been given a chance to do yet. The form validates live, so every required field reports itself on first paint. Errors are now shown only for fields the reader has actually edited.

Touched fields are tracked from the field id RJSF already passes as `onChange`'s second argument — no diffing, no dependency on widget internals. `customValidate` then skips `addError` for fields not in that set. The decision logic is a pure module (`src/utils/touchedFields.ts`) with unit tests.

A new **`showAllErrors`** prop (default `false`) reveals everything at once for the cases where the whole form must answer for itself — submit, and the job designer's preflight.

One subtlety worth flagging: the `RJSForm` is keyed on `showAllErrors`. RJSF only re-validates when its schema or form data change, so flipping the prop alone left the *previous* validation result on screen — the toggle silently did nothing. The remount forces a fresh pass. It happens on submit, not while typing, so the cost isn't felt.

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Empty compute, first paint | `Time Limit`, `Queue`, `Nodes`, `Cores` all required | **no errors** |
| After clearing the Nodes field | that field's error | that field's error (unchanged) |
| Empty compute, `showAllErrors` | — | **identical to the "before" column** |

The last row is the point of the table: `showAllErrors` reproduces today's behavior exactly, so nothing is lost — only deferred. I confirmed the "before" column by stashing the change and re-running the same script against the original code.

## 2.3 Cluster cards, presets and a live estimate

The step asked for a cluster, a queue, nodes, cores and a walltime as five schema fields — a dropdown listing cluster *names* and nothing to choose between them on, four required fields empty on arrival, and no statement anywhere of what the answers add up to. A reader could configure 4 × 32 × 12 h without being told that is 1536 core-hours, three times their quota, until the run failed.

Behind **`useComputeCards`** (default off), four fields move out of the schema form into their own surface above it:

- **`ClusterCards`** — each cluster as a card carrying price, max walltime and typical queue wait, so the choice is a comparison rather than a guess. Selecting one also picks that cluster's first real queue, since a queue chosen on the previous cluster is meaningless on this one.
- **`ComputeResources`** — presets (Debug / Standard / Production) **clamped to the cluster's published limits**, so the button that exists to avoid an invalid configuration cannot produce one; bounded steppers for nodes and cores; walltime as the `HH:MM:SS` the scheduler takes. Typed values past a limit are allowed and flagged inline, on the same touched-field rule as 1.1.
- **`ComputeEstimatePanel`** — core-hours, cost and queue wait as metric tiles over a quota meter. Each degrades on its own: core-hours need only the job, cost needs a published price, the meter needs an injected allowance. A tile with nothing behind it shows an em dash, never a zero.

### How it stays out of trouble

- The four fields are **hidden, not removed**, so the ESSE schema still validates them and nothing downstream learns a second shape.
- Writes go through the same `handleFormUpdate` path as a keystroke in the schema form — same touched-field bookkeeping, same validate-then-`onUpdate` gate.
- **Espresso's advanced options are untouched.** The group left holding only two documentation links is retitled *Documentation*, because calling it "Cluster" would send readers looking for a picker that moved.

### `utils/computeEstimate` is public API on purpose

Three surfaces need the same answer to "what does this job cost" — the panel here, job-designer's context-strip chip, and its submit preflight's budget check — and three implementations would be worse than none. It lives here, beside the form that holds the live values, and is exported. job-designer carries an identical copy with a `TODO` to delete it once this ships.

## Verification

`npm test` green (44 tests), `tsc` clean, lint clean. Measured in the running demo rather than assumed:

- presets fill the fields and the estimate follows synchronously;
- **Production on a 2-node cluster applies as 2 × 16 × 6 h**, not the nominal 4 × 32 × 24 h;
- the Nodes stepper disables at the cluster's limit, while a typed 24 h walltime reports *"Over the 6 h queue limit"* and the meter reads *"over by 268 core·h"*;
- toggling the surface off brings all four schema fields back.

## Demo changes

- **"Start empty"** reproduces the state a new job actually starts in — the case 1.1 exists for.
- **"Show all errors"** and **"Cards + estimate"** switches flip between the modes.
- Mock cluster metadata and a quota, standing in for what the webapp would inject.
- `LOAD JSON` now remounts the form. `ComputeForm` derives its form data in its constructor, so loading JSON previously updated the state but left the form untouched — a pre-existing demo bug.

author: matsvarn
body: ## What Changed OpenCode Go sessions no longer send a duplicated `opencode-go/` prefix in the runtime `modelID`. - Inventory slugs are built from the catalog map key (`Object.entries(provider.models)`), not `model.id`, so discovery matches `opencode models` and `getModel(providerID, modelID)`. - `parseOpenCodeModelSlug` is a first-slash split only. That is OpenCode's own `parseModel` shape. - `toOpenCodeRuntimeModel` peels a repeated `provider/` prefix **only** for hosted OpenCode catalogs (`opencode`, `opencode-go`), whose keys are documented as bare IDs. Other providers can legitimately use a key that starts with `provider/` (e.g. `huggingface/huggingface/CodeBERTa` → `{ providerID: "huggingface", modelID: "huggingface/CodeBERTa" }`). - Chat `sendTurn` and text generation both call `toOpenCodeRuntimeModel`. The UI, picker, persistence, and resume cursor still store `opencode-go/deepseek-v4-pro` (and the same shape for `kimi-k2.7-code`). ## Why [Issue #3571](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/issues/3571) reports `ProviderModelNotFoundError` for OpenCode Go models. Two observed request shapes: ```text Model not found: opencode-go/opencode-go/deepseek-v4-pro. Did you mean: deepseek-v4-pro, …? Model not found: opencode-go/deepseek-v4-pro. Did you mean: deepseek-v4-pro? ``` Current OpenCode (`getModel(providerID, modelID)`) looks up `s.providers[providerID].models[modelID]`. The error formatter always prints `providerID/modelID`. Official Go docs use config `opencode-go/` and API model IDs such as `deepseek-v4-pro` and `kimi-k2.7-code`. On current `origin/main`, a well-formed application slug `opencode-go/deepseek-v4-pro` already serializes to `{ providerID: "opencode-go", modelID: "deepseek-v4-pro" }`. The remaining bug is the doubled prefix: 1. Inventory used `${provider.id}/${model.id}`. When `model.id` is already namespaced, the picker/session slug becomes `opencode-go/opencode-go/deepseek-v4-pro`. 2. First-slash parse then sent `modelID: "opencode-go/deepseek-v4-pro"`, which `getModel` rejects. An earlier revision stripped a duplicated prefix for **every** provider. That is wrong for a legitimate catalog key that starts with `providerID/` (Hugging Face). Prefix repair is now limited to hosted OpenCode catalogs whose keys are bare. PR #5251 is OpenCode 2 preview support and does not change this 1.x serialization path. ### Why this seam | Option | Rejected because | | --- | --- | | Normalize in the UI / model picker | Duplicates provider-specific runtime rules on every client; resume and text generation still serialize independently. | | Change the shared `provider/model` contract | Breaks OpenCode display, persistence, and every other provider that needs the namespace. | | Strip duplicate prefixes for every OpenCode provider | Breaks catalogs whose map key already starts with `provider/` (`huggingface/huggingface/CodeBERTa`). | | **Inventory map key + hosted-only runtime strip** | New inventory uses the lookup key OpenCode actually indexes. Persisted doubled Go/Zen slugs are repaired at the adapter boundary without rewriting other catalogs. | ### Compatibility - OpenCode Go: `{ providerID: "opencode-go", modelID: "deepseek-v4-pro" }` (and `kimi-k2.7-code`). Doubled persisted slugs are repaired. - OpenCode Zen: doubled `opencode/opencode/gpt-5.4` is repaired the same way; well-formed `opencode/gpt-5.4` is unchanged. - OpenRouter-style IDs with slashes (`openrouter/qwen/qwen3-coder`) keep `modelID: "qwen/qwen3-coder"`. - Hugging Face slash catalog keys keep `modelID: "huggingface/CodeBERTa"`. - Unknown `acme/custom-model` is passed through. - Bare `deepseek-v4-pro` still fails with the existing `provider/model` validation error. - New sessions and resume `sendTurn` share the same helper. ## Tests and commands Red on pre-fix `main` (fake OpenCode client, no credentials): - Doubled Go slug received `modelID: "opencode-go/deepseek-v4-pro"`. - Resume doubled Go slug received `modelID: "opencode-go/kimi-k2.7-code"`. - Inventory received slug `opencode-go/opencode-go/deepseek-v4-pro`. Green after this revision: ```bash vp test run \ apps/server/src/provider/Layers/OpenCodeAdapter.test.ts \ apps/server/src/provider/Layers/OpenCodeProvider.test.ts \ apps/server/src/provider/opencodeRuntime.cliParsers.test.ts # 68 passed vp test run apps/server/src/textGeneration/OpenCodeTextGeneration.test.ts # 9 passed vp run --filter t3 typecheck vp lint ``` Use the workspace `vp` (vite-plus 0.2.2), not a newer global CLI. ## Risk / rollout - Low: OpenCode-only serialization and inventory slug construction. - Persisted doubled Go/Zen slugs start working without a data migration. - Well-formed slugs were already correct; this does not change their runtime request. - Remaining uncertainty: a correctly split `{ providerID: "opencode-go", modelID: "deepseek-v4-pro" }` can still fail if the spawned OpenCode server does not have `opencode-go` in its live provider map (auth/catalog). That is outside this serialization fix. Not retested against a live OpenCode Go subscription. ## Checklist - [x] This PR is small and focused - [x] I explained what changed and why - [x] I included before/after screenshots for any UI changes (not a UI change) - [x] I included a video for animation/interaction changes (not applicable) Status: DRAFT — NOT READY FOR REVIEW.

author: watanabe-kf1983
body:
## Summary

A build can now be handed values from the command line and from an MCP
agent, alongside the environment channel that shipped in #415:

```bash
mood build . --var git_commit_id=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD) --var channel=nightly
```

```jinja2
Built from {{ build_info("vars.git_commit_id", "(dev)") }}
```

`--var` is repeatable and available on `build` and `watch` — the preview
server renders a template with the value in place rather than its
fallback. The MCP `build` tool takes the same cargo as a `vars` mapping.

Both channels merge onto what `MOOD_VARS_*` injected, winning ties. The
merge happens after the config is constructed
(`config.with_injected_vars(...)`) rather than through
`ProjectConfig(vars=...)`: an init argument outranks the settings sources
whole, so it would replace what the environment supplied instead of
merging with it.

**Names are taken as written, not lowercased.** The environment channel
lowercases what it decodes because environment variable names are
uppercase by convention; a command line and a JSON argument carry no such
convention to undo. Passing them through also means a dotted name —
`--var ci.run_id=7` — reaches the store as `vars.ci.run_id`, which the
environment channel has no spelling for.

Only the first `=` splits an assignment, so a URL keeps the ones in its
query string. A name with no `=`, or an empty name, stops the run before
the project directory is looked at, with a message that names the
expected form. Typer offers no built-in `NAME=VALUE` type
(`list[tuple[str, str]]` is rejected as a complex sub-type, and
`typer.Option(parser=...)` discards the parser's message and reports only
the offending token), so the parse is a handful of lines in `cli.py`.

The reference gives `vars` a top-level section of its own rather than a
subsection of Configuration overrides: it is cargo the caller hands to
templates, not a configuration key with a default to override.

This completes the supply channels; `manifest.*` (#7) is the remaining
piece of the task.

## Test plan

- [x] `make ci` passes locally
- [x] `MOOD_VARS_CI_RUN_URL=... mood build showcase/starter --var
git_commit_id=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD) --var "note=a=b"` — the
colophon lists all three, with `vars.note` intact as `a=b`
- [x] `mood watch showcase/starter --out-dir ... --var channel=preview` —
the published colophon carries `vars.channel` beside `processor.command |
watch`
- [x] `mood build showcase/starter --var oops` — the error names the
expected form and exits 1
- [x] The CLI test fails as intended when the call site is rewritten to
`ProjectConfig(vars=...)`: the environment's row disappears from the
colophon while the `--var` rows remain

## Checks

- [x] `make ci` passes locally
- [x] If user-visible behavior changed, `docs/reference/` (and
`docs/guides.md` when relevant) are updated to match — `cli.md` gains the
`--var` option under `build` / `watch` and promotes Injected values to a
top-level section covering all three channels; `template.md` follows the
anchor
- [x] If built-in resources under `src/another_mood/resources/schemas/`
changed, the corresponding appendix in `docs/reference/` is in sync —
unchanged

author: clkao
body:
Stack layer on top of #719. Entity `b8ewpvd65epkckvng0n38809`.

## What this changes

FO write authority is decided entirely by path. `«write.classify»` answers "may I
write this path", and for any entity under `.spacedock-state/**` the answer is
unconditionally `allowed-state`. No rule in the contract asked whether the *work*
belongs in this workflow, so the filing decision was governed by a mechanism that
cannot express the question. The failure is not the FO writing where it may not —
it is the FO writing what does not belong, in a place it is fully authorized to
write.

This adds a `## Workflow Fit Gate` section to `fo-write-core.md` between the
mutation gate and the write-scope list, plus one sentence on the `New entity
files` bullet. Reading order becomes: may I write this path, does this work
belong here, here is what I may write. `fo-write-core.md` is the file every FO
reads in its own host event immediately before its first mutation, which is
exactly the moment before `spacedock new`.

No command grammar change, no stored-format change, no classifier-table change,
no dev README edit. `«write.classify»`'s outcome for every path is identical
before and after. 41 → 53 lines, the declared estimate hit exactly.

## The wording is not the captain's draft, and the drive is why

The ideation spike ran the drafted text against the specimen it was drafted from
— the 2026-08-14 release journey the captain banned ("DOC-ONLY TASK IS BANNED") —
and it did not refuse it. Two independent readers holding the draft reached "fit
passes" by the same route: `docs/site/**` is `blocked-product` in the classifier
table sitting directly above, therefore docs-site content is product this
workflow builds, therefore the gate's exclusion list — which names only
process-work classes — does not reach it. The draft excludes the wrong category,
and the table above it supplies the defeater.

Three changes, each falsified into existence rather than tuned:

- The primary test is **name the output's existing home**, an open question,
  rather than membership in a closed list of process-work classes. The banned
  specimen was not process work; it was a release narrative with a home in the
  release ritual.
- An explicit **the classifier is not evidence of fit** clause, because both
  drafted arms used the classifier as their affirmative fit argument.
- The **anti-reshape** rule, so a fit failure cannot be repaired by bolting on a
  mechanism. `docs/dev/README.md:136` already bans doc-only tasks and the FO had
  it — then reshaped the entity eleven minutes after the ban until it satisfied
  the proof policy. A proof-shape rule is satisfiable by adding machinery, so it
  selects for machinery rather than refusing the work. A fit rule is not
  satisfiable that way.

## Proof

No committed test, no lint, no CI lane, no fixture. The entity's
enforcement-honesty clause is binding: this is contract prose executed by a
model, and a Go reimplementation would prove table content, not FO obedience —
`fo_write_core_mutation_gate_test.go` is the precedent.

The measurement is a two-arm N=3 reader drive over three scenarios, scored by a
rule committed before any reader runs. It is pre-registered and **unrun**;
validation owns it. Materials live in the state checkout under
`_evidence/fo-workflow-fit-gate/`.

`go test ./internal/contractlint/` is green plain and `-race` (AC-5). Also ran
`internal/ensigncycle` green, since three of its tests read this file and a break
there is invisible to the named suite.

## Declared deviations

The shipped wording departs from the captain's drafted seed, on the recorded
evidence above. Approved at the ideation gate.

The validation reader recipe takes the state-the-action framing rather than
read-only tools. Granting `Read,Grep,Glob` would let the reader open the live
`fo-write-core.md`, which on a checkout of this branch *is* the amended arm, so
the baseline arm would read the amendment and arm separation would collapse.

Surface is one shipped file at the exact declared line count, well inside the
±6 tolerance. Evidence artifacts are state, not shipped product.

## Summary

Adds a React `IconTile` wrapper and React Storybook coverage for the existing `@pathableai/styles` icon tile CSS contract.

This brings the React Storybook closer to parity with the existing styles Storybook `Interaction Controls/Icon Tile` entry. The wrapper does not introduce new styling; it maps React props to the documented `pathable-icon-tile` classes already provided by the styles package.

## Changes

- Added `packages/react/src/components/IconTile/IconTile.tsx`.
- Exported `IconTile` and its public prop types from `packages/react/src/index.ts`.
- Added `packages/react/src/stories/interaction-controls/IconTile.stories.tsx` with the Storybook title `Interaction Controls/Icon Tile`.

## Component Contract

`IconTile` renders a non-interactive `<span>` with the base `pathable-icon-tile` class.

Supported props:

- `size`: `compact`, `default`, `large`
- `shape`: `square`, `circle`
- `status`: `default`, `success`, `error`, `warning`, `info`
- Standard span attributes through `HTMLAttributes<HTMLSpanElement>`
- Consumer-provided SVG/icon content through `children`

The component forwards custom attributes and `className`, and falls back to the base class when unsupported values are supplied at runtime.

## Storybook Coverage

The new React Storybook file includes:

- `Playground` for controls-based exploration.
- `Default` for base class and decorative-icon semantics.
- `SquareAndCircle` for shape variants.
- `SizeVariants` and `CircleSizes` for compact/default/large sizing.
- `StatusVariants` for default/success/error/warning/info status treatments with meaningful SVG labels.
- `InlineAlignment` for icon-with-text alignment.
- `LongContent` and `Narrow` for text wrapping and mobile resilience.
- `AllVariants` for deterministic visual-regression coverage.
- `CustomAttributes` for forwarded attributes and class names.
- `UnsupportedValuesFallback` for runtime fallback behavior.
- `StatusRowComposition` for realistic usage in a raised surface.

## Accessibility Notes

- `IconTile` is intentionally non-interactive and does not add button semantics or focus behavior.
- Decorative use is documented with `aria-hidden=true` on the tile and hidden SVG content.
- Meaningful status icons are demonstrated with `role=img` and `aria-label` on the SVG.
- Nearby visible text is used in composition stories so status meaning is not communicated by color alone.

## Validation

Local validation passed:

- `pnpm --filter @pathableai/react lint`
- `pnpm --filter @pathableai/react typecheck`
- `pnpm build:docs-react`
- Git Bash Storybook runner: 50 suites passed, 555 tests passed

GitHub validation passed:

- React typecheck
- React build + package validation
- JS lint
- Storybook build (HTML + React)
- Storybook accessibility tests
- Storybook visual smoke
- Storybook Quality Gates
- Storybook coverage
- Packed Next.js consumer
- React server compatibility advisory

Expected skipped checks:

- `CI Full / Markdownlint` skipped because this PR does not change Markdown files.
- `CI Full / Behavior contracts` skipped because this PR does not change `behavior-contracts/**`, `packages/styles/**`, Storybook app files, `package.json`, or `pnpm-lock.yaml`.

author: mearleycf
body:
## Summary
Closes #18 (blocking finding from the frontend Council review).

`text-sea-green` / `text-amber` / `text-classic-crimson` were used as plain text color directly on the light `--card` background (`#E6F5FF`) across 13 usages in 13 components — including the large "healthy" safe-to-spend dollar figure, the single most-viewed text in the app. Computed contrast:
- `sea-green` on card ≈ **1.72:1**
- `amber` on card ≈ **1.73:1**
- `classic-crimson` on card ≈ **4.46:1** (also just under the 4.5:1 AA threshold)

All three fail WCAG 1.4.3 (needs 4.5:1 for normal text).

## Fix
Swapped all on-card/on-white usages to the `-500` shade of each existing color ramp (already defined in `global.css`, just unused for text). Verified via computed sRGB relative-luminance contrast:
- `sea-green-500` → 5.48:1 (card), 6.10:1 (admin white bg)
- `amber-500` → 5.93:1 (card), 6.60:1 (admin white bg)
- `classic-crimson-500` → 7.15:1 (card), 7.96:1 (admin white bg)

Note: the issue's suggested `-450` shade was checked first but doesn't actually clear 4.5:1 for sea-green (4.07:1) or amber (4.41:1) — `-500` was the first shade in the ramp that does for both, so I standardized on `-500` for all three colors for consistency.

Left the 3 existing `text-classic-crimson-150` usages untouched — those render directly on the dark page background (loading/error states), not on a card, and `-150` is already the correct light-on-dark choice there.

**Companion fix:** the Dashboard header's date subtitle (`text-white/80` on `bg-dodger-blue`, ≈2.5:1) is replaced with `text-foreground/90` (dark navy at 90% opacity), which clears ≈6:1 against that same blue. This is a visual change (dark text instead of light text under the white title) — flagging it explicitly since it's a judgment call rather than a pure hex swap: the header's blue background is too light-to-mid to support *any* WCAG-compliant light-colored text at normal size (even 100% opaque white only reaches 3.11:1 on it), so full compliance required going dark instead of just adjusting opacity.

## Test plan
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean
- [x] `npx vitest run` — same 3 pre-existing unrelated `SafeToSpendCard.test.tsx` failures, no new failures
- [x] Verified visually in browser: Dashboard, Forecast Details, and Budget Settings admin pages — dollar figures and header subtitle are now clearly legible
- [x] Confirmed computed color values match the intended token via `getComputedStyle`

author: pixnop
body:
Fixes #24

Verdict: both prongs from the issue, ceiling and cache, landed together, since a raised ceiling alone still hard-fails once the catalog outgrows it, and a cache alone still hard-fails on the growth spurt itself.

## Per-endpoint ceiling

`mods.vintagestory.at/api/mods` now gets a 16 MB ceiling instead of the generic 4 MB one. Implemented as an optional `maxBytes` on `UrlRule` entries in `API_URL_RULES` (`src/ipc/validation.ts`), not a special-cased `if` in the fetch path: the catalog rule sits ahead of the general `/api` rule for that hostname, and `getApiUrlMaxBytes` looks up whichever rule actually matched the request. Every other allow-listed endpoint (`/api/tags`, `/api/authors`, `/api/mod/:id`, the auth and version endpoints) keeps the 4 MB bound unchanged.

16 MB: the catalog is ~3.5 MB today for ~8000 mods with no pagination offered by the API. 16 MB is roughly 4-5x that, years of headroom at the mod-count growth this project has seen, while staying a bounded, allow-listed exception rather than an open-ended one.

## Disk cache with serve-stale

`netHandlers.ts` now write-through caches the catalog response to `userData/Cache/ModCatalog/` on every successful fetch, keyed by a hash of the full request URL (so different search/filter queries get their own entry). On a failed fetch, network down, ceiling tripped, or a non-2xx status, it serves the last good cached body back verbatim (the renderer's parsers never see the difference) with a logged warning, instead of throwing. No TTL beyond that: the cache self-heals the moment the next fetch succeeds. A cache miss still fails exactly as before, and a corrupt or unreadable cache file degrades to the plain failure path rather than surfacing garbage.

Staleness over a dead search page: a mod list that's a few minutes or hours old is still a usable search page; a blank one with an error banner is not. This only applies to the catalog endpoint, nothing else is cached.

## Tests (`tests/ipc/`)

- `api-url-ceiling.test.ts`: the generic 4 MB ceiling holds for ordinary endpoints, the catalog (including with search/filter query strings) gets 16 MB, and the allow-list still rejects everything else.
- `mod-catalog-cache.test.ts`, against a mocked `electron` module (`net.request`, `ipcMain`, `app.getPath`): write-through on success, stale-served-with-a-warning on failure, cache miss still throws, a corrupted cache file degrades to the plain failure path, only the catalog endpoint is ever cached, and the ceiling is honored end-to-end through the fetch path itself (not just the rule table).

Branched from current `dev` (`c15931d`); `vitest.config.ts`'s `@src` alias and raised coverage thresholds already existed there from other in-flight work, so no infra changes were needed to make the new tests runnable.

## Gates (local, CI is down)

- `npm run typecheck`: clean
- `npm run lint:ci`: clean (pre-existing eslint-plugin-react version warning only)
- `npm run format:check`: clean
- `npm run test:coverage`: 72 files, 644 passed / 2 skipped; statements 65.29% / branches 62.25% / functions 68.98% / lines 67.04%, all above the 63/60/67/64 floors
- `npm run build:unpack`: builds and packages cleanly

author: tfausak
body:
Closes #1661

## What changed

`docs/prior-art-lessons.md` was a study artifact with nothing tying it to daily work. This gives the permissive prior art a place in the loop, split by how often the reader needs it.

- **`CLAUDE.md`** (+11 lines) carries only the decision: consult *after* deriving the rule from `docs/rules.txt`, the CR wins every disagreement, a missing clone is a skipped step. It points at the rest.
- **`docs/agents/implementing.md`** gains a subsection under `## Cards`, where card-finding already lives — what each corpus is for. `_scratch/phase` for finding the producing card (1,216 test files named for card and rule), `_scratch/mtgish` for an effect's field shape (33,479 cards as first-order typed ASTs), `_scratch/argentum-engine` for modeling questions.
- **`docs/agents/researching.md`** gains a line: the corpora are a lead, never a citation.
- **`docs/prior-art-lessons.md`** gains section 11 with the evidence, and the corrections below.

## The correction

Sections 8.7 and 8.8 had phase as code-per-card at 0% declarative, alongside MTGO and Manalink. Verified against the clone: `types/ability.rs` has a 232-variant `Effect` enum fed by a ~90-file oracle parser — Magarena's shape in Rust, not Manalink's. The real criticism is parser-as-truth plus an identity check surviving in the core: `game/precast_copy_shortcut.rs` gates on `source.name == "Witherbloom Apprentice"`, which their own `CLAUDE.md` forbids. That is section 8.1's discipline-not-construction point observed a second time, and it sharpens rather than weakens pawl's claim.

mtgish was missed by all three earlier waves. MIT, and the closest published analogue to pawl's open half.

Section 8.10 now records that this section's own entry was wrong, since the doc's meta-lesson (section 9) applies to itself.

## Design calls

- **Detail in `docs/agents/`, decision in `CLAUDE.md`.** The first draft put the whole per-corpus breakdown at top level; that is paid on every session and duplicates section 11 for anyone who follows the pointer. Rejected.
- Consult *after* deriving, never before — both new sources are parser-shaped where pawl's is AST-shaped, and reading a model first imports it.
- phase is a card-finding index, not a design reference. Rejected treating it as a peer architecture, which is what its issue history would tempt.
- Facts travel freely; ported code carries the MIT notice; card text stays Wizards IP regardless.
- Every mention is worded so a missing clone is a skipped step. `_scratch/` is gitignored; the `AllPrintings.json` bullet gained the same caveat.

## CR citations

None — no rules claims. The one CR-adjacent statement is that another engine's green test is not evidence of a rule's answer, with argentum's knowingly-wrong Blood Moon test as the example (already recorded in section M3).

## Verification

Docs only; no code touched. `hooky fix` clean on the staged files. Every quantitative claim was checked against the clones before being written: the 232 variants, ~90 parser files, 1,216 test files, 33,479 mtgish cards, both licenses, and the `precast_copy_shortcut.rs` identity check (confirmed production code — the file has no `cfg(test)`).

Self-review cut two overstatements: the section 8.8 table gave phase a qualitative "high" in a column of measured percentages (it is unmeasured), and a claim that mtgish marks its unparseable residue — it does not, so that is now recorded as a negative finding, since a card's presence in its data is not evidence the rules text came through whole.

Suite not run: no Haskell changed.

## Does the rules core case on an effect's identity?

No. No code in this diff.

## Deferred

Whether mtgish's vocabulary should feed pawl's opcode design directly (section 6's Forge table is frequency; mtgish is field shapes) is left open — a design question for M4, not a workflow one.

author: olegiv
body:
Two independent fixes that surfaced while wiring per-post view counts into a
site theme. Both are in `analytics_int`'s blast radius, hence one PR, but they
are separate commits and can be reviewed independently.

## 1. No-op placeholders for module template funcs

`Registry.AllTemplateFuncs` only returns funcs from **active** modules, and
`html/template` resolves function *names* at parse time. So a theme calling a
module func has a hard dependency on that module being active at boot.

The failure mode is the reason this matters: it is not a 500. `theme/manager.go`
logs a single `WARN`, drops the theme, and `loadActiveTheme` falls back to
whichever theme sorts first. The site silently renders in a different theme, and
because themes are parsed only at startup, **the breakage is deferred to the
next restart** — long after the module was toggled.

Six funcs had no placeholder: the three from `analytics_int`, plus
`exampleFunc`, `exampleVersion` and `sentinelVersion`.

`analyticsPostStats` returns `map[string]int64` rather than `PageStats` because
`analytics_int` imports `internal/render` — the real type would be an import
cycle. Only the name is resolved at parse time, and `AddTemplateFuncs` replaces
the placeholder before any theme is parsed, so the map never reaches a live
render. `internal/testutil` already uses this shape.

`TestEveryModuleTemplateFuncHasRendererPlaceholder` enumerates every shipped
module and fails if any template func lacks a placeholder. It lives in
`cmd/ocms` because that is the only package importing all modules; in
`internal/render` it would be an import cycle. No allowlist: site-specific
themes live outside this repo and cannot be audited from here.

**Verified:** deactivating `analytics_int` and restarting now leaves the theme
loading normally with the counter simply absent. Before this change that
sequence swapped the whole site to the `default` theme.

## 2. Taxonomy archives excluded from post view counts

`getPageStats` matched language-prefixed paths with `LIKE '%/slug'`, anchored
only at the end — so it also matched `/category/slug` and `/tag/slug`. A post
whose slug doubles as a category or tag slug absorbed its own archive's views.

Not hypothetical: on a live site **4 of 22 published posts collided**, and after
five hits on the colliding archive an article reported **22 views instead of
16** — a 37% inflation.

`page_id` is never populated by the tracker, so path matching is the only
mechanism available. The leading `%` also covers language-prefixed archives
(`/ru/category/slug`) and cannot swallow a real article: the pattern requires a
slash *after* the segment, and slugs never contain slashes — a post slugged
`category` lives at `/category` and is unaffected.

`page_analytics_reads` deliberately gets no filter: reads are only emitted from
pages carrying the `single-page` body class, which archives never have.

Two tests cover both directions, and I confirmed they are not vacuous — with the
filter removed the exclusion test fails with `Views = 6, want 2`.

## Notes for review

- The `example`/`sentinel` placeholders are strictly additive and were added
  because the new test is otherwise red on arrival. Happy to split them out.
- Commit 2 changes results for every site using `analytics_int`. Only downward,
  and only for slugs that collide with a taxonomy term.
- `go build ./...`, `go vet`, and `cmd/ocms`, `internal/render`,
  `modules/analytics_int`, `internal/theme`, `internal/handler` all pass.

author: madmax983
body:
Follow-up to #17 (merged). Refs #3.

A six-angle code review with adversarial verification was run against the merged branch —
anti-theatre/mutation, oracle fidelity, downstream consumer, CI & supply chain, Rust
correctness, and honesty/AC coverage. This fixes what survived verification.

The most useful findings were about this project's own claims, which is the uncomfortable
half of the exercise.

## The refactor had weakened the tests it was meant to serve

Mutation testing found two accessors introduced by the REFACTOR commit could each be
sabotaged with the **entire 45-test suite still green**:

| Mutation | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `PerftCase::fen_fields()` → hardcoded `4` | suite green | `fen_fields_accessor_agrees_with_the_raw_fen` FAILED |
| `PerftCase::verified_counts()` → filter removed | suite green | 2 tests FAILED |

Every assertion about Kiwipete's four-field FEN routed through `fen_fields()`, so the
accessor could lie and nothing disagreed. `verified_counts()` was worse than it looked: the
differential harness *appeared* to filter by provenance, but every `p` count is also over
the replay budget, so those rows were excluded for the wrong reason and the provenance
semantics were never actually pinned.

That is a general lesson worth the entry it got in the decision log: **an accessor that
every assertion routes through is a single point at which all of them can be made to lie.**
D-0016 now requires a test pinning any such accessor against a direct computation.

## Corrections to this project's own claims — D-0016

| Claim | Was | Is |
|---|---|---|
| Oracle count totals | "51 counts, 44 verified, 7 published-only" | **55 counts, 44 verified, 11 published-only** |
| Verified fraction | implied 86% | **80%** |
| `p` flag meaning | "too deep to replay" | too deep **or** `perft(0)`, which `go perft 0` cannot report |
| Source URL redirect | HTTP 308 | **301** on GET; 308 is the HEAD response |
| Transient toolchain failure | CI run 2 | **run 1** |

The verified figure (44) was right; the total was understated, which flattered the fraction.
All three totals are now asserted by `fixture_provenance_totals_are_what_the_project_claims`
so they cannot drift again unnoticed.

Correcting the fixture header moved its SHA-256, so `ORACLE_SHA256` moved with it — the
pinning mechanism working as designed, not a weakening of it.

## Correctness

- **`is_available()` could hang forever.** It piped the child's stdout, never read it, then
  called `wait()` — a deadlock against any engine writing more than the pipe buffer.
  Stockfish's banner is small enough to be safe today, which is exactly why this would have
  waited for issue #6 to bite. "Is this binary runnable" must never hang; stdout is now
  discarded.
- **Arithmetic overflow panic.** `parse_counts` computed `previous + 1` unguarded → panic in
  debug/test builds at `u32::MAX`. Now `checked_add`.
- **Dropping a position's *first* published row was undetectable.** Contiguity was only
  checked between adjacent tokens, and `2,3,4` is as contiguous as `1,2,3`. The first depth
  is now anchored to 0 or 1.
- **A crashed engine reported `NoNodeCount`** with no hint it had died; the exit status is
  now in the error.
- **`validate_fen`'s doc contradicted its behaviour** — it said "structural check, not a
  legality check" while enforcing exactly one king per side. The check is right (two white
  kings in an oracle fixture means a mistyped rank), so the doc now says what the code does
  and names what remains out of scope for #4.

## CI

- The **D-0002 acceptance-document guard searched only `docs/`**, so the forbidden document
  was allowed anywhere else in the tree. Now repository-wide over tracked files — and
  verified to fire against a probe `ACCEPTANCE.md` at the root.
- The **ASCII-only check passed vacuously when the fixture was absent**: `grep` on a missing
  file returns non-zero, which the `if` read as "no non-ASCII bytes found". Existence is
  asserted first.
- The **`Cargo.lock` check asserted the crate names, never their versions** — the one thing
  a lockfile exists to nail down. Now asserts `0.6.x` / `0.5.x`.
- The **dependency-DAG check counted dev- and build-dependencies** as architectural edges.
  Filtered to normal dependencies.
- The **nightly cold-cache job ran the suite with no Stockfish and no
  `BOIDBOARD_REQUIRE_STOCKFISH`**, so the differential tests skipped silently on the one
  runner whose green tick is supposed to mean "a clean machine can do this".
- A comment cited decision `D-0039`, which does not exist.

## Anti-theatre scan

Its own comment claimed it caught `assert_eq!(x, x)` — no such rule existed. Added. The
`#[ignore]` rule was evadable via `#[cfg_attr(..., ignore)]`. Extended.

All seven rules were then **proven to fire**, each against a probe:

```
assert!(true)                  exit 1   assertion that cannot fail
assert_eq!(x, x)               exit 1   assertion comparing a value with itself
#[ignore]                      exit 1   ignored test
#[cfg_attr(all(), ignore)]     exit 1   ignored test
#[allow(dead_code)]           exit 1   crate-level lint suppression
clippy without --all-targets   exit 1   not the full AC1 command
bare cargo fmt                 exit 1   can never fail
```

## AC4 remains open — D-0017

The annotated tag exists locally at `a1f70323c6d56629a18e959894f0815efa0d3ac9` but still
cannot be pushed: HTTP 403 across four attempts, while branch pushes from the same session
succeed and the egress proxy records no relay failures. The session credential is scoped to
`refs/heads/*`, and no available GitHub API tool creates tag refs.

Recorded as an open criterion rather than worked around — a lightweight tag, a branch named
like a tag, or a local-only tag would each produce a green tick for something AC4 does not
ask for. One command completes it:

```sh
git tag -a archive/boids-sim-attempt a1f70323c6d56629a18e959894f0815efa0d3ac9 \
  -m 'Quarantine: prior attempt, PR #2 (closed unmerged).'
git push origin archive/boids-sim-attempt
```

Quarantine enforcement (D-0001) does **not** depend on the tag — it keys off the commit SHA
and is live today. D-0001's evidence line was corrected, since it had claimed otherwise.

## Verification

```
54 tests (was 45)
cargo fmt --all -- --check                              exit 0
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings   exit 0
cargo test --workspace                                  exit 0
./scripts/anti-theatre.sh                               exit 0
```

author: dromediansk
body:
Dev and production pointed at the same hosted project, so every schema change was tried out in production — and 0003_auth.sql opens with `truncate family_members cascade`, which is not a migration you can rehearse on live data.

This is the Supabase CLI stack rather than a plain Postgres container, because a plain container cannot run this app: 0003_auth.sql adds a foreign key to auth.users and a trigger on it, sign-in is Google OAuth, and live updates need Realtime. Storage, Edge Functions, analytics and the mail catcher are off — nothing here uses them — which leaves seven containers.

Three things worth knowing:

- auto_expose_new_tables is on, and has to be. Every query goes through PostgREST as service_role and no migration issues a GRANT; the hosted project predates the always-revoked default. Off, the tables exist locally and answer "permission denied". The field is removed on 2026-10-30, at which point the migrations need explicit GRANTs in production too.

- Ports are shifted to 544xx so this can run beside another local Supabase project. 3001 is allow-listed alongside 3000 because `next dev` quietly takes the next free port, and an origin missing from that list does not error — it redirects to site_url, so sign-in looks like it worked and lands on the wrong port.

- seed.sql inserts no members. handle_new_auth_user picks the admin with `not exists (select 1 from family_members)`, so a seeded member would strand the first real sign-in as pending, waiting on an admin who does not exist. scripts/seed-dev.mjs runs after that sign-in instead and builds the family around the row it created. It provokes the claim notices by editing and deleting claimed wishes rather than inserting rows, so what lands in the table is whatever the triggers actually write.

The CLI is here for the local stack only. Production has no supabase_migrations.schema_migrations table, so `supabase db push` would read it as empty and replay everything, truncate included; README and CLAUDE.md say so, supabase/.temp is gitignored, and the seed refuses any non-loopback URL.

Migrations are unchanged — the CLI accepts the 0001_ names as they are.

author: beennnn
body:
## Le défaut, mesuré sur l'instance

Juste après la mise en service d'alpha.13, l'add-on a redémarré Core (déploiement touchant `rest`), puis le drapeau « passe maintenant » a mis **85 s** à être vu au lieu de ≤ 15 s :

```
20:05:47  redémarrage de HA demandé par l'add-on
20:05:48  sonde : déclencheur actif, scruté toutes les 15 s
20:07:42  drapeau levé (Core répond de nouveau depuis 20:07:34)
20:09:07  « déclencheur reçu — passe anticipée »      ← 85 s
```

`ha()` appelait `curl -fsS` **sans `--max-time`**. Pendant un redémarrage de Core, le proxy du Superviseur accepte la connexion puis reste muet : curl attend le délai TCP par défaut. La boucle de scrutation ne scrutait donc plus — elle était bloquée dans **un seul** appel. Le même défaut touchait `wait_core_ready`, dont le commentaire promet « 20 essais × 15 s = 5 min de patience » : vrai seulement si chaque essai rend la main.

## Le correctif

Une borne **optionnelle**, posée par l'appelant et **uniquement sur les sondes** — les lectures qui doivent répondre tout de suite (`core_ready`, `run_now_requested`, `probe_run_now`). Pas de plafond global : `check_config` prend couramment 60 s et un backup complet bien plus, les couper serait pire que le mal. Les appelants la posent en `local` ; la portée dynamique de bash la rend visible dans `ha()` et la fait disparaître au retour.

`--max-time 0` étant le défaut de curl (aucune limite), une seule forme d'appel couvre les deux cas.

⚠️ **Erreur commise en chemin, gardée en commentaire** : la première version construisait l'option conditionnellement avec `[ -n "$x" ] && opts=…`. Cette liste rend 1 quand le test est faux → sous `set -e`, `ha()` sortait **avant** le curl et **tous** les appels API échouaient d'un coup. Les tests l'ont attrapé immédiatement.

## Vérifié

- Le stub `curl` du test gagne un **mode gel** qui reproduit les deux comportements du vrai curl : sans `--max-time`, 45 s d'attente ; avec, code 28 à l'échéance. Le nouveau cas lève le drapeau pendant que Core est muet, le rétablit au bout de 12 s, et attend la passe dans les 25 s.
- **10/10** sur `test_run_now_trigger.sh`, et le nouveau cas **échoue sur alpha.13** (`RUN_SH_UNDER_TEST` pointé sur `origin/main`) — il reproduit donc bien le défaut observé.
- `test_restart_on_rest.sh` toujours vert, `shellcheck` propre.

author: jeffreycrum
body:
Closes #284.

## The hole

`validate_global_review_head_advance` shape-checks the **reported** `head_sha`
against `is_hex_sha` (7–64 hex) on every head-advancing coding event. But it
deliberately **skips** the ancestry comparison when the **stored**
`last_head_sha` fails the same check, rather than refusing — and that asymmetry
is correct: the stored value is server-held, nothing rewrites it but a
successful head-advancing send, so refusing there would wedge the session
permanently behind an error whose remedy names a field the caller cannot reach.

The gap was that neither site which *seeds* `last_head_sha` checked shape at
all. The turn templates spelled the field `head_sha:<HEAD>`, so an agent that
emitted the placeholder literally stored the string `"HEAD"` — and drift
detection was then silently off for the rest of that session. That is precisely
the hole the advance guard was added to close.

## The fix

Hoist `is_hex_sha` to both seed sites, where a refusal is recoverable and names
a value the caller owns:

- `parse_task_list_event` (`collab_events.rs`) — the `task_list` send.
- `start_global_review_session` (`state_machine/mod.rs`) — the
  `collab_start_code_review` shortcut. New `CollabError::MalformedHeadSha`.
  Placed in the constructor rather than the MCP handler because it is the only
  path to `CollabSession::new_global_review`.

Both refuse before anything is written, so the caller corrects and re-sends.
Both trim first: `handle_collab_start_code_review` reads its shas through
`require_str`, which does not trim, and `.claude-plugin/commands/collab.md`
resolves them from the *output* of `git rev-parse HEAD` / `git merge-base` —
output that ends in a newline. Without the trim the check would refuse the
correct sha for the branch on the strength of a trailing `\n`.

The skip arm keeps its behaviour for sessions already in flight, and now says
so out loud rather than returning a bare `Ok(())`: a `tracing::warn!` records
that drift detection ran degraded for that send. Its retirement criterion is a
runnable query —

```sql
SELECT id, last_head_sha FROM collab_sessions
 WHERE ended_at IS NULL
   AND NOT (length(last_head_sha) BETWEEN 7 AND 64
            AND lower(last_head_sha) NOT GLOB '*[^0-9a-f]*');
```

— returning no rows. The `ended_at IS NULL` scope is load-bearing: `collab_end`
only stamps `ended_at` and nothing deletes a row, so an unscoped sweep counts
finished sessions forever and never comes back empty. `GLOB` because SQLite
ships no `REGEXP` and this crate registers none. `lower(...)` because
`is_hex_sha` takes uppercase via `is_ascii_hexdigit`.

Every surface that told agents to write the placeholder now names
`git rev-parse HEAD` and forbids the literal: both task-list worker prompts,
the five head-advancing turn templates, the orchestrator command doc,
`docs/COLLAB.md`, and the `collab_start_code_review` tool schema.

## Verified, not assumed

- **The seed-site enumeration is complete.** Independent reviews tabulated
  every `last_head_sha` write in the crate — both constructors, all four
  head-advancing `apply_event` arms, DB insert/update/hydration, migrations —
  and confirmed exactly two take caller input into storage. The other four are
  already gated before `apply_event`.
- **Backward compatible.** No path re-runs either check against already-stored
  data; a session that stored `"HEAD"` before this change behaves exactly as it
  did, via the skip arm.
- **The template regression test is not vacuous.** It was verified by
  reintroducing a `head_sha:<HEAD>` placeholder and watching it fail.
- **`base_sha` is deliberately not shape-checked** (emptiness only), and the
  docs now say so explicitly rather than leaving symmetry to be inferred.

## Shape of the change

51 test fixtures were swept to named 40-hex constants *before* the enforcement
landed, so each commit leaves the tree green. 11 tests added: two seed-site
refusals, the shortcut refusal at the MCP layer, a bounded-echo test on each
seed site, the shortcut's trim and whitespace-only handling, the skip arm's
existence refusal, `is_hex_sha`'s accepting edges at exactly 7 and 64
characters, and the turn-template placeholder guard.

## What the review round changed

The first three commits were reviewed by four specialist agents; every finding
below was confirmed against the source before being acted on.

- **The shortcut refused padded input.** Covered under The fix above — this was
  the one defect that broke a documented caller rather than merely reading
  wrong.
- **The skip arm was silent.** It returned `Ok(())` for a session whose drift
  detection had just been downgraded to an existence-only check,
  indistinguishable at every call site from "ancestry verified" — a collapse
  this file already argues against twice.
- **The retirement criterion could not be run or satisfied.** It was spelled as
  a `REGEXP` sweep with no `ended_at` scope; see The fix for all three defects.
- **`MalformedHeadSha` echoed an uncapped string.** The `task_list` refusal was
  bounded with a dedicated test while its sibling — the path whose input
  carries *no* upstream cap, since `require_str` applies none — shipped
  unbounded. The bound and its `chars().take()` helper now live in
  `collab::error` and are shared, so the two cannot diverge.
- **Two comments stated things the code does not do.** The `PLACEHOLDER_HEAD`
  doc claimed the resulting `branch_drift:` misattributes blame to the reported
  head; it does not, and the sibling constant added in the same PR said the
  opposite. Both refusals also claimed "a branch name" is refused — this is a
  shape check, so a branch named `deadbeef` passes it.
- **Three test gaps.** The skip arm's refusal path (the half
  `require_checkpoint_proof` leans on) had no coverage; `is_hex_sha`'s
  accepting edges were unpinned in both directions; and nothing stopped a turn
  template from regressing to the placeholder that caused this issue.

## Known follow-ups, deliberately out of scope

1. **The reported-head shape refusal is classified Terminal.** A `head_sha`
   that fails `is_hex_sha` on `implementation_done` / `review_fix_global` /
   `review_local` / `final_review` is refused with a `branch_drift:` prefix,
   which classifies **Terminal and unrecoverable** — so "you sent `HEAD`
   instead of a sha" ends the session rather than asking for a retry, on the
   most trivially correctable mistake in the protocol. Pre-existing since #273.
   Reclassifying it touches failure-class handling broadly, so it wants its own
   issue; the templates fixed here remove the reachable cause in the meantime.
2. **Three uncapped caller strings remain at `handle_collab_start_code_review`.**
   `repo_path`, `branch`, and `base_sha` still use bare `require_str` while
   `task` goes through `sanitize_content`. This PR closed the `head_sha` half
   by bounding what the refusal echoes back; the other three are untouched.
3. **The shape check has a residual hole, now documented rather than implied.**
   A branch or tag whose name happens to be 7–64 hex characters (`deadbeef`)
   satisfies it and is stored, then re-resolves on every later ancestry check.
   Uppercase `A–F` is likewise accepted. Nothing in the protocol closes this;
   the mitigation is that agents are told to send `git rev-parse HEAD` output.
   `docs/COLLAB.md` says so plainly so the guard is not over-trusted.

## Test plan

- `cargo test -p ironmem --no-fail-fast` — 37/37 targets, 1752 passed, 0
  failed (lib 1400 passed, 1 ignored)
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — clean
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` — clean
- `python3 scripts/check_collab_turn_templates.py` — OK (10 templates, 10 rows)
- `python3 -m pytest tests/` — 385 passed
