---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>pnpm/pnpm (pnpm)</summary>

### [`v11.22.0`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v11.22.0): pnpm 11.22

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v11.21.0...v11.22.0)

##### Minor Changes

- Added `pnpm cache path`, which prints the directory pnpm uses for its metadata cache. CI setups can use it to cache that directory — including the lockfile verification log, which lets a job skip re-checking an unchanged lockfile against the configured supply-chain policies.

- `--config.config-dir` no longer reaches the config through a project's `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, and neither do the `--config.` spellings of the other settings a project manifest may no longer contribute (`--config.pnpm-home-dir`, `--config.workspace-dir`, `--config.global-pkg-dir`, `--config.root-project-manifest-dir`). None of them was ever a supported way to set those directories: pnpm resolves them from the environment, and these flags took effect only because the project-manifest merge re-applied the command line afterwards. The dedicated flags, such as `--dir` and `--global-dir`, are unaffected [#​13629](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/13629).

- `pnpm config set` refuses to write a setting to a project's `pnpm-workspace.yaml` that pnpm does not read from there, rather than leaving a key in the file that does nothing. Those settings are `configDir`, `pnpmHomeDir`, `stateDir` and the others that name machine-level state. The command fails with `ERR_PNPM_CONFIG_SET_NOT_A_PROJECT_SETTING`, naming where the setting does belong when it belongs somewhere. `pnpm config delete` still clears one that a file already carries, in whichever spelling it uses [#​13629](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/13629).

- Added a new setting `minimumReleaseAgeExcludePrune`. When enabled, `pnpm add`, `pnpm update`, and `pnpm remove` prune the entries of `minimumReleaseAgeExclude` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` that the freshly written lockfile no longer resolves: versions that are gone are dropped (an entry is removed once none of its versions remain), and entries for packages that are no longer in the lockfile are removed too. Name patterns (`@scope/*`) are always kept. The cleanup is skipped when the install's lockfile does not cover the whole workspace (`sharedWorkspaceLockfile: false`), since entries another project still needs would look stale.

  Renamed `cleanupUnusedCatalogs` to `catalogPrune`, so that catalog pruning and release-age exclude pruning use one vocabulary. `cleanupUnusedCatalogs` continues to work; when both are set, `catalogPrune` wins.

- A project's `pnpm-workspace.yaml` can no longer choose where pnpm keeps its credentials, its own installation, or the registry it downloads its next version from. One of those settings is `configDir`, which decided where `pnpm login` writes the granted token. `bin`, `dir`, `globalBinDir`, `globalDir`, `npmrcAuthFile`, `pnpmHomeDir`, `stateDir`, `userconfig` and `workspaceDir` are ignored there now too, and pnpm warns about the ones it finds. `cacheDir` and `storeDir` are unaffected [#​13629](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/13629).

- Resolving a Node.js runtime version (`devEngines.runtime` / `runtime:` specifiers) is now much faster: the per-version release metadata is cached in the pnpm cache directory after its signature is verified, and an exact stable version such as `runtime:22.23.2` no longer downloads the Node.js release index. A pinned runtime whose metadata was fetched once resolves without any network access, which removes the noticeable delay on the first `node` invocation in a project pinning an already-downloaded runtime [#​13899](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/13899).

##### Patch Changes

- Fixed intermittent `ERR_PNPM_ENOENT` and `ERR_PNPM_ENOTEMPTY` errors while renaming `_tmp_*` directories during installation with `nodeLinker: hoisted`, in workspaces that also use `patchedDependencies`.

- `pnpm add` no longer re-resolves the dependency graph when `pnpm-lock.yaml` already holds a version satisfying the request — promoting a transitive dependency to a direct one, or adding to a second workspace package what a first one already depends on, now only saves the dependency in `package.json` and records its importer entry. A satisfying locked version is necessary but not sufficient: the install still falls back to a full resolution for a dist tag, an alias, a `workspace:`/`catalog:`/git/tarball specifier, `--save-peer`, an overridden package, a `catalogMode` other than `manual`, and — under `resolutionMode: time-based` or `lowest-direct`, which resolve a direct dependency to the low end of its range — a range several locked versions satisfy.

- Global installs now switch over atomically. The command shims in the global bin directory point at a stable per-package link rather than at the directory a particular install produced, so `pnpm add -g` and `pnpm update -g` activate a new version by moving that one link instead of rewriting every shim. A command can no longer be missing from `PATH` while an install is in progress, and a failed install leaves the previous version in place.

- `pnpm audit --fix` and `pnpm audit --fix update` no longer add `minimumReleaseAgeExclude` entries for patched versions that were published before the `minimumReleaseAge` cutoff. The publish time of each minimum patched version is now checked against the registry metadata, and only versions young enough to be blocked by the age gate get an exclusion entry [#​11563](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/11563).

- `pnpm add <pkg>@​<version>` and `pnpm update <pkg>@​<version>` under a non-manual `catalogMode` now move the catalog entry's resolution to the requested version. Previously, when the catalog entry was a range that covered the requested version but resolved to a different one, the request was dropped silently: nothing was installed, nothing was written, and no error was raised.

- A project that wasn't part of an install that moved a catalog entry now follows the entry the next time it is installed. It used to keep the version the entry resolved to before — a version the entry no longer allowed — and no later install corrected it, so one catalog entry ended up resolved to two versions.

- `pnpm add <pkg>@​<version>` and `pnpm update <pkg>@​<version>` under `catalogMode: strict` no longer fail with `ERR_PNPM_CATALOG_VERSION_MISMATCH` when the catalog entry is a range that the wanted version satisfies. The dependency keeps using the catalog; only a version that really falls outside the catalog's range is rejected [#​13715](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/13715).

- A changed `catalogs` or `pnpm.overrides` block no longer has to be the only change for `pnpm install` to update the lockfile in place. Editing an override while also removing a dependency, or changing a catalog entry in the same commit as a range bump, is now absorbed in one pass instead of re-resolving the whole dependency graph [#​1

author: hawkar-usls
body:
## Demiurge Lab Supervisor v1

This PR is stacked on the already-green self-cycle #3 and removes manual intervention between counterfactual windows **within one admitted objective**.

### Parent

```text
PARENT_LOOP = #3@71bb2e72e8c72a03d715edb203e0e87e829ff5bb
PARENT_LOOP_CI = SUCCESS / Python 3.11+3.12+3.13
```

### Supervisor state machine

```text
NO ADMITTED OBJECTIVE -> WAIT_NO_ADMITTED_OBJECTIVE

ADMITTED OBJECTIVE
  -> RUN OBJECTIVE WINDOWS
  -> improvement? continue
  -> fixed point? WAIT_FIXED_POINT
  -> plateau? WAIT_PLATEAU
  -> hard segment budget? BUDGET_EXHAUSTED + continuation checkpoint
```

The supervisor does not invent a target or purpose. This is deliberate:

```text
AUTONOMY != SELF_GENERATED_PURPOSE
AUTONOMY != BUSY_LOOP
```

### Exact continuation

A `BUDGET_EXHAUSTED` checkpoint binds:

- objective ID;
- resume config and replayed score;
- target and weights;
- root seed;
- absolute next window index;
- generation/candidate/patience policy;
- cumulative generation/adoption counters;
- parent checkpoint receipt.

`resume_from_checkpoint()` continues the deterministic absolute window sequence rather than restarting window zero. Tampered or internally inconsistent checkpoints fail closed.

`WAIT_PLATEAU` and `WAIT_FIXED_POINT` checkpoints cannot continue the same objective; a new admitted objective is required.

### Crash-recovery truth boundary

The checkpoint is returned in-memory. This PR **does not** claim it survives process or host loss by itself. A later explicit persistence adapter is required before crash recovery can be claimed.

```text
CHECKPOINT_IN_MEMORY != CRASH_DURABLE_CHECKPOINT
```

### Budgets

```text
max windows per segment = 64
max generations per window = 64
max total generations per segment = 4096
max candidates per generation = 16
max patience windows = 16
```

### Effect ceiling

No network, subprocess, file write, SQLite write, source mutation, automatic merge or external-effect surface is added.

```text
SELF_CYCLE_WITHIN_ADMITTED_OBJECTIVE = TRUE
MANUAL_INTERVENTION_BETWEEN_WINDOWS = FALSE
SELF_GENERATED_OBJECTIVE = FALSE
AUTONOMOUS_EXTERNAL_ACTION = FALSE
SOURCE_WRITEBACK = FALSE
AUTHORITY_DELTA = 0
MASS_EFFECT_BUDGET_DELTA = 0
CI_GREEN != MERGE_PERMISSION
```

body:
The docked download-manager panel (drawn over the bottom of the feed/preview via `render.go`'s `drawDownloadPanel`) already laid its per-post rows out with the toolkit — a `VBox` of `HBox` rows, each `Label | ProgressBar | status Label`. Its **chrome** was the last hand-drawn pixels in the view: the panel surface and its 1px top divider were bare `painter.FillRect`s, the `Downloads (N)` header was a font glyph-blit, and the `Clear` affordance was `FillRoundRect + StrokeRoundRect + glyph-blit`.

Per the project rule ("il ne doit rien y avoir de dessiné a la main; tout doit etre composé de widgets du toolkit"), `drawDownloadPanel` now assembles a widget tree with **no scene-level painter primitives left**, following the idiom of the three sibling migrations (Settings #190, Network log #191, Accounts #192):

- **Panel surface + 1px top divider** → solid `toolkit.Backdrop` fills (Step 0), byte-identical to the old `FillRect`s.
- **`Downloads (N)` header** → a top-anchored `toolkit.Label` fed the reader's TrueType face via `m.side.font`, at the same origin/ink → same pixels.
- **`Clear`** → a stock `toolkit.Button` pill at `dlClearR`. Its centred label lands at the same x the old `+pad` inset produced (`dlClearR` is the text width plus `2·pad`), exactly as the Settings #190 Done pill. Hit-testing is unchanged (`dlClearR → HitClearDownloads`), so the Clear-downloads flow is preserved.

The row `VBox`/`HBox`, the `downloadRow`/`DownloadItem` model, `IsDownloadQueued`, `downloadStatusText`, `layoutDownloadPanel` and hit-testing are all untouched.

The plain `Clear` pill is a stock Surface-faced `toolkit.Button` — the panel is `SurfaceAlt`, not an accent band, so no on-accent `ButtonProminent` derived-theme inversion is needed. **No genuinely-missing composite was found.**

Rendering the feed with a populated panel (queued/active/done/failed + row-cap overflow) is **byte-identical** to the pre-migration renderer except for **72–80 pixels confined to the Clear pill's corners** (radius `4` → the Button's `6`) — the same deliberate, accepted change the Settings #190 Done pill made.

body:
## What changed

- routes Spoke's desktop SDK transport through the released `tauri-plugin-jolt` commands;
- registers the plugin and its `jolt:default` Tauri capability;
- deletes Spoke's handwritten Rust daemon proxy, response parser, timeout policy, and parallel error taxonomy;
- moves the existing `/spoke/*` write invariant into Spoke's SDK / ACL seam so it applies before either the desktop or web adapter;
- removes obsolete legacy-host string classification and documents the shared adapter;
- extends the distribution contract to require the plugin dependency, registration, and permission.

## Why

Pastey already uses the shared plugin, while Spoke maintained a second implementation of generic daemon proxying and structured host errors. The shared adapter is the deeper module: URL policy, timeouts, multipart handling, response parsing, and host error taxonomy now have one implementation and one test surface. Spoke continues to own its application namespace policy, and the daemon independently enforces the approved session capabilities.

## Red → green

1. Added a desktop SDK test expecting `plugin:jolt|daemon_request`; it failed because Spoke invoked the app-defined `daemon_request`, then passed after enabling plugin mode.
2. Added a public SDK / ACL test requiring an out-of-namespace publication to fail before transport; it initially published `/profile`, then passed after the Spoke write wrapper moved into `src/jolt`.
3. Extended distribution verification to require the plugin dependency, registration, and capability; it failed on the missing Cargo dependency, then passed after the Rust shell migration.
4. Rust compilation exposed `serde_json` as a direct `generate_context!` requirement; retaining that one shell dependency restored the build.

## Verification

- `npm test` — 18 files, 86 tests passed
- `npm run build`
- `npm run verify:distribution`
- `yarn install --immutable`
- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo test`
- `cargo test --doc`
- `git diff --check`

Spoke has no `scripts/test-local.sh`, so the equivalent documented project checks were run directly.

## Follow-up

This PR intentionally does not consolidate App Compatibility Declaration parsing, unavailable classification, updater lifecycle, or application-owned startup UX. Those remain in private card 125 for separately reviewed slices.

author: lurzar
body:
## Summary

- add a capability-protected Admin user index with bounded search and filters
- manage only the approved `admin` and `super-admin` roles through Laravel Gates, Form Requests, and a transactional domain service
- preserve the mandatory base `user` role and protected super-admin lifecycle
- revoke affected authorization sessions, clear permission cache state, and record minimized audit events
- add responsive accessible English/Malay Inertia UI and canonical documentation

## Security and data boundaries

- browser payloads use public user ULIDs and omit internal IDs, credentials, sessions, Planning data, and package models
- the transaction locks the protected role first, then actor and subject accounts deterministically, and reauthorizes the actor before mutation
- stale revisions fail without mutation; refreshed client state retains the conflict explanation
- administrative grants require active verified accounts
- role changes fail closed when durable activity capture is unavailable
- migration and rollback reject unsafe pre-existing mappings or direct permission assignments instead of discarding authorization state

Final Codex Security diff scan reviewed all 18 implementation surfaces at content digest `4539671b75e720e11cb408f96d7ad2117edbf7bb6817e12be763f40e72da3f7d` with zero findings. Independent code review verdict: Ready.

## Validation

- `composer check`
  - 206 backend tests, 1,044 assertions
  - 53 frontend tests
  - Pint and PHPStan
  - TypeScript typecheck and production build
  - Composer and npm security audits
- `git diff --check`

No browser testing was performed, per the repository's scripted-test preference.

## Migration and rollback

The migration adds `users.view`, `users.manage-roles`, and `users.manage-super-admin` plus reviewed protected-role mappings. It preserves existing data and aborts when pre-existing or rollback-time authorization drift would be unsafe. Rollback removes only the deterministic issue-owned permission state; operational role restoration must use verified audit or backup evidence.

Closes #133
Refs #130

author: dafran
body:
## El problema
El personaje gato (Michi) reutilizaba el cuerpo y la cara del pug. En el gesto "excited" (que se usa en el saludo del hub, al acertar, y al elegirlo en el selector), el pug abre el hocico con la **lengua colgando** — jadeo de perro. En un gato se veía raro: parecía que jadeaba, y los gatos no jadean.

## El arreglo
Michi ahora tiene su **propia boca de gato (ω)**: un trazo suave con el surco central y las dos curvas. En "excited" se abre apenas con un puntito rosa para dar vida, **sin lengua colgando**. Turbo y Bruno (perros) conservan el jadeo, que en ellos sí corresponde.

Implementado en el *skin system* (`mgCharSkin`) con un marcador `mouth: "cat"`, así que el cambio queda aislado al gato.

## Verificación
Renderizado del gato en "excited" (saludo del hub, ×3 densidad): boca de gato correcta, sin lengua — se lee como gato contento, no como perro jadeando. (Captura adjunta en la conversación.)

author: chengsth
body:
Adds `song.html`: a pancake sing-along that the browser **performs itself** with the Web Audio API. There is no audio file and no library — the page synthesises the drums, bass, chords and melody as it plays, so it still works offline like the rest of the site.

## Two bands, one tune

The same melody ships with two arrangements, and the 🎤 / 🎷 chips swap between them **mid-song** without stopping:

| | Pop | Jazz |
|---|---|---|
| Tempo | 112 bpm, straight eighths | 132 bpm, **swung** eighths |
| Drums | four-on-the-floor kick, clap on 2 and 4 | brushes and ride cymbal |
| Bass | root-note pulse | walking bass line |
| Chords | triads (I–V–vi–IV) | sevenths (Imaj7–vi7–ii7–V7) |

The melody is written in C major pentatonic so it sits well over both progressions, and the last two bars are forced to the home chord so the song ends resolved instead of hanging on a suspension.

## Singing along

The words are stored as `syllable/note/beats` tokens, so one piece of data drives both the tune and the karaoke:

- syllables light up **one at a time**, in time with the melody
- a pancake stack bounces on the beat, grows taller through the chorus, and somersaults whenever the song says *flip*
- tapping any line in the lyric sheet starts the song from there
- an optional **🎙️ Words out loud** toggle reads each line as it comes around, reusing the reading voice already picked in the picture book and chapter book
- <kbd>Space</kbd> starts and stops it

## Changes

- `song.html` — new page (song data, audio engine, karaoke screen)
- `index.html` — new card and nav pill, in the existing pastel card style
- `README.md` — a section describing the page

## Testing

Driven in Chromium end to end: navigation both ways, playback start/stop, the space-bar toggle, switching bands mid-song, jumping via the lyric sheet, and reaching a clean ending at 100%. No console errors on either page.

The arrangements were also rendered through an `OfflineAudioContext` to confirm neither band is silent or clipping (pop and jazz land within 0.1% of each other on RMS, peaks 0.85 and 0.75).

Two bugs found and fixed during that testing:

- the karaoke line was a flex container with a gap, so syllables of one word rendered as separate items — *"Pan cake"* instead of *"Pancake"*
- the screen-event queue was filled beat-events-first, leaving it out of time order; since it is read strictly front-to-back, syllable highlights would have flushed in a clump at the end of every bar instead of tracking the tune

## Note on the live site

The site publishes from `main`, so the song appears at https://chengsth.github.io/rabbit/ about a minute after this merges.

author: sunprema
body:
Closes #161

A 21-chapter systems-design book in seven parts, persona `the-crafter`, theme `swiss`.

## What's here

| | |
|---|---|
| Book id | `designing-edge-to-cloud-operational-platforms` |
| Chapters | 21, in seven parts, plus a cheatsheet |
| Execution mode | `skill_command` — the bookbank plugin's skills were invocable in-session and `create-book-from-issue` was run as a skill, deferring to `write-book`'s queue procedure |
| Cover | Typeset from the book's own design system (no image model, no art round-trip); no `images[]` slots declared |
| Research | `research.json`, 31 sources, per-concept claims/snippets/pitfalls |

The issue's premise — *the cloud can optimise operations, but the field must remain safe and useful when the cloud, network, or individual services are unavailable* — is carried as the book's spine. Every chapter states where the safety boundary falls rather than blurring it: the book teaches availability and graceful degradation as architectural properties, and is explicit that operational safety is owned by dedicated, independently certified systems outside this platform's scope.

## Checks

- **`validate_book.py`** — **0 errors**, 3 warnings. All three are the deliberate `"sources": []` markers the research contract asks for on claims I could not source, so a later verify pass can find them.
- **`qa-book.py`** — 23 pages rendered at 1440px and 500px: **0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes**.

## Conventions

- Branch is `claude/book-161-edge-to-cloud-operational-platforms`, following the `claude/book-<issue>-<slug>` convention. This **overrides** the dispatch wrapper's generic session-branch name, because the branch name is functionally load-bearing for the image-request Action.

## Issue parse — reinterpretation recorded

The issue's **Seed concepts** field held a full prose outline rather than one concept per line. Applying the conservative parse, the 21 explicit `### Chapter N` headers became the `concepts[]` entries (each carrying its Part as `unit` and its bullet list distilled into `brief`). The surrounding framing prose, the requested recurring chapter format, and the appendix list were folded into `notes` for the build and are preserved in `research.json`; the appendices themselves ship as the cheatsheet, per the issue's note to keep things tight.

## Environment substitutions

Recorded so the drift is visible rather than silent:

1. **`gh` CLI absent** — GitHub MCP tools used instead, at the same scope (issue read/label/comment, PR create).
2. **`WebFetch` egress-blocked for every domain attempted** (`kafka.apache.org`, `cwiki.apache.org`, `docs.confluent.io`, `aws.amazon.com`, `en.wikipedia.org` and others). Research therefore rests on **WebSearch result summaries plus the primary-source URLs those searches surfaced**, not on full-page reads. Claims were deliberately held to well-established, corroborated mechanics; version-specific and numeric assertions are listed in `research.json`'s `volatile` for a later pass to re-verify directly. This is the one thing worth a reviewer's attention.
3. **Chromium needs `--no-sandbox` under root.** `render-cover.sh` and `qa-book.py` hard-code their flag lists, so `CHROME_BIN` (their own documented extension point) was pointed at a small wrapper in the session scratchpad. No plugin file was modified — the plugin tree was treated as read-only throughout, and the diagram-kit and book-progress runtimes were vendored via `library/vendor.sh`.
4. **No WebP encoder available** (neither Pillow nor `cwebp`; nothing was installed to obtain one). The cover was rendered through the headless browser at exactly 16:10, 1600×1000, supersampled at 2×, and ships as **`cover.png`** — which `build-library.py`'s `cover_rel()` resolves at the same precedence as `cover.webp` (`cover.{webp,png}` at the book root), and which `apache-camel` in this repo already does. The gallery will not fall back to a gradient.

No omissions otherwise: both required checks ran for real, and the cover is a genuine render rather than a placeholder.

author: ewrogers
body:
## Summary

- replace the deferred self-draw replay workaround with the verified 7.41 translucent-walk branch patch
- derive `is_walking` from accepted steps, confirmed progress, pending route work, rejection, and stall state
- reapply full processor affinity during the bounded startup window for direct loader and daemon REST launches
- reject native cast commands when the exact system message `That doesn't work here.` arrives during the bounded response window
- document the combined release behavior and add focused state coverage

## Behavior

At RVA `0x001F36F1`, the default launch patch changes `75 1E` to `75 2A`. This routes the preserved translucent transition through the full human appearance update and supersedes the deferred packet replay introduced by `fe548f3`. The executable is never modified on disk; unsupported fingerprints and byte mismatches fail closed.

`is_walking` no longer trusts the client's stale route-active byte. It remains true across confirmed steps while a planned route has pending work, and clears for rejected or blocked steps, empty or completed routes, and a one-second stall.

The loader now monitors the bounded post-resume startup window and restores the full system affinity if the client resets itself to CPU 0. Direct loader launches and daemon REST launches share this path.

After the native client accepts a cast request, daRPC keeps the command pending for 500 ms. An exact system-channel `That doesn't work here.` response completes it as `Failed(Rejected)`; silence succeeds and unrelated messages do not consume it.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo test --workspace --all-features`
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
- `mdbook build docs`
- native Windows i686 focused tests: 231 passed, 1 ignored
- native Windows i686 focused Clippy with all targets/features and warnings denied
- native Windows i686 DLL and loader build
- prior native direct and isolated daemon REST launch checks observed affinity restored from `0x1` to `0xFF`
- prior suspended-launch and authorized live-client byte checks verified the runtime patch

The no-cast-map response is covered by deterministic packet-message tests. Live gameplay verification was not performed because it would require logging into a game account.

author: anthonyhdd
body:
*"Je tombe souvent sur des doublons à la suite."* It is a server bug, and it is measurable.

## The mechanism

Both live overloads of `feed_page` sort by

```sql
order by least(h.n_attempts, 3) asc, <score> desc, h.created_at desc
```

and paginate with

```sql
and (p_before is null or h.created_at < p_before)
```

…where the client sends `S.cursor = rows[rows.length-1].created_at` — **the created_at of the page's last row**. Under a non-chronological sort that row is not the oldest one in the page; it is merely the one that ranked lowest, and its timestamp sits somewhere arbitrary in the page's range.

Run against the live database while writing this:

```
page 1: 8 rows.  page 2: 8 rows, of which 2 were already in page 1.
```

**`kfSeen()` can never catch those.** It is written by `activate()`, so it knows only the slides that were actually *looked at* — and the duplicate arrives while its twin is still sitting unviewed a few slides below. That is precisely why they land next to each other rather than a session apart.

## The client half — what ships here

No row is mounted if its id is already on screen, and repeats inside a single page collapse too. The count is emitted as `feed_dupe_blocked {n, of}` rather than absorbed in silence: it is the only reading of how much of each page the broken cursor re-serves, it should fall to zero when the cursor is fixed, and it is the proof that it did.

## The server half — written up, deliberately NOT applied

`infra/2026-08-16-feed-pagination-cursor.sql`. It matters well beyond duplicates:

> the same mismatch also **SKIPS** every row newer than the pivot, from every later page — and no client-side de-duplication can hand back a hide the query never returned. The feed is quietly smaller than the corpus, and `rows.length < KF_PAGE` then latches `S.done` and ends it early.

The proposed form goes back to **OFFSET**, which the original 5-argument overload already used before the rewrite dropped it. The ordering is deterministic (no `random()`), and the two leading sort keys are volatile enough — `n_attempts` moves on every play, the score on every reaction — that a keyset cursor would drift under the reader. `p_before` is demoted to a "feed opened at" epoch guard so hides published mid-scroll cannot shift the window. It **adds a rung and edits nothing**, so pages loaded before the migration are untouched.

Left unapplied on purpose: it is a live RPC change and it is your call when it goes in. Say the word and I'll apply and verify it.

## Tests

The regression test fails without the fix, and its failure output is the report verbatim:

```
p0,p1,p2,p3,p4,p5,p6,p7,p1,p2,p3,p4,p5,p7
```

Passing: `every slide on screen is a different hide (8 slides, 8 distinct)` and `the re-served rows are counted ({"n":6,"of":8})`.

`node scripts/check.mjs` green, `main` merged in.

author: tm-elden
body:
## Intent

Build the redaction pipeline (C14) and the search index (C4 retrieval layer) that will feed the manager/planner bot in a later task.

Part 1 - src/ap_redact/ (new module): a deterministic pipeline package dir -> redacted chunk stream + redaction report.
- Person identifiers scrubbed by default: author on every label row, owners.analyst.id / owners.reviewer.id / owners.agent.* in the manifest.
- Secret detection: regex set for known key formats (AWS, GitHub, PEM headers, JWT-shaped, emails, SSN-like patterns) plus an entropy check on long tokens. A high-severity hit means the package is NOT indexed - fail closed - and the reason is recorded in the redaction report for the console to surface later (no console UI built in this task).
- Business content (supplier names, part numbers, quantities, contract refs) is explicitly NOT redacted - don't over-redact.
- confidentiality (from the manifest) maps to chunk metadata for role-based retrieval filtering, not content removal.
- Per-profile allow/deny field paths in profiles/<name>/redaction.json, loaded the same way as the existing reason_codes.json pattern (src/ap_gate/profiles.py) - no file present means core defaults only.
- Redaction report is a store sidecar keyed to (package_id, version), never written into the package's own qa/ directory - packages are immutable after publish, so this must not touch package content.
- Test: a fixture package salted with fake secrets - assert none appear in any indexed chunk, and assert an authorized human can still read the raw, unredacted package from the store directly.

Part 2 - src/ap_index/ (new module):
- Chunk each approved package (only status: approved in the store) into typed rows: manifest summary fields, each override/judgment/truth row, RUN_SUMMARY.md sections, exception rows. Each chunk tagged with package_id, package_version, as_of, profile, field_path/row id, confidentiality.
- Index in SQLite FTS5 (verified available on this system's sqlite build) with the tags as filterable columns alongside the full-text index. No vector database, no embeddings - the entire pilot corpus is ~45K tokens/year; FTS5 + structured filters is the right tool at this scale, not a vector DB.
- ap_index consumes only the output of ap_redact - never raw package content - so nothing unredacted can structurally end up in the index.
- Reindex hook: when a package's review status changes (approve/recall via ap_review), re-index just that one package. A full rebuild at this scale is seconds, so no over-engineered incremental update logic. Deliberately not wired as an automatic side effect of ap_review.ReviewWorkflow.transition (would invert module layering) - reindex_package() is a plain function a caller invokes after a transition.
- Scoping filters (approved-only, confidentiality-by-role) are computed and ready to apply at query time - search(query, filters) and get_chunk(chunk_id)-style functions only. NOT building the /chat/manager endpoint or any LLM call in this task, just the index and its query surface.

Acceptance criteria:
- Both modules have real test coverage per the acceptance bars above (tests/test_ap_redact.py, tests/test_ap_index.py).
- examples/commodity-commit-v1 indexes cleanly end to end (redact -> index -> query) as the reference case, once approved through the existing review workflow in the test.
- CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md gets module-map entries for ap_redact and ap_index at the same bar as the existing phase-2 entries.

Implementation notes/decisions made along the way:
- Added ap_gate.profiles.load_profile_redaction following the exact reason_codes.json/training_grade.json no-file-means-defaults precedent.
- Person-identifier scrubbing runs in two passes: structured field removal (owners.*.id, agent subtree, author field on label rows) plus a free-text mention-replacement pass, since RUN_SUMMARY.md prose independently re-types the analyst id ("**Analyst:** planner.example") which the structured scrub alone would miss.
- Secret entropy detector excludes pure-hex tokens and uses a 4.6 bits/char threshold (tuned empirically: sha256 content hashes ~3.9, business-content external_refs like "contracts://supplier-ACME/..." ~4.3, real random secrets ~4.7-5.0) to avoid false-positiving on the package format's own legitimate hash fields and contract references.
- FTS5 search sanitizes free-text queries by literal-quoting every token before MATCH, because raw part-number-shaped queries like "BBU-100" are misparsed by bare FTS5 syntax as a NOT operator.
- reindex_package() re-derives index membership from the store's current status on every call (approved -> redact+index; anything else -> ensure removed) rather than diffing a transition, and is invoked by the caller (e.g. a test, or a later API route) after ap_review.ReviewWorkflow.transition - not wired in automatically, to avoid ap_review depending on ap_index.

## What Changed

- Added `src/ap_redact/` (C14): a deterministic `redact_package(package_dir, manifest, ...)` pipeline producing a `Chunk` stream plus a `RedactionReport`. Scrubs person identifiers (`author` on label rows, `owners.analyst.id`/`owners.reviewer.id`/`owners.agent.*`) via both structured field removal and a word-boundary free-text mention pass, runs a secrets scan (`secrets_scan.py`: AWS/GitHub/PEM/JWT/email/SSN-like regexes plus an entropy check tuned to exclude hex content hashes) that fails the package closed on any high-severity hit, carries `confidentiality` through as chunk metadata rather than redacting it, and supports per-profile `redaction.json` allow/deny field-path overrides. `report.py` persists the `RedactionReport` as a store sidecar keyed by `(package_id, package_version)`, outside the package's own immutable bytes/`qa/`.
- Added `src/ap_index/` (C4): SQLite FTS5-backed retrieval built only on top of `ap_redact.Chunk` output (`IndexStore`/`index_store.py`), with tag columns for filterable metadata (`package_id`, `package_version`, `as_of`, `profile`, `field_path`, `confidentiality`) alongside full-text search. `index_package` replace-on-writes a package version's chunks; `search(query, filters)` literal-quotes query tokens before FTS5 `MATCH` to avoid misparsing part-number-shaped queries; `reindex.py::reindex_package` re-derives index membership from the store's current status (approved → redact+index, otherwise → remove) as a plain function invoked after an `ap_review` transition, not wired in automatically.
- Extended `src/ap_gate/profiles.py` with `load_profile_redaction`, following the existing `reason_codes.json`/`training_grade.json` no-file-means-defaults pattern.
- Added `tests/test_ap_redact.py` and `tests/test_ap_index.py` covering the secret-salted-fixture redaction guarantee, raw-package-still-readable-from-store guarantee, and an end-to-end `examples/commodity-commit-v1` approve → redact → index → query flow.
- Updated `AGENTS.md` with module-map entries for `ap_redact` and `ap_index`, and added a `CHANGELOG.md` entry for the phase-3 slice.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The only change since round 1 is the fix to src/ap_redact/redact.py: mention-scrubbing now uses a \b-bounded regex instead of str.replace, correctly eliminating the substring false-positive risk on business content (e.g. a short id no longer matches as a substring inside an unrelated word), and the added len(v) > 2 filter for analyst/reviewer ids only affects candidacy for the free-text mention pass — structured field removal via scrub_manifest_dict/scrub_label_row is unaffected and still unconditionally drops those fields regardless of length. Verified no other files changed in this fix round (working tree clean, diff limited to redact.py).

## Testing

`Ran the targeted ap_redact/ap_index pytest suite (all 16 pass, including a new regression test I added for the branch's last commit), verified that new test actually catches the pre-fix bug by reverting redact.py and re-running it

body:
On staging, every `wp` invocation logs one mcp-adapter error per Post Kinds ability: `WordPress ability 'post_kinds/list_kinds' does not exist.` The underscore names in that log are the pre-#126 build — updating the staging plugin clears those specifically — but the mechanism outlives the rename: `Abilities_Manager::filter_mcp_server_abilities()` appends all 13 declared names to `wp_pinch_mcp_server_abilities` unconditionally, and under WP-CLI the MCP adapter builds its tool list in a lifecycle where `wp_abilities_api_init` never registered them. Any advertised-but-unregistered name gets logged as an error by the adapter.

Same defect and fix as link-extension-for-xfn#19.

## What changed

The filter now bails before `init` (which also keeps it from triggering the abilities registry's lazy init earlier than core intends), then advertises only the names `wp_has_ability()` confirms. `wp_has_ability()` rather than `wp_get_ability()` because the getter fires `_doing_it_wrong()` for missing names — the guard shouldn't swap adapter errors for core notices.

## Test

`tests/phpunit/integration/McpServerAbilitiesTest.php` (mirrors the link-extension-for-xfn regression tests, reflection-reset of `WP_Abilities_Registry::$instance` in `tear_down`) asserts:

- with no abilities registered, the filter returns the incoming list untouched
- existing non-Post-Kinds entries pass through unchanged
- once the registry initializes, all 13 registered abilities are advertised
- with two abilities unregistered, exactly the remaining subset is advertised

Confirmed the tests bite: 3 of 4 fail against the unguarded filter.

Local runs: full unit (1090) and integration (146) suites green, PHPCS 0 errors, PHPStan level 5 clean.

## Summary
`whatsapp.group_allow_from` in config.yaml now authorizes mention-triggered group turns — previously only the `WHATSAPP_GROUP_ALLOWED_USERS` process env var did, and under `gateway.multiplex_profiles` the documented config surface was silently dropped.

Root cause: triggered WhatsApp group messages carry `user_id=None` (shared-transcript observe path strips sender identity), so authorization falls to the chat-scoped path in `_is_user_authorized`. That path only knew Telegram/QQ chat keys, and its adapter-extra fallback resolved the adapter by the routed profile — under multiplex, the WhatsApp adapter is registered on the default profile, so the lookup failed closed and the fallback never fired. Result: invisible drop (`Ignoring message with no user_id from whatsapp`, DEBUG only) unless the same allowlist was duplicated as a root `.env` var.

Fixes #87830 (reported by @NehoraiHadad).

## Changes
- `gateway/authz_mixin.py`: chat-scoped fallback now falls back to the gateway's own platform config (the same values that gated intake) when the routed-profile adapter lookup yields nothing; for WhatsApp/WhatsApp Cloud, honors `group_allow_from` as the chat allowlist — gated on the effective `group_policy` actually being `allowlist` (open/disabled carry no restriction signal, so no fail-open), with phone/LID/JID alias expansion matching intake semantics.
- `tests/gateway/test_whatsapp_group_allow_from_authz.py`: 7 regression tests — config allowlist authorizes no-user-id turns, routed-profile (multiplex) sources, wildcard; denies unlisted groups, `group_policy: open` with a stale list, and the no-config case. Sabotage-verified: 3 tests fail on unfixed `origin/main`.

## Validation
| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `group_allow_from` in config, mention in listed group (multiplex) | silent drop | authorized |
| Same, `group_policy: open` | drop | still denied (no fail-open) |
| Unlisted group | drop | still denied |
| Targeted suites (whatsapp/telegram/auth_fallback/multiplex authz) | — | 36 passed |

## Changelog Entry
To be copied to the [draft changelog](https://github.com/DataBiosphere/toil/wiki/Draft-Changelog) by merger:

 * The WDL quickstart example now specifies a WDL version and is covered by a test.

## Description

Fixes #5534.

The WDL in the quickstart has no `version`, so it is parsed as draft-2 and `toil-wdl-runner` fails on it:

```
(Ln 1, Col 1) MissingVersion, document should declare WDL version; draft-2 assumed
WDL.Error.EvalError: Cannot evaluate no expression for message

This ports the example to WDL 1.0 (`input` sections, `~{}` placeholder, the call passing `message` through), so the inputs file uses `write_simple_file.message`.

Verified locally on an Apple Silicon macOS host with Docker:

```
$ toil-wdl-runner wdl-helloworld.wdl wdl-helloworld.json -o out --logDebug --retryCount=0
Workflow stopped. Success: True
{"write_simple_file.write_file.test": ".../out/write_simple_file.write_file/wdl-helloworld-output.txt"}
$ cat out/write_simple_file.write_file/wdl-helloworld-output.txt
Hello world!

$ pytest src/toil/test/wdl/wdltoil_test.py -k test_documentation_quickstart -x -q
1 passed, 35 deselected

New **Fee Discount** doctype — an operator-editable list at `/app/fee-discount`: one row per Flash username granting a **0–100% discount off the FLASH fee** (processor fees are never discounted), with checkboxes scoping it to **Card Top-Ups** and/or **Bank Cashouts**, an **Active** toggle to suspend without deleting, and a notes field for who approved it / until when.

The companion flash PR (lnflash/flash — feat/fee-discounts) reads the active rows via REST through a 60s-cached reader that **fails open to 0%** — a missing doctype, ERPNext blip, or malformed row charges the standard fee and never blocks a credit or an offer. Because of that fail-open, a drifted field name would not error anywhere — it would silently stop discounting — so the contract test pins the exact fieldnames the reader selects.

`test_fee_discount_contract.py` — doctype contract (fieldnames, autoname, checkbox defaults) + controller validate() behavior via the suite's no-Frappe-runtime stub pattern. `221 passed` locally (2 pre-existing collection errors on main from missing local deps, untouched).

author: kjbrum
body:
<!-- Suggested title: [Admin] Add the metaobject details form extension contract -->

### Background

Admin Web is adding an internal target that lets an app replace the visible form area on an app-owned Metaobject details page. Admin still owns route state, validation, Save, Discard, and persistence.

This PR adds the app-facing authoring and testing contract for `admin.metaobject-details.form.render` on the active `2026-10-rc` line. Core accepts the target from `2025-10`; new SDK features land on the active release-candidate line.

Related work:

- Superseded Admin Web Stage 0/1 prototype: https://meteorite.shopify.io/repos/shop/world/pulls/2004976
- Core target registration: https://meteorite.shopify.io/repos/shop/world/pulls/2005108
- Admin Web Stage 2 runtime: https://meteorite.shopify.io/repos/shop/world/pulls/2005109
- Stage 2 architecture: https://metaobject-ui-extension.quick.shopify.io/llms.txt
- Target registration playbook: https://extensibility-target-playbook.quick.shopify.io/

### Solution

Add a narrow `MetaobjectFormApi` and map it to the new Admin render target.

The supported API contains only:

- `extension`, `intents`, and `navigation` from the baseline Admin runtime;
- `snapshot`, a read-only signal with `value` and `subscribe`;
- async `setFieldValue({key, value})`; and
- `setSaveHandler(handler | null)` for pending writes that Admin must await before saving.

The snapshot contains the complete trusted form definition whenever the target launches:

```ts
interface MetaobjectFormSnapshotField {
  key: string;
  type: string;
  value: string;
  editable: boolean;
  errors: string[];
}
```

Admin launches the target only for definitions with at most 40 trusted fields. Larger definitions remain entirely native instead of receiving a truncated snapshot.

`setFieldValue` returns `SUCCESS` or one of these structural error codes:

- `UNKNOWN_FIELD`
- `READ_ONLY`
- `COMPUTED`
- `UNSUPPORTED_FIELD_TYPE`
- `INVALID_VALUE`
- `VALUE_TOO_LARGE`
- `NOT_ACTIVE`

The target intentionally does not expose raw form state, submit, reset, mutation helpers, a GraphQL client, tools, pickers, or caller-supplied app identity. A generic Host can expose an incidental empty `data: {}`, but `data` is not part of this supported contract.

### Component architecture

The target allows seven Polaris components:

- `Grid`
- `GridItem`
- `Heading`
- `Section`
- `Text`
- `TextField`
- contextual `MetaobjectField`

`<s-metaobject-field fieldKey="..." />` asks Admin to render its native editor for a field in the current route form. This preserves native behavior for references and other complex field types. The extension can combine these host-rendered fields with custom Remote DOM editors.

The Preact example demonstrates the expected lifecycle:

```text
snapshot.value
  -> render current host values
  -> queue async setFieldValue writes
  -> register setSaveHandler for the newest queued write
  -> clear the handler with setSaveHandler(null)
  -> unmount with render(null, document.body)
```

It also restores the host value after structural rejection and reports transport failures separately.

### Tester and package behavior

- Add a target-specific tester factory with the same narrow API.
- Initialize `intents` as `{launchUrl: undefined}` without a fake `invoke` method.
- Initialize `snapshot` with no fields and no unsupported `peek` method.
- Omit the unsupported incidental `data` object.
- Export the new API types and both named and default `MetaobjectFormComponents` types.
- Add a minor changeset for `@shopify/ui-extensions` and `@shopify/ui-extensions-tester`.

### 🎩

This prototype intentionally omits new automated test coverage. Validate the package contract with build and static checks:

```sh
yarn build
yarn type-check
yarn lint
```

Then verify a consumer project:

1. Import `@shopify/ui-extensions/preact`.
2. Declare `admin.metaobject-details.form.render` as the target.
3. Read `shopify.snapshot.value` and subscribe when reactive updates are needed.
4. Await `shopify.setFieldValue({key, value})` and handle each error code.
5. Register the newest pending write with `shopify.setSaveHandler`.
6. Clear the handler with `shopify.setSaveHandler(null)` during cleanup.
7. Render a native field with `<s-metaobject-field fieldKey="..." />`.
8. Confirm that TypeScript rejects unsupported APIs such as `data`, `submit`, `reset`, and `snapshot.peek()`.

A full browser tophat also needs the matching Core registration and Admin Web branch. Follow `tooling/metaobject-form-extension-tophat/README.md` in the Admin Web change after Core deploys.

### Validation completed

- Package build
- Type-check
- Lint
- `git diff --check`

### Checklist

- [ ] I have :tophat:'d these changes. The real app-dev tophat waits for deployed Core registration and a human-linked development shop.
- [x] I have updated relevant documentation, the target example, and tester guidance.

author: creditcomebackclub
body:
## Root cause
The agreement popup opened a tab that showed nothing and landed on the portal's **Overview** tab.

The server is fine — a live request to `portal-agreement-view` with a real token returns:
```
status       : 200
content-type : text/html; charset=utf-8
body         : 18513 bytes of valid HTML
```
`curl` never reproduced the bug because **curl has no service worker**.

This is a PWA. The SW's `navigateFallbackDenylist` covered the static marketing/legal pages but not server endpoints, so any *navigation* to `/.netlify/functions/*` got the precached `index.html`. The new tab booted the SPA, which has no route for that path and renders at its default `'overview'` tab — precisely the reported symptom. The existing comment above that config describes this exact failure mode; function endpoints were just never added.

## Fix
- Add `/^\/\.netlify\//` and `/^\/api\//` to `navigateFallbackDenylist`. `/api/*` redirects to functions via `netlify.toml`, so this also fixes **`guide-download`** (opened as `/api/guide-download?token=...`), which had the same latent hijack.
- Check the `window.open()` result in `viewSignedAgreement`, matching what `RecoveryPlanTab` already does — its absence is why this failed silently rather than surfacing anything.

Verified both patterns are baked into the generated `dist/sw.js`.

## Note on rollout
`registerType: 'autoUpdate'`, so existing clients pick up the new SW automatically — but a client with the old SW cached may need one reload before the fix takes effect. Worth a hard refresh when testing.

## Test plan
- [ ] Billing → "View signed agreement" renders the document in a new tab (hard-refresh first to pick up the new SW)
- [ ] The tab no longer lands on the Overview tab
- [ ] Blueprint still opens (Supabase-signed PDF, different path — confirm no regression)
- [ ] `/api/guide-download?token=...` serves the guide rather than the app shell
- [ ] With popups blocked, a clear "Popup blocked" toast appears instead of silence

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches client PII document access (token-in-URL auth and HTML proxying) with mitigations (short TTL, re-resolution, CSP); PWA denylist changes affect all function/API navigations for installed clients until the SW updates.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes **“View signed agreement”** opening a blank tab that lands on **Overview** by stopping the PWA service worker from treating navigations to **`/.netlify/functions/*`** and **`/api/*`** as SPA routes (same issue as latent **`guide-download`** hijacks).
> 
> **Agreement delivery** no longer returns a Supabase Storage signed URL (which forces HTML as `text/plain` and shows raw markup). **`portal-agreement-url`** now mints a **120s HMAC view token** and returns a same-origin link to new **`portal-agreement-view`**, which re-resolves the client’s document via shared **`_agreementDocument`** (three onboarding storage paths), verifies the token matches that resolution, and serves the HTML with **`text/html`** plus a strict **CSP**. **`ClientPortal`** surfaces a **popup blocked** toast when `window.open` fails.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 28998ba72f30b7ca5346fc06e0f80672351e7b8f. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

author: fametrano
body:
Follow-up to #967, from the post-merge review on it
([comment](https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/pull/967#issuecomment-5309440110)).
`17af5e89` landed a `_PythonPubKeyTweakChain` that states two things about
itself which nothing held.

**It serializes before it steps.** The comment says why — *a chain left
stepped by a call that raised would answer the next tweak from a point its
caller never received* — and the new `_Case` in `bool_parameter_test`
repeats it. Swapping the two lines left the suite at **27895 passed**.

**It answers `compressed`.** Replacing the parameter in the body with a
hardcoded `True` was killed only by `test_a_kind_refuses_a_non_bool`, which
is the *kind* of the argument and not the answer it asks for.

Neither has a caller to reach it: both derivations pass the literal `True`,
and the only refusal a path can provoke is the sum at infinity. That is what
makes them a contract rather than a behaviour — the union alias has mypy
check one call against both implementations — and a contract with no caller
is a comment unless something asserts it. Both are asserted here, and each
fails its own line of `test_the_chain_contract_no_derivation_here_asks_for`.

### And one thing the class docstring did not say

The two implementations *do* part on `compressed`, while the docstring says
the contract is the bindings':

```
python    tweak_add(t, compressed="yes")  ->  BTClibTypeError: invalid compressed type: str
bindings  tweak_add(t, compressed="yes")  ->  03...   (no raise; the chain has stepped)
```

`bytes_from_point` refuses a value that is not a bool; libsecp256k1's
serialization takes it for the flag it is truthy as. This one is the
stricter, which is the side to be on — and it is what makes the ordering
matter at all, the other implementation never raising there. Unreachable
from here, `compressed` being typed `bool` and passed as one, so it is
written down rather than left to be rediscovered.

Not asserted of the bindings: their behaviour there is a dependency's, and a
suite that pinned it would go red for a check they grew.

### Verified

- gate: `uvx pre-commit run --all-files`, every hook Passed
- suite and ratchet: `27896 passed, 6 skipped`, coverage 100.00%
- both mutations, under `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1` with a passing baseline
  before and a passing control after: the swapped order and the ignored flag
  each now fail, by name

Refs #966 — the script engine's two verifications and the eleven unguarded
imports are what is still between here and an installed btclib that answers
without the bindings.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Summary by Sourcery

Assert the behaviour contract of the Python BIP32 pubkey tweak chain around the compressed flag and serialization order, and document the stricter semantics versus the bindings implementation.

Documentation:
- Clarify in the changelog and _PythonPubKeyTweakChain docstring how compressed is handled, the stricter validation of non-bool values, and why serialization precedes the tweak step.

Tests:
- Add a dedicated BIP32 test verifying that _PythonPubKeyTweakChain enforces bool-only compressed, serializes before stepping, and remains consistent with the bindings chain where their behaviour is relied upon.

body:
## Summary

Captain requirement: click a client's name/icon anywhere it appears → land on their patient page (`/(app)/today/[clientId]`, the "Salama"/PatientDetails/EHR screen).

Adds a shared `ClientLink` component (`src/components/ClientLink.tsx`) — wraps `Avatar` + caller-supplied name/subtitle content in a single `Pressable` routed to `/(app)/today/<clientId>`, with `accessibilityRole="link"` and label `Open <name>'s page`. Every screen below reuses it instead of a hand-rolled Pressable, so the affordance can't drift between screens.

## Inventory (every client name/avatar rendering found, and what happened to each)

**Linked (new):**
- `today/index.tsx` — next-session countdown banner: client name is now an underlined link (no Avatar there originally, so none added — text-only affordance to avoid a mismatched avatar tint on the brand-strong background).
- `today/index.tsx` — schedule `SessionCard` rows: **already** navigated whole-row to `/(app)/today/<clientId>` before this PR (unchanged, confirmed by new test).
- `patterns/index.tsx` — caseload list, `ClientRowWide`/`ClientRowNarrow`: see "Judgement calls" below — name/avatar split into its own `ClientLink`.
- `patterns/[clientId].tsx` — all three header states (`NoReadingsYet`, `PatternsView`, `RiskReview`) — Avatar+name header now a `ClientLink`. `RiskReview` passes `avatarTone="risk"` to preserve its forced-risk avatar tint even when reached via `?risk=1` on a non-acute client.
- `patterns/history.tsx` — added a small `ClientLink` chip above the existing `PageHeader` (previously the client's name only appeared in prose/eyebrow text, no discrete link element existed here).
- `patterns/safety-plan.tsx` — Avatar+name header now a `ClientLink`.
- `session/index.tsx` — pre-capture screen's existing-client card (Avatar+name) now a `ClientLink`.
- `session/review.tsx` — **session review header**: added a small `ClientLink` chip between the Back link and the note title (there was no discrete client-identity element in the header before — the title is the session label, not the client's name). Renders nothing (no dead link) when `client` doesn't resolve for the `clientId` param.

**Deliberately left as plain text (prose, not a discrete identity element):**
- Back-link labels ("Back to Amara's patterns"), `PageHeader` eyebrows ("Prep · Amara · 10:30"), narrative sentences ("You're ready for Amara", "Amara doesn't have a completed safety plan yet"), and the in-flight recording status pill ("Recording · Session 5 with Amara"). Turning every inline first-name mention into a link would be link-soup and isn't what "click the name/icon" means for a sentence. The recording-status case is also a deliberate safety call: navigating away mid-recording is risky, so it stays inert.
- `Escalate.tsx` shows the client's `tokenId`, never the name — out of scope.
- `charts.tsx` `clientLabel` is chart-annotation text inside an SVG-like drawing, not a tappable UI element.
- `settings/index.tsx` shows only an aggregate client count, no per-client identity.

## Judgement calls (row primary-action conflicts, per the brief's rule)

- **`patterns/index.tsx` `ClientRowWide`/`ClientRowNarrow`**: the row's own tap already opens `/(app)/patterns/<id>` (charts/trends), which must stay the row's primary action. Restructured so the name/avatar is its own **sibling** `Pressable` (`ClientLink`, → patient page) next to a second **sibling** `Pressable` (→ patterns page), both siblings of the pre-existing Outreach icon buttons — matching the file's own established "no nested `<button>`" pattern (see the pre-existing N3 comments this PR extends). Same flex proportions preserved (name 2.4 / rest 6.7 / outreach 1.2 = 9.1+1.2, same as the original 9.1+1.2 total). Narrow layout: the badge stays inline next to the name inside `ClientLink`; the session/score/trend/risk block became a second, indented `Pressable` below it.
- **`session/index.tsx` PreCapture card**: no conflict — the card wasn't tappable before, so `ClientLink` was a pure addition.
- **`today/index.tsx` next-session banner**: no conflict — the adjacent "Review & prep" button already went to the same route; the name itself just wasn't independently tappable before.

## Accessibility
Every new tappable uses `accessibilityRole="link"` with an `Open <name>'s page` label, is a standard RN `Pressable` (keyboard-focusable on web), and no button is nested inside another button anywhere touched by this PR.

## Tests
- `src/components/__tests__/ClientLink.test.tsx` — the shared component's own role/label/navigation.
- `src/app/(app)/today/__tests__/index.test.tsx` — today list: session row press → `/(app)/today/<id>`; banner name link → same target.
- `src/app/(app)/session/__tests__/review.test.tsx` — session review header chip → `/(app)/today/<id>`.
- `src/app/(app)/patterns/__tests__/history.test.tsx` — history header chip → `/(app)/today/<id>`.

## Verified
- `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean.
- `npm test` (harnesses + `jest --ci`) — 7 suites / 31 tests pass.
- `npx expo export --platform web` — succeeds, all 30 exported pages still carry the `noindex, nofollow` meta tag (CI's static-export check).

## Out of scope
- The patient page (`today/[clientId].tsx`) itself is unchanged beyond being the nav target — its content/Salama presentation wasn't touched.
- No drive-by refactors beyond what the sibling-pressable split required.

author: vlad-scherbich
body:
## Summary

Stabilize two flaky ddprof scenarios on CI runners:

### `ddprof_julia`

* CI flakes on `julia:latest`: first CPU profile cycle often has 0% stack match because JIT symbols aren't in `.debug/jit` yet.
* Fix: set **`allow_first_profile_failure: true`**, an existing analysis knob already used by `full_host`, `python_gunicorn_3.12`, etc.

### `ddprof_live_heap`

Intermittent CI failure: `should have been 100% +/- 5% … but was 94% with 6% error`

* alloc-space calls exactly two functions: `allocate_memory` (94%) and `leak_function` (6%). The scenario **intentionally** leaks via `leak_function` on every 3rd iteration. 
* The alloc-space regex only counted `allocate_memory→operator new`, so ~6% of bytes were being excluded by mistake.
* Fix: regex now covers **both** paths:
```regex
^.*;main;(allocate_memory\(unsigned long\);operator new\(unsigned long\)|leak_function\(int\))$
```

## Test plan
- [] CI green on ddprof matrix shard (both scenarios pass)
- [] ddprof_julia: first profile may fail tolerance; second+ should match true_main stacks
- [] ddprof_live_heap: alloc-space assertion at 100% ± 5% with both allocation paths in regex

author: aaronsb
body:
`package-lock.json` is tracked now, and the recipe uses `npm ci` so what
arch-repo builds and signs is what the lockfile records rather than whatever the
registry resolves that day.

That changes what the **release tarball** has to contain. arch-repo takes the
recipe from the default branch and the tarball from the tag, so `npm ci` fails
against `v1.1.0`'s tarball, which predates the lockfile:

```
npm error The `npm ci` command can only install with an existing
npm error package-lock.json with lockfileVersion >= 1.
```

A packaging fix needs no release. This is not one — the tarball itself has to
change, which is the case that does.

author: jjddean
body:
Ten commits from a production-hardening pass. Nothing here has been deployed —
production still runs the pre-fix build.

## Security

- **Privilege escalation.** `users.syncUser` passed `args.role` and `args.email`
  into `resolveUserRole`, which grants `admin` for either. Any signed-in user
  could call `syncUser({ role: "admin" })` and read every tenant's data. Proven
  end to end against the real Convex HTTP API, then re-run after the fix to
  confirm it refuses. Production had no unexpected admins.
- Three unauthenticated endpoints: an action that dropped the whole search
  collection and fetched arbitrary URLs (deleted, zero callers), a public
  mutation writing rule proposals from any MRN, and a webhook secret compared
  non-constant-time.
- `rule_definitions.upsert/setEnabled` write a table with no `orgId` and had no
  role check — any user could disable a blocking validation rule for everyone.
- `org_hmrc.getModeForOrg` returned any org's HMRC mode to anyone.
- Public tariff lookup moved out of an unauthenticated Convex action, which
  could not be rate limited per caller, into a limited API route.

## Duplicate customs filings

- `beginFollowUp` claims a declaration before amend/cancel dispatch. Both routes
  previously set status only after HMRC replied, so a double-click or a retry
  filed twice at CDS.
- Submit no longer reverts its claim on a 2xx with no `X-Conversation-ID` — HMRC
  had accepted, and re-opening invited a duplicate live entry.
- Amend/cancel persist status inside try/catch after acceptance, so an expired
  token cannot report a successful amendment as a 500.

## Customer-facing errors

Convex production redacts thrown `Error`s to "Server Error" — the original
reported crash was a readable guard message being hidden. 330 to 47 plain
throws; 81 UI sites use a safe renderer; `ApiError` preserves messages our own
routes author. A static test asserts the pattern repo-wide and caught four
instances nobody had reviewed.

## Onboarding

The reported `completeManagedService` crash plus four related defects: re-signup
lock-out, portal email squatting, direct-entry failure, opaque errors.

## Documents

All five upload flows discard orphans on failure, with a daily sweep as backstop
— it removed 22 real orphans on dev.

## CNS

Cancel outcomes classified on both ingest paths; follow-ups correlate by
`X-CSP-ID`, which they previously did not record at all.

## Schema

Three additive, optional changes — `documents.by_file`,
`notifications.originatingOperation`, `users.emailNormalized` plus index. No
field removed, no type narrowed. Every existing row validates.

## Tests

155 H1, 133 CNS, 51 unit, 14 portal, 18 authenticated E2E — including
cross-tenant and portal isolation attacks using real sessions and real IDs.

## After merge

1. Deploy Convex and Vercel **together**. Convex alone would show raw error
   payloads to the old UI; the new UI calls functions Convex would not yet have.
2. Run `users:backfillEmailNormalized` with `dryRun:false` on production.
3. Unrelated but live: `STRIPE_PRO_PRICE_ID` and `STRIPE_PAYG_PRICE_ID` are
   missing from production Convex, so two of three plans cannot check out.

author: nwodobe
body:
> **La migration reste NON APPLIQUÉE.** Cette PR corrige un document ; elle ne touche aucune base de données.

Le script livré par #168 **échouait sur PostgreSQL et n'installait donc rien**. Constaté par exécution sur une instance PostgreSQL 16.13 jetable, pas par relecture.

Un seul fichier : `docs/migrations/aflp_acces_perimetres_20260816.sql`, **+28 / −8**.

---

## 1. Ce qui échouait

```
psql:aflp_acces_perimetres_20260816.sql:74:
ERROR:  cannot use subquery in check constraint
```

La contrainte `profils_zone_cluster_coherents` contenait un `select` :

```sql
check ( cluster is null or zone is null
        or zone = (select c.zone_code from public.aflp_clusters c
                   where c.code = public.profils.cluster) )
```

PostgreSQL interdit toute sous-requête dans un `CHECK`. Les sections 1 à 3 étant encadrées par `begin; … commit;`, **la transaction entière était annulée** : ni les tables `aflp_zones` / `aflp_clusters`, ni les huit colonnes de périmètre sur `profils`, ni les trois fonctions de périmètre.

État relevé juste après l'échec, sur la base de test :

```
           objet            | count
----------------------------+-------
 tables aflp_*              |     0
 colonnes perimetre profils |     0
 fonctions aflp_*           |     0
 lignes profils             |     3
```

Le script ne cassait rien — **il ne faisait rien**. Appliqué en l'état, il aurait laissé croire à une migration passée alors que la base serait restée inchangée, et l'écran Administration aurait continué d'afficher « périmètre à renseigner » sans que personne comprenne pourquoi.

## 2. La correction

Une clé étrangère composite exprime la même règle, de façon déclarative. Sa sémantique par défaut (`MATCH SIMPLE`) couvre déjà le cas du périmètre partiel : dès que `cluster` **ou** `zone` est `NULL`, la contrainte ne s'applique pas — exactement l'intention du `cluster is null or zone is null` d'origine.

```sql
alter table public.profils       drop constraint if exists profils_zone_cluster_coherents;
alter table public.aflp_clusters drop constraint if exists aflp_clusters_code_zone_unique;
alter table public.aflp_clusters add  constraint aflp_clusters_code_zone_unique unique (code, zone_code);
alter table public.profils       add  constraint profils_zone_cluster_coherents
  foreign key (cluster, zone) references public.aflp_clusters(code, zone_code)
  on update cascade not valid;
```

**L'ordre des `drop` compte** : la clé étrangère dépend de la contrainte unique, et l'ordre inverse casse le rejeu (`cannot drop constraint … because other objects depend on it`). Je m'en suis aperçu en testant l'idempotence, pas en relisant — d'où l'insistance sur l'exécution réelle.

Le `not valid` d'origine est conservé : les lignes existantes ne sont pas rejetées.

Section 6 (retour arrière) mise à jour en conséquence, section 5 complétée par un contrôle des trois contraintes.

## 3. Vérifications

Toutes menées sur **le fichier du dépôt**, pas sur une reconstruction, avec une table `profils` reconstituée et trois comptes fictifs.

**Trois exécutions consécutives sur une base neuve** — aucune erreur, l'idempotence annoncée en en-tête est désormais réelle.

**Objets créés**

```
 zones              |     2
 clusters           |     6
 colonnes perimetre |     8
 fonctions aflp_    |     3
```

**Contraintes en place**

```
            conname             | contype
--------------------------------+---------
 aflp_clusters_code_zone_unique | u
 profils_authority_level_valide | c
 profils_zone_cluster_coherents | f
```

**Comportement**

| Cas | Attendu | Observé |
|---|---|---|
| `GBEKE_2` + `DIABO` | accepté | `UPDATE 1` |
| `GBEKE_1` + `DIABO` | refusé | `violates foreign key constraint … Key (cluster, zone)=(DIABO, GBEKE_1) is not present` |
| cluster seul, zone `NULL` | accepté | `UPDATE 1` |
| `authority_level='ROI'` | refusé | `violates check constraint "profils_authority_level_valide"` |
| `authority_level='GLOBAL'` | accepté | `UPDATE 1` |

**Non-régression** — les trois comptes de départ conservent leur rôle, `Supervisor` compris. Aucune conversion, aucune suppression.

Portes `verifier-js`, `verifier-html`, `verifier-liens` : **0 nouveau**. Aucune ligne ajoutée à un `*-baseline.json`.

## 4. Ce que cette PR ne fait pas

- **Aucun SQL exécuté sur une base réelle.** Seule une instance PostgreSQL locale et jetable a servi, supprimée après les tests.
- **La section 4 reste commentée** — colonne `villages.cluster_code`, trigger, politique RLS d'écriture. C'est elle qui rend le périmètre opposable côté serveur, et la seule partie capable de couper l'accès à des utilisateurs légitimes. Elle relève d'une décision séparée.
- **Aucun fichier hors `docs/migrations/`.**

## 5. Deux points pour le Branch Manager

**Cette PR est techniquement éligible à l'auto-fusion** — `docs/migrations/**` n'est pas sur la denylist, contrairement aux PR précédentes. Elle ne sera pourtant pas fusionnée seule : `agent-conditional-auto-merge.yml` exige le label `agent-auto-merge`, que je n'ai pas posé et ne poserai pas.

**Il n'existe toujours pas de script de retour arrière complet.** La section 6 est en commentaire et, de son propre aveu, ne supprime pas les colonnes de périmètre — pour ne pas perdre les affectations zone/cluster saisies depuis la migration. Le retour arrière est donc partiel par conception. Cela mérite d'être su avant d'exécuter quoi que ce soit sur la base de production en pleine campagne.

author: danialjaved
body:
Rune's input layer was written for a mouse. A sweep of `src/Rune.App` found zero references to `PointerDeviceType` and zero to `ManipulationMode`: nothing in the app had ever asked whether the thing touching it was a finger, a pen or a mouse. On a 2-in-1 held as a tablet the reading half was broken and most of the editing half was unreachable.

**Heads up on scope.** The branch was sitting at parity with `main` after #12 merged, with all of v0.8.0 still uncommitted in the working tree. That work is in here too, in the same commit, because it interleaves with the touch changes in the same files and could not be split cleanly after the fact. The v0.8.0 half is unchanged from what was already on disk.

## The blocker

`BeginSelection` captured the pointer on any press that landed on a glyph. Capturing a touch contact stops the ScrollViewer panning, and on a page of prose nearly every pixel is a glyph, so **a finger could not scroll the document at all**. Everything else was downstream of that.

## Touch changes

- **Gesture ownership** is one mechanism (`BeginExclusiveGesture` / `EndExclusiveGesture`) shared by all six canvas drags. It disables the scroll modes **and** `ZoomMode` together. That second part is not obvious and was got wrong first: with only the scroll modes off the page correctly refused to pan, but direct manipulation went on watching the contact in case it became a pinch and took the capture back the moment the finger moved.
- **`PointerCanceled` and `PointerCaptureLost` are handled**, for the first time. Six drag flags used to be cleared only on `PointerReleased`, so a gesture the system took away stranded the viewer mid-drag with panning still switched off. `SignaturePad` had always handled both; the viewer never did.
- **Text selection by finger**: hold selects the word under it, and the lift raises the existing menu with Highlight / Underline / Strikeout / Copy. A press landing on that selection drags it wider.
- **Form fields raise the soft keyboard** through `InputPaneInterop`, the same interop shape `PrintService` and `ShareService` already use. A PDF field is pixels PDFium drew rather than a XAML text input, so Windows saw nothing take focus and a field could be tapped and then never typed into.
- **Hit targets**: slop on links, fields and stamp bodies; corner handles keep their drawn size but gain a 24 DIP reach; the tap-versus-drag threshold for placing a picture loosens so finger jitter stops sizing it at random. Every one of these is zero or unchanged for a mouse, and `TouchMetrics` pins that by test.
- **Palm rejection** for ink: only the contact that began a stroke may extend it, and touch is ignored while a pen is drawing.
- **Routes for what only a keyboard could reach**: a second tap disarms a tool (Note, Image and Eraser have no options panel and so no Done button, which left a tablet stuck in eraser mode), delete moves into the hold menu, bookmark and the command palette into the hamburger, presentation goes back on a left-third tap.
- **Sizes**: find bar, zoom pill, sidebar switcher and Home button go to 40 px via a new `TouchTargetMin` token. The 34 px header is deliberately left alone, since those buttons sit in a 44 px bar with 2 px gaps and widening them would loosen the proportions the header is built on.

## Worth a reviewer's attention

**Hold-then-drag in one gesture does not work, and cannot.** The plan called for it. A contact cannot be reclaimed from direct manipulation once it has started: deciding to own the gesture 500 ms in gets the capture revoked the instant the finger travels. A trace showed it exactly, anchor set, ten stationary moves, then one move of three pixels followed by `PointerCaptureLost`, and the visible result was a selection one character wide. Ownership has to be decided on the press itself, which is why hold selects a word and a separate press extends it. That is the same mechanism a phone's selection handles use, without the handles.

## Testing

427 tests pass, up from 414.

This machine has no touchscreen, so the app was driven with `CreateSyntheticPointerDevice` + `InjectSyntheticPointerInput`, which produce genuine touch pointers that WinUI reports as `PointerDeviceType.Touch` and that direct manipulation treats as a finger. Verified on screen: a finger drag scrolls with no selection wash, hold selects a word, the markup menu appears on lift, a second press drags the selection out to three lines, and a mouse drag-select is unchanged.

Not verifiable here, and worth checking on real hardware:

- **The touch keyboard actually appearing.** `TryShow()` returns `true`, so Windows accepts the request, but the pane stays hidden while a hardware keyboard is attached and the device is not in tablet posture.
- **Pen palm rejection**, which needs a real digitizer.

`PROJECT.md` has not been updated for the touch work. Its section 7 gotchas deserve the direct-manipulation lesson above.


---

# Added since this PR was opened

## A website (`site/`)

Plain HTML and CSS published to GitHub Pages by `.github/workflows/pages.yml`.
No npm, no generator, no build step: the workflow copies `site/` and publishes
it, so there is nothing to keep patched.

- `index.html` landing page, `features.html` (every feature, the touch gestures,
  all 47 shortcuts), `privacy.html`.
- **`privacy.html` is the one that earns its keep.** The Store listing's privacy
  policy URL currently points at a raw GitHub blob, and certification follows
  that URL.
- `tools/gen-site-shortcuts.ps1` writes the shortcut tables from
  `ShortcutCatalog.cs`, which already calls itself the single source of truth
  for them. Hand-copying would have made a fourth copy after the app,
  PROJECT.md and the README, and those have drifted before.
- `tools/gen-site-images.ps1` reuses the Store screenshots at web size, 3.3 MB
  down to 1.1 MB. That set is deliberately licence-safe, so it did not need
  reshooting.

Checked at 375px, 768px and 1280px, light and dark, no horizontal overflow.

**On merge this deploys to https://danialjaved.github.io/rune/.** Pages is
already enabled with its source set to GitHub Actions; the workflow only fires
from `main`, so nothing has deployed yet.

⚠️ One thing to weigh before merging: the download section's "Go to Releases"
button points at GitHub Releases, which is still on **v0.4.0**. The Store and
winget routes are current. Either cut the 0.8.0 release first or accept that one
stale link for now.

## Accessibility

The app had **zero `AutomationProperties` anywhere**, and over twenty controls
are icon-only with a tooltip as their only label, so a screen reader announced
"button" for the whole toolbar, the zoom pill, the find bar and the sidebar
switcher.

30 names added in XAML and 11 to the code-built bars. They are trimmed rather
than copied from the tooltips: a tooltip is written for a sighted user hovering
and carries explanations and shortcut hints a screen reader should not read out.
