author: kemetra
body:
> **Contains a governed decision record.** `KHEPRI-DEC-019` is a proposal until you merge it — I drafted the record, I did not authorize it.

`R7-01`'s design note plus the decision answering its §6 question, which you authorized ("do recommended").

## The finding that reframes it

While drafting the record I found that **`RRA-001` already anticipated this exact case.** Its Requirements section reads:

> "Preserve the opaque owner ID as **the only future attachment point for separately approved commercial authentication**."

The attachment point was reserved for this purpose from the start, and reaching it requires something *separately approved* — which is what `KHEPRI-DEC-019` supplies. So this is the **anticipated** shape, not a widening, and **no `RRA-001` amendment is made or needed**. The design note's original framing of it as a reluctant last resort is superseded, and §6 says so rather than quietly rewriting itself.

## Why `FR-037` is not weakened — on evidence, not assertion

`FR-037` names **opacity**, not provenance. The two minting sites are the same construction, character for character:

```python
f"own_{secrets.token_urlsafe(18)}"                  # sessions.py:126      (RRA, per redemption)
f"{_OWNER_ID_PREFIX}{secrets.token_urlsafe(18)}"    # organizations.py:151 (RCA, per organization)
```

18 CSPRNG bytes as 24 URL-safe characters, both times. And `allocate_owner_id` takes **no argument at all**, so `FR-032`/`FR-033` are satisfied by construction rather than by review.

## What the record fixes and what it withholds

**§2 fixes the shape** so `R7-02` implements rather than re-decides: a new function sibling to `redeem`, taking an opaque `owner_id`, minting its own `session_id`, accepting nothing else that identifies a caller, and performing no authorization of its own.

**§4 makes the safety argument testable** — RRA's existing tests must pass unmodified, and *editing any `test_rra*` file is a conflict with this decision to be recorded, not resolved by editing the test.*

**§5 withholds everything else:** no product code, no endpoint, no schema, no `redeem` change, no authorization inside RRA. `R7-02` and later remain separately reviewable.

## Also reported, not corrected

- **`RRA-001`'s footer** says it is "draft and does not authorize product implementation" while the registry marks it `active` and its code is merged and shipping. **Ten specifications carry that line.** `AGENTS.md` resolves it — registry is authoritative for state, Markdown cannot override it — so the footer is stale prose. A decision record is not the vehicle for a specification's prose pass.
- **Two stale §15 roadmap rows** (§8 of the note): `R6` still reads `BLOCKED` though `R6-01`…`R6-08` are merged, and `R7` reads "Depends on R6".
- The record is written in its **merged form** because `active` is the only non-retired state the registry admits (`validator.py:15`). Its header states that explicitly.

## Test plan

- [x] `khepri-gov validate` — passed, with `KHEPRI-DEC-019` registered
- [x] `ruff check .` — passed
- [x] CI 5/5 green
- [x] Docs and governance only; no `src/` or `tests/` changes
- [x] Every code claim verified against the tree (4 FKs, both `owner_id` constructions, `redeem`'s single production caller, the `isolation.py` quote, all cited line numbers)

author: enesyilmazcode
body:
## What was wrong

`circuit3d/js/simulate.js` was one IIFE, `(function (App) { ... })(window.App = window.App || {})`, whose only surface was `App.runSimulation()` / `App.stopSimulation()`. The solver and the presentation were the same function: `runSimulation` built the graph, enumerated paths, computed currents, and in the same loop called `lightUpLED()`, `activateBuzzer()` and `showResults()` against `document` and `THREE`.

There was no way to call the solver with a circuit and assert on a number, which is why every physics bug in issues #8, #9, #10, #11 shipped uncaught.

## What changed

`circuit3d/js/simulate.js`

- UMD tail instead of the bare IIFE. In the browser it still does `window.App.runSimulation = ...` at load time, exactly as before. Under node it sets `module.exports`. No bundler, no dependency, no module system in the page.
- New pure `analyze(components, wires)` holds all the computation that used to be inline in `runSimulation`: buttons, batteries, path enumeration, per-branch resistance, forward voltage and current. It returns `{ status, lines, ledsOn, buzzersOn, branches }` and touches no DOM, no THREE, no AudioContext.
- `runSimulation` is now presentation only: call `analyze`, render `lines`, light `ledsOn`, sound `buzzersOn`, swap the toolbar buttons.
- The buzzer audio block moved below a `── Presentation ──` divider so the file reads pure-then-impure. Its code is unchanged.
- Exported surface: `{ PROPS, UnionFind, bbNodeId, buildGraph, findAllPaths, analyze, install }`.

The physics is untouched. Every number this branch produces is the number `main` produces.

`test/simulate.test.js` (new)

13 golden tests on the node built-in runner, no dependencies. Series, parallel with a shared resistor, voltage divider, reverse diode, short, open circuit, two batteries in series, degenerate boards, and node extraction.

The four cases that are wrong today are pinned twice: an active test asserting the wrong number the engine actually returns, so the solver replacement produces a visible diff, and a skipped test holding the analytically correct answer with the issue that will unskip it.

## How I verified it

`node --check circuit3d/js/simulate.js` passes.

Browser load path, simulated in a `vm` context with `window` defined and `module` absent:

```
window.App.runSimulation : function
window.App.stopSimulation: function
```

`node --test`:

```
✔ series battery, resistor, LED: one branch at (9-2)/220
✔ parallel LEDs behind one resistor: WRONG TODAY, full current in both (#8)
﹣ parallel LEDs behind one resistor: KCL holds, 15.9 mA each (#8)  # blocked on the solver replacement, issue #8
✔ voltage divider: loop current is right, node voltage is absent (#9)
﹣ voltage divider: V(midpoint) = 4.5 V (#9)  # blocked on the solver replacement, issue #9
✔ reversed LED: WRONG TODAY, lights at full brightness (#10)
﹣ reversed LED: stays dark and says so (#10)  # fixed by issue #10
✔ LED across the battery with no resistor is reported as a short
✔ resistor and LED not wired to the battery leave the circuit open
✔ two 9V batteries in series: WRONG TODAY, same current as one (#11)
﹣ two 9V batteries in series: 18 V drives 72.7 mA (#11)  # blocked on the solver replacement, issue #11
✔ empty board and battery-less board report their own status
✔ buildGraph merges columns, rails and wired holes into one node each
ℹ tests 13
ℹ pass 9
ℹ fail 0
ℹ skipped 4
```

The golden numbers the tests pin, all from this branch and all identical on `main`:

| circuit | reported today | analytically correct |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 9V, 220R, LED series | 31.818 mA | 31.818 mA |
| 9V, 220R, two parallel LEDs | 31.818 mA per LED | 15.909 mA per LED (#8) |
| 9V, 220R, 220R divider | 20.454 mA, no V(X) | V(X) = 4.5 V (#9) |
| reversed LED | on, 31.818 mA | off (#10) |
| two 9V in series | 31.818 mA | 72.727 mA (#11) |

## Not included here

- No physics fix. #8, #9, #10, #11 are untouched on purpose, so the fix for each produces a diff in this test file.
- The KCL property test the issue asks for is present only as the shared-resistor case. A general property test over random circuits needs a correct solver to check against.
- No `npm test` script: `package.json` belongs to the remotion build and is outside this change. Run `node --test` from the repo root.
- I did not run the tests in a browser. The browser path is verified through the `vm` check above, not through a real page load.

Closes #24

author: neo-opus-ada
body:
Resolves #17240

Resolves #17251

The published package stops carrying the DevIndex corpus, the portal's generated SEO artifacts, and — the one that matters most — Agent OS plane state. **Unpacked 97.32 → 66.71 MiB, tarball 39.19 → 28.43 MiB, 7,420 → 7,385 files.** Three `.npmignore` repairs plus a gate that observes what actually ships, because nothing did: `package.json` declares no `files` array, so `.npmignore` is the sole gate on package contents and every line in it was unverified.

Evidence: L3 (a real `npm pack --dry-run --json` before and after, in a checkout that actually holds live `.neo-ai-data/logs`, `sqlite/` and `wake-daemon/` — plus the published `neo.mjs@13.1.0` tarball fetched from the registry and inspected) → L3 required (both close targets are "what does the tarball contain", answerable only by packing). Residual: none.

## Leading with the negative result

**Nothing leaked.** Before writing a word of #17251 I fetched the published `neo.mjs@13.1.0` from the registry and listed it: it contains exactly two `.neo-ai-data` entries, `concepts/edges.jsonl` and `concepts/nodes.jsonl`. The intended carve-out, nothing else.

It was clean **by environment, not by rule** — the release was cut from a checkout whose `.neo-ai-data` happened to hold only that subtree. This PR is a guard repair, not an incident response, and it is worth being precise about that because the rest reads worse than the situation was.

## What changed

**1. `apps/devindex/resources/*.json` → `apps/devindex/resources/data/**` (#17240)**

@neo-opus-grace's finding, verified: the rule stopped matching on *both* axes at once when the corpus moved into `data/` and grew a `.jsonl` — wrong directory (no `data/` segment, and `*` does not recurse) and wrong extension. 26.5 MiB with no framework consumer; the browser store fetches `users.jsonl` over HTTP from `Neo.config.basePath`, never from the package.

**2. `.neo-ai-data` → `.neo-ai-data/*` (#17251)** — the defect that matters

A negation under a bare directory exclusion does not widen that exclusion. It **removes** it.

| `.npmignore` | packs |
|---|---|
| `.neo-ai-data` + `!.neo-ai-data/concepts/` | concepts **+ `logs/server.log` + `sqlite/graph.sqlite`** |
| `.neo-ai-data` alone | nothing |
| `.neo-ai-data/*` + `!.neo-ai-data/concepts/` | concepts only ✅ |

`ignore-walk` must descend into the directory to honour the `!`, and once it descends the bare pattern no longer suppresses the siblings it was written to suppress. In this checkout that made **24 entries packable**: every kb/mc/nl server log, `deployment-state/snapshot.json`, `harness-state/*.json`, `wake-daemon/` in-flight files, and the 704 KiB Memory Core SQLite graph — agent memories, session records, A2A edges.

Excluding the *children* keeps the parent walkable, so the carve-out re-includes exactly one subtree and everything else stays excluded — **including subdirectories that do not exist yet**, verified by planting a new one in the fixture. This is the shape `.gemini/*` already used four lines below, for the same reason. The repo contained its own fix.

**3. `apps/portal/sitemap.xml` + `llms.txt` excluded (#17240 AC-5)** — 3.2 MiB of generated SEO artifacts addressed to crawlers of the deployed site, which no installed package is. Regenerated by the release prepare step, so excluding them cannot make the deployment stale.

**4. A gate that observes the tarball (#17251 AC-3)** — `check-package-contents.mjs`, a `paths`-scoped workflow, and a spec. It names the directories that must never ship and runs a **real pack**, because reasoning about ignore-file patterns is precisely what produced both defects.

## Two measurement notes, both of which nearly produced a wrong fix

**The isolated fixture lied.** `apps/devindex/resources/data/` — the trailing-slash directory form — excludes correctly in a minimal reproduction and does **not** exclude in this repo. The surrounding `/apps/**` rules and their ~60 negations change how a directory-form pattern resolves here. I had a green fixture and a still-27%-oversized package at the same time; only the real pack disagreed. `/**` is required, and the comment says so at the line so the next person does not re-derive it from a fixture.

**The CI job cannot prove the half that matters.** A runner has no live `.neo-ai-data/logs` or `sqlite/`, so those files cannot appear in its pack and a green there says nothing about them. The workflow states this inline rather than letting a green read as coverage it does not have — that false confidence is exactly what let the original defect survive. The Agent OS half is covered by the unit spec over the rule logic and by the red-proof below.

## Deltas from ticket

**None substantive.** Both tickets' ACs are delivered as written. Two additions worth flagging:

- #17240 AC-5 asked for an explicit recorded decision on the portal artifacts; I excluded both and recorded the reasoning inline in `.npmignore` rather than only in this body, since the body is not where the next editor of that file looks.
- The DevIndex directory also holds small hand-maintained policy files (`allowlist`/`blocklist`/`optin-sync`/`optout-sync`, ~2.5 KB). They go with the exclusion: their only consumer is the in-repo crawler service, which resolves them from `projectRoot` and cannot run from an installed package. Recorded at the line.

Both tickets defer the `files`-allowlist migration in `package.json`, and this PR honours that — it is the better long-term shape and a large enough behavior change to deserve its own ticket.

**Decision Record impact:** `none`.

## Test Evidence

`.npmignore` (packaging rules): `npm pack --dry-run --json`, before and after, in a checkout holding live Agent OS state.
`buildScripts/util/check-package-contents.mjs` (new gate): `test/playwright/unit/buildScripts/checkPackageContents.spec.mjs` — **10 passed**.
`package.json` (npm script): `npm run check-package-contents` — passes against the fixed tree.

```bash
npm run check-package-contents
npm run test-unit -- test/playwright/unit/buildScripts/checkPackageContents.spec.mjs
```

| Probe | Result |
|---|---|
| package before | 7,420 files · 39.19 MiB tarball · 97.32 MiB unpacked |
| package after | 7,385 files · 28.43 MiB tarball · **66.71 MiB unpacked** |
| `.neo-ai-data` entries after | exactly 2 — `concepts/edges.jsonl`, `concepts/nodes.jsonl` |
| entries **added** by this change | **0** — asserted, not assumed |
| **gate vs. the real pre-fix listing — red-proof** | **33 violations** (24 `.neo-ai-data/`, 9 `apps/devindex/resources/data/`) |
| gate vs. the post-fix listing | **0 violations** |
| carve-out falsely flagged? | no — 2 `concepts/` files present, 0 flagged |
| published `neo.mjs@13.1.0` | 2 `.neo-ai-data` entries, both `concepts/` — clean |
| `lint-guard-ci-parity` · `lint-npm-script-entrypoints` · `lint-script-plane` | all OK |

The red-proof feeds the gate the **genuine pre-fix package listing** rather than a synthetic path, so it demonstrates the check would have caught the real defects — including that it does not flag the legitimate carve-out. The spec adds the cases real data cannot supply: a *new* sibling of the carve-out (must fire), and `concepts-backup/` (a string-prefix lookalike that a naive `includes()` would wave through).

## Post-Merge Validation

**None.** The change is verified by the same command that defines the deliverable, run against a checkout that actually holds the guarded files — a merged state adds no observation. Bound worth stating instead: the workflow's green will only ever prove the DevIndex and `resources/content` rules, for the reason given above.

## Commits

- `83ac5a63cf` — the three `.npmignore` repairs, the gate, its workflow, its spec, and the npm script.

## Review

Cross-family review required (§6.1) — Claude-authored, so this needs a GPT seat, and that bench has been dark ~19h with all Codex seats sharing one account and quota. Flagging rather than assuming. Merge is human-gated

## What changed

- fixes all seven Phase A qualification-evidence defects without creating v9/v10 or rewriting historical v1/v7 fixtures
- adds one shared fail-closed evidence core for v7/v8 JSON, digest, regular-file, symlink, and path invariants
- makes `machine_reference_scorer` reopen exact retained candidate output and execution receipts; stale scorer rows fail after output replacement
- adds a closed machine-reviewer raw-output contract and recomputes unanimity/disagreement from retained reviewer bytes
- unifies the 14 canonical Core Gate IDs across protocol v2 and classification v8, including runtime equality checks in assembler and provenance verifier
- redefines exact-wheel v2 as a Candidate Full raw-inventory-bound synthetic public journey, not holdout execution
- makes commercial scale v2 reject periodic synthetic evidence and require actual-candidate 1k/10k/100k process bindings

- pins the OpenCode bridge to 1.18.16 / a3647eb025c7615159d417dcc49fc39fdaeba65b and labels the compaction hook exact-version experimental

## Root cause

The draft infrastructure trusted several caller-authored or incomplete bindings: scorer rows were not tied to retained candidate output, reviewer consensus did not reopen strict raw reviewer output, exact-wheel semantics confused an artifact journey with holdout execution, protocol/classification Gate IDs could drift, and one external runner could receive mutually incompatible trust-domain inputs. The scale surface also lacked a claim-eligible actual-candidate discriminator.

## Evidence classification and release state

All reviewers are machine reviewers; no Human Gold, legal-expert conclusion, or `human_verified` evidence is asserted. This commit is qualification infrastructure only. body:
Brings this repository from **v0.3.1 to v0.7.0** in one snapshot. Six versions landed since the last sync (0.4.0, 0.5.0, 0.6.0, 0.6.1, 0.6.2, 0.7.0); `CHANGELOG.md` carries the full record.

Decode-ahead streaming shipped in 0.4.0 and arrives here with this snapshot.

## What lands

- **`de(cell_source=…)`** — a public bring-your-own cell source, byte-identical to `de(adata=, reference=<AnnData>)`
- **`de(archive=…)` reads `layout='cell'` (`.csad`) archives**; `de(shard_archive=…)` is now the deprecated spelling
- **`de(tau_star=…)` / `de(tau_star_se=True)`** — signed rank-shift estimate and its standard error
- **`de(lfc_threshold=…)`** — an effect-size floor applied at the rank level
- **In-memory external reference** with no target∪reference concat; **decode-ahead streaming** (4.7×); **GPU device decode** (~1.57× at 5.54 M cells)
- **`requires-python` → `>=3.11`**; CI runs a 3.11 / 3.12 matrix
- ⚠️ **Breaking:** `test_statistic` → `U` → **`Ueffect`**, and directional columns are now `tau=<±τ>_{p,Ueffect,padj}`

| gate | result |
|---|---|
| suite (no GPU, shardad + numba present) | **528 passed, 182 skipped** |
| `ruff check src tests` | clean |
| `codex:codex-review` | 5 rounds to convergence; 12 findings, 10 applied, 2 accepted as-is |

The cross-provider review earned its keep. Worth naming: **three factual errors in the contributor docs**, corrected here —

- the shardad-gated suite list named two modules when there are three (`test_cell_stream.py` was missing)

Also fixed: a `0.3.1` changelog sentence that described this repository in the third person, and `.gitignore` rules for a script that is not part of this repository.

author: solo-jordan
body:
Fixes the same-account self-mute failure reported from the dsc-adv-agents field incident: two sessions of one repo agent coordinated on one Quase thread, and each session's poller silently consumed the other's posts as "own replies" (ten posts over twelve hours, zero notifications, in both sessions independently).

## The three layers, all landed

**1. Documentation** — `SKILL.md` gains a same-account paragraph in the monitor section: the auto-mute assumes a different-handle counterpart; same-account threads must arm with `--include-self`. That flag's docstring is promoted from "(debugging)" to a required operating mode. The arm step and the frontmatter trigger description now name the same-account case explicitly.

**2. Detection over configuration** — the poller now emits `QUASE-MONITOR-SELF-MUTED` on every poll that suppresses own-handle replies: the count, the handle, and the recovery step. Recovery matters: muted replies are already consumed (cursor advanced), so the instruction is *read the thread via `get_replies`, then re-arm with `--include-self`* — re-arming alone would not replay them.

**3. Arm-time warning** — `QUASE-MONITOR-ARM-WARNING` when the root post is authored by the muted handle **and mentions no other handle**. The second condition keeps the normal ORIGIN arm quiet (you author the root but mention the counterpart); a root with no other handle mentioned has no cross-repo counterpart, so every reply worth emitting would be muted. Emitted in the seed poll and once in monitor mode.

## Sibling sweep (PL-P17 WI-1 generality audit)

- **Account-scoped read-state**: inbox read-state and seen watermarks are shared across sessions of one account, so one session's mark-read blinds the other's `check_inbox`. Documented in the same-account paragraph: the armed monitor, not the inbox, is the coordination channel.
- **Seed-poll diag relabeled** `muted=` → `mute_handle=` — the incident report noted the clue was on screen (`muted=dsc_adv_agents`) and unreadable; the old label read as a count or a status, not as "this handle will be silenced".
- **Stale `curl -4` in CLAUDE.md** corrected to what the poller actually does (explicit `-A` User-Agent); self-mute guards added to the don't-simplify list.
- **Repo hygiene**: a `__pycache__/poller.cpython-311.pyc` committed in #1 is untracked, and bytecode is ignored going forward.
- New traps bullet in SKILL.md so a future "simplification" pass doesn't remove any of the three guards.

## Verification

- `arm_warning` unit-tested against 8 synthetic roots (self-author/no-mentions, self-mentions-only, counterpart-mentioned, TARGET arm, missing root, unresolved handle, display_name fallback) — all pass.
- Live `--once` against the real handoff thread with fresh state: `QUASE-MONITOR-SELF-MUTED` fired on this agent's own ack reply, no false arm-warning (root authored by @solo).
- Live `--once --include-self`: the same reply emitted as `QUASE-REPLY` instead.
- Both manifests JSON-validated; `py_compile` clean.

Versions: plugin `1.2.0`, marketplace metadata `1.2.0` (minor with minor).

body:
## Summary

- Add `scripts/install.sh`, which downloads the matching Linux amd64/arm64 release archive, verifies it against `SHA256SUMS`, and installs a single binary to `~/.local/bin`. It does not modify shell configuration files and supports `--uninstall`.
- Document the install script as the recommended install path in the README, with `PORTCLUE_VERSION` / `PORTCLUE_INSTALL_DIR` overrides and an explicit uninstall command. The release archive and `go install` paths stay available.
- Note in SECURITY.md that the script uses the same checksum-verified release artifacts, and that a tag-pinned script URL from this repository is preferred over copies hosted elsewhere.
- Update CONTRIBUTING.md scope wording now that an official installer exists, and record the change in CHANGELOG.md as 0.1.1.

Documentation examples are pinned to `v0.1.1`, so the `raw.githubusercontent.com` install URL resolves once that tag is published.

## Test plan

- [x] `make check`
- [x] `sh -n scripts/install.sh`
- [x] Install and uninstall against the published v0.1.0 release into a temporary directory, confirming `portclue --version` reports `0.1.0` and the binary is removed afterwards
- [x] Confirm a corrupted archive fails checksum verification instead of installing
- [x] Confirm unsupported arguments and non-Linux/unsupported architectures exit with an error

author: moelayyan90
body:
## What changed
- serve `/.well-known/x402` as a compatibility alias of the canonical XGuard facilitator manifest
- serve `/.well-known/monetization` as machine-readable pricing metadata derived from the canonical provider manifest
- preserve GET/HEAD, cache, ETag, CORS, and no-sniff discovery behavior
- add tests for the x402 alias, monetization pricing fields, HEAD/conditional requests, and non-interception of unrelated methods

## Why
External discovery probes reached both paths and received 404 responses. These compatibility endpoints let registries and pricing crawlers discover XGuard without changing the authoritative x402 `/supported`, facilitator, settlement, or billing behavior.

## Safety
No settlement, authentication, fee-accounting, payment, or facilitator-routing logic is changed. The monetization response reads the existing canonical provider pricing instead of defining a second price source.

author: mmarques30
body:
## Resumo

Ao abrir o dialog **"Editar lançamento"**, o sistema agora busca o registro em `aprendizado_participante` para o padrão estável da descrição da transação e exibe chips de sugestão em cada campo editável relevante.

### O que mudou

- **`src/lib/lcr.functions.ts`**: nova função `getAprendizadoPorDescricao` — recebe `empresa_id` + `descricao` (texto bruto), aplica `padraoEstavelDescricao` e retorna o registro aprendido (conta, histórico, natureza, participantes)
- **`src/routes/_authenticated/conciliacao_.$empresaId.tsx`**:
  - Estado `editDescOriginal` captura a descrição original ao abrir o dialog (sem refazer a requisição a cada tecla no campo Descrição)
  - `useQuery` carrega o aprendizado para aquela descrição com `staleTime` de 5 min
  - Componente `SugestaoAprendida`: chip visual com ícone Sparkles + texto em destaque; aparece abaixo do campo somente quando o valor aprendido difere do valor atual
  - Chips adicionados em: **conta contábil**, **histórico contábil**, **tipo de movimento**, **participante débito** e **participante crédito**

### Comportamento

- Nenhum chip é exibido se a descrição da transação não tem padrão estável (ex.: descrições únicas sem prefixo reconhecido)
- Nenhum chip é exibido se o campo já está preenchido com o valor aprendido
- Clicar no chip aplica o valor ao campo imediatamente; o usuário ainda precisa salvar

## Summary by Sourcery

Strengthen the release drift gate by enforcing a committed, valid, and fresh baseline file and aligning root hygiene and CI tests with the canonical release_gates.yaml configuration.

CI:
- Add regression tests that verify release_gates.yaml:drift.baseline_file points to an existing JSON baseline, matches the required schema, remains within a staleness threshold, and is correctly loaded by ReleaseGateChecker.
- Add an end-to-end test ensuring drift gates fail when pass-rate regresses against the committed baseline, preventing silent PASS when the baseline is missing or stale.

Tests:
- Extend release gate checker test suite with drift baseline path, schema, freshness, loader, and gate-behavior checks tied to the real repo configuration.
- Add assertions that DEFAULTS remains in sync with release_gates.yaml and that the drift-related sections exist at module level.

Chores:
- Commit validation_baseline.json at the root and update root hygiene checks to allow this baseline JSON while keeping other root-level artifacts constrained.

- The published site failed to load because the JavaScript assets were placed under `jss/` while `index.html` expects `js/`, so the page couldn't load the application scripts.

### Description
- Rename the JavaScript asset directory from `jss` to `js` and place `data.js` and `app.js` in `js/` so `index.html` can load them using the existing `<script src="js/data.js">` and `<script src="js/app.js">` tags.

- Ran `node --check js/data.js` which completed successfully.
- Ran `node --check js/app.js` which completed successfully.
- Verified with ripgrep that `index.html` references `js/data.js` and `js/app.js` and there are no remaining `jss/` references, which succeeded.

author: martinkrakowski
body:
Remediation-plan item **6.4(c)** — the **wizard-orchestration** leg of **HEX-018**, one package per PR. Depends on **ADR-0048** (plan item 0.2) and reads the registry doctrine from **ADR-0057**. Does not touch governance (#497), monaco-orchestration, or project-configuration; those are sibling PRs.

## The rule applied

ADR-0048 Decision 1 defines the directions operationally:

> `ports/in` = driving/inbound: the use case implements the inbound port; a driver depends on the port. `ports/out` = driven/outbound: the use case depends on the port; an infrastructure adapter implements it. **If an infrastructure adapter `implements` the interface, it is an outbound port and belongs in `ports/out`.**

Decision 2 adds that the doc comments must be corrected so folder and comment agree.

This package has **no infrastructure adapters** — `src/infrastructure/index.ts` is a bare `export {}` — so the "an adapter implements it" half of the test can never fire here. The half that does fire is the other one, and it fires cleanly: three ports are constructor-injected into a use case and called from `execute()`. That is the sentence "the use case depends on the port," verbatim. All three additionally carried a doc comment stating that infrastructure adapters implement them; ADR-0048 cites `process-intent.port.ts:4` as the in-tree evidence for exactly this package.

## Direction classification — all seven ports

| Port | Depended on by a use case? | Implemented by an infra adapter? | Direction | Action |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ProcessIntentPort` | yes — `ProcessIntentUseCase` ctor-injects, calls `process()` | none in tree; comment claimed so | **driven** | moved to `ports/out` |
| `ProjectWizardStatePort` | yes — `ProjectWizardStateUseCase` ctor-injects, calls `getCurrentState()` | none in tree; comment claimed so | **driven** | moved to `ports/out` |
| `ValidateStepPort` | yes — `ValidateStepUseCase` ctor-injects, calls `validate()` | none in tree; comment claimed so | **driven** | moved to `ports/out` |
| `IProjectWizardController` | no | no — implemented by the React UI and by `WizardMultiContextFake` (`packages/shared/__tests__/doubles/`), both **drivers** | driving | **stays** in `ports/in` |
| `QueryActiveWorkspacePort` | no | no | driving (as authored) | **stays** in `ports/in` |
| `SetActiveWorkspacePort` | no | no | driving (as authored) | **stays** in `ports/in` |
| `ClearActiveWorkspacePort` | no | no | driving (as authored) | **stays** in `ports/in` |

The three `*ActiveWorkspacePort` contracts have no in-tree implementer and no in-tree consumer, so the folder signal cannot be re-derived from usage. The commit that introduced them (`618d5e23`) states the intent outright: *"Extended 'wizard-orchestration' with ActiveWorkspace value object + **3 inbound ports** and WizardCompletionSignalPort outbound port (no anaemic pass-through use cases; **the React Context is the adapter**)."* The React Context is a **driving** adapter, not an infrastructure one, so ADR-0048's operational test does not fire in either direction and the authored classification stands. They are left alone deliberately — moving a port on a hunch is the failure this ADR exists to stop.

`IProjectWizardController` is the same shape with clearer evidence: its own comment says implementations come from the UI, and its only in-repo implementer is a UI test double.

## Files moved

Three `git mv`s, all **100% renames** (the move is its own commit, so the rename detection is not defeated by the comment rewrite that follows it):

| From | To |
| --- | --- |
| `src/application/ports/in/process-intent.port.ts` | `src/application/ports/out/process-intent.port.ts` |
| `src/application/ports/in/project-wizard-state.port.ts` | `src/application/ports/out/project-wizard-state.port.ts` |
| `src/application/ports/in/validate-step.port.ts` | `src/application/ports/out/validate-step.port.ts` |

Import updates in the five use-case modules that reference them (`process-intent.use-case.ts`, `process-intent.ts`, `project-wizard-state.use-case.ts`, `project-wizard-state.ts`, `validate-step.use-case.ts`) plus both port barrels. Nothing outside `packages/wizard-orchestration` imports these three types — the ports are not reachable from the package's public entry at all, since `application/index.ts` exports only the three projection functions.

> Incidental observation, not changed here: `use-cases/process-intent.ts` and `use-cases/project-wizard-state.ts` are byte-level duplicates of their `.use-case.ts` siblings, exporting the same class names, and neither is referenced by `use-cases/index.ts`. Out of scope for a directory move; flagged for a follow-up.

## Manifest / `context.yaml`: three entries need to move — **not** edited here

`.architecture/contexts/core/wizard-orchestration/context.yaml` is Primary-only in this arc, so the required edit is reported rather than made. ADR-0057 §1 makes it a genuine defect rather than cosmetics: the registry's one hard invariant is **accuracy**, and *"direction follows ADR-0048 — `in` = driving, `out` = driven — regardless of which folder the file currently sits in."* Three entries are now stating the wrong direction.

Required change — move three names from `layers.application.ports.in` to `layers.application.ports.out`:

```yaml
    ports:
      in:
        - IProjectWizardController
        - QueryActiveWorkspacePort
        - SetActiveWorkspacePort
        - ClearActiveWorkspacePort
      out:
        - WizardCompletionSignalPort
        - ProcessIntentPort
        - ProjectWizardStatePort
        - ValidateStepPort
```

No entry is added or removed — the same seven names are declared, three under a different key. No symbol is renamed, so ADR-0047 `port-single-ownership` is untouched.

Two adjacent registries were checked and need no action:

- `.architecture/generator.config.yaml:92-98` maps the same three names to `wizard-orchestration` under a `# wizard-orchestration — in-ports` **comment** heading. The YAML is a flat `Name: context` map, so ownership is unaffected and only the grouping comment is now stale. Left alone rather than edited, since it is an `.architecture/` registry and sync's `yaml-config.adapter` writes this file. Worth a one-line comment regrouping whenever Primary lands the `context.yaml` change.
- `packages/ui/.architecture/manifest.yaml:270-282` carries an identical stale copy of the pre-split monolithic manifest, but the file is **git-ignored** (`git check-ignore` confirms) and untracked. Nothing to change.

No blocker: the `context.yaml` edit is a three-line key move, fully specified above.

## Barrel drift

`ports/in/index.ts` and `ports/out/index.ts` carry **no** `@generated` marker; `yarn sync:dry` reports both under its 171 *skipped* barrels, so they are hand-written and preserved under ADR-0026, and editing them in place is what the walker expects. The `@generated` `ports/index.ts` re-exports `./in/index.js` and `./out/index.js` — both folders still exist and are still populated, so it needs no change and got none.

`sync:dry` output before and after the move is **byte-identical apart from the elapsed-time line**: same 140 ops, same `Barrels : 0 created, 1 updated, 0 deleted, 0 unchanged, 171 skipped`. The single barrel update is `agentic-interaction`, pre-existing on `main`. Sync also scaffolds `ports/in` / `ports/out` / `use-cases` per module, but this package already had all three folders and still does, so there is no scaffold churn in either direction.

## Behaviour preservation, by measurement

`dist/` was built on `main`, snapshotted, the source moved, and the package rebuilt from scratch (`rm -rf dist` + `--force`, no cache). The two trees were then compared file-by-file:

- **164 artefacts before, 164 after.** 152 paths in common, of which **134 are byte-identical**.
- The 12 "missing"/"new" files are exactly the four emitted artefacts (`.js`, `.js.map`, `.d.ts`, `.d.ts.map`) for each of the three ports, relocating `ports/in

author: aduneer
body:
Groundwork for a README demo GIF, plus the grammar bug that writing it surfaced.

## The tape

`demo/demo.tape` is a [vhs](https://github.com/charmbracelet/vhs) script, so the demo is **reproducible**: when the UI changes, `vhs demo/demo.tape` re-renders it instead of someone re-performing a screen recording by hand.

It is deterministic by construction, which matters because a scripted recording that depends on shuffle order would drift:

- `demo/demo-deck.txt` carries fixed **past** due dates, so the two overdue cards always come up in the same order (due-only review sorts most-overdue first).
- `la ciudad` is dated 2027, so it stays out of the due review — which doubles as a demonstration that scheduling genuinely holds cards back. The menu says "2 due" over a three-card deck.
- The reversed act is scoped by the `places` tag, which matches exactly one card, so the expected answer is known in advance.
- Setup is hidden and works on a temp copy, so the recording never touches a real deck.

Storyboard: launch → 2 due → typo caught and overridden → clean answer and promotion → summary → statistics dashboard → reversed review via tag filter.

## The bug it exposed

The tag list rendered `1. places (1 cards)`, which the GIF would have immortalised. Counts are printed in six places, so this adds `count_label` to `text.*` and routes them through it. One site (`N of M cards match`) had a verb-agreement problem no pluraliser fixes, so it is reworded to `Showing 1 of 3 cards`.

The progress-bar ratio `(1/1 cards)` is deliberately left alone — it reads correctly as a ratio.

## Verification

283 checks pass, up from 278. No warnings on gcc or clang. The tape's exact keystroke sequence was replayed through the built binary and every beat lands as scripted: `(2 due)`, `Q: la biblioteca`, the near-miss override, promotion to Box 3, `Total Reviewed: 2`, `1. places (1 card)`, and the reversed `A: city` accepting `la ciudad`.

**The GIF itself is not committed yet** — it needs `vhs` and `ttyd` installed. The README gets its image link in a follow-up once the file exists, rather than pointing at a missing asset now.

author: mrveiss
body:
## Thinking Path

Two implementations configure the VNC account and read different env vars: the
canonical `autobot-slm-backend/ansible/roles/vnc` role reads `VNC_USER`
(`lookup('env', 'VNC_USER')` in `defaults/main.yml`), while the standalone
recovery scripts `autobot-infrastructure/shared/scripts/utilities/fix-vnc-desktop.sh`
and `fix-vnc-wsl.sh` read `AUTOBOT_VNC_USER`. Setting one does nothing on the
other path, silently — the unit is written for the default account and the
failure only shows up later as a service that can't read its own password file.

Before picking a survivor I grepped the whole repo (docs, `.env` templates,
systemd units, ansible group_vars/defaults, CI) for both names on
`origin/Dev_new_gui`:

| name | occurrences (`\b`-bounded) | files |
|---|---|---|
| `VNC_USER` | 32 | `fix-vnc-desktop.sh`, `fix-vnc-wsl.sh`, `roles/vnc/defaults/main.yml`, `pipeline-scripts/detect-hardcoded-values_test.py`, `scripts/systemd_heredoc_expansion_test.py` |
| `AUTOBOT_VNC_USER` | 6 | `fix-vnc-desktop.sh`, `fix-vnc-wsl.sh`, `pipeline-scripts/detect-hardcoded-values_test.py`, `scripts/systemd_heredoc_expansion_test.py` |

Raw counts are dominated by the two scripts re-using their own local shell
variable `VNC_USER` inside every heredoc unit body — that's internal reuse,
not an external interface. Narrowing to the actual *external* read site (the
one line per file that reads the process environment) gives the real signal:
`AUTOBOT_VNC_USER` is the external read in both scripts; `VNC_USER` is the
external read in the ansible role's `defaults/main.yml` — one site each.

The deciding factor is which name **the deployed system actually reads**. The
ansible `vnc` role is the one wired into real automated deploys
(`setup-user-backend.yml`, `provision-fleet-roles.yml`, `enroll-node.yml`,
`deploy_role.yml`, `deploy.yml` all include it); `fix-vnc-*.sh` are standalone
manual recovery utilities under `shared/scripts/utilities/`, not invoked by
any playbook or CI job. I also checked whether either variable is actually
*set* anywhere on that deploy path today — group_vars, inventory, `.env*`
templates, systemd unit files, CI — and it is not: neither `VNC_USER` nor
`AUTOBOT_VNC_USER` is exported/assigned anywhere in the repo, so both
currently resolve to the hardcoded `autobot` default in practice. That rules
out "whichever is already configured on a host" as a tiebreaker, and leaves
"which name the canonical, actually-deployed implementation reads" —
`VNC_USER`.

## What Changed

- `autobot-slm-backend/ansible/roles/vnc/defaults/main.yml`: `vnc_user` now
  resolves `VNC_USER` first, falling back to `AUTOBOT_VNC_USER` (deprecated
  alias, kept for one release), then the `autobot` default.
- `autobot-infrastructure/shared/scripts/utilities/fix-vnc-desktop.sh` and
  `fix-vnc-wsl.sh`: the VNC-user resolution block now checks `VNC_USER` first,
  falls back to `AUTOBOT_VNC_USER`, then defaults to `autobot` — same priority
  order as the role, so the two paths can no longer silently diverge.
- `changelog/unreleased/14314-vnc-user-env-var-consolidation.md`: changelog
  fragment.
- `scripts/vnc_user_env_var_test.py`: new guard test (see Verification).

No script was deleted or forked into a third variable name; both paths were
consolidated onto the role's variable per the issue's direction, with the
alias kept working for a release rather than dropped, since an existing host
may already have `AUTOBOT_VNC_USER` set.

## Verification

- `bash -n` on both edited scripts, and a YAML parse of `defaults/main.yml` —
  all clean (static checks only; no application code executed, per policy).
- Manually replayed the existing static-substitution logic in
  `scripts/systemd_heredoc_expansion_test.py::test_the_vnc_units_resolve_to_a_real_user`
  against the edited scripts (same technique that test itself already uses —
  text substitution, no execution): all 14 `User=`/`Group=`/`WorkingDirectory=`/
  `Environment=HOME=` directives across both scripts still resolve to a
  non-empty literal (`autobot`), so that pre-existing guard stays green.
- New guard `scripts/vnc_user_env_var_test.py` parses the ordered env-var
  lookups out of the role's `vnc_user:` line and both scripts' resolution
  blocks and asserts the **invariant** — canonical var checked first, alias
  still present, and the two implementations share at least one variable name
  — rather than asserting today's exact spelling.
- Confirmed the guard turns red on the original bug shape by re-running its
  regexes against the pre-fix text: the role's old line
  (`lookup('env', 'VNC_USER') | default(...)`) still yields `['VNC_USER']`,
  but the scripts' old line (`VNC_USER="${AUTOBOT_VNC_USER:-autobot}"` — no
  `-n "${VNC_USER:-}"` guard) yields `[]`, so
  `test_every_implementation_checks_the_canonical_var_first` and
  `test_every_implementation_reads_the_same_canonical_variable` both fail on
  that text, and `test_every_implementation_checks_the_canonical_var_first`
  fails again if the role is reverted to drop the `AUTOBOT_VNC_USER` fallback.
- `python3 -m py_compile scripts/vnc_user_env_var_test.py` — compiles clean.
- Did not run pytest, deploy, or install anything, per policy — CI executes
  the suite.

Closes #14314

author: steipete
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users upgrading a multi-agent installation with an unmigrated legacy cron store could have `openclaw doctor --fix` leave the configuration upgrade unapplied. The config write safety check repeatedly saw ownerless jobs in `cron/jobs.json`, even though the retained legacy owner was known.

## Why This Change Was Made

Owner materialization now covers both the SQLite cron partition and a still-active legacy JSON source before the config write rechecks ownership. The JSON rewrite is atomic, preserves explicit and session-scoped owners, and refuses to overwrite a source that changed during the operation. All scheduler and config callers await completion.

Production LOC grows because the legacy JSON source requires a durable compare-before-replace path that did not exist in the SQLite-only materializer; the migration remains in the existing ownership boundary without a new compatibility layer.

## User Impact

`openclaw doctor --fix` can now complete the ownership/config migration and then import legacy cron jobs into SQLite without manual intervention or lost job ownership.

## Evidence

- Regression was demonstrated failing before the fix with `Config write refused: ... contains 1 ownerless legacy cron job(s)` and passing afterward.
- Focused Vitest: 28 tests passed across cron materialization, config refusal, and authored config-write integration.
- Real upgrade fixture: 120 ownerless legacy crawl jobs, mixed two-agent config, and empty SQLite. Doctor exited 0, converted `agents.list` to explicit keyed entries, removed retired `contextTokens`, archived `cron/jobs.json`, and produced 121/121 owned SQLite cron rows (including the Doctor-created heartbeat). `PRAGMA integrity_check` returned `ok`; `foreign_key_check` returned no rows.
- Targeted oxlint: 0 warnings/errors.
- Core typecheck passed. The broader core-test typecheck reached an unrelated pre-existing `ui/src/lib/nodes/index.ts` `Uint8Array<ArrayBufferLike>` error.
- No live provider or channel send was performed.

- `experiments/tabular_robust_regression_v1/analysis.py` — deterministic pure-Python entrypoint: mean baseline, closed-form ridge (λ=1.0, bias unregularized), **Huber IRLS with the centered MAD (median |r − median(r)|, ×1.4826, δ=1.345) for exactly 50 iterations**, seeded Gaussian covariate perturbation (std = severity×0.5, Box-Muller, seed 42+severity) at 0/0.25/0.5/0.75; MAE/RMSE/R²; 27 flat metrics; byte-identical across reruns.
- `TABULAR_ROBUST_REGRESSION_V1` declared with frozen non-colliding family signals, its own `paper_directive`, five `method_facts` transcribing the implementation.
- 17 tests: entrypoint determinism/layout, dual-capability routing, facts self-consistency + misdescription blocking, full composition (design → execute → 2 ExperimentResults → **54 dataset-qualified markers** → cold hydration == live → regression context), four negative controls.

## Review P1 fixes (pre-freeze, entrypoint-only)

1. **Centered MAD** — the implementation now computes the actual median absolute deviation about the residual median, as its own method_facts declared; Huber values shifted accordingly.
2. **Exactly 50 IRLS iterations** — the convergence early-stop contradicted the C3-0 pre-registration ("fixed 50 iterations"); removed. Converged iterates are numerical no-ops.

Both recorded in `evidence/case3_architecture_delta.json`.

## Disclosed exception (owner adjudication)

One protected-surface change in G1→Q0: a **generic Unicode superscript fold** (²→2) in the metric-harvest normalization — without it the frozen question's "R²" never harvests the ASCII `_r2` metrics and the paper would omit the R² results its own question asks about. Claimed GENERIC (same class as the existing lowercasing; Case-1 harvest set test-proven unchanged). If ruled capability-specific → criterion 12 → ARCHITECTURE FAIL with this branch as evidence.

Full CI selection **5586 passed / 0 failed** locally on the predecessor content; both P1 fixes verified by the 17-test suite post-fix. Ruff 1962 ≤ 1963.

author: lewismarshall
body:
Foxes were a gene vector driving a fixed if/else ladder: every fox on the island hunted, regrouped and bred by the same script, and evolution could only touch how fast its legs were. They now have both halves a rabbit has — an explicit gene vector for the **body**, and a neural net for the **decisions**.

## The neural net

`src/sim/foxBrain.js` — a 14 → 8 → 6 net, same shape and same mutation rules as a rabbit's:

| Decision | What it gates |
|---|---|
| `chase` | Commit to a rabbit it can see |
| `sprint` | Spend stamina to close, rather than trotting after it |
| `track` | Follow a scent to prey it cannot see |
| `group` | Close on a packmate while not hunting |
| `rest` | Lie up: no movement, upkeep drops to 45% |
| `breed` | Want a litter (still gated on the breed-energy threshold) |

`bloodlust` is gone — "how badly do I want to kill this rabbit" is an opinion, and opinions belong in the net where they can depend on hunger, range and whether the pack is there. `src/sim/net.js` is new: the feedforward maths both species' brains are built from, shared so the two can never inherit by subtly different rules.

**You can see it**: trait bars, a plain-English blurb and the literal wiring in the fox inspector; a "Fox instincts" trend section in the Population panel; and two new states on the map — motes at the nose while tracking a scent, sleep bars while lying up.

**The nose.** Sight says where a rabbit is; scent says roughly which way to walk. It reaches slightly less far than sight in the open, but survives the canopy that costs a fox 45% of its vision — so woodland is where a fox hunts by smell and open ground is where it hunts by eye. A rabbit's scent scales with what it's doing: bolting leaves a hot trail, sitting still barely registers, underground leaves nothing.

## Survival and gestation

A mid fox now goes **~9 minutes** from full without food (~20 lying up), against ~1.4 before. Gestation is **58→30s**, down from 110→68s. Both as requested; the brake on fox numbers is energy and territory, not the clock.

## Balance

Measured on identical seeded islands — 5 rabbits + 5 foxes scattered, 64×64, 15 sim-minutes, 20 seeds:

| | rabbits left | rabbit extinctions | foxes left | fox extinctions | both alive at the end | caught |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| before | 39.8 | 0/20 | 0.0 | **20/20** | **0/20** | 2.6 |
| after | 6.8 | 1/20 | 3.8 | **0/20** | **19/20** | 23.4 |

Feeding the foxes was the easy half. Four brakes stop them eating the island bare, each added because the harness showed the run collapsing without it: **territory** (a vixen won't den next to another fox), a **recovery period between litters**, a **quiet resting fox** so a warren isn't permanently panicking, and a **burrow that conserves energy** — rabbits spend 30–60% of their lives underground, and at the surface burn rate that was slow starvation for the whole warren.

Also fixes an **alarm-relay loop**: sheltering rabbits kept each other's second-hand alarm alive indefinitely, so a warren that went to ground never heard an all-clear, never came up and never ate.

**Known weak spot, stated plainly**: heavier prey seeding (20 rabbits + 5 foxes, 24 seeds) ends with both species alive in 13/24, up from 0/24 — but about half those runs still end in a classic overshoot the prey doesn't recover from. That needs a stronger prey refuge than burrows and woodland currently give, and it's the scenario to re-run first after any change here.

## Rebasing onto the swim gene (#17)

Worth calling out: #17 makes a shoreline a *wall* below swim skill 0.35, which is a much worse world for a fleeing rabbit — every lake edge is somewhere it can be pinned. Rabbit extinctions in the headline scenario went from 5/20 to 9/20 **on the merge alone**, with no change of mine involved. Two numbers absorbed it, found on identical seeds: the fox's nose came down to 0.9× its sight, and the territory radius went 18 → 24 tiles.

## Balance is gated now, not eyeballed

Every balance change in this project has been judged by a headless script run by hand, which means nothing was gated on it. So:

- `scripts/ecosystem.mjs` + `make ecosystem` / `ecosystem-scatter` / `ecosystem-boom` / `ecosystem-json`
- Every run seeds `Math.random` (which the sim and map generator both draw from), so runs are **reproducible** and two configs can be compared on identical islands. Reproduce any run with `npm run ecosystem -- --seed <n> --runs 1`.
- `src/sim/ecosystem.test.js` runs a small seeded batch in CI — "the foxes all died out again" is now a test failure. Assertions guard against collapse, not today's numbers.
- A `Makefile` so there's one obvious command per task; `make check` runs exactly what CI runs.

Follow-up ideas are filed as #18 (tunable starting traits), #19 (shaping the environment), #20 (making evolution legible) and #21 (the sim loop is O(n²) in population).

Full write-up with the reasoning and the rejected alternatives: `docs/plans/fox-neural-nets.md`.

body:
<!-- Thanks for submitting a pull request! Please provide enough information so that others can review your pull request. -->

**Summary**

<!-- Explain the **motivation** for making this change. What existing problem does the pull request solve? -->
<!-- Try to link to an open issue for more information. -->
<!-- Any other information related to changes. -->

<!-- In addition to that please answer these questions: -->

Two gaps, both found by measuring what a build actually emits.

*Analyzable ESM output* dropped four references to the runtime form without recording why, so `stats.optimizationBailout` said nothing an ESM build could act on: a `chunkFormat` chunks are not imported through, a renamed `importFunctionName`, a target whose `environment.module` is false, and a set `publicPath` under the wasm-relative form. Each names itself now. The wasm form also gave up on the whole compilation as soon as one binary was reached from two runtimes; it groups runtime keys by the binaries they share instead, so a runtime reaching neither keeps its baked url while the sharing pair falls back together.

*Dead runtime code*: helpers were emitted that nothing calls — the public path under an assign-only `__webpack_public_path__`, the entry module id, `startupEntrypoint` where no chunk is awaited, and the `globalThis` polyfill plus chunk-css filename for a css loading runtime module that renders `null`. Each is the same shape: a runtime requirement declared before the decision that would have used it. `yarn test:size` reports −997 B on `target/universal-all-module-types node/main` and −342 B on each of six runtimes that lose their `global` block, with no asset growing.

**What kind of change does this PR introduce?**

<!-- E.g. a fix, feat, refactor, perf, test, chore, ci, build, style, revert, docs or describe it if you did not find a suitable kind of change. -->

fix

**Did you add tests for your changes?**

<!-- Please note: in most cases, if you change the code, we will not merge your changes unless you add tests. -->

Yes. New config cases `wasm/analyzable-mixed-wasm-loading`, `runtime/startup-entrypoint-only-when-awaited`, `output/public-path-assign-only` and `css/loading-runtime-only-when-rendered`; new stats configs under `statsCases/analyzable-esm-fallbacks` covering each newly reported reason. Every assertion was checked to fail on the unmodified `lib/`.

**Does this PR introduce a breaking change?**

<!-- If this PR introduces a breaking change, please describe the impact and a migration path for existing applications. -->

No.

**If relevant, what needs to be documented once your changes are merged or what have you already documented?**

<!-- List all the information that needs to be added to the documentation after merge that has already been documented in this PR. -->

n/a — no option changed; the new bailout reasons surface through the existing `stats.optimizationBailout`.

**Use of AI**

<!-- If you have used AI, please state so here. Explain how you used it.
Make sure to read our AI policy (https://github.com/webpack/governance/blob/main/AI_POLICY.md) or your Pull Request may be closed due to irresponsible use of AI. -->

AI (Claude Code) was used throughout: to search for candidates by analysing emitted bundles for runtime helpers nothing reads, to write the implementation and the test cases, and to run the verification. Every candidate it proposed was hand-verified in the emitted output before being acted on — several early ones were false positives and were discarded rather than "fixed". All claims here are backed by runs reported in the session: `yarn test:size` against a baseline for the byte figures, and each new assertion confirmed to fail without the corresponding `lib/` change.

author: copilot
body:
The `build` GitHub Actions job failed during image build because `uv sync` compiles `cbor2==5.2.0` with `--no-build-isolation-package cbor2`, but the environment did not include `wheel` (`bdist_wheel` missing). This PR adds the missing build prerequisite in the builder stage.

- **Root cause addressed**
  - `cbor2` is built without isolation in the `uv-builder` stage.
  - The stage had compilers and headers but not `wheel`, causing `bdist_wheel` failure.

- **Change**
  - Install `wheel` into the uv virtualenv immediately before `uv sync`.

- **Dockerfile update (targeted)**
  ```dockerfile
  RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/uv \
      uv venv --seed \
      && uv pip install wheel \
      && uv sync --frozen --no-install-project --no-dev --no-build-isolation-package cbor2
  ```

body:
## 摘要

按 `weekly-update-summary` 技能 v2 生成 2026-W33（2026-08-10 ~ 2026-08-16）周报：md 底稿落 `doc/report.2026-W33.md`，周刊版 html 已成稿（知识库因凭据未授权未能发布，见下）。同时执行技能 Phase 7 / 7.5：归档 28 个 changelog 碎片进 `CHANGELOG.md`，并修复归档后暴露出的 5 处死链。

本期三条结论：

1. **8 条新能力全部零功能验收**。29 份验收报告按类别拆开是发布验收 11 / 每日巡检 10 / 缺陷复测 5 / PR 验收 3，**功能验收 0 份**——13.8% 这个通过率没有回答本周任何一条新能力靠不靠谱。上期把「体量最大的新能力零验收」写进 P1，本期从「一条零验收」变成「全部零验收」。
2. **重复归档率从 26% 涨到 48%**，29 份报告去重后只有 15 个独立事项（同一次稳定冒烟归档 5 份、另一次 4 份、同一个 PR 验收 3 份）。这是上期排第一位的 P0，连续第四周点名、第四周恶化，质量闸这张表本身正在失去可读性。
3. **正式发布成功率三周连跌后首次回升到 50%**（6 次尝试 / 3 成功），且没有复发上期「15 次尝试里 9 次砸在同一提交」的形态——那恰是上期唯一一条已定位到具体对象的待办。

## 改动 diff

**文档（doc/）**
- `doc/report.2026-W33.md`：新增。W33 周报 md 底稿，九章结构（质量闸 / 业务价值看板 8 条 / 团队与用量 / 一周脉络 / 上期落地对照 / 下期优先级 / 术语表 / 附录 A 验收 29 份 / 附录 B PR 27 个 / 附录 C 工程数据）。
- `doc/index.yml`、`doc/guide.list.directory.md`：登记 `report.2026-W33`（技能 Phase 7 索引同步）。
- `doc/debt.platform.llm-gateway.md`、`doc/design.cds.web-entry.md`、`doc/design.frontend.mobile-refactor.md`、`doc/design.knowledge-base.store.md`、`doc/design.visual-agent.md`：把指向已被归档碎片的 5 处链接改写为「碎片已归档进 `CHANGELOG.md`」的既有表述（沿用 `debt.knowledge-base.md` 里的写法），消除死链。

**更新记录**
- `CHANGELOG.md`：`bash scripts/assemble-changelog.sh` 归档碎片到 `[未发布]` 段，按日期降序插入；随后按 Review 意见摘回 1 份碎片的 406 行，实际归档 28 个。
- `changelogs/*.md`：28 个碎片随归档删除；`2026-08-11_stable-smoke-runtime-equivalence.md` **刻意保留**（理由见下）。
- `changelogs/2026-08-16_weekly-w33.md`：新增本 PR 自身的碎片。

**代码**：无。本 PR 不含任何可执行代码改动。

## Review 修复记录

Codex 两条评审均属 AGENTS.md §5.5 的 **A 类直接缺陷**，已在 `ae0ad53d9` 修复：

**P2 提交统计失真** —— 根因是本仓库检出为**浅克隆**（`git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` 为 `true`），正是技能纪律 2 点名的冷启动场景，历史被截断导致少数 28 个提交。已 `git fetch --unshallow` 重算：

| 项 | 原值（浅克隆） | 修正值 |
|---|---|---|
| 主干提交 | 181 | **209** |
| 逐日 | 15/61/54/28/6/12/5 | **34/69/55/28/6/12/5** |
| 署名 | Claude 94 | **Claude 122** |
| 类型分布 | fix 109 / docs 23 / feat 12 / polish 4 | **fix 128 / docs 24 / feat 19 / polish 5** |

派生结论连带修正：两天占比 64% → 59%，fix/feat 占比 60%/7% → **61%/9%**。PR 集合（27 个）与去重 diff（863 文件 / +78,767 / -6,590）不受影响，边界提交未变。口径行补记了这次重算过程，供下次重跑做幂等对照。

**P1 归档误删仍待核对的 D6 碎片** —— `changelogs/2026-08-11_stable-smoke-runtime-equivalence.md` 是被**刻意**从 `.entropy-manifest.yml` 撤回的（见 `doc/debt.prd-agent.md` 的 `2026-08-13-avatar-editor-no-design-doc`，状态 `open`），目的正是让 D6 每轮继续报账；而 D6 只枚举 `changelogs/*.md`，文件一删这条债务就永久失访。已还原该碎片并从 `CHANGELOG.md` 摘回其 406 行，模拟 D6 确认它重新被报为 `UNPROCESSED_CHANGELOG`。

**另修一条自查发现的** —— `navCoverage` 守卫判红：用量口径里 `route:/providers` 与 `route:/web-hosting` 两个路由都不存在。网关控制台是独立系统、不在主系统路由表内，改为 `none:平台能力`；网页托管的真实路由是 `/web-pages`。**红绿闭环已验**：改回错误 token 该守卫立刻变红，恢复后转绿。

## 测试

- [x] `prd-admin` 全量测试：**174 文件 / 1451 用例全绿**（含 `navCoverage` 守卫 12 用例）
- [x] `python3 scripts/doc-readability-check.py --ratchet --baseline-ref origin/base` —— 按 CI 口径与目标分支比对，**死链 0、裸引用 0**，六项欠账均未上升；新报告本身通过导读校验
- [x] `python3 scripts/tests/doc-readability-ratchet.test.py` —— 通过
- [x] `python3 scripts/tests/test_claude_memory_contract.py` —— 通过
- [x] `python3 scripts/tests/test_skills_audit_contract.py` —— 通过
- [x] 周刊版 html 六项硬约束逐项核对：无 `<script>`、无 `data:image`、无外部 http 资源、带 `meta viewport`、29 个 `<a href>` **全部**带 `target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer"`、emoji 字符数 0
- [x] 防漏数据对账：附录 A 份数列相加 = 29（等于头部验收份数），附录 B 行数 = 27（等于头部 PR 收口数），两表均全量无节选
- [x] 数据口径复核：27 个 PR 在**完整历史**下逐个 `git merge-base --is-ancestor` 验证全部可达；周归属按本地 commit date 而非 GitHub `mergedAt`
- [x] `CHANGELOG.md` 完整性：摘回的 406 行残留为 0，未误删同日其它碎片的行（`### 2026-08-11` 区块仍有 340 行），空日期区块与 base 一致（唯一一个 `### 2026-03-17` 为既有）
- [ ] 真人通过预览域名验收 —— **不适用**：本 PR 仅改 `doc/` 与 `changelogs/`，按 `cds-first-verification` 规则的例外条款无需 CDS 部署验证

**自测路径声明（CLAUDE.md §8.1）**：走的是「已有校验脚本 + 硬约束逐项核对 + 红绿闭环」这条。断言的是——五个守卫脚本退出码为 0、死链数为 0、附录行数与头部数字相等、html 六项硬约束逐项为真、`navCoverage` 在错误 token 下确实会红。

## 风险与已知边界

- **五源不可达，本期周报只有一半事实**。日报知识库 / 缺陷台账 / 团队洞察 / 采用度 / 上期周报条目五个数据源，主系统接口对本次采集凭据返回「未授权」；已尝试两条路径（`AI_ACCESS_KEY` 直连、`/api/v1/auth/login` 口令登录）均被拒。后果：一周脉络七天**无日报深链**（仅据 git 重建）、缺陷趋势无法给出、团队与用量整节为空。按纪律 12 已在基线行、正文对应章节、页脚**四处**逐条声明为证据空白，**没有用「0」冒充「不可用」**。恢复凭据后可回补，已列入下期 P1。
- **周刊版 html 未发布到知识库**。同一凭据问题导致 `publish.py` 在 `find_store` 阶段即失败；已按技能纪律 8 的退化路径跑 `--local` 落本地成稿（61 KB，六项硬约束校验通过）。凭据恢复后需带 `--replace-same-date` 补发一次，届时库里同一周应有且只有一条。
- **归档是不可逆的目录变更**。28 个碎片已 `git rm`，内容进 `CHANGELOG.md [未发布]` 段，待下次发版 promote。
- **回滚**：纯文档变更，`git revert` 即可，无数据迁移、无 Breaking Change。

## 后续事项

**由本 PR 的 Review 暴露、但按范围熔断不在此展开的（B 类）**：

- 周报技能 Phase 7.5 明确要求「不要按周过滤，无差别合并所有积压」，**未预料到「被刻意撤回登记的碎片」这种情况——下一次跑周报还会再删一次**。修法二选一：`assemble-changelog.sh` 支持跳过未登记碎片，或让 D6 能从归档记录继续追踪未处理项（Codex 建议的第二条路）。属改工具/改技能，需独立 PR。

**按报告「下周（W34）优先级」**：

author: ayar20260808
body:
Aus der hochgeladenen Design-Vorlage (`Hero_Elektroplanung.dc.html`) übernommen und als eigenständiges, abhängigkeitsfreies CSS/HTML neu gebaut — das Original war eine Vorschau-Datei mit Verweisen auf ein externes Framework (`_ds/...`, `support.js`), das im Projekt nicht existiert.

## Was übernommen wurde

- Sieben Symbole aus der Vorlage extrahiert und als eigene Dateien abgelegt: Deckenleuchte, Ausschalter, Herd-Anschlussdose, Taster, Einbau-Spot, Erdung, Rollladenmotor.
- Das Foto ist dasselbe wie im Hero (`hero-plan.jpg` wiederverwendet, gleiches Seitenverhältnis) — hier in Graustufen mit `mix-blend-mode:multiply` auf den hellen Sektionshintergrund gelegt, wirkt wie ein helles Wasserzeichen statt eines kräftigen Fotos. Langsamer Zoom über 44 Sekunden.
- 15 Symbolplatzierungen (7 Motive, mehrfach an verschiedenen Stellen), Positionen und Blitz-Rhythmus 1:1 aus der Vorlage übernommen: alle 0,4 s startet das nächste Symbol seinen eigenen 6-Sekunden-Zyklus.

## Einordnung

Liegt hinter den deckenden Leistungskarten und wird nur in den Fugen und im freien neunten Rasterplatz sichtbar — deshalb bewusst nicht weiter abgeschwächt, die Kartenflächen schützen die Lesbarkeit ohnehin. `#leistungen` bekommt dafür `position:relative`/`overflow:hidden`, Kopf und Kartenraster werden explizit auf `z-index:1` gesetzt.

## Gemessen

Keine fehlende Datei, kein JS-Fehler, kein horizontaler Überstand bei 390, 768, 1920 und 2560 px Breite, Seite 1 weiterhin 0 px Abweichung. HTML-/SVG-Tags und JSON-LD geprüft.

author: thecsdoctor
body:
💡 What: Memoized `type.toUpperCase()` in the `LabelOverlay` component by extending the existing `labelCache`.
🎯 Why: Calling `.toUpperCase()` repeatedly per node on every frame during canvas rendering generates a massive amount of short-lived string allocations, causing Garbage Collection (GC) pauses that degrade FPS.
📊 Impact: Eliminates thousands of string allocations per frame, stabilizing memory usage and improving frame times for large graphs.
🔬 Measurement: Run the application and observe stable memory usage (via Chrome DevTools memory profiling) and smoother panning/zooming.

author: ross0x01
body:
## Summary

- generate chat titles from the original user message instead of the auxiliary-vision-processed message
- ignore internal `<image_description ... trust="untrusted">` parts as defense in depth
- keep image-only conversations titled exactly `New chat`
- keep text-plus-image conversations titled from only the user-written text

## Why

Follow-up to #1113. Auxiliary vision replaces an image part with an internal text description before DeepSeek sees it. Title generation was also receiving that processed message, so image-only chats could expose internal markup such as `<image_description filename="...">` in the title.

The active DeepSeek request still receives the auxiliary description. Only the title-generation input now stays on the original user message.

## User impact

- image plus `Tell me about this image` produces a title based on that text
- image without user text remains `New chat`
- internal auxiliary markup never becomes visible as a chat title

## Validation

- full Jest suite: 365 suites / 3,772 tests passed
- `corepack pnpm run typecheck`
- ESLint on all changed TypeScript files
- Prettier on all changed TypeScript files
- `git diff --check`

## Manual verification

1. Start a new paid DeepSeek chat with only an image. Confirm its title is `New chat`.
2. Start another chat with an image and `Tell me about this image`. Confirm the title is derived from that text and contains no `image_description` markup.
3. Confirm DeepSeek still receives and answers from the MiMo-generated visual description.

#### 7f38ebbabf35e067114a9ccdd56103132c880b4f 
[JSC] Apply Promise.try spec change
https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=321890
rdar://185064567

Reviewed by Sosuke Suzuki.

Test262 is updated[1] to include the latest spec change proposal
for Promise.try[2], which uses PromiseResolve instead of a promise
created by NewPromiseCapability. This simplifies our Promise.try
implementation since we can just use @promiseResolve and @promiseReject
helpers instead. Also this removes the reference to
@newPromiseCapability in JSC code. So we drop PromiseOperations.js and
its JS builtins, and replace @newPromiseCapability with C++ version for
remaining WebCore users.

WebCore users can be replaced by using normal Promise + first-resolving
handler. This is fixed in a subsequent change.

[1]: https://github.com/tc39/test262/pull/5072
[2]: https://github.com/tc39/ecma262/pull/3883

author: tvanhens
body:
`db.live(build)` — a standing `db.q` on the session socket. Same builder, same pull map, returns a `get()` / `subscribe(cb)` store (`useSyncExternalStore`-shaped) instead of an Effect.

```ts
const todos = db.live((q) =>
  q.where("?e", Todo.title, "_").find("?e").pull({ title: Todo.title, done: Todo.done }),
)
todos.get()        // readonly { title; done; eid: Eid }[] | undefined
todos.subscribe(cb) // () => void

const eids = db.live((q) => q.where("?e", Todo.title, "_").find("?e")) // readonly Eid[]
```

## What changed

- `packages/alchemy/src/schema/Live.ts` (new): `LiveStore`, `LiveQueryBuilder`, `LiveFind`, `LiveQuery`, `LiveRow`, `TypedLiveDatabaseClient`, `makeLive`.
  - `find` takes exactly one entity var — a var bound as `Eid` by the builder. `find("?e", "?n")`, `find("?n")` on a value attr, and unbound vars are type errors.
  - `.pull(map)` is the literate `eid.pull` map; rows are `PullResult` + `eid`. No `.pull` → `Eid[]`.
  - Refresh is driven by `session.onT` (server `t` frames and `ack.t` after a `transact` on the same socket): re-run the same q with `minT: t`, then N+1 pulls fenced at the q's `res.t` (bounded concurrency, a failed row drops). No `bump`, writers don't mention the store.
  - Short-circuit when `res.t <= lastBasis` — snapshot reference stays stable. One pass in flight; a `t` landing mid-pass coalesces into one follow-up.
  - Failed pass keeps the last snapshot, sets `store.error`, retries with bounded backoff; `close()` detaches the `onT` listener.
- `schema/Session.ts`: `SchemaFx.Session.connect` captures the Effect services and returns `db` extended with `live`; `TypedSession.db` is `TypedLiveDatabaseClient<C>`.
- No worker / transactor / replica changes. No React package — the store is the primitive.

## Test plan

- `bun run typecheck` clean, incl. `test/schema/live-types.ts` fixtures (row types; `@ts-expect-error` for multi-var `find`, value-attr var, unbound var, attr var, out-of-catalog pull attr).
- `bun test packages/alchemy` — 125 pass. New `test/live.test.ts` (11 tests): initial q/pull frames, `t` frame → q with `minT` + pulls fenced at `res.t`, same-`t` short-circuit keeps the reference, `transact` on the same session refreshes with no manual invalidation, no-`.pull` → `Eid[]`, unsubscribe stops notifications, mid-pass `t` coalescing, `close()` mid-pass, subscriber-before-first-result, failed pass retries and recovers, one refused row drops.
- `bun run test` — 281 pass / 0 fail.

Closes #5

author: sagak-dev
body:
## What changed

- Added a dedicated `pengram-theme.css` visual layer so existing application logic and selectors stay intact.
- Added a final precedence layer to override the legacy Anki-desktop fidelity stylesheet without deleting its structural browser rules.
- Reworked the desktop chrome into a compact floating navigation treatment.
- Rebuilt deck rows as large editorial cards with stronger typography, spacing, counters, and hover feedback.
- Restyled deck detail, browser/settings panels, dialogs, form controls, metrics, and tags.
- Redesigned review mode around one large question card, a focused answer reveal action, and a floating four-rating dock.
- Added touch-first responsive rules for iPad and smaller screens, plus reduced-motion handling.

author: cemozturkish
body:
Sözcel's hexagons had no frame where it mattered most: the keyboard keys never carried the drawn ring at all, and a board tile dropped its frame the moment it was revealed, because `.letter-box.correct/.present/.absent` tinted the ring with the tile's own fill so it melted into it. The result was that the played half of the board and the whole keyboard read as soft blocks beside the framed, unplayed half.

All of it is in `frames.css`, and only Sözcel is affected — `.letter-box` and `.key` exist on no other page.

**What changed**

- `.key::after` joins the ring overlay list, so keys are drawn with the same hand-drawn stroke the tiles use.
- The key's ring mask repeats the key's own `131.27% / 111.71%` mask scale. The two masks are cut from the same canvas, so at plain `contain` the ring would draw a stroke floating *inside* the key's enlarged silhouette instead of on its edge.
- The stroke is pinned to `#000` for tiles (in every state) and keys, replacing the per-state tints and the `var(--ink)` fallback. Every fill these hexagons can take — the paper of an empty tile, the greys of a revealed one, the key colors — is something other than pure black, so the frame stays visible on all of them and in either palette. Note this does change the empty tile's stroke in the earth palette, where `--ink` is the brown `#4C382A`; the board is now uniformly black-framed rather than half brown, half black.
- Avatar frames and the honeycomb are untouched — they keep following `--ink`/the palette.

**Testing**

No test suite in this repo (QA is manual browser testing). Rendered the tiles and keys in all four states — empty, correct, present, absent — against the real `frame-fill.png` / `frame-ring.png` assets in headless Chromium to confirm the ring lands on the drawn silhouette at both the tile's and the key's size, rather than floating inside it. Faded states (`opacity: .4`) fade the ring with the fill, matching the existing treatment.

author: beestoxd
body:
Closes #150

Saving a spawn or AFK point used to reach into `SHARDS.CUBOIDS.REGIONS.spawn` and overwrite it. That is harmless on a fresh server, where the region is empty and the setup commands are the only thing that will ever fill it in. On a server that already has its shard zone configured it means `/setspawn` quietly drags the reward region along to wherever the admin happened to be standing. That is what happened in #150: the reporter ran `/setspawn`, their shard zone moved off their spawn build to 0 0 0, and players started earning shards in the wrong place.

## Only bootstrap a region that still follows setup

`configureSetupShardRegion` now returns early unless the region's stored location is empty, or still equal to the spawn/AFK location this setup run is replacing. An empty region is a fresh install and gets filled in exactly as before. A region that still matches the previous setup value is one nobody has moved, so it keeps travelling with `/setspawn`. Anything else was pointed somewhere deliberately and is left completely alone now, `ENABLED` and `BOUND` and `CUBOID` included.

The check compares the raw serialized strings instead of parsed `Location` objects. `LocationUtils.parse` returns null when the world named in the value is not loaded, so a region pointing into an unloaded world would look empty and get overwritten anyway. Both sides of the comparison come from the same `LocationUtils.serialize` call, which makes the string match exact.

`setSetupLocation` reads the old value before it writes the new one and hands it down, because by the time the shard helper runs the config key already holds the new location.

## Setting the AFK point no longer moves the spawn region's world

`WORLD` was written on both paths, so `/setafk` rewrote the spawn shard region's world with whatever world the AFK point sits in. It is now written only on the spawn path, alongside the other spawn keys.

## Notes

`RADIUS` was already protected this way on its own; the guard simply moved up a level so it covers the rest of the region too, and existing radius behaviour is unchanged. No config or language keys were added, so there is nothing to translate.

`SetupShardRegionOwnershipTest` covers the four cases: an empty region, a region still following setup, a region the owner moved (using the values from #150), and a region configured before setup was ever run. Suite is green at 215 tests.
