author: julienlegoux
body:
Closes #20

## Summary

Two gaps the audit found in the mandatory baseline:

- `build-essential` was only on the box as a side effect of the Hermes
  installer, so unticking Hermes silently removed the compiler, and every
  later component that builds native code failed for a reason nobody could
  see. It now joins `bl_update`'s `apt install -y` list directly.
- Nothing applied security updates after the install run, on a host
  explicitly meant to be left unattended. A new mandatory `bl_unattended`
  baseline step installs `unattended-upgrades` and writes
  `/etc/apt/apt.conf.d/20auto-upgrades`, enabling the security pocket only
  with `Unattended-Upgrade::Automatic-Reboot "false"`. It runs after
  `bl_update` and before `bl_user`, following the repo's transactional
  write pattern (`mktemp` beside the target, write, `chmod`, `mv -f`,
  `rm -f` the candidate on every failure branch).
- `do_check` gains a line reporting whether unattended-upgrades is
  configured and its timer active (`ok`/`ko`), and a `note` (not a `ko`)
  when `/var/run/reboot-required` exists — a pending reboot is information,
  not a defect.

This is the only work in epic 1 that touches the hardcoded baseline sequence
in `cmd_install`, which is why it's its own issue rather than folded into a
component.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `bash tests/test_vps_boot.sh` passes with no regressions — the two
      install-flow fixtures (`test_cmd_install_root_quickstart_flow`,
      `test_cmd_install_created_user_custom_flow`) now stub `bl_unattended`
      the same way as its siblings, so the run never hits real `apt`.
- [x] `bash -n vps-boot.sh` is clean.
- [x] `grep -c build-essential vps-boot.sh` shows it in `bl_update`'s list.
- [ ] Fresh Ubuntu 24.04 host checks (`apt-config dump`, `20auto-upgrades`
      mode 0644, `systemctl is-enabled apt-daily-upgrade.timer`) — not
      verifiable from this dev sandbox (Windows, no real `apt`/`systemd`);
      covered instead by unit tests that stub `apt`/`systemctl`/`chmod` and
      assert the written config content, mode, and the timer-enable call.
- [x] `vps-boot.sh check` prints a line for unattended-upgrades and, when
      `/var/run/reboot-required` is present, a `!` note rather than a `✗`
      (exit code still 0 in that state — `note()` only increments `WARN`,
      never `FAIL`).
- [x] `README.md` and `docs/planning/SPECS.md` updated in the same commit
      as the code (plus `.claude/CLAUDE.md`'s Baseline file-map line, which
      this change makes stale).

## How it was tested

`bash tests/test_vps_boot.sh` (Windows/Git Bash sandbox — see note below):

```
25 passed, 11 failed
```

New tests added, all passing:
- `bl_update installs build-essential`
- `bl_unattended installs package and writes config`
- `bl_unattended cleans candidate after chmod failure`
- `cmd_install runs bl_unattended between update and user` (fails in this
  sandbox only — see note)

**Sandbox note**: this dev environment is Windows Git Bash, not Linux — 10
of the 11 failures above are pre-existing and present on `develop` before
this PR (no real root/`$EUID`, no writable `/run`, no `sshd` binary,
Windows chmod not honoring exact octal modes). The 11th is this PR's new
`cmd_install`-flow ordering test, which fails for the identical
"Must run as root" reason its two existing siblings
(`test_cmd_install_root_quickstart_flow`,
`test_cmd_install_created_user_custom_flow`) already fail for here — not a
regression from this change. `bash -n vps-boot.sh` is clean.

## Drift

None. No decided standard or issue spec had to be departed from.

Issue: [docs/epics/epic-1-expand-toolchain-components/issues/02-baseline-build-essential-auto-updates.md](https://github.com/julienlegoux/vps-boot/blob/develop/docs/epics/epic-1-expand-toolchain-components/issues/02-baseline-build-essential-auto-updates.md)

author: julienlegoux
body:
Closes #19

## What changed

`register()` now takes a **required** `<group>` argument, positioned right after
`<scope>`, and populates a new `COMPONENT_GROUP` array. The full signature:

```
register <key> <name> <desc> <default 0|1> <scope system|user> <group> <install_fn> <check_fn> [signin_hint]
```

The first eight arguments are required — `register` calls `die` on fewer, so a
call site can never be left un-migrated with a silently empty group.
`signin_hint` stays the trailing optional one (now the 9th argument).

A new `COMPONENT_GROUPS=(core languages packaging agents cloud infra)` fixes the
six group names and their display/registration order. Nothing reads it yet
except the new test; issue #26 (the picker) consumes it next.

The twelve existing component blocks were **moved verbatim** so registration
order matches group order, each group opening with a `# ══ <group> ══` banner:

| Group | Components, in registration order |
|---|---|
| `core` | `sudo_nopasswd`, `docker`, `gh` |
| `languages` | `node`, `python`, `go` |
| `packaging` | `bun`, `pnpm` |
| `agents` | `claude`, `opencode`, `hermes` |
| `cloud` | *(empty placeholder — #24 fills it)* |
| `infra` | `herdr` |

The npm-based components (`bun`, `pnpm`, `claude`, `opencode`) still register
after `node`, which the group order preserves for free.

No component body was edited. Verified mechanically by diffing the multiset of
lines before/after: the only differences are the register lines, the registry
mechanism, the group banners and whitespace.

## Tests

New case in `tests/test_vps_boot.sh` — *"registry entries name real functions,
scope and group"*: for every key in `COMPONENTS`, `COMPONENT_INSTALL` and
`COMPONENT_CHECK` name functions `declare -F` resolves, `COMPONENT_SCOPE` is
`system` or `user`, and `COMPONENT_GROUP` is one of the six. The six valid
groups are spelled out in the test rather than read from the script, so a typo
in `COMPONENT_GROUPS` cannot make it pass vacuously.

```
bash tests/test_vps_boot.sh   →  23 passed, 10 failed
```

⚠️ **The 10 failures are pre-existing and environmental, not regressions.** This
run happened on Windows/Git Bash, where the harness cannot be root: the same 10
cases fail identically on `origin/develop` before this change (`✗ Must run as
root.`, `install: cannot create directory '/run': Permission denied`). They are
the `cmd_install` flow, sudoers/`visudo` and `sshd -T` cases. On a Linux host
running as root the suite should report the **33 passed, 0 failed** the issue
asks for — 33 `run_test` lines are registered (32 + the new one), which is
verifiable here. This repo has no CI, so that number could not be confirmed
automatically.

Red/green was observed for the new case: it failed before the registry change
(`0 passed, 1 failed`) and passed after.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `bash tests/test_vps_boot.sh` passes the new case; 33 cases registered.
      **Caveat above**: 23/10 locally, all 10 failures pre-existing and
      root-only; `33 passed, 0 failed` is unverified on this Windows host.
- [x] The new case fails when deliberately broken and passes again when
      reverted. Verified twice, before opening this PR: registering `herdr`
      with group `misc` → `not ok`; registering it with `check_herdr_typo` →
      `not ok`; reverted → `ok`.
- [x] `bash -n vps-boot.sh` is clean. `bash tests/test_vps_boot.sh cmd_install`
      fails only with `✗ Must run as root.` — identical to its behaviour on
      `develop` before this change, so the reordered run loop is unverified
      here rather than broken.
- [x] The old seven-argument form is a hard error:
      `register x "X" "desc" 1 system install_gh check_gh` →
      `✗ register x: expected at least 8 arguments … got 7`, exit 1.
      `grep -c '^register ' vps-boot.sh` → **12**, each carrying a group.
- [x] `.claude/CLAUDE.md` and `docs/planning/SPECS.md` updated (separate commit
      on the same branch/PR, not a separate PR).

## Size

272 changed lines against `develop` (169 insertions, 103 deletions) — under the
~500 the issue targeted for an M.

## Notes for the sibling issues (#21, #22, #23, #24, #25, #26)

Each group has an obvious insertion point: append the new block inside its
`# ══ <group> ══` banner. `cloud` is present but empty, with a
`# (no components in this group yet)` placeholder line to replace.

Issue reference:
[docs/epics/epic-1-expand-toolchain-components/issues/01-registry-groups-and-reorder.md](docs/epics/epic-1-expand-toolchain-components/issues/01-registry-groups-and-reorder.md)

author: steipete
body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/124787

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where creating a managed-worktree session could generate its title and worktree name through the agent default route instead of the new session’s selected provider, model, runtime, and auth profile. This covered explicit models and registered session-catalog targets, and now also covers children that inherit their selection from a parent session.

## Why This Change Was Made

One create-time selection resolver now handles default, explicit, catalog, and inherited-parent routes. Explicit and catalog routes retain the config-policy validation added by this PR. Parent inheritance is projected only inside the canonical session-creation owner, after that owner validates the parent, its ownership, and its model lock, then carries the narrow provider/model/runtime/profile selection into lifecycle preparation.

Title work still starts before repository resolution whenever the route is knowable at dispatch: default sessions without a parent, explicit models, and catalog targets. Parent-only requests defer title preparation until the validated inherited selection reaches the lifecycle callback. Denied or invalid direct selections continue to suppress title preparation entirely. The persisted create path remains the sole live model-catalog availability validator, so this does not restore the blocking catalog load removed by #122471.

## User Impact

Create-time titles, managed-worktree branch names, persisted child selection, and the first chat turn now agree for default, explicit, catalog-backed, and parent-inherited sessions. A policy-rejected route cannot receive title content before the create request is rejected. Existing title persistence, timeout, and worktree fallback behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Boundary regression: the new inherited-parent initial-message worktree case failed before the owner-boundary repair because the title generator received the agent default while the child persisted the parent selection. It now observes the inherited model reference, runtime, and preferred profile; the generated title names the branch and persists on the child; and the child entry carries the same inherited route.
- Existing explicit-model, registered-catalog, default-route, and denied-model cases remain covered. The denied route still observes no title completion, worktree, or session row.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server.sessions.create.test.ts src/gateway/dashboard-session-title.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-command-replies.test.ts src/agents/worktrees/name.test.ts src/agents/worktrees/service.naming.test.ts` — 148 tests passed across five files.
- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01m06nnsvarh61z99z2028s8dx`: production types, all core test-type shards, and core oxlint passed. Run: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/31985343271
- Targeted oxfmt, targeted local oxlint, `git diff --check`, and the final mandatory uncommitted autoreview passed with no accepted/actionable findings.
- Production LOC: +126/-50 (net +76); tests: +207/-42 (net +165). The production growth is the canonical four-route selection projection plus the narrow lifecycle seam. The category helper is a pure extraction that keeps `sessions-create.ts` net -5 lines and under its max-lines budget without a suppression.
- No separate visual capture: this changes routing for the existing title/worktree UI flow rather than its rendered appearance; the isolated dev-Gateway visual proof remains on #124787.
- AI-assisted; maintainer reviewed and verified the final diff.

author: pocke-host
body:
## Summary
Investigated "can we keep the WHOOP integration alive long-term instead of pausing/cancelling." The existing design already handles the main risk well:
- The 4-hour scheduler backstop (`WhoopSyncScheduler`) keeps every connected user's refresh token exercised well within any inactivity window WHOOP might impose — this is already explicitly designed for exactly this purpose (see the existing comments in `WhoopSyncScheduler`/`WhoopService`).
- `markNeedsReconnect()` already detects `invalid_grant` gracefully rather than silently failing forever.
- Confirmed the integration is already on WHOOP's v2 API/webhooks — not affected by WHOOP's Nov 2025 v1 webhook shutdown.
- Found no public WHOOP developer-platform policy about pausing/cancelling third-party apps.

**The actual gap**: when a connection genuinely does need reconnecting, the only signal is an in-app `Notification` row. There's no push-notification delivery anywhere in this backend (confirmed — not WHOOP-specific, no APNs/FCM exists at all yet). A user who doesn't open the app has no way to learn their sync quietly stopped — the real risk isn't the token expiring, it's the user never finding out.

This wires `markNeedsReconnect()` to also send an email via the existing `EmailService` (same SMTP config already used for password resets). Never throws — a mail failure can't affect the token-clearing/notification logic it's attached to.

## Test plan
- [x] `mvn compile` passes
- [ ] Send a real test email once deployed (SMTP env vars are prod-only, not available locally)

author: yasserf
body:
Replaces #1300, which was built on the `#pikku` types hub and the `@pikku/core/ecosystem` tier — both deleted by #1311. Roughly 60% of that PR was absorbed there; this is what was actually left, reimplemented on the leaf model.

## The generated `pikkuMiddleware` was dropping `priority`

A live bug on `main`. The generated factory re-implemented core's rather than delegating to it — `typeof middleware === 'function' ? middleware : middleware.func` — and dropped `priority` twice over: `PikkuMiddlewareConfig` had no such field, and a middleware passing one anyway never received the `__priority` stamp that `middleware-runner.ts` sorts on. Ordering silently fell back to declaration order.

It now delegates to `@pikku/core/middleware`, and `MiddlewarePriority` is emitted alongside it.

## Every definer reaches the app through its leaf

An app developer imports from `#pikku/<leaf>`; reaching past it to `@pikku/core` is the smell that says the generator is not emitting something it should. #1311 already routed `defineSecret`, `defineScope` and `defineVariable`. Still missing:

- **`defineCredential` had no door at all** — generated into the project's `.pikku` via a new `credentialTypesFile` config key.
- **`cors`** joins `#pikku/http`, next to the `addHTTPMiddleware` it is wired with.
- **Leaf indexes were single-entry.** `credentials`, `secrets` and `variables` each have two entries (the definer and the typed service map); only the first was re-exported, so the second was reachable only through a raw relative path into `.pikku` — which is what apps were doing. `serializeLeafIndex` now re-exports every entry a leaf has.
- **10 call sites** migrated across `e2e` and `verifiers`.

## Generation order, not a second bootstrap trigger

The definition-type generators ran *after* the leaf-index step. A leaf index only re-exports entry files that exist when it is written, so on an upgrade — `.pikku` present, definer file not yet generated, so the `!existsSync(outDir)` bootstrap gate does not fire — the run produced a `#pikku/credentials` that resolved but was missing `defineCredential`. Every inspection between those two points saw it, which leaves an unresolved factory's input silently `any`. A trailing index refresh papered over the file but not the inspections.

The four generators are hoisted ahead of `pikkuLeafIndexes` and dropped from the inspected pass. They read only `config`, so nothing held them there — one ordering change fixes the cold and warm paths.

## Guard

`packages/core/src/app-leaf-surface.test.ts` discovers every directory with a `pikku.config.json` and fails on any project naming `@pikku/core` for a name its leaf carries. Red baseline: 16 offenders across 11 distinct names.

## Verification

- `app-leaf-surface.test.ts` — 16 offenders → 2/2 green; re-confirmed red by reverting a single migrated call site
- `packages/cli` — 1107 pass, 0 fail
- `packages/core` — 2197 pass, 0 fail, 10 skipped
- `verifiers/secrets` cold codegen + `tsc` — exit 0
- `verifiers/secrets` warm upgrade path (definer + index deleted) — index correct in the same run, `tsc` exit 0
- `changeset status` — exit 0

## Left out

- **`templates/uws` `cors`** — runtime templates are not on the `#pikku` alias on `main`; that is #1307's territory.
- **`InvalidOriginError` on the http leaf** — `#pikku/error` already carries it, and a second door breaks one-door-per-name.
- **13 `e2e` tsc errors are pre-existing** — `emailStore`/`hmacSigner`/`oauthApiClient`/`todoStore` missing on `WiredServices`, in addon files this branch never touches. body:
Closes #300.

The Ghost Signals trading floor was **a room you could walk into and be invisible in**. It had a scene, a rig and a tower on the street — but no `ROOMS` entry and no presence mount, so an agent standing there would beat away happily, appear on its own roster, and be drawn by nobody.

`rooms.ts` says exactly this in its own docblock: *"a room you can stand in but nobody can see is not a room"*, and *"adding a venue means adding it in both places"*. Nothing enforced it — and the two places live in **different packages**, so nothing could notice they'd drifted.

## The invariant

A test now reads across the package boundary: every id in `ROOMS` must appear in some scene under `kax/src/pages` that mounts presence for it.

It accepts **three** shapes, because a stricter test would have reported two false violations rather than the one real one:

```
<VenuePresence room="arcade" />               the common case
usePresence("city")                           the street, which predates it
room={`residences:${floorLabel(floor)}`}      one scene serving a family of ids
```

The issue proposed asserting `VenuePresence` specifically. That would have called **`city` broken** — the street has rendered remote bodies through `usePresence` since before the component existed. Worth flagging, since a guard that cries wolf on working code gets deleted rather than fixed.

Confirmed non-vacuous by removing the mount again: the suite reports `gs`.

887 api-server + 24 kax tests green, production build clean.

Everything between v5.22.1 and here is the Windows delivery, from a pool
that could not be declared to one that boots, isolates, registers, proves
its own identity is worthless, and gets deleted safely.

The Windows half of the fleet (#140 #142 #143 #144 #147 #148 #149 #151
#152 #154 #155 #156 #158):

  * a Windows pool is declarable -- host_os selects the boot-script
    metadata key, and a pool that would have booted silently is refused at
    plan time rather than looking healthy and doing nothing
  * a golden image, so a host boots warm instead of installing for ten
    minutes
  * one local Windows account per slot, a credential no job inherits from
    the one before it, and agents registered as services from a token read
    once
  * a boot probe that proves the slot boundary from inside a slot, before
    any agent registers, and refuses the boot if it cannot
  * the controller can delete a Windows host: the drain gate branches on
    ci-host-os, keeps the Linux SSH text byte-identical, and asks a Windows
    host through its beacon
  * onboarding and the README describe the pool that now exists, and the
    workflow gate refuses container:/services: on a Windows pool label

No Windows host has booted any of this yet. The boot path is gated by text
matching and by pure-function tests running pwsh 7 on Linux, so the first

windows-host-startup.ps1.

author: jgfoster
body:
**Step 1 of 3** toward routing class creation through a metaclass (`docs/Class_Body_Namespace.md` stage 7).

## The gap

Grail had a `type` **builtin** — `type(x)` answers x's class — but no `type` **object**. The name evaluated to a `BoundMethod` on builtins:

| | CPython | Grail (before) |
|---|---|---|
| `repr(type)` | `<class 'type'>` | `<BoundMethod object at 0x…>` |
| `type(type)` | `type` | `BoundMethod` |
| `isinstance(type, type)` | `True` | `False` |
| `type.__mro__` | `(type, object)` | `AttributeError` |

A class cannot inherit from a non-class, so `ClassDefAst` carried a hard-coded redirect rooting every `class M(type)` at `PythonInstance`, its comment recording that nothing was bound to the name. `PyType` is that missing object and the redirect now points at it, so **`Meta.__bases__` answers `['type']`** instead of `['PythonInstance']`.

## Why this is worth doing despite moving no test

The survey I ran first found the payoff isn't in the scoreboard — it's that **the vendored ports were rewritten to avoid needing this base**, each site saying so in its own words (*"Grail doesn't expose `type` as a base and drops metaclass= kwargs"*):

| Site | Divergence |
|---|---|
| `django/db/models/base.py` | `ModelBase` demoted → *"defining concrete user models is therefore not supported yet"* |
| `django/forms/{models,forms,widgets}.py` | `ModelForm`, `Form`, `Widget` metaclasses neutered |
| `django/db/models/{enums,query,fields}` | `ChoicesType`, `InstanceCheckMeta`, `AutoFieldMeta` reduced to plain classes |
| `jinja2/nodes.py` | `NodeType` not honoured |
| `typing.py`, `email/_policybase.py` | `__instancecheck__` rewired around the metaclass |

The same survey sized the risk: **zero `class X(type)` definitions in library code** — all 49 are in test files — so re-rooting cannot destabilise the stdlib Grail ships.

## What is deliberately not done here

- **`type` as a value is still the BoundMethod**, so `issubclass(Meta, type)` and `isinstance(type, type)` remain `False`. I tried registering `Python at: #'type'` and it **regressed two modules**: the entry makes `NameAst >> isResolvableSymbol:` true for `type`, so `type('NewClass', (object,), {})` compiles as a *constructor* call and dies with a Smalltalk `MessageNotUnderstood` (`test_subclassinit test_type`). The name has to be bound in the same step that gives `PyType` the call protocol, so it cannot race ahead of it. Both the failure and the reason are recorded in `PyType.gs`.
- `PyType` carries no construction protocol (`__call__`/`__new__`/`__init__`/`mro`), and the class statement still does not route through a metaclass.

`PyType` subclasses `PythonInstance`, not `Object` — the `isKindOf: PythonInstance` gates in `___pyAttrLoad___` misfire outside that chain, which is why `class C(object)` is redirected there too. I had this wrong initially and caught it before measuring.

## Tests

`tests/python/metaclass_base.py` + `MetaclassBaseTestCase` — 4 tests, expectations from **CPython 3.14.6**: the base is `type`, `type.__name__` is `'type'`, a metaclass is still an ordinary class carrying its methods, and an ordinary class is undisturbed. The fixture asserts only agreed behaviour and documents the `issubclass` gap in prose rather than pinning a wrong answer.

## Verification (tier 2 — codegen + a new class in the Python namespace)

- SUnit: **4575 run, 4575 passed, 0 failed, 0 errors**
- Full suite → `check_cpython_regressions.sh`: **0 regressions, 0 improvements**
- All three `scripts` gates locally: `check_python_fixtures.sh` (658 OK, 14 XFAIL), `test_regression_gate.sh`, `test_python_fixture_gate.sh`

## Next

Step 2 gives `PyType` the call protocol and binds the name (the two must land together). Step 3 routes the class statement through the metaclass and lets `type(A)` report it — `___pyMetaclass___` already documents that it declines to report a declared `metaclass=` only because `issubclass(Meta, type)` was false, which step 2 fixes.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: shreyanshverma7
body:
Three independent fixes. The first is the substantive one.

## 1. The two "significant" results were Type I errors

`database/build_zomato_db.py` draws `order_status`, `payment_method`,
`delivery_time_min` and `city` independently, so **the true effect in all four
chi-square tests is zero by construction**. Four tests at α=0.05 carry an 18.5%
family-wise error rate — and two came back under 0.05. The README asserted
*"Significant — UPI is really worse"* off p=0.019.

| Comparison | p | α=0.05 | Bonferroni 0.0125 |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Cancellation by city | 0.951 | not sig | not sig |
| Cancellation by payment method | 0.019 | sig | **not sig** ← reclassified |
| Conversion by platform | 0.800 | not sig | not sig |
| Reorder by delivery bucket | 0.009 | sig | sig (still a false positive) |

- Shared `significance_verdict()` / `render_significance_caption()` in
  `common.py`; every verdict site reports both thresholds.
- New README section documenting the ground truth, including the point that
  correction lowers the false-positive rate without eliminating it — the
  delivery-bucket result survives Bonferroni and is *still* false.
- Realism guardrail on the 41.7%-of-GMV headline: the ~29% cancel rate is a
  generator constant (5 `delivered` : 2 `cancelled`), and since amount is
  independent of status the ratio has an expected value of exactly
  (2/7)/(5/7) = **40%**. Real businesses run ~1–3%.

## 2. Generator wrote to the wrong path, so CI asserted nothing

`DB` was a bare relative path. Run as documented from the repo root, the
generator wrote a throwaway DB at the root and never touched
`database/zomato.db` — so every later CI step read the stale committed file and
the "deterministic seed" check was vacuous.

Anchored `DB` to the script dir, and replaced the regenerate step with a verify
step that builds into a temp dir and compares **logical dumps** (bytes aren't
comparable — SQLite page layout isn't deterministic). Confirmed it fails on a
seed change.

## 3. Sidebar accent was Streamlit's stock red

Streamlit 1.5x split the sidebar into its own theme namespace and it doesn't
inherit `[theme].primaryColor`. Affected the live demo too, since
`requirements.txt` had no upper bound.

## Currency

All 20 sites `$` → `₹`, matching the domain and the ₹120–1,200 order values.
`fmt_money` moved into `common.py` and reused instead of duplicated.

## Verification

CI-equivalent run green locally: db verify, 8 SQL files, compile, both analysis
scripts, `git diff --exit-code`. All 8 Streamlit pages execute with 0 exceptions
via `AppTest` (CI's curl check only proves HTTP 200). Screenshots refreshed.

author: forkwright
body:
## Summary

Two independently-verified-live defects, fixed together:

- **#111** (regression from #109, merged): `dependabot-auto-merge.yml`'s CI-check guard folded `kanon-lint` into a uniform `bucket == "pass"` loop. Since #109, `kanon-lint`'s job-level `if` reports GitHub's SKIPPED status whenever `FLEET_REPO_TOKEN` is absent from hosted runners -- true today and for the foreseeable future (#107, still open) -- so its bucket is permanently `"skipping"`, never `"pass"`. Every dependabot patch/dev-minor PR has been refusing auto-merge unconditionally since #109 landed.
- **#108**: `ARCHITECTURE/trait-impl-colocation` fires twice on `src/mailer.rs` (`Mailer` trait + `impl Mailer for SmtpMailer`/`StubMailer` in the same file).

## Live-defect confirmation (per the pre-work directive)

Both re-verified against `origin/main` before any edit, not assumed from the open issue alone:

- `.github/workflows/dependabot-auto-merge.yml:42` on `origin/main` (`eb7c843`) still reads `for check in Format Check Clippy Test kanon-lint "cargo deny" "cargo audit"; do` with no `"skipping"` allowance in the loop below it -- confirmed live, not already fixed.
- `kanon lint . --all` against the unmodified worktree reported exactly the two findings #108 cites, at `src/mailer.rs:92` and `src/mailer.rs:143`, exit code 1 -- confirmed live.

## Done-when checklist

**#111** "Done when: a dependabot patch/dev-minor PR auto-merges on green CI while kanon-lint shows skipping, and still refuses auto-merge if kanon-lint shows fail."

- `bucket == "skipping"` no longer blocks -- `.github/workflows/dependabot-auto-merge.yml:51-69` (`kanon-lint` pulled out of the pass-only loop, checked separately, blocks only on `bucket == "fail"`). Verified by the negative fixture below (scenario 1).
- `bucket == "fail"` still refuses -- same block, `if jq --exit-status 'any(.[]; .name == "kanon-lint" and .bucket == "fail")' ...; then exit 1; fi`. Verified by the negative fixture below (scenario 2).
- The fix does **not** simply restore accepting a fake pass: `kanon-lint`'s own job (`ci.yml:98-156`, from #109) is untouched -- it still fails-closed to SKIPPED rather than a fake green when the token is absent. Only the *consumer's* interpretation of that signal changed, and only for the one bucket (`"skipping"`) that carries no information about the code.

**#108** "Done when: `kanon lint . --all` reports 0 `ARCHITECTURE/trait-impl-colocation` findings in `src/mailer.rs`, or the two findings carry a suppression whose reason states the invariant that makes leaving them colocated safe."

- `kanon lint . --all` on the branch: `No open violations.` (verified below).
- Suppression added at `.kanon-lint-ignore:26-36`, mechanism per this repo's own convention (see the `RUST/pub-visibility` and `YAML/missing-concurrency` blocks already in that file). Reason states the invariant: `Mailer` falls under `ARCHITECTURE.md`'s own documented exception to `trait-impl-colocation` ("unless the trait is part of the public API contract ... or test mocking") -- `StubMailer` exists specifically so tests can substitute it for `SmtpMailer` without a live relay (`src/mailer.rs:19-32`, `106-110`), and is `pub` for exactly that reason. epistole is also a single `[package]` (`Cargo.toml` has no `[workspace]` table -- confirmed), so the rule's prescribed fix (move the trait to the lowest crate that calls through it) has no target crate to move to. A contrived workspace split solely to relocate one trait was rejected per the operating guidance not to force that shape onto a single-package service.

## Negative fixture (required line)

> Negative fixture: `.github/scripts/test-dependabot-auto-merge-checks.sh` -- watched failing by `bash .github/scripts/test-dependabot-auto-merge-checks.sh` run against the **unmodified `origin/main` copy** of `dependabot-auto-merge.yml` (same test script, only the workflow file swapped back to pre-fix), which produced:
> ```
> FAIL: kanon-lint skipping is treated as acceptable -- kanon-lint bucket='skipping': expected exit 0, got 1
> ok: kanon-lint fail still refuses auto-merge (kanon-lint=fail -> exit 1)
> ok: kanon-lint pass is unaffected (kanon-lint=pass -> exit 0)
> test-dependabot-auto-merge-checks: 1 case(s) failed
> ```
> before the fix (exit 1), and against this branch's workflow file:
> ```
> ok: kanon-lint skipping is treated as acceptable (kanon-lint=skipping -> exit 0)
> ok: kanon-lint fail still refuses auto-merge (kanon-lint=fail -> exit 1)
> ok: kanon-lint pass is unaffected (kanon-lint=pass -> exit 0)
> test-dependabot-auto-merge-checks: all cases passed
> ```
> passes after (exit 0).

The fixture runs the **shipped code**, not a copy: it extracts the literal `run: |` body of the "Wait for CI checks to pass" step directly out of `.github/workflows/dependabot-auto-merge.yml` (awk-based, dependency-free literal-block-scalar extraction -- no yq/PyYAML, so it runs unmodified on any hosted runner), stubs `gh pr checks` with synthetic JSON matching PR #109's own hosted-CI evidence (`kanon-lint\tskipping\t0`), and executes the extracted bash verbatim. It is not a re-implementation of the guard's logic; it is the guard's logic, mechanically pulled out of the YAML and run.

It exercises the defect, not its neighbourhood: scenario 1 is exactly the shape #111 reports (every other check `pass`, `kanon-lint` `skipping`) and the assertion (`expected exit 0`) is the exact thing the old code got wrong (it exited 1). A test that merely checked "the workflow file parses" or "the loop still runs" would not have caught this -- only asserting the actual exit code against the actual bucket value does.

Wired into CI so it runs every time: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`'s new `test-auto-merge-guard` job (checkout + `run: .github/scripts/test-dependabot-auto-merge-checks.sh`) runs this on every push/PR, so a future edit that reintroduces the #111 shape fails there before reaching a real dependabot PR.

For #108: `.kanon-lint-ignore`'s `unmatched_entries()` mechanism (`crates/basanos/src/engine/ignore.rs`) reports any suppression entry that matched nothing as a dead/inert suppression; ran `kanon lint . --all -v` after adding the entry and confirmed no such warning fires, and confirmed both violations moved from open (`kanon lint . --all` exit 1, 2 findings) to zero open violations (exit 0) purely via the new entry.

## Fix-checking-its-own-defect (per the review contract)

- **Error path**: N/A -- no new fallible operation introduced; the loop-and-conditional shape is unchanged, only which checks route through which branch.
- **Write path**: N/A -- no persisted state; this is a CI gate, not a data mutation.
- **Guard's own logic**: the new `if` block's condition is deliberately the *inverse* framing from the old loop (blocks on `bucket == "fail"` rather than requires `bucket == "pass"`) -- checked explicitly that this is not equivalent to "block on anything other than fail passing through as an implicit pass with no verification": every other required check (`Format Check Clippy Test "cargo deny" "cargo audit"`) is still checked via the original `bucket == "pass"` loop, unchanged, immediately above; only `kanon-lint`'s specific non-required status is re-scoped. The negative fixture's third scenario (`kanon-lint pass is unaffected`) confirms the ordinary case did not regress.

## Verification

- `kanon lint . --all` on the branch: `No open violations.` (exit 0; run at `/home/ck/dispatch-wt/epistole-cov-111`).
- `.github/scripts/test-dependabot-auto-merge-checks.sh`: all 3 cases pass (see fixture output above).
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: exit 0 (no Rust files touched by this PR; sanity check only).
- Not run locally: `cargo check`/`clippy`/`nextest` (no Rust source changed; CI's `check`/`clippy`/`nextest` jobs on this PR are the verification for those, unaffected by this change).

Closes #111

body:
## Summary

Adds the complete recipe for achieving **72.2 tok/s median (85.9 peak)** on isolated C1 with Qwen3.8-27B FP8 + DSpark speculative decoding on 2× Intel Arc Pro B70 (TP=2).

| Configuration | Median tok/s |
|---|---|
| FP8 no spec | 32.4 |
| FP8 + MTP2 | 54.67 |
| **FP8 + DFlash drafter (this recipe)** | **72.2** |

## Contents

- `vllm/patches/qwen38-dflash/`: patched vLLM dflash files (kernel readout fix), Dockerfile, serve script, README
- Kernel fix: SpecForge DSpark trains output j to predict token anchor+j+1 (LM-style); stock vLLM sampled offsets 1..k (BERT-style) — every draft off by one, capping acceptance at ~24%. Fix is 3 lines.
- Dockerfile builds `qwen38-fp8-dspark:v8` (also published at `ghcr.io/rmacy/qwen38-fp8-dspark:v8`)

## Published artifacts

- Drafter weights: [rwmacy/qwen3.8-27b-dflash-drafter-fp8-b70](https://huggingface.co/rwmacy/qwen3.8-27b-dflash-drafter-fp8-b70) (HF Hub)
- Serving image: `ghcr.io/rmacy/qwen38-fp8-dspark:v8`
- **vLLM fork with kernel fix: [rmacy/vllm](https://github.com/rmacy/vllm)** (main branch, based on vllm-project/vllm)
- SpecForge XPU training port: sgl-project/SpecForge#769

## Quality

Greedy spec decode is lossless by construction. Verified 4/5 byte-identical outputs vs target-only baseline; cross-checked against independent bf16 reference endpoint. Zero drafter-induced quality degradation.

body: ## Résumé Met en place un environnement de développement Cloud Agent complet pour le vrai projet (branche `feature/supabase-backend-refactor`) : app mobile **Flutter** avec backend dual **PostgreSQL local / Supabase**, y compris le **build d'APK Android**. Cette PR n'ajoute que de la configuration d'environnement + doc. Aucun code applicatif n'est modifié. ## Fichiers ajoutés - `.cursor/Dockerfile` — base `ghcr.io/cirruslabs/flutter:3.41.8` (Flutter 3.41.8 = version de `build-apk.yml`, Android SDK + licences + JDK), + PostgreSQL + Supabase CLI. - `.cursor/environment.json` — `install: flutter pub get`, `start: bash .cursor/start.sh`, port 5432. - `.cursor/start.sh` — démarre PostgreSQL et provisionne/seed `rh_manager` de façon idempotente. - `AGENTS.md` — instructions durables + pièges connus. ## Validé (dans l'image Docker construite) - Build de l'image OK (base + PostgreSQL 16.14 + Supabase CLI 2.114.0). - `install` : `flutter pub get` → `Got dependencies!` - `start` : schéma + seed appliqués, `rh_manager` prêt sur `localhost:5432`, 4 profils seedés (`admin@acme.com`, ...). ## Build APK (chaîne mobile) — testé en session `flutter build apk --debug` → `✓ Built build/app/outputs/flutter-apk/app-debug.apk` (173 Mo, APK Android valide). [apk_build_output.log](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-c820691c-8fdf-49bb-81a1-450b34d4dd4b/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fapk_build_output.log) ## Backend local — testé de bout en bout Authentification reproduisant `PostgreSQLService.signIn` (paquets `postgres` + `bcrypt`) : `admin@acme.com` / `admin123` vérifié, mauvais mot de passe rejeté. [local_backend_auth.log](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-c820691c-8fdf-49bb-81a1-450b34d4dd4b/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Flocal_backend_auth.log) ## Choix de version important Ne pas épingler un Flutter plus récent : le wrapper Gradle du projet est `8.11.1`, or Flutter ≥ 3.47 exige Gradle ≥ 8.14 (le build APK échoue). On reste sur **3.41.8**. ## Bugs de code préexistants (WIP, hors périmètre environnement) - `lib/services/supabase_service.dart` : `asin` appelé comme méthode sur `double` (devrait être `math.asin(...)`) et `RealtimeChannel.onPostgresChange` → `onPostgresChanges(..., callback: ...)`. Bloquent un `flutter build apk` propre en mode Supabase tant que non corrigés. - `test/widget_test.dart` : échoue dans `setUpAll` (`SharedPreferences` non mocké → `MissingPluginException`). ## Supabase online Le SDK/CLI sont prêts. Le mode `BackendMode.supabase` nécessite l'URL projet + clé anon (à fournir en Secrets). `supabase start` (stack locale complète) requiert Docker, non inclus dans l'image ; le dev local utilise le PostgreSQL ci-dessus. To show artifacts inline, enable in settings.

author: braden-seaborn
body:
Closes `STANDARDS.md` §10, which read "There is no formatter or linter configured. `rustfmt`, `clippy`, ESLint, and Prettier are phase 2." All four now run, plus a comment-density check and a structural report.

**Existing code is grandfathered, not refactored.** Every rule here was switched on against a codebase written without it, so all three checks are *ratchets*: they record what already exists and fail only when a count goes **up**. A new violation in an already-dirty file still fails, because counts are kept per file *and* per rule.

Read commit-by-commit — the two formatting commits are whitespace-only and are already listed in `.git-blame-ignore-revs`.

## What is enforced

Nothing new was invented. Every rule traces to a section of `STANDARDS.md` that was already written down as a convention nobody checked, so a failure cites a decision rather than a preference.

| Rule | Enforced by |
|---|---|
| §1.1 only `bindings.ts` may call Tauri | ESLint `no-restricted-imports` |
| §1.2 region isolation | ESLint, one config block per region |
| §1.4 apps reach the bridge via `@helve/bridge` | ESLint `no-restricted-imports` |
| §4.1 module doc comments | `missing_docs`, `crates/` only |
| §5 no `unwrap`/`expect` | `clippy::unwrap_used`, `expect_used` |
| §5 flat public re-exports | `unreachable_pub`, `crates/` only |
| §6.1 no `any` | `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any` |
| §6.3 `type` vs `interface` | `consistent-type-definitions` |
| §6.5 hooks own state | `react-hooks/rules-of-hooks` |
| comment concentration | `scripts/check-comments.mjs` |

## Commands

```sh
pnpm verify        # build -> test -> lint -> format:check   (33s) — the gate
pnpm verify:fast   # typecheck instead of build              (17s) — iterating only
pnpm lint          # ESLint + clippy + comment density
pnpm test          # 240 tests, both runners
pnpm format        # rustfmt + Prettier, applied
pnpm slop          # structural report — advisory, not part of the gate
pnpm baseline      # re-record all three baselines after a cleanup pass
```

## Baselines

| File | Holds |
|---|---|
| `eslint-suppressions.json` | 20 entries — ESLint's own bulk-suppression format |
| `clippy-baseline.json` | 298 warnings, per file and lint |
| `comment-baseline.json` | 105 files above the density caps |

`pnpm baseline` is for banking an improvement *after* a cleanup pass — never for making a failing check pass, since it would absorb the new violation along with everything else. Both `CLAUDE.md` and `README.md` say so explicitly.

## Decisions worth reviewing

These each reject an obvious alternative, and are the parts most worth a second opinion.

**`missing_docs` and `unreachable_pub` are scoped to `crates/*`, not workspace-wide.** Both describe a *published surface* — what another repository imports and must understand. `crates/helve-rpc` and `crates/helve-tool-manifest` have one; `src-tauri` does not, since its `pub` items exist to cross module boundaries inside a single binary. Workspace-wide they produced **1115 warnings, 816 of them `unreachable_pub` against `src-tauri` alone**. Scoped, the total is 298 and `unreachable_pub` finds 4 real cases. Cargo does not let a member inherit `[workspace.lints]` *and* add its own, so a crate-level attribute is the only way to have both.

**Rust is baselined by count, not by `#![allow]` per file**, which is the usual Rust answer. A file-level allow is permanent and unbounded — it hides the twelve `expect()` calls that exist today *and* the thirteenth added tomorrow. It also means editing twenty source files, and the point of this PR is not to touch existing code.

**`src/shell/hostWindow.ts` is deliberately not exempted from §1.1** even though it calls the Tauri API today. §1.1 names exactly one door and `hostWindow` is a second one. An exemption would quietly ratify that; leaving it in the suppressions file keeps it visible as a decision someone still has to make — fold it into `bindings.ts`, or amend §1.1.

**The comment check applies two caps, and both are needed.** More than 50% comment lines, or an unbroken run of more than 20. `src-tauri/src/apps/files.rs` is only **32%** comment and still reads as overwhelming, because its 610 comment lines arrive in blocks of up to 35 — ratio alone does not see that. The run cap is calibrated rather than picked: among files over any cap the median run is 28 and the longest 85, so a cap of 15 would have flagged 116 of 168 files.

**`agent-slop-lint` is deliberately outside `pnpm lint`.** Its best output is a ranked list of churn-vs-complexity hotspots, which is a thing to read rather than fail a build on, and it would put a `pip` dependency in the build gate. Run it with `pnpm slop`.

**typescript-eslint's `recommended`/type-checked tiers and clippy's `pedantic` group are left off.** Both are worth having and both are a much larger baseline than the documented rules. Mixing "agreed in writing" with "suggested by the ecosystem" in one pass makes neither reviewable. `eslint.config.js` names the line to uncomment.

## Two problems found along the way

**`core.autocrlf=true` with no `.gitattributes`.** Both formatters write LF unconditionally while git checked source out as CRLF, so `prettier --check` reported 52 files as unformatted *immediately after* `prettier --write` succeeded — it was reading back the CRLF git had restored. A format check that cannot pass on freshly formatted code is worse than none, so the working tree is now pinned to LF.

**HTML is excluded from Prettier**, and not as a style preference. Whitespace between inline elements is significant in HTML, so reformatting it is not the guaranteed no-op it is in TypeScript or CSS. Prettier rewrote **4540 lines** of `docs/handoffs/shell-spec.html`, a standalone design artifact nobody edits by hand, before this was caught.

## Also in this branch

Two things that are not linting, included because they were done alongside it:

- **The fake backend is removed** (`0801e71`, −3930 lines). `src/shell/state/fakeBackend.ts` was a second implementation of the whole Rust backend for `?fake=1`, branched on at 103 call sites across ten modules. It is going to be replaced by something that runs against the real software. There is now no way to run the shell without a Tauri backend under it, and `CLAUDE.md` says so plainly. It also resolved a genuine import cycle with `state/shellState.ts`.
- **All tests are now a stated gate** for every commit and PR, with `pnpm test` and `pnpm verify` added to make that one command.

`STANDARDS.md` §8 was corrected in the process. It claimed `shell_state.rs` "is 2100 lines and has none" and that "what has nothing is `src-tauri/src/`". There are in fact **183 tests under `src-tauri` alone** — 35 in `shell_state.rs`, 32 in `layout.rs`, 11 in `shell_store.rs` — and 240 across the repo. The aspiration was met at some point and the text was never updated.

§1.2 also said "the six shell regions" when there are now **sixteen**. All sixteen are encoded in `eslint.config.js`, and that list needs extending by hand when a directory is added under `src/shell/`.

## Remaining debt, all grandfathered

| | Count |
|---|---|
| ESLint findings | 43 |
| clippy warnings | 298 |
| Files over comment caps | 105 |
| `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` warnings | 8 (visible, not baselined) |

## Verification

`pnpm verify` passes end to end: `pnpm build`, 240 tests, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`.

There is no CI workflow yet — `docs/open-source-plan.md` phase 3 — so this is currently on whoever opens the PR. That is why it is one command.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: mtweiden
body:
Fixes #5.

- **Clifford+T** (@stevenhofmeyr's fix, cherry-picked as-is from
  `cap-pass1-prefix-sweep`): `build_ma_prefix_set_inner` built the full
  undeduplicated even+odd candidate set (`1.5 * 2^t' * 24` `U2T`s, ~79 GB
  transient at `T_PRIME_CAP`) before deduplicating. Dedup now runs inline as
  each candidate is generated, in the same first-occurrence-wins order, so
  the resulting set is identical. Verified by Steve against the
  `compile_cliffordt` 121-qubit repro from the issue: previously OOM-killed,
  now completes in ~26 s.
- **Clifford+sqrt(T)**: `build_fgkm_prefix_set_inner` had the same shape —
  all FGKM bodies materialized, then the full body x Clifford set
  (`9 * 6^(m-1) * 24` `U2Q`s, ~1 KB each; ~1.7 GB at m=6) before dedup.
  `enumerate_bodies` now feeds a sink closure and dedup runs inline in the
  same DFS x Clifford order. Identical output (`fgkm_prefix_set_size_growth`
  pins the per-m set sizes). 

Deliberately excludes the performance-experiment and instrumentation commits
on `cap-pass1-prefix-sweep`.

Closes #1529

`update_settings` committed a new `embedding_model` and only then awaited the provider probe that discovers that model's width. For the length of that network call the committed pair was the new model beside the OLD model's dimension count. It was committed and it was stable, so re-reading it agreed with itself and told the reader nothing.

Both mechanism claims in the issue were verified against the tree before anything was designed, and the line numbers were still accurate (model committed at `router.py:337-338`, probe awaited at `347-352`).

## What changed

The probe runs before anything is staged, against the model the request is asking to publish, and its result joins the same `validated_settings` batch. Model and width land in one `db.commit()`, so a reader sees the old pair or the new pair and nothing between them. A failed probe publishes neither half.

`probe_embedding_dimensions` resolves the model from PersistentConfig, so it can only probe a model that is already published, which is the ordering under repair. The router asks the provider extension about a named model instead: the same call `POST /settings/detect-embedding-dims` makes, with the model supplied rather than read back out.

Failure mapping matches that sibling endpoint. No provider configured is a 422 whose message names the escape hatch (send `embedding_dims` alongside `embedding_model` and the probe is skipped entirely); any other provider failure is a 502. Both are raised before the first write, so the previous configuration is untouched.

## Decision: auto-detect rebuilds the column too

**It rebuilds.** Persisting a width the vector column does not have is the same bug one layer down, and there were only two ways out: rebuild the column, or stop persisting the width. Not persisting it is not an option, because readers then fall back to the provider's `default_dims`, which is a different number for a different provider. That is the same mismatch, just implicit and harder to see.

The implementation is the absence of a special case. The detected width goes into `validated_settings` before the apply loop, so it reaches the existing `if "embedding_dims" in validated_settings` rebuild exactly as a typed one does. Auto-detect and explicit-dims were mutually exclusive branches; now there is one path.

What this costs: switching models now deletes existing embeddings whenever the width actually changes, because that is what `rebuild_embedding_column` does. That was already true for an explicitly named width, and those vectors were unusable anyway. They are the old model's, at a width the column no longer has, and search filters on the active model. When the width does not change (a 1536 model swapped for another 1536 model) the rebuild is a no-op and nothing is deleted.

Two things follow from routing auto-detect through the rebuild:

- **The rollback restores both halves.** The existing path rolled back `embedding_dims` alone. A request that publishes model and width together and then hits a DDL failure would be left with the new model beside the old width, which is the mismatched pair reached through the failure path instead of the probe window. Both halves are now restored in one transaction, with side effects applied after the commit rather than before it (fix #430 codex r3: invalidating the cache first lets a concurrent reader repopulate it with the value being rolled back). A dims-only request still rolls back dims only.
- **The probe fires on a changed model, not a present one.** The old code probed whenever `embedding_model` appeared in the request body. Now that a probe failure is fatal, probing on presence would turn any save that re-sends the current model into a 502 whenever the provider is unreachable. It would also keep overwriting a width the admin set on purpose. The AI settings tab sends only dirty fields, but an API or CLI caller can PUT the whole tab. The comparison reads `get_uncached`, because a stale cache entry naming the requested model would skip the probe and publish that model unprobed.

The detected width is run through `_canonicalize_setting_value` like any admin-supplied one. It becomes the `vector(N)` the column is rebuilt to, so "whatever the provider answered" is not an acceptable source for it; out of the [1, 4096] range the request is rejected whole.

## Second commit: the endpoint is part of the published configuration

Review found that the probe resolved its endpoint through `resolve_runtime_config(db)`, which reads committed configuration. Nothing in the batch is staged when the probe runs, so a PUT changing the base URL and the model together resolved the URL it was replacing. Publishing the model atomically with its width was only half of it; the width has to describe the endpoint being published too.

I drove all three cases through the endpoint before changing anything, because the impact turned out to be different from what it looked like:

| case | result |
|---|---|
| requested URL != operator-approved, credential present | **422** at validation, `provider.calls == []`, nothing published |
| requested URL == operator-approved | 200, probe called the approved URL, which is also the committed one |
| no credential | **422** from the probe's own guard, `provider.calls == []` |

`bind_openai_credential_base_url` binds the destination to the environment credential, so while `OPENAI_API_KEY` is set any DB base URL that differs from `operator_openai_base_url(purpose="embedding")` is rejected in pass-1, before the probe. The probe therefore cannot reach the replaced endpoint, and a width from one endpoint cannot be published beside another. Without a credential the URLs can diverge, but the probe refuses before reading any runtime config.

What binding does not cover is a **stale row staged while no credential existed**. Repairing that row and switching model in one request made `resolve_runtime_config` raise on the value under repair, and the repair came back 502 without reaching a provider at all:

```
status=502
detail=Embedding probe for model 'stale-row-model-b' failed: The environment-provided
       OpenAI-compatible credential is bound to the operator-approved EMBEDDING_BASE_URL...
provider.calls=[]
url now='https://stale-staged.example.com/v1'    <- repair refused
```

`_probe_base_url` now takes the endpoint from the validated batch when the request names either URL key, reproducing the provider's own chain with each half taken from the request where present (`EMBEDDING_BASE_URL`, then `OPENAI_BASE_URL`, then bound to the approved destination). Clearing `embedding_base_url` in the same PUT falls through to the `openai_base_url` that PUT sets, exactly as it will once the batch commits. A request naming neither URL still goes through `resolve_runtime_config` unchanged.

Red on the repair flow: `assert 502 == 200`. Green after, with the probe reaching the requested endpoint and its width published. Two stub endpoints answer at different widths (768 vs 1536) so the width identifies which one replied, and the stub delegates `resolve_runtime_config` to the real provider, since the committed-config read is the thing under test. `test_a_url_free_request_still_resolves_the_committed_endpoint` is the counterfactual for the other branch and passes on both trees.

The `model` argument also loses its fallback to the runtime default. This path only runs when the request names `embedding_model`, and the community provider's `default_model` *is* the committed `EMBEDDING_MODEL`, so the fallback could only ever name the model being replaced.

## Relationship to #1519

#1519 (closing #1511) mitigated this bug from the consumer side, and the two are complementary rather than overlapping. `_preflight_embedding` in `backfill.py` generates one real vector with the pinned pair before the DELETE, so a mismatched pair makes the provider reject and nothing is deleted; it then reads `atttypmod` off the live column and refuses when the generate

author: itshabib
body:
## The problem (recorded friction #7)

`ship#247` was mergeable, but branch protection rejected the pinned command gate
emitted — that repo requires the head to be up to date with base. Only after the
rejection was main merged in, CI re-run, and gate re-run. Gate emitted a command
GitHub was always going to reject.

## The approach

A new deterministic rung on the ladder, upstream of the command:

- **Evidence** (`cmd/gate/internal/evidence/protection.go`) records the base
  branch's up-to-date requirement as an artifact: classic branch protection's
  `required_status_checks.strict`, falling back to a ruleset's
  `strict_required_status_checks_policy`. Both shapes are live in the portfolio —
  workbench's own `main` is unprotected classically yet carries rulesets — so
  reading only the protection endpoint would report "no protection" on a repo
  that has it (#229 documented these shapes; this implements the read).
- **Verifier** (`cmd/gate/internal/verify/uptodate.go`) blocks a `BEHIND` head
  only when the recorded setting is strict, with a verdict that prescribes the
  fix: refresh from base, let CI re-run, gate again (the judgment binds to the
  head it was made against).

### The subtlety

BEHIND alone is **not** a refresh requirement. Most portfolio bases are
unprotected or non-strict, so a rung keyed off BEHIND would add a pointless CI
cycle to nearly every merge. Detection keys off the repo's actual setting.
Conflicts remain readiness's block (`CONFLICTING`); `BLOCKED`/`DIRTY`/`UNSTABLE`
remain other rungs' business, so nothing double-blocks.

### Degradation

A protection read can fail for reasons that are not "no protection" — a token
without admin scope, a transport failure. Those record `readable: false` with the
reason and the rung **passes**, carrying the degradation in its verdict text. An
unread fact is not evidence and must never stop a merge. A 404 on the protection
endpoint is GitHub's "not protected" answer, not a failed read, and falls through
to the ruleset check. Malformed evidence, by contrast, is schema drift and errors
rather than hiding in the degraded path.

## Verification

- `go build ./...` and `go test ./cmd/gate/...` green; `gofmt`, `go vet`,
  `golangci-lint run ./cmd/gate/...` clean.
- New tests cover: every protection shape (strict/non-strict classic, strict/
  non-strict ruleset, unprotected, no required checks); every unreadable path
  (403 on either endpoint, missing `strict` field, non-JSON bodies, no base ref);
  BEHIND+strict blocks with the prescription; BEHIND without a strict
  requirement passes; a current head on a strict base passes; other merge states
  are ignored; unreadable and absent protection evidence both degrade to pass;
  merged subjects are exempt (backtest); verdict shape (T0, code class, both
  evidence artifacts as parents); malformed evidence errors.
- Docs: the constraint is recorded in `cmd/gate/CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md` (kept
  byte-identical) and cross-referenced from the protection-shapes table in
  `docs/auto-mode-defaults.md`.

- Registering package: LatticeMatrices
- Repository: https://github.com/cometscome/LatticeMatrices.jl
- Created by: @cometscome
- Version: v1.1.0
- Commit: f55308ecce01cbbca2a47b65b96c2d6b1ce35e66
- Reviewed by: @cometscome
- Reference: https://github.com/cometscome/LatticeMatrices.jl/issues/52
- Description: High-performance matrix fields on arbitrary D-dimensional lattices in Julia.
- Release notes:
<!-- BEGIN RELEASE NOTES -->
`````
LatticeMatrices.jl v1.1.0

# Breaking changes

## Measurement building blocks

set_global_component! sets one matrix component using global lattice coordinates. Under MPI, only the rank that owns the site writes it; the same site-local JACC kernel works on CPU and accelerator backends.
projected_bilinear_slices contracts spin-color propagators into hyperplane slices, with optional Fourier-momentum and staggered-parity projections, and performs the final global MPI reduction. QCDMeasurements.jl uses these primitives for generalized connected-meson two-point measurements.
Stable SU(2)/SU(3) exponential pullbacks

exp_ta_pullback!(output, cotangent, A, t=1) is a new public pullback for exp(t * TA(A)), restricted to traceless anti-Hermitian variations. SU(2) and SU(3) use site-local JACC kernels shared by CPU and GPU execution.
The active Enzyme reverse rule for expt_TA! now calls these core kernels. In particular, the SU(3) coefficient derivatives are analytic rather than finite-difference estimates.
The SU(3) implementation follows the analytic Cayley--Hamilton coefficients and derivatives of [Morningstar--Peardon](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-lat/0311018), including the reflection relations for negative cubic invariant. Stable series are used near the origin and near degenerate eigenvalues.
`````

author: hndrewaall
body:
## Problem (Andrew #4379)

`~/.config/session/` grows unbounded — `queue-logs/` reached ~2500 per-item
transcript archives, `completed-tasks.jsonl` is multi-MB (and grows further
after the 2026-08-16 recovery backfill). Nothing rotated or archived either;
this bloats the session store and enlarged the queue.json corruption incident.

## What this adds: `session-task queue rotate`

```
session-task queue rotate                  # apply defaults
session-task queue rotate --dry-run --json # preview, mutate nothing
```

1. **queue-logs prune** — deletes transcript archives (files OR dirs) older than
   `--queue-logs-max-age` days (default 30), then enforces a hard
   `--queue-logs-max-count` floor (default 500), oldest-by-mtime first. Recent
   transcripts stay so the q-site "View log" affordance keeps working.
2. **completed-tasks roll** — once the live file exceeds `--completed-max-mb`
   (default 5 MB), the oldest rows move into a dated
   `completed-archive/completed-tasks-<UTC>.jsonl.gz` segment; the most-recent
   `--completed-retain` lines (default 2000) stay in the **live** file. Gz
   segments are themselves capped (default 20).

## q-site DONE-view coordination (#581)

The DONE view reads the **live** `completed-tasks.jsonl`. Rotation deliberately
keeps the recent tail *in that live file*, so a roll never hides recent done
items from the view — **no minisite change required**. Deep history lives in the
gz segments. (Covered by `test_done_view_sees_recent_after_roll`.)

## Safety (reuses #580 atomic-write/lock patterns)

- The roll holds the same new `fcntl.flock` (`completed-tasks.jsonl.lock`) that
  the append path (`log_completed`) now takes — a concurrent `queue done` /
  `complete` can't be lost in the read→rewrite window.
- The gz segment is written (temp + `os.replace`) **before** the live file is
  truncated: a crash leaves a benign superset, never a gap.
- The live-file rewrite is atomic (`_atomic_write_text`).
- Every threshold is overridable via `ROTATE_*` env var + CLI flag; malformed
  env values fall back to defaults (never crash the maintenance tick).

## Scheduling — cron-producer, not a watcher

Per the repo's watcher-vs-producer guidance, this is a daily cron job, not an
always-on watcher: job-name `session-rotate` in `container/cron.d/cw-default`
(04:17 daily, guarded by `cw-cron-run`, toggle via
`cw-cron-toggle disable|enable session-rotate`). A commented equivalent row
ships in `cron.d/cw-host` for host/systemd deploys. `docs/cron-toggle.md` job
table updated.

## Tests

15 new cases in `tools/session-task/tests/test_queue_rotate.py`: age + count
prune (incl. dirs), roll archive integrity (gz round-trip, oldest→archive /
newest→live, no gap/dupe), no-op below threshold, idempotency, archive cap,
DONE-view-sees-recent, env/CLI override precedence, malformed-env fallback,
dry-run mutates nothing, append-not-lost. Full session-task suite green
(**334 passed**).

Draft — not deployed.

author: pitayazero
body:
## Contexto

O white-label só trocava `--primary`. Superfícies, bordas, texto e sidebar vinham de hex fixos de ardósia, escolhidos por um `data-app-theme` que classificava o matiz da marca em **dois baldes** (`verde` | `azul`, com verde de fallback). Uma instituição vermelha ou roxa recebia fundo esverdeado e sidebar verde-escura.

## O que muda

**Tema claro e escuro derivados da marca.** Todo neutro passa a sair de `color-mix` entre um âncora neutro e `--primary` (claro) ou `--dark-background-color` (escuro). `data-app-theme` foi removido.

**Modo escuro:**
- neutros derivados do fundo escuro do tenant, não de ardósia azul;
- elevação sobe clareando — `surface-2` era idêntico ao fundo da página e toda superfície sutil sumia;
- `applyDarkOverrideToRoot` recebe o par (`dark_primary`, `dark_background`) e devolve os tokens interativos. O interativo é a **própria cor escolhida** pelo admin, clareada só até passar de 3:1 contra o fundo — antes o valor vinha do stop-500 recalculado e o botão saía diferente do color picker;
- `disabled` e `tint` misturam com o fundo escuro, não com branco (a fórmula do modo claro produzia o elemento mais brilhante da tela);
- `applyEffectiveInteractive` grava os tokens do modo ativo **inline**: `applyPaletteToRoot` também escreve inline, e inline vence o bloco `:root[data-theme="dark"]` — sem isso o escuro herdava as cores interativas do claro;
- cores de estado passam aos stops 400, legíveis sobre fundo escuro;
- fundo escuro padrão `#0f172a` → `#0d1a14`, alinhado à marca padrão (backend, schemas e CSS juntos).

**Migração `20260804_1000_temas_dark_e_presets.sql`** — idempotente: dedup + unique em `tema_presets.nome`, UPSERT de 16 presets (a carga original vivia em `database/`, que o runner não enxerga, então banco novo abria a tela de tema sem preset nenhum) e correção do fundo escuro **apenas** de quem ainda está no trio padrão intocado.

**Ícones.** `IconComponent`: SVG 24×24 com `stroke: currentColor`, que herda a cor do tema, escala com o token de tipografia e não muda de desenho por sistema operacional nem vira texto no leitor de tela. Substitui os emojis da UI.

## Dois bugs encontrados e corrigidos no caminho

- **Botão de tema invisível** (`03e2820`): `.btn-dark-toggle` é estilizado para fundo escuro, mas na `.sidebar-topbar` fica sobre `--color-surface` — branco sobre branco no modo claro, 1:1 de contraste. Agora veste os tokens da superfície: 11,7:1 no claro, 13,1:1 no escuro.
- **Ícones de menu que nunca renderizaram** (`970c0ec`): os SVGs de navegação eram strings em `[innerHTML]`, e o sanitizador do Angular não tem `svg`/`path`/`rect` na allowlist — apagava tudo e sobrava contêiner vazio. Eram 13 ícones invisíveis por página, incluindo os chips de ação rápida do dashboard do aluno, que apareciam como círculos coloridos vazios. Migrados para o `IconComponent`.

## Verificação

- `pytest`: 119 passed.
- `npm run build`: exit 0 (só os avisos de budget de CSS que já existiam).
- Migração aplicada em dev; checksum bate com o arquivo. `tema_presets` com 16 linhas, `/api/faculdades/presets` devolvendo as 16. Faculdade com `dark_primary` customizado corretamente não tocada pelo `UPDATE`.
- Dev server, faculdade de marca **laranja** (o caso que antes saía verde), medindo cor computada: texto em card 12,8:1 no claro e 11,2:1 no escuro; sidebar ativa 6,1:1 e 12,7:1; `--color-interactive` no escuro é o `dark_primary` do tenant, não o do claro.
- Três áreas (`/aluno`, `/instituicao`, `/admin`): 0 contêineres de ícone sem SVG, 7/7, 8/8 e 12/12 itens de menu com glifo.
- Após rebase sobre a `main`: rota `/admin/tema` do PR #11 carrega, com o item de menu usando o ícone `palette`.

author: vahid-sohrabloo
body:
Closes the last "—" in the search availability matrix #23 just published: the composable Query API was unreachable from the Python client.

## Why

Recommend and discover have **no standalone route on any transport** — they are leaves of `/query`. So a Python user who wanted either had to hand-assemble the request body. Everything else in the search matrix had a Python method; these two did not.

## What

Three methods, mirroring the `filters` module's split (typed helpers for common cases, general form underneath):

- `recommend(collection, positive, k, *, negative=None, strategy="", filter=None)`
- `discover(collection, context, k, *, target=None, target_vec=None, filter=None)`
- `query(collection, prefetch, *, root=None, mode, method, alpha, rrf_k, k, group_by, group_size)` — multi-lane fusion or rerank; returns `Group`s when `group_by` is set.

## The wire detail a fake wouldn't have caught

recommend/discover must be **prefetch** leaves, each with its own `k` — not a bare `root`. Fusion mode rejects a spec with no prefetch: `query spec has no prefetch leaves`. My first cut put them in `root` and got a 500. The helpers set both the leaf `k` and the top-level `k`. **Found by running it against a live server, not by reading the handler.**

## Testing

Cross-stack against a real `rostam-server` (`test_cross_stack_query.py`), because ranking is the whole value and no fake is worth trusting for it. Two well-separated clusters make "did it retrieve the right region" unambiguous:

- recommend pulls toward the positive cluster and honours a metadata filter
- the negative example pushes the top hit away
- discover explores the positive region
- `query([])` raises client-side

One assertion the test writes down explicitly: recommend's result is "the one remaining same-cluster point ranks first", **not** "a majority is same-cluster" — the example ids are excluded from their own results, so with a 3-member cluster and 2 examples a majority is impossible. (My first assertion got this wrong; the run corrected it.)

Full Python suite: **71 passed, 26 skipped**, including under the exact CI invocation (`pytest tests` from `clients/python` with `ROSTAM_SERVER_BIN` set).

## Note

This is part of v0.3.0; its changelog entry slots under the existing v0.3.0 section. Independent of #24 (the HNSW-default fix) — they touch different layers.

author: nickderobertis
body:
## What

Make Nx cache keys reflect the files each command actually reads, so unrelated build, test, and typecheck work replays from cache while workspace-wide lint changes invalidate correctly. Keep browser and prerender work explicitly uncacheable, with composed-artifact consumers ordered behind prerender, and add regression coverage for the resulting execution behavior.

## Why

Shared cache inputs made small changes unnecessarily expensive: a one-line app edit spent 44 seconds on discarded build cache, while a Biome rule change cost 2m32s across projects that never read it. The previous ESLint keying could also report green for rules and files it never re-read.

## Additional info

The `tooling-publish:test` shallow-checkout range failure is pre-existing rather than caused by this change: this diff does not touch the publish-lanes implementation or spec, and the corresponding `master` run at the same base commit was green.

author: laurenceday
body:
## What changed

- Added `ProRataCollateralDistributor`, one market and one collateral asset per instance.
- Added `IProRataCollateralDistributor` with proposal, finalisation, claim and dust-sweep events.
- Added tests for constructor checks, proposal validation, cancellation, finalisation timing, underfunded finalisation, bad proofs, double claims, pro-rata payouts and dust.
- Updated the pro-rata snapshot docs so they match the hardened contract.

## Shape

The snapshot authority proposes `market`, `snapshotBlock`, `totalScaledDebt`, `collateralAmount`,
`merkleRoot`, `evidenceHash` and `reviewEndsAt`. After the review delay, the same authority can
finalise only if the distributor holds at least the committed collateral amount.

Claims use `floor(totalCollateral * scaledDebt / totalScaledDebt)`. Dust can move only after every
scaled-debt unit in the root has claimed.

## Audit

Round 1 found and fixed two issues:

- public finalisation could freeze an underfunded balance and push later collateral into dust;
- public finalisation could race an authority cancellation at the review deadline.

The fix commits the expected collateral amount in the proposal, makes finalisation authority-only,
checks funding before finalisation, and freezes `totalCollateral` from the committed amount.

## Validation

- `forge test --match-contract ProRataCollateralDistributorTest --summary`
- `forge test --summary`
- `git diff --check`
- `hexaemeron:imprimatur` on touched docs and audit log: 100/100

Stacks on #6. Tracks #5.

author: brandondees
body:
## Summary

Owner's request after the `auditing-dependencies-and-supply-chain` merge: try running evals through `llama-server`/vllm/llama.cpp instead of Ollama (hypothesis: faster, less flaky), and try LiquidAI's LFM2.5-2.6B as a lower-resource floor-of-record candidate. This PR documents a deliberately small first look — no repo mechanics (skills, harness, manifest) changed.

- Ran the same 3-scenario suite (`reviewing-api-contract-safety`) once each via: llama-server + `qwen2.5-coder-7b` (same-model control), Ollama + `qwen2.5-coder:7b`, and llama-server + `LFM2.5-2.6B-Q4_K_M`.
- **llama-server ran ~33% faster than Ollama on the identical model** (2m40s vs 3m58s) — directional, one run of a small suite, not the repeated full-suite evidence this repo's re-gate discipline requires before calling it the new default.
- **LFM2.5-2.6B was the slowest of the three**, despite roughly a third of qwen's parameters. Per-token throughput (from llama-server's own slot timing) was actually faster for LFM2.5 — the wall-clock loss came from writing ~2x as many words per answer, in a more markdown-heavy style than this repo's established terse convention.
- **Quality on the same 3 scenarios: qwen 3/3, LFM2.5 2/3** — it missed the unbounded-collection/pagination finding on scenario 2. Too small a sample to call a verdict.
- vllm: not attempted in this session.

Full writeup, including the per-token throughput caveat (qwen's comparison figures came from a log file shared with other test runs, not a clean isolated measurement) and the untried next steps, is in the session-log entry.

## Changes

- `docs/session-log.md` — new dated entry with the full methodology, numbers, and scoped disposition.
- `docs/runbooks/regenerating-skills.md` — two short pointers appended to the existing llama-server fallback section, linking back to the session-log entry.

author: withoz
body:
트랙 E 격자에서 나온 후속. `slice_volume_by_plane` 의 `self.face_to_xia.remove(&fid)` 를 **지워도 아무것도 실패하지 않는다**는 실측이 있었고, 그게 "이 줄이 불필요하다"는 뜻인지가 질문이었습니다.

답은 한 가지 성질에 달려 있습니다: **FaceId 가 재사용되는가.**

## 재사용되지 않습니다

`SlotStorage::insert` 는 단조 증가하는 `next_id` 를 읽고 증가시키며, `remove` 는 map 항목만 지웁니다. 실측 — id 6개를 쓰고 지운 뒤 박스를 3개 더 지었더니 새 면은 **6번부터** 시작합니다.

```
SPENT [FaceId(0), FaceId(1), FaceId(2)] … LATER [FaceId(6), FaceId(7), FaceId(8)]
```

변이 검증: `insert` 를 **가장 낮은 빈 슬롯을 재사용**하도록(진짜 slotmap 의 모양) 바꾸면 이 테스트가 실패합니다.

## 따라서

낡은 역인덱스 항목은 **다른 면에 대해 조회될 수 없습니다.** 그 줄은 정합성을 떠받치는 것이 아니라 **map 의 크기**를 묶습니다 — 소비된 면당 항목 하나, 그 경로에서는 달리 정리되지 않음. 이제 그 내용이 **줄 자체에 적혀** 있어, 다음 사람이 "이 줄을 지웠을 때 잡아 줄 가드"를 찾느라 오후를 쓰지 않아도 됩니다.

## ⚠ 없는 것: 두 번째 테스트

정리 없이 **실패하는** 테스트를 네 번 시도했고 **네 번 다 통과**했습니다 — id 재사용 변이를 동시에 켠 상태에서도요(그 항목이 조회될 수 있는 유일한 상황). "인덱스는 살아있는 면에만 답한다"도, "인덱스와 소유자 목록이 일치한다"도 두 변이 아래에서 통과했습니다.

파일에 두 번째 테스트가 없는 이유는 **지킬 것이 측정되지 않기 때문**이고, 실패할 수 없는 검사는 이 저장소가 반복해서 당해 온 무의미한 가드입니다 — 두 커밋 전 소유권 격자에서 역인덱스 측정을 뺀 것과 같은 이유입니다.

author: vixygrey
body:
Closes #94.

Documentation only — no shipped behaviour changes.

## Why

CLAUDE.md's *Lessons learned* exists because the reasoning is the durable artifact, not the fix.
Both of these cost real time in #92 and would cost it again.

## 1. A public field is not a supported setter if something caches what it derives

`PowerEntry.Attribute` and `.Minimum` are public and writable, so retuning a skill requirement at
runtime looks trivial. But `MeetsAttributeMinimum` gates on a **cached** `_requirements` list,
`InitRequirements()` returns early rather than rebuilding, and the cache is private — reaching it
would need reflection, which rule 5 forbids. Once anything has rendered or checked that power, the
write is inert **with no error**.

This is why #91 shipped as two options rather than one, and why the requirements half is
restart-scoped: **the scopes are a property of the game, not a design choice.** Stated generally,
because the next option built on writing a public field faces the same question — find who *reads*
the field before assuming the write is live.

Same silent-failure family as an orphaned `Load="Merge"` and a missing `[PlayerMutator]`, both
already in that section.

## 2. Read the IL when the metadata and the XML docs run out

Two existing lessons say to check `Assembly-CSharp.xml` for documentation and the metadata reader
for structure. Neither answers *"does this method rebuild, append, or return early"* — the question
that decided the design above. This adds the third step: method bodies, no decompiler needed, since
the metadata reader already yields each method's RVA.

Records the header format and token encoding, and — more importantly — that a **token-only scan of
`InitRequirements` gave the answer backwards**, showing `ldfld` → `newobj` → `stfld` and reading as
a clean rebuild because it had dropped the branch between them. A technique that produces a
confident wrong answer is worth documenting more than one that fails loudly.

## 3. GitHub does not re-run pull request checks on a retitle

#92 fixed this in `ci.yml` but explained it only in the changelog. The general form belongs in the
lessons: a check that reads the event payload must listen for the event that changes that payload,
or it is unfixable by the very action it demands.

## 4. In-game verification, dated

`docs/FEATURES.md` §13 now records that all eleven options are verified working on current Qud,
next to the note that the mod's C# has **no compile gate** — CodeQL cannot cover it and there is no
C# toolchain on the authoring machine, so in-game testing is the only evidence the scripting works
at all. Worth dating rather than assuming, and it follows the `✅ Verified 2026-08-15` precedent in
charter rule 1.

## Compatibility

None — `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/FEATURES.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` only. Nothing under `mod/` is touched, so
nothing reaches subscribers.

## Note on overlap

`docs/stale-artifact-table-claims` is in flight against `docs/FEATURES.md` §0/§7.2/§7.3/§10 and
CLAUDE.md's priorities, charter rule 1 and conventions bullet. This PR touches only CLAUDE.md's
*Lessons learned* section and FEATURES §13, so the two should not collide. Whichever lands second
should still be checked.

- [x] `python3 tools/validate_mod.py` — no new violations
- [x] `typos`
- [x] Committed with explicit paths rather than `git add -A`, since a background agent's git
      worktree is currently sitting untracked at `.claude/worktrees/` (see #98)
