author: aprilnea
body:
`virt/arcbox-vm-driver` is the VM driver port: the vocabulary of "a VM on this host" — the serializable `VmSpec` family, the object-safe `VmDriver`/`VmHandle` traits, the capability traits, and the `net::GuestNetwork` port — that VMM adapters (Firecracker, VZ, the in-process HV engine, later Cloud Hypervisor) implement and orchestrators consume. No `arcbox-*` dependency; it sits below every adapter.

**Mandatory handle surface vs capabilities.** A handle must only identify (`id`/`record`), observe (`state`/`events`, never blocking; `Exited` broadcast once) and stop (`shutdown`: `Kill` always succeeds, `Graceful{timeout}` falls back to kill; Drop kills unless detached). Everything else is an `Option<&dyn Cap>` accessor — `Vsock`, `VsockListen`, `Checkpoint` (quiescing is its own business: `Resume`/`HoldQuiesced`; there is no pause verb on the handle), `Adopt`/`Detach`, `Prepare`/`PreparedVm` (spawn the VMM ahead of a boot: pid journaled, READY listener bound before the guest starts; `boot` is exactly prepare-then-boot), `Balloon`, `Console`, `DebugSnapshot` — and `capabilities()` must agree with the accessors. There is no `Unsupported` error variant.

**testkit** (feature): `FakeDriver` (real state machine, events, every capability incl. Prepare, scripted failures, `guest_dial`/`push_console`), `FakeNetwork` (10.200.0.0/16 leases, quarantine ledger, `NetworkReconcile` token protocol), and `driver_contract!(mod_name, harness_expr)`, which expands to one `#[tokio::test]` per contract check over a `ContractHarness`; `FakeHarness` is the reference harness. An adapter runs the contract in its own (ignored, hardware-backed) test crate: enable `testkit` in dev-deps, implement `ContractHarness`, `driver_contract!(fc, FcHarness::new())`. `tests/fake_contract.rs` runs it against the fake, fully claimed and with nothing claimed.

No consumer is wired yet, by design — R1 wires `arcbox-vm` through the Firecracker adapter (`virt/arcbox-fc-driver`, in flight). The crate is added to the `linux-engine` CI job (check / test / musl check).

Validation: `cargo fmt --check`; `cargo clippy -p arcbox-vm-driver --all-targets [--all-features] -- -D warnings`; `cargo test -p arcbox-vm-driver --all-features` (30 unit + 28 contract tests); `cargo check --target aarch64-unknown-linux-musl -p arcbox-vm-driver --all-features/--all-targets`; `cargo doc --no-deps --all-features` with zero warnings; `cargo metadata` resolves; `cargo package --no-verify` packages.

Design: company repo `engineering/arcbox/architecture/vm-stack-redesign.md` (charter P4b execution design, D-VM1 / D-VM7 / D-VM9); the `Prepare` capability is the amendment the R1 seam map called for (external-process VMMs are two-phase: warm-pool slots pre-spawn the jailer, the pid is journaled before boot, a boot can be killed mid-staging, READY must be listening before the guest starts).

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> New library crate and CI coverage only; no production wiring or changes to existing VM execution paths in this PR.
> 
> **Overview**
> Introduces **`virt/arcbox-vm-driver`**, a new port crate with **no `arcbox-*` dependencies** so VMM adapters and orchestrators meet at a shared seam. The crate defines serializable **`VmSpec`** (and related types), object-safe **`VmDriver` / `VmHandle`** with mandatory identify / observe / shutdown, optional capabilities via **`Option<&dyn Cap>`** accessors (vsock, checkpoint, prepare, adopt/detach, balloon, console, debug), and a second **`GuestNetwork`** port with quarantine / reconcile cleanup tokens.
> 
> **`DriverCapabilities`** must align with what handles expose; unsupported behavior is **`None` on accessors**, not a dedicated error variant. The optional **`testkit`** feature adds **`FakeDriver`**, **`FakeNetwork`**, and **`driver_contract!`** contract tests; **`tests/fake_contract.rs`** runs the contract against the fake with full and minimal capability sets.
> 
> Workspace **`Cargo.toml` / `Cargo.lock`** register the crate; the **linux-engine CI** job now **checks, tests, and musl-checks** `arcbox-vm-driver`. **No runtime consumer is wired in this PR** (follow-on adapter work is expected).

author: ghazmotiebipro
body:
تقوية الاستقلالية المجانية: تحويل ذاكرة تعلم الأوبشن من الاعتماد الوحيد على GitHub Actions Artifacts إلى طبقتين: hot artifacts + durable `bot-state` branch، بدون أي تدخل من المستخدم وبدون اشتراك جديد.

### Durable state
- فرع `bot-state` موجود ومخصص للحالة الآلية فقط.
- Options runner يحافظ على أي state محلية/Artifact حديثة ويسترجع من `bot-state` فقط الملفات الناقصة.
- لا يمكن للفرع الدائم أن يطغى على hot state أحدث.
- ملفات التعلم الدائمة: options alert dedupe, signal journal, outcomes, calibration.

### State Vault
- Workflow مستقل بعد نجاح Options Contract Radar أو Options Performance Auditor.
- ينسخ فقط ملفات الحالة المسموح بها إلى `bot-state`.
- يفحص JSON/JSONL، حد journal، shadow>=training، learning adjustment cap، واستقلال performance auditor.
- يرفض أي key اسمه يوحي بـ token/secret/api_key/authorization/password/credential.
- كل state commit يحمل `[skip ci]` لتجنب تشغيل الرادارات بسبب حفظ الحالة.
- لا Telegram ولا API مدفوع ولا استضافة جديدة.

### Performance continuity
- Auditor يستطيع استرجاع outcome/calibration من `bot-state` عند غياب Artifacts.
- حالة منع تكرار milestone/weekly report تحفظ كذلك في `state/performance`.
- Artifacts تبقى fallback/backup وليست الذاكرة الوحيدة.

### Safety
- لا تغيير في stock scoring.
- لا تغيير في strict options scoring/blockers.
- لا تغيير في Gamma/GEX أو CALL/PUT decision engine.
- لا أسرار في durable state.
- Free Autonomy يبقى كما هو.

### Tests
- hot state is never overwritten.
- missing files restore from durable branch.
- invalid durable JSON is ignored.
- git/fetch failure is non-fatal.
- restore happens before hardened options engine.
- vault secret guard + skip-ci + bot-state push.
- performance auditor durable fallback.
- new files included in pytest/compile/Ruff gates.

author: drothschild
body:
The rest-screen coach remark now talks about **the set the athlete just did** when the rest lands inside an exercise or superset group, and keeps previewing the **upcoming** exercise only when the rest lands between two different exercises.

Fixes #270

## Two remark shapes

`buildRestCommentaryPrompt` takes a `shape`, and both halves of the prompt change with it:

| | `lastSet` | `upNext` |
|---|---|---|
| message heading | `## Last Set` | `## Up Next` |
| subject line | `Bench Press (strength) \| Set 2 of 3 \| 8 reps @ 135lbs RPE 8 \| target 3x8 \| rest 90s` | `Bench Press (strength) \| Set 2 of 3 \| target 3x8 \| rest 90s` |
| history section | the **performed** exercise's recent working sets | the **upcoming** exercise's |
| closing system rule | "Comment on the set they just finished…" | "Comment on the exercise that is coming up…" |

That last row is the point of the split: the old rule line was unconditional, and shipping it alongside a `## Last Set` message would have told the model to ignore its own data.

## The discriminator, and where it came from

`ScheduleRest` leaves `advance_after_set` from exactly two sites, and they differ in `setIndex`:

- `transition.lv:66-70` — the round-repeat rest writes `setIndex: s.setIndex + 1`, so **always ≥ 1**, and `exerciseIndex` stays inside the current superset group.
- `transition.lv:103-107` — the group-exhausted rest writes `setIndex: 0` and moves `exerciseIndex` to a fresh `h.next_active_landing`.

So during `Resting`: **`setIndex >= 1` ⟺ inside the exercise/group; `setIndex === 0` ⟺ between exercises.** Snapshot-only, and positional rather than identity-based, so a routine listing the same exercise twice back to back still reads correctly. `Resume` and `AppForegrounded` re-enter `Resting` without touching `setIndex`, so a rehydrated or foregrounded rest reads the same as the one it recovers. No engine changes — no `.lv` edits, no new state fields.

Verified against the source rather than taken on trust; the issue body's line references were off by a few lines in two places (`setType` is written at :190, not :186; `SetDone` routes at :208-210, not :206) but every claim held.

## Working sets only

The guard is `setType !== 'warmup'`, **never** `=== 'working'`. `transition.lv:190` stamps the entry's own `kind` for non-strength entries, so a cardio set is `'cardio'` and a stretch set `'stretch'`; an equality test would have silently killed the feature on every non-strength exercise. Both are covered by tests.

A warmup set yields silence, not a fallback to the up-next shape — matching the store's rule 3, where no key means no call and no placeholder. Note the scope: the guard applies where the *last-set* shape would apply. A rest that lands *between* exercises keeps the up-next remark regardless of what preceded it, since that remark is not about the finished set at all. Flagging it because the spec's two rules can be read as touching on this.

## Skip staleness — two layers, both needed

`SetDone` ("Skip Set") routes straight to `advance_after_set` and never writes `lastLoggedSet`, so a rest reached by skipping still carries the *previous* set.

1. **Pure, in `restCommentaryTarget`.** `lastLoggedSet` must belong to the entry the round actually just left — resolved by `performedEntryIndex`, which reads the last member of the current superset group still active at round `setIndex - 1`. This catches the cross-member case: log one superset partner, skip the other.
2. **Latched, in the store.** `claimLogIndex` gives each logged-set index exactly one rest's worth of remark; a *second* rest naming the same set means the visit in between was a skip. The rest that owns a claim can re-read it, so a remount or pause/resume still shows the comment it already paid for.

Layer 2 is not redundant. For a standalone exercise, log-then-skip and log-then-log leave engine states that differ only in `loggedSets.length` and in which set `lastLoggedSet` names — and the exercise id is the same either way, so no snapshot-only test can separate them. Deleting either layer fails a test.

**Known residual, deliberately not fixed:** on a no-rest superset hop, logging partner A and then skipping partner B produces a remark about A's set. Both layers pass it — A really was performed, in the same round, seconds earlier — so it is a slightly stale remark rather than a fabricated one. Closing it would need per-entry attribution that the engine's `LoggedSet` (exercise id only, no entry index) cannot supply without an engine change.

## The accepted cost

The cache key moves from `sessionId#entryIdx` (one call per exercise per session) to the rest's own position, `sessionId#exerciseIndex:setIndex` (one call per rest). That pair is unique per rest within a session, including across the superset round-robin, and it collapses to the old behaviour for the up-next shape. Roughly a 4x call increase on a 4x4 workout, accepted in the issue in exchange for the remark being about something that actually just happened; warmup silence is what keeps it from being worse.

`restCommentaryKey` is exported and `session.tsx` now calls it instead of rebuilding the key inline — a hand-rolled copy there would have gone stale the moment the key changed, and `src/app` is invisible to jest, so a structural test asserts the screen calls it.

Rules 2 (staleness/`generation`) and 3 (rest never depends on the AI) are untouched, as is `pendingRequests` in-flight dedupe.

## Verification

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `npm test` | 96 suites, 1822 tests | 96 suites, **1852** tests |
| `npx tsc --noEmit` | clean | clean |
| `npm run lint` | 0 errors, 51 warnings | 0 errors, 51 warnings |

**Mutation testing: 30 mutants, 29 killed (97%), 0 anchor misses, 0 non-compiling.** Every surface the change touches was mutated, not one representative site: the discriminator (3 mutants), the warmup guard (2), both skip-staleness layers (6), the cache key (3), `performedEntryIndex` (5), the target/prompt wiring (5), the prompt builder's shape branches and the RPE-sentinel and zero-planned-set guards (5), and the screen's key call (1).

One survivor, **classified as an equivalent mutant under reachable engine states**: dropping `supersetPosition` from the group-start derivation. On every state the engine can produce at `setIndex >= 1`, `exerciseIndex` is the first member active at the *next* round, and a member active at round + 1 is necessarily active at round too — so `exerciseIndex` can never sit past the member being looked for, and the backwards scan finds the same entry either way. It is kept as a defensive guard for `hydrate`-restored positions, which no rule validates, and the reasoning is recorded in the source.

A first pass left a second survivor — a mutant reading group-member activity at the upcoming round rather than the completed one — because every superset fixture used set counts that made the two rounds agree. Closed with a 3-set/2-set fixture in the third commit.

## What tests cannot prove

The prompt **wording** is pinned against drift, not shown to be effective. Two judgements in particular want a live run before this leaves draft:

- the `lastSet` brief's framing ("has just finished the set described in the next message…") and its closing rule;
- the added rule telling the model that the recent-sets list may already contain the set above and must not be compared against itself. This exists because `PersistSet` is fire-and-forget, so whether the just-logged set has reached the DB by the time `loadHistory` runs is a genuine race; without the rule the coach can compare a set to itself. Whether the sentence lands, or just adds noise to a 4-rule prompt, is a wording call.

Not verified: no simulator run, and no live API call against either provider.

Self-audit found three choreo flags shipped as promises rather than behaviour: `arrivalBadges` was never consumed, `groupGrid` applied a CSS class with no rule behind it, and `breathCue` was declared on two tools and unconsumed.

All three are now implemented, and a new test walks every tool's choreo keys to fail on any flag app.js does not consume or any class with no CSS behind it. It caught `breathCue` and the dead `.group-grid` class on its first run — the kind of gap that is invisible in review because the tool card still looks complete.

Tests 41/41.

author: steipete
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `openclaw cron` help advertised `--json (default: false)` for commands whose results were already always JSON, while other always-JSON commands did not accept `--json` at all. This made the CLI's documented surface contradict its shipped output behavior.

AI-assisted: yes (Codex).

## Why This Change Was Made

JSON-result commands now share one declaration for their primary names, aliases, early stdout routing, and honest compatibility flag: `--json` is described as the explicit machine-output spelling because command results are JSON by default. `list` and `show` keep their real human/JSON switch. `scratch` keeps raw reads by default, returns JSON for writes with or without `--json`, and describes that operation split directly in help.

The early router cannot derive this from the Commander tree: `runCli` resolves built-in machine output before command registration and parsing (`src/cli/run-main.ts:1057`), while Commander only dispatches through its registered tree during parsing. The prior hardcoded name set is therefore replaced by one declaration that also creates the registered commands and aliases. Registration-vs-router coverage fails if the two observable surfaces drift.

The hidden `gateway restart-handoff capabilities|consume` sibling had the same proven no-op flag. It now reuses the same honest description; behavior and protocol output are unchanged.

## User Impact

| Command | Before | After | Default result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `status` | advertised `default: false`; flag ignored | explicit machine-output spelling | JSON |
| `add` / `create` | advertised `default: false`; flag ignored | explicit machine-output spelling | JSON |
| `rm` / `remove` / `delete` | advertised `default: false`; flag ignored | explicit machine-output spelling | JSON |
| `enable`, `disable` | always JSON; rejected `--json` | accepts explicit machine-output spelling | JSON |
| `run` | always JSON; rejected `--json` | accepts explicit machine-output spelling | JSON |
| `edit` | always JSON; rejected `--json` | accepts explicit machine-output spelling | JSON |
| `get`, `runs` | advertised `default: false`; documented no-op spelling | honest explicit spelling retained | JSON results; existing parse-error streams unchanged |
| `list`, `show` | human by default; `--json` honored | unchanged | human |
| `scratch` read | raw text by default; `--json` honored | unchanged | raw text |
| `scratch` write | JSON regardless of flag | output shape unchanged; help says writes return JSON by default | JSON revision result |

`docs/cli/cron.md` already established that `get` and `runs` accept `--json` as the explicit machine-output spelling. The docs now state that rule once for every JSON-result command, explicitly include `status`, and describe the human-rendered `list`/`show` paths plus scratch's raw-read/JSON-write split.

No CLI flag was removed: existing scripts keep working, and the previously rejected spelling is additive on `enable`, `disable`, `run`, and `edit`.

## Evidence

Pre-fix regressions failed for all nine JSON-result registrations, `edit --json`, and gateway restart-handoff help. The follow-up scratch regression also proved that the proposed human-write branch changed the shipped default: it failed until no-flag writes again used the JSON renderer and mutation routing again reserved machine stdout.

Validation on the rebased head:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/program/root-command-descriptions.test.ts src/cli/cron-cli/register.cron-simple.test.ts src/cli/cron-cli/register.cron-edit.test.ts src/cli/cron-cli/register.cron-scratch.test.ts src/cli/machine-output-modes.test.ts src/cli/gateway-cli/register-restart-handoff.test.ts` — 153 tests passed across two shards.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` — passed on the exact pushed head in Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01m06g5wm5vj8ceakz0ey1az95`; typecheck, test typecheck, lint, dead-code, formatting, runtime-cycle, and architecture guards green ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/31980611403)).
- Exact-head hosted CI exposed and now covers one related stale inventory: `cron enable`, `disable`, `run`, and `edit` were still classified as mutations with no JSON report. Their obsolete JSON-N/A entries are removed, and the owning `root-command-descriptions` suite is in the focused proof above.
- The earlier broad built-CLI matrix covered every affected cron command and representative aliases with and without `--json`, plus byte-identical restart-handoff output ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/31978483208)).
- Final built-CLI scratch proof started a real isolated Gateway on loopback port 19243. It proved raw reads without `--json`, scratch-plus-revision JSON reads with `--json`, JSON writes with and without `--json`, revision monotonicity (1 then 2), exact latest content (`alpha`, then `beta`), empty stderr, and the final help wording without `default: false`. `PROOF_PASS` on the final production commit in Testbox `tbx_01m06fv9wgenrwc5qz3r0dm43p` ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/31980345445)); the later head changes only the stale JSON-capability test classification.
- `pnpm docs:check-mdx` — passed for 774 files.
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode uncommitted --stream-engine-output` — clean, no accepted/actionable findings.

The original broad matrix captured stdout and stderr separately for every affected command with and without `--json`. The final follow-up added successful real-Gateway scratch RPC proof for all four read/write × flag cases.

Production LOC: +65/-48 (net +17) | Tests: +122/-5 | Docs: +3/-1. The production growth replaces duplicated output-policy names with one registration/router declaration; scratch write behavior stays on its original JSON path.

## Summary

Implement the offline execution runner for the reviewed and merged PR #134 FotMob UTC-native successor feature-construction protocol.

This PR does **not** execute the preserved 21,326-row campaign during review and does not check in a result receipt or feature projection. It adds the deterministic runner, CLI, adversarial tests and execution documentation only.

## Current-main refresh after PR #133 merge

- current `main` / exact base: `c747b7bfc88c789161f984f74c844e0a7e26ca97`
- exact unchanged PR head: `764d9562ca3c77fa12399e61604418f76e7a575a`
- changed files: exactly 4
- GitHub mergeability after explicit base refresh: clean / mergeable
- draft: false
- no submitted reviews or unresolved inline review threads

PR #133 changed only its separate PR69 formal-invariance protocol/docs/tests. PR #136 changes a disjoint four-file FotMob UTC-native runner surface and does not import the new #133 module. The #136 implementation head itself did not move during this refresh.

The cached `refs/pull/136/merge` object still points to the pre-#133 synthetic merge and is therefore **not** cited as current-base validation evidence.

## Hosted validation on the exact unchanged #136 head

Tests run `31982789792` / #608 previously executed the exact head against the pre-#133 base.

- syntax: success
- test shard 1/8: success

The aggregate `test` job did not execute because GitHub Actions refused to start another runner after the account billing/spending limit was reached. That job contains no additional tests; it only asserts successful shard and syntax results.

After #133 merged, push run `31984197297` / #609 on new `main` also failed before runner allocation: all jobs have zero executed steps / runner_id 0. This is infrastructure exhaustion, not a repository test result. No fresh current-base CI result is claimed.

## Exact upstream pins

- PR #134 canonical protocol SHA-256 `b3cc9a8e5ca05f199b7e404fa8288074e77d76fa5f21224c5bddb48ca1aac411` / `5,809` bytes
- PR #134 protocol implementation blob `57cc133a7fb9daa76c5d5d8e9156903e583c6575`

## Runner contract

- timezone-aware canonical FotMob UTC chronology only
- strict prior history; same-kickoff fixtures use pre-group state and batch updates
- source-scoped duplicate/identity conflicts fail closed
- form uses last five strictly prior rows with exact `MISSING` semantics and no default

- historical freshness remains `NOT_RECONSTRUCTIBLE_WITH_CURRENT_EVIDENCE`, numeric null and normalized `BLOCKED`
- receipt includes total rows, raw status counts, normalized AVAILABLE/MISSING/BLOCKED counts, same-kickoff accounting and identity/lineage conflict accounting

1. `domain/fotmob_utc_native_successor_feature_construction_qualification.py`

3. `tests/test_fotmob_utc_native_successor_feature_construction_qualification.py`
4. `docs/fotmob_utc_native_successor_feature_construction_qualification.md`

That is feature-materialization qualification only, not model approval.

Next reviewed boundary after successful execution:

`PRE_REGISTER_REVIEWED_FOTMOB_UTC_NATIVE_EXPECTED_GOALS_MODEL_VALIDATION_PROTOCOL`

### Motivation

- Add an explicit, optional assertion state for Factors and Controls to support provenance and presentation of analytic findings while preserving `undefined` as the default/migrated state.
- Surface a compact, accessible selector and marker UI for assertion state in the Inspector and on cards without changing existing Root Cause / Key Factor or Control status prominence.

### Description

- Introduce a new `assertionStateSchema` with values `"Confirmed"`, `"Working"`, and `"Inferred"` and allow `assertionState` optionally on Factor nodes and Controls in `src/features/maps/schema.ts` and V4 serialization rules.
- Add guarded store actions `setFactorAssertionState` and `setControlAssertionState` and wire `assertionState` through clone/serialize (`toMap`) and history/undo/redo in `src/state/useAppStore.ts`.
- Add `AssertionState` UI helpers: `AssertionMarker` and `AssertionStateField` in `src/components/AssertionState/AssertionState.tsx`, plus compact markers rendered on Factor and Control cards and an Inspector selector that includes accessible explanatory text and explicitly explains that Inferred is analytically derived (not necessarily uncertain).
- Add a `CaseSummary` presentation component that counts and displays assertion-state totals and explanatory help, and include assertion state in the `Legend` and presentation surfaces; add minimal styling in `src/styles/index.css`.
- Add unit tests in `tests/unit/assertion-state.test.ts` covering schema restrictions, optional state semantics, undo/redo persistence, serialization checks, and the Case Summary counting helper.

Closes #5436

## Summary

`PROSE_MAX_MEASURE = 105` capped user/assistant/thinking prose at the live-transcript render entry points (`history.rs` streaming, thinking, user, assistant paths), so wide terminals showed full-width tool cells beside a 105-column prose rail — the surviving residue of the frame cap removed for #5322.

- Default is now full content width: the constant is gone; every entry point resolves its width via `TranscriptRenderOptions::prose_width`, so the main cache and the full-screen overlay agree.

- Documented in `docs/CONFIGURATION.md`, `config.example.toml`, and `CHANGELOG.md`.

body:
## 무엇이 달라지나 (설치받는 사람 기준)

`implementer` 에이전트 파일을 에디터에서 열면 프리뷰가 죽었다. 이제 안 죽는다.

```
AS-IS  Error in user YAML: mapping values are not allowed in this context
       at line 2 column 174
TO-BE  정상 렌더 (설명 313자 그대로)
```

## 원인

`description` 이 따옴표 없이 이 문장을 담고 있었다:

> ... work moves from deciding to **building: a** feature ...

YAML 의 plain scalar 안에서 `콜론+공백`은 **중첩 매핑의 시작**으로 읽힌다. 그래서 엄격한
파서는 정확히 그 자리(column 174)에서 죽는다. 독립 파서(Ruby Psych)로 사용자가 본 것과
**같은 메시지·같은 열**을 재현했고, 따옴표를 씌워 PARSE OK 로 만들었다.

**Claude Code 자신은 관대해서 이 파일을 읽었다.** 그래서 아무도 안 물었다 — 한 소비자가
너그럽다는 사실은 계약이 아니고, 우리는 이 파일을 남의 저장소에 설치한다.

배포판(`templates/agents/`)과 개발 사본(`.claude/agents/`) **양쪽에** 있던 결함이라 둘 다
고쳤다. 따옴표 표기는 형제 파일(`data-analyst`·`reviewer`·`strategist`)이 이미 쓰는 방식이다.

## 재발 방지

`tests/frontmatter-yaml.test.ts` — 우리 소유 `.md` 전부를 훑어 plain scalar 안의 콜론을 찾는다.

- 파서를 의존성으로 들이는 대신 **이 결함 종류 하나**만 본다(3줄짜리 frontmatter에 dep 하나는 과하다)
- 대신 **canary** 로 탐지기가 실제로 무는지 먼저 보인다 + 오탐 가드(따옴표·`[...]`·`https://`)
- `.claude/local-plugins/`(ECC 가 들여온 남의 번역 문서, 같은 위반 **13건**)는 범위 밖 —
  우리가 못 고치는 것 때문에 상시 red 인 게이트는 아무도 안 돌린다(#237 이 없앤 관행)

## 딸려 온 것

따옴표 **2바이트**가 상주 토큰을 +1 시켜 ratchet 게이트가 물었다(설계대로 작동). 정당한
증가라 `npm run cost:baseline` 갱신 + `NORTH_STAR` 실측 수치를 **같은 커밋**에 담았다.
`vitest related` 나 grep 으로 영향 범위를 골랐으면 못 봤을 게이트 2종이다 — 전체를 돌려서 잡혔다.

## 검증

- `npm run ci` **exit 0** — 99 files · 1428 tests · branches 88.59%
- 독립 파서로 전후 대조 (FAIL col 174 → PARSE OK, 본문 313자 보존)
- **음성 대조** — 따옴표를 되돌리면 새 게이트 red, 복원 후 `shasum` 일치
- 전수 스캔 849개 파일 → 우리 소유 위반 **0건**

author: ccharland
body:
Manual runs of publish.yml do not have tag context unless a tag ref is selected or provided explicitly, so github.ref_name can resolve to a branch name and break tag-based verification. This change makes the manual-dispatch contract explicit and aligns the workflow UI with the existing tag-resolution path.

Workflow dispatch input

Updates the optional tag input description to clearly indicate it should be provided for manual runs started from a branch ref.
Keeps dry_run and tag as the manual dispatch surface, with clearer ordering and intent.
Tag resolution guidance

Tightens the resolve-tag step messaging to direct operators to the tag workflow input for manual runs.
Clarifies that explicit input takes precedence over github.ref_name when dispatching manually.
Operator-facing behavior

Removes misleading guidance that implied selecting the ref alone was sufficient in all manual cases.
Makes manual verification of an existing signed release tag easier to understand from the workflow UI.
workflow_dispatch:
  inputs:
    dry_run:
      description: "Run with -WhatIf (no actual publish)"
      type: boolean
      default: true
    tag:
      description: "Tag to verify and publish (e.g. v0.6.0). Provide this for manual runs started from a branch ref."
      type: string
Fixes https://github.com/ccharland/CharlandCustomizations/issues/99

author: acamarata
body:
Four backend defects, each confirmed against a running local stack rather than by reading code. Several turned out to be worse than reported.

## 1. `profile` relationship did not exist

The mobile roster and presence queries select `profile { display_name avatar_url }` on `np_list_members` / `np_list_presence` (`apps/mobile/src/lib/collabOps.ts`), but no such relationship was defined — so those documents failed GraphQL validation outright rather than merely rendering blank.

It cannot point at `np_profiles` or `auth.users`. PR #95 scoped both for role `user` to the caller's own row, Hasura applies the target table's permission when traversing a relationship, and widening that filter would (a) re-expose every user's email and (b) break `GET_PROFILE`, which selects `np_profiles` unfiltered and takes row `[0]`.

Migration 029 adds `np_member_profiles`, a view with **no email column at all**, and the relationships point there. Row scope: the caller, plus members of lists the caller owns or belongs to.

`display_name` is nulled when it is just the email — hasura-auth seeds `display_name` from the signup address, so dropping the column alone still leaked it through the "safe" field. Verified on a fresh signup.

**Verified as role `user` with a real JWT:**
| Probe | Result |
|---|---|
| Alice reads roster (self + Bob) | both resolve, names + avatars |
| Alice reads Bob's `np_profiles` row | `[]` |
| `email` on `np_member_profiles` | field does not exist |
| Carol (shares no list) lists profiles | only herself |
| Carol targets Bob directly | `[]` |
| Alice reads her **own** email | still works (`GET_PROFILE` unbroken) |

## 2. hasura-auth routes that do not exist in 0.36.0

Probed the running container — both the Go front-end and the Node server it proxies to. These all return 404 `route-not-found`: `PATCH /user`, `GET /user/sessions`, `DELETE /user/sessions/{id}`, `DELETE /users/{id}`, `POST /user/mfa/totp/generate`, `POST /user/mfa/totp/disable`.

Replaced with the routes that exist: `POST /user/email/change`, `POST /user/password`, `GET /mfa/totp/generate`, `POST /user/mfa`. Sessions and auth-user deletion have no HTTP equivalent, so they go through admin GraphQL over `auth.refresh_tokens` / `auth.users` — scoped to `x-hasura-user-id` **in the query**, since admin bypasses permissions.

`deleteAuthUser` no longer treats 404 as success: it re-reads the row and throws if it survives. Previously the final step of every account deletion silently no-opped while the action reported success, leaving the login credential alive.

**Also found:** auth root fields are hasura-auth's own (`user`, `users`, `deleteUsers`, `authRefreshTokens`), not `users_by_pk` — hasura-auth re-applies that configuration on every startup. Every `getUserEmail` call in `account-ops.ts` and `collab-ops.ts` was throwing `field 'users_by_pk' not found`, so **changePassword and invite mail were already broken** before this PR.

**Live results:**
- `listSessions` → 8 real sessions with id/createdAt/expiresAt/type (previously 404)
- `revokeSession` own id → success; bogus/other id → `Session not found` (no false success)
- `changePassword` wrong current password → 401; correct → password actually changed (old password then 401, new 200)
- `changeEmail` → `auth.users.new_email` set, old address preserved pending confirmation

## 3. Auth port had two sources of truth

Compose sets `AUTH_PORT`; the handlers hardcoded `auth:4000`. New `lib/auth-service.ts` derives the base URL from `AUTH_PORT`, and the compose override forwards `AUTH_PORT` / `HASURA_AUTH_URL` / `MINIO_*` into the functions container — which was receiving only four env vars.

`.env.example` now documents that **`AUTH_PORT` must never be 4001**: hasura-auth 0.36.0 proxies unhandled routes to a fixed internal 4001, so that value makes the Go server proxy to itself and 502 every proxied route (`/signout`, `/user/mfa`, `/mfa/totp/generate`). Confirmed by container logs and by a sibling stack on 4000 proxying correctly to the same Node server.

## 4. Export and deletion exercised end to end

Both reached MinIO with HTTP `Authorization: Basic`, which MinIO rejects, and the export returned an unsigned `?expires=` URL. The existing SigV4 signer was extracted into `lib/s3-presign.ts` and is now used by the export PUT, the download URL and the object purge (also de-duplicating it from `storage-presign.ts`).

**Live run on a throwaway user:**
- `requestDataExport` → download URL fetched **HTTP 200**, real JSON: 2 lists, 1 todo, 1 subtask, 1 comment, profile
- `deleteMyAccount` → before: auth user present, 2 lists / 1 todo / 1 comment / 1 profile / 2 members / 2 refresh tokens; after: **all zero**, auth user `null`, sign-in **401**

## Verification

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean in `backend/functions` and `apps/mobile`; `npm test` 36/36 passing (10 suites). No version bumps.

## Not fixed (reporting only)

- `enableMfa` sets `task_users.mfa_enabled = true` when it only *generates* a TOTP secret; activation is a separate `POST /user/mfa` call. Route fixed, semantics left alone — the action schema has no confirm step.
- Role vocabulary is inconsistent across layers: the DB check constraint allows `owner|admin|member`, `collab-ops.ts` validates `owner|editor|viewer`, and the web SPA's transfer-ownership mutation writes `"editor"` — which the constraint rejects.
- `np_list_members` select for role `user` returns only the caller's own row plus rows of lists they own, so a non-owner member sees a roster of one. Left alone as a permissions-policy decision.
- The `ntask` MinIO bucket did not exist locally; nothing in the stack provisions `MINIO_BUCKET`.
- The web SPA (separate repo) still never selects `profile` in `GET_LIST_MEMBERS`, and reads `member.profile?.email`, which this design deliberately does not provide.

author: jgreathouse9
body:
## Related Links

- New case: `benchmarks/cases/compsc_pennsylvania_r.py`; new bundle: `benchmarks/reference/compsc_pennsylvania_r/`
- Companion Path-A case it complements: `benchmarks/cases/compsc_pennsylvania.py`
- Docs: `docs/compsc.rst` (Verification), `docs/benchmarks.rst`
- Paper: Boussim, O. (2026), *Compositional Synthetic Controls*, [arXiv:2607.16991](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.16991)
- Reference: `csc_replication.R`, provided by the author

## What

- Added `benchmarks/reference/compsc_pennsylvania_r/` — the author's script with a full-precision capture block appended, plus `manifest.json` and the generated `reference.out` / `reference.json` / `provenance.json`.
- Added `benchmarks/cases/compsc_pennsylvania_r.py` (11 pinned cells) and registered it.
- Corrected the Arkansas attribution in `compsc_pennsylvania` and in `docs/compsc.rst`.
- Regenerated `comparison.csv` (23 rows) and `docs/validation.rst`.

## Why

`compsc_pennsylvania` validated against the paper's printed tables because nothing else existed — the case docstring says so. Tables rounded to three decimals cannot separate a real disagreement from a printing convention, which is exactly what had happened: Table 1 lists nine donors, mlsynth gives Arkansas 0.000924, and the case recorded that as a solver artefact on the assumption that `quadprog::solve.QP` drove the weight to zero.

It does not. Running the author's script, `quadprog` returns 0.000924 for Arkansas as well — agreeing with mlsynth to 6e-10 — and reports ten active donors. The gap is between the paper's table and the author's own code. The old reason was a guess made without a reference to run, which is the kind of stated cause that should not survive contact with the actual implementation.

## How

The script is unedited above an appended `== REFERENCE VALUES ==` block; the only other change is taking the input path from `argv`. It runs against `basedata/pa_aeps_generation.csv`, the panel mlsynth itself reads, so both sides see identical inputs. The script derives its own donor pool (structural zeros plus OH, WV, VT), and on the pre-filtered panel that step leaves the same 42 donors it derives from the author's full 51-state file — verified, not assumed.

## Verification

- Path: cross-validation against the author's implementation, run live and captured with provenance.

| quantity | max abs difference |
| --- | --- |
| all ten donor weights | 3e-9 |
| Aitchison pre-RMSPE | 1e-10 |
| share pre-RMSPE (pp) | 2e-9 |
| Table 2, 20 years × 5 columns | 1e-7 |
| placebo RMSPE ratio | 1e-8 |
| placebo retained count | exact |
| placebo p-value | 1e-11 |

Solver tolerance across a chain of 43 QPs including the 42 placebo refits, with no tuning on either side.

- Tolerances: each `*_diff` cell is pinned at zero with roughly an order of magnitude of headroom over the observed residual — tight enough that a real divergence fails, loose enough to survive a different BLAS.
- Determinism: both sides are deterministic (active-set QP here, `quadprog`'s dual method there, no RNG in either path).
- Data equivalence measured, not assumed: run against the author's own `data_energy.csv` instead, the reference moves 1e-7 on the weights and 7e-6 on the effects. The two files agree to 1e-5 relative (max 147 MWh on gas out of millions). Worth measuring because the same class of check on `Synth::synth` in `spillsynth_iterative_germany` moves an estimate by 149 USD under a smaller perturbation — a deterministic active-set QP on a well-conditioned log-odds design behaves, a nested V search need not.
- Nothing fails to match. The Arkansas weight, previously the one recorded discrepancy, agrees.

## Scope checks

<!-- BENCHMARK / VALIDATION -->
- [x] Replication path stated; cross-validation with the reference run live and captured, per `agents/agents_benchmarking.md`
- [x] Expected values come from the committed capture, read through `load_reference` so the constant and the run cannot drift apart; the generator is committed
- [x] Each tolerance justified against the measured residual
- [x] Determinism checked
- [x] Pinned quantities are the ones that move — every weight, every Table-2 cell, the full placebo — not a summary
- [x] Branch is benchmark authoring only, plus the two-line correction to the stale attribution it disproves

## Designs

`benchmarks/reference/compsc_pennsylvania_r/comparison.csv` — 23 rows, max |Δ| 0.0 at the rounding used there.

## Test Steps

- [x] `python benchmarks/reference/generate.py compsc_pennsylvania_r`
- [x] `python benchmarks/run_benchmarks.py --case compsc_pennsylvania_r` — 11/11 cells pass
- [x] `python benchmarks/run_benchmarks.py --case compsc_pennsylvania` — still passes after the docstring correction
- [x] `python benchmarks/reference/export_comparison.py compsc_pennsylvania_r`
- [x] `python benchmarks/reference/build_validation.py`
- [x] `pytest mlsynth/tests/ -k "compsc or benchmark or registry"` — 72 passed, 1 skipped
- [x] Docs build clean

## Attribution and provenance

`reference.R` is Boussim's script, provided by him directly and not published as a package, so the bundle records it as author-provided rather than as a repository at a pinned commit. The file header names him, states that authorship of the method and of the script is his and that mlsynth claims neither, and marks the two additive changes; nothing in the estimation path is altered. Redistributing it here was the maintainer's decision, on the basis that the method is not proprietary and no private data is involved. If the script is published later, the manifest should gain that pointer.

The bundle needs R with `quadprog` to regenerate; the case itself reads the committed capture and needs no R.

author: mikkoparkkola
body:
Discovery skips a backend whose tool cache is empty, so accepting the first empty `tools/list` reports success about a backend nobody can find.

An earlier bounded retry looked right and **did nothing**: an empty result is cached with a fresh timestamp like any other, so each attempt re-read the same cached emptiness within microseconds and never reached the backend. That retry was removed rather than left as decoration; this restores it with the mechanism that makes it real.

## The change

- cache invalidation, so a cached answer can actually be asked again
- warm-start re-asks a bounded number of times before believing an empty list
- a test pinning that an empty result *is* cached, which is what made the old retry inert

## Review caught a race, and it was the dangerous direction

Invalidating unconditionally could erase a tool list another reader had populated between the caller observing emptiness and acting on it — turning a backend that had just become discoverable back into an invisible one.

Invalidation is now **conditional and evaluated under the same write lock as the clear**, so nothing slips between the decision and the effect. There is no unconditional form at all; leaving one would leave the footgun for the next caller. A test asserts a populated value survives an invalidate-if-empty and is not refetched.

## Accepted residual, stated rather than hidden

The empty-list budget is per warm-start task, not per backend instance, so a config reload that replaces a backend mid-loop inherits whatever the count had reached — a replacement whose tools register late gets fewer than the full number of re-asks. Keying the count to the instance means tracking identity through the retry closure, which is more machinery than the case earns: the failure is reduced patience for a backend reloaded in the same minute it started, not invisibility. Recorded in the code.

3529 tests pass, clippy clean under `-D warnings`, format clean.

author: milocaetano
body:
Two things on the chart-trading surface were fighting the price action.

## The aim label

It parked against the right edge whatever the pointer was doing, so aiming
at a price on the left of the plot meant crossing the whole chart to click
the thing you were already pointing at. It now rides beside the cursor — a
fixed gap to its left, flipping right near the left edge, never under the
crosshair it belongs to — with the dashed line running from under the
cursor out to the axis, so the label beside the hand and the price on the
gutter read as one statement.

**A label that follows the pointer can never be landed on** — move toward
it and it moves with you — so the click no longer needs it. The held
modifier is the deliberate act, the label states what the click will do,
and the hand cursor is up wherever the aim is. This was raised with the
user and chosen deliberately: the first design shipped a target that could
not be reached.

The aim is therefore the **last claimant on the canvas**, and stands *down*
rather than merely refusing its press — no line, no label, no hand cursor,
no place — wherever something already holds the pixel: an annotation a
press would grab or the canvas's own chrome (the pane answers that, exactly
as it answers "a tool is armed"), an armed limit/stop from the ticket, this
module's own lines and ✕s, and the layer switch. That last one matters:
hidden means unpainted, and with the label no longer the target, a hidden
layer would otherwise turn the whole plot into an invisible order button.

## The resting order tag

`#6 BUY STP 1 @ 180615 ✕` sat over the newest candles for as long as the
order worked. It now rests as `BUY LMT 1` — an order line is `ACCENT`
whatever its side, so side, kind and size are the only things the chart
cannot say otherwise; the price is already on the gutter chip and the id
only matters once you mean to act. The full statement, with its ✕, arrives
under the pointer, on the dock row's hover, and throughout a drag.

Roughly 72 px at rest against 215 px open (`final-pill.png` vs
`final-open.png`). **The cancel costs no extra gesture:** the ✕ sits at a
fixed x independent of the text, and the tag opens across the whole price
row, so it is already painted before the pointer arrives at it.

## Evidence

- **Four checks** green on a branch cut from `origin/main`: `cargo fmt --all
  -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`,
  `cargo build --workspace`, `cargo test --workspace` (59 suites, 1363 app
  tests).
- **Performance — declared and measured.** Every touched path is
  **per-frame**; nothing per-trade or per-depth is touched.
  `refresh_open_tags` is O(orders) and refills its buffer, so hovering an
  order allocates nothing after the first frame; the new yields in
  `compute_cmd_preview` run only while a modifier is down; the pane's gate
  costs three bool reads otherwise. The aim line now reaches the axis and
  pays up to 96 dash segments against `main`'s ≤40, bounded by
  `CMD_LINE_MAX_DASHES`.

  Paired, interleaved release runs under a live Binance tape, identical
  hooks (`QUANTICK_PAPER_DEMO=1`), `APP_HEALTH_SUMMARY`:

  | | fps | frame_avg_ms | frame_cpu_ms |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `main` ×3 | 59 / 59 / 59 | 16.81 / 16.69 / 16.84 | 2.245 / 2.439 / 2.210 |
  | branch ×3 | 59 / 59 / 59 | 16.70 / 16.68 / 16.71 | 2.318 / 1.834 / 2.739 |

  Mean `frame_cpu`: **2.298 ms vs 2.297 ms** — flat, and the spread within
  each side is larger than the difference.
- **visual-qa** — six captures, all PASS, taken off the virtual desktop so
  the run never competed with the trader: aim flipped right at the left
  edge, mid-band, and against the axis at its minimum line length; the pill
  and the open form; and the aim absent from the pane that does not own
  paper input.
- **trader-ux-review** — no Blocker. Rafa loses a gesture and a mouse
  journey on entry and loses nothing on cancel; Marina keeps the
  Shift-to-level drawing drag; Duda cannot reach anything irreversible.
- **ui-harness** — every changed surface has a hook, added here:
  `QUANTICK_CMD_PREVIEW=<side>[@<0..1>]` parks the aim at a stated x,
  `QUANTICK_PAPER_ORDERS=<rungs>` rests orders on the first print (the
  scripted demo's own order is 220 prints away, 0.4 % out, and a lively
  tape filled it before the shutter three runs running), and
  `QUANTICK_PAPER_ORDER_HOVER=1` opens every tag with nobody at the mouse.

## arch-review

`code-review` at `high`, run twice — the second time over the final HEAD.
**15 findings, 14 confirmed and fixed here**, 3 deferred below. Four were
money-losing:

- moving onto the tape chip nulled the paint's pointer but not the press's,
  so the pill collapsed with no ✕ while a plain click on the chip cancelled
  the working order underneath;
- with the layer hidden the whole plot placed and journaled orders nothing
  painted;
- a modifier resting under the hand turned an armed ticket's click into a
  stop instead of the limit it armed, and left the ticket armed;
- sweeping toward the axis popped a ✕ open under the cursor, so the click
  cancelled an order while everything on screen said "place".

The root was one thing: the two deletions this branch made — `preview.hover`
from the press, the unconditional ✕ from the paint — each removed half of a
paint/press pair, and what replaced them were *shared formulas* rather than
shared values, handed different pointers and different rects.
`handle_chart_input` now decides once and both sides read the answer, the
pattern `cmd_preview` already had one field away.

### Deferred, deliberately

- **The open tag repeats the feed's full price precision** (`snap` rounds
  to `mark.scale()`, and a Binance mark has scale 8), so the *opened* form
  is wider than the tag this change shrinks. Predates this branch, does not
  bite an integer-quoted instrument like WIN, and fixing it changes what
  price an order is placed at — outside this mission's scope.
- **`QUANTICK_PAPER_ORDERS` does not survive a timeline reset**: a replay
  seek mid-capture sweeps the rungs and the hook is already disarmed.
  Development hook only; relaunching reaches the state.
- **The aim label covers the last stretch of its own minimum-length line**
  within 120 px of the axis. Cosmetic: the label sits on the aim's row and
  is the marker there, so the row is never unmarked.

### Out of scope

The position, stop and target tags keep the full form — there is at most
one of each, and none of them is the tag that filled the screen. Horizontal
parking and a density setting in the Trading tab were both considered with
the user, who chose hover-expand over them.

author: srgirsky
body:
An independent critic read his cap as **"a bike helmet."** It was, and the cause is arithmetic.

`BRIM_REACH` was **0.600** while the plate's root — the dome's own front ring, `CAP_LEVELS[-2]` at y_centre −0.040, half_y 0.565 — sits at **−0.605**. The tip was 0.005 ft *less far forward than its own root*. The bill sloped backwards into the dome and projected nothing.

## It is batch 6's Theo lesson, verbatim, one character later

> *"The bill/brim reach is the TIP's absolute forward y — a reach less than the dome's own front projects NO bill (Theo's batting helmet)."*

A lesson in prose did not survive a single kid. His script now refuses to build it:

```python
assert -BRIM_REACH < dome_front - 0.05
```

**And no gate could have caught it.** A bill buried inside the dome changes no silhouette, so `silhouette.lint`, the head-box metrics and `measure:fidelity` are blind to it *by construction*. The whole cap read wrong with every check green. When a feature lives inside another form's envelope, the only instruments are an assert and an eye.

The correct value was in the same file the whole time — the section header cites *"the brim reaches ~0.68ft forward of the axis"* — and the note beside the wrong constant described a lighting **intent** (*"round 6 raised and flattened the plate so the key light reaches the forehead"*), which reads like a considered decision rather than a bill shortened past its own root. **Check a constant against its own header's citation before believing the note next to it.**

## The fix

Set to the critic's measured targets (overhang 5.6% of head height vs the concept's ~35%; bill narrower than the crown at 72% vs 118%): `BRIM_REACH` 0.600→1.050, `BRIM_HALF_W` 0.340→0.640.

**Zero triangle cost** — it moves vertices, it doesn't add any. LOD0 stays 6770/7000; the file stays 352KB.

Re-scored by a third independent critic on the rebuilt board: **4,4,3,4,4,4** — *"bill now adequate (60px past crown, 26% of head depth)"*. Status stays `needs-polish` on hairMass 3, his hair carrying 5% of the concept's strand count — which is the roster's dominant defect, not his.

## ★ The critic loop needed fixing too, and that's the reusable half

His first critic scored **2,3,2,2,3,2** with two headline claims that were **false**: *"ears ARE NOT BUILT"* (he has an `EarSpec`, calls `build_ear`, and the ear is visible) and *"the cap has no bill"* (it existed, just too short). Told which claims to verify rather than repeat, the next critic scored **2,4,3,3,4,3** on a barely-changed build.

A brief that names the known traps buys more accuracy than an instruction to be harsh. Three are now written into the skill:

1. Never call a feature absent without grepping its builder
2. Crop before calling anything a hole — a face-atlas eye at a grazing angle reads as damage
3. `TEAM_MASK` renders raw grey on the board and **tinted at runtime**, so judge its *extent*, never its colour

## Verification

- `npm test` **1759 passed / 12 skipped / 0 failed**; `validate:models` **38/38**; `audit:v2-layout` clean
- `measure:fidelity` unchanged but for ankle daylight **improving** 42.2 → 26.5
- Checked on screen at `/v2/?anims=1`: `model model`, the bill clears the face, and the cap panel renders **gold** — the team tint working
- Scores written **before** the board was re-rendered, hash taken from that board

author: franckmb
body:
## Contexte

PR A du **dernier lot du programme work-loop** (P3-21). Formulation fondateur : « on veut bouger qu'UN seul truc ; si le reste peut rester à l'identique, on ne va pas se priver. » Aujourd'hui régénérer après un verrou rebrasse tout ce qui n'est pas verrouillé — des placements qu'on aimait mais qu'on n'avait pas épinglés.

**Cette PR est inerte seule** : le moteur accepte le champ, personne ne l'émet encore. La PR B (backend) l'allumera.

## Contenu

**Terme de stabilité, plié dans la phase 2 existante du solve** : +1 par séance qui retrouve son placement précédent (nouveau champ optionnel `previousAssignments`).

Le point qui rend le lot sûr — **séparation lexicographique** : le chaînage est multiplié par 4096, soit plus que la masse maximale de stabilité (2000). La stabilité ne départage donc **que les ex æquo exacts** ; elle ne peut mathématiquement renverser aucun arbitrage, ni faire tomber une séance (le placement reste verrouillé à son optimum par la contrainte de phase 2 déjà en place). Un créneau verrouillé n'a pas de variable dans le modèle : jamais payé deux fois. Le score rapporté est recalculé aux **poids d'origine**, stabilité exclue — « à score égal » reste littéralement vérifiable, `SCORE_FORMULA_VERSION` inchangé.

**Granularité par séance** (SM1 garde son mardi même si son jeudi doit bouger). **Pas de réglage club** : un comportement, pas une option. **Non appliqué au verdict** (`/validate-assignments`) : un déplacement manuel est une volonté explicite.

**Contrat 2.10 → 2.11** (champ d'entrée), inventaire complet propagé.

## Preuves

- **Les 14 goldens ne bougent pas** — c'est l'assertion du lot : champ absent/vide = chemin byte-identique. Un golden qui bouge aurait été un STOP.
- **BCCL réel** : les 90 placements réinjectés → **score identique (21646)**, temps inchangé (~4 s), phase 2 largement sous son plafond.
- **Mesure de convergence** : après ajout d'une contrainte interdisant un créneau occupé, **exactement 1 séance déplacée** (l'équipe touchée), les autres restent en place. Falsifié dans l'autre sens.
- **Test de référence** : on repasse au solveur une solution optimale *alternative* — il la restitue exactement ; sans le champ, il redonne l'autre.
- **Test sémantique** : la stabilité ne prime JAMAIS une contrainte ni un écart de score réel (créneau devenu interdit → il bouge ; gain de score réel → il bouge), falsifié dans les deux sens.

## Correctif attrapé en route

`ValidateAssignmentsContractSchemaTest` codait la version **en dur** ('2.10') et dérivait en silence (le moteur ne compare que le MAJOR) — il lit désormais `engine/CONTRACT_VERSION`, la source de vérité.

## Validation

- `make -C engine test` : **492 tests verts**, goldens zéro diff
- `make -C backend tests-complete` : **1509 verts** · rector propre · groupe contract **54 verts** contre le moteur 2.11 vivant
- `smoke-solver.sh` : **COMPLETED**
- `/security-review` non requise : ni auth, ni données personnelles, ni intégration externe — terme d'objectif solveur + champ de schéma optionnel

## Doc

Fiche `/generate` réécrite (terme, preuve lexicographique, immunité des verrous, score), **ADR-0001 amendé** (le troisième palier de l'objectif : placement > chaînage > stabilité — même décision structurante qui grandit, pas une nouvelle frontière), trace état des lieux, roadmap P3-21 réduite au reste-à-faire. Dérive corrigée dans `solver-errors.md` (une référence de feature suivait mécaniquement chaque bump au lieu de rester à la version où elle a atterri).

author: swgiacomelli
body:
Closes #5.

Adds the private locator that turns a coordinate into a table position. Nothing
here interpolates and nothing here is public: `evaluate` (#6) is still
unimplemented, and every document touched says so.

## What landed

`src/lookup.rs`, one new private module, no new public items.

- `search(&[u16], u16) -> (usize, u32)` — the greatest index at or below the
  coordinate, plus the probes it took.
- `locate(&[u16], u16, Boundary, Boundary) -> (Result<Cell, Side>, u32)` — the
  boundary sides, then the search.
- `Cell { coordinate, lower }` with `coordinate()` / `lower()` / `upper()`.
- `BilinearSurface::locate_x` / `locate_y` — `pub(crate)`, an inherent `impl`
  inside `lookup.rs`, so `surface.rs` is untouched and the issue reads as one
  file.

One algorithm serves both axes: it takes `&[u16]`, not `&[u16; NX]`, so it is
compiled once instead of once per `NX` and once per `NY`. Axis identity
re-enters only in the two wrappers, which map a neutral private `Side` onto the
four `SurfaceError` variants using the existing `x_min`/`x_max`/`y_min`/`y_max`.
That is how "share one algorithm without erasing axis-specific public errors"
is satisfied structurally rather than by discipline.

## The one decision worth reviewing

**The obvious binary search would have made the acceptance evidence unassertable.**

The `lo`/`hi` partition-point loop shrinks its window to `floor(w/2)` on one
branch and `ceil(w/2) - 1` on the other, so its trip count depends on the
coordinate; `ceil(log2(len + 1))` is only a worst case. On a 2-knot axis a
coordinate at or above the last knot finishes in one iteration and one below it
takes two. A test asserting an exact comparison count would be flaky by data.

The base/size form shrinks by `size -> ceil(size / 2)` on **both** branches:

```rust
while size > 1 {
    let half = size / 2;
    let mid = base + half;
    if axis[mid] <= coordinate { base = mid; }
    size -= half;
}
```

Exactly `ceil(log2(len))` probes for every coordinate on a given axis. That
turns the white-box check into `assert_eq!` rather than `assert!(<=)`, which is
what actually distinguishes a binary search from a scan that got lucky. No early
exit on an exact match, deliberately — it would trade a uniform, auditable step
count for a data-dependent one.

Costs, all documented and `debug_assert_eq!`-enforced:

| case | comparisons |
| --- | --- |
| below domain | 1, no search |
| above domain | 2, no search |
| in domain | `2 + ceil(log2(len))` |

For a 1024-knot axis that is 12 against up to 1024 for a scan. The counts are
returned from `search` and `locate` so the tests measure the real implementation
rather than a reimplementation of it; callers discard them and an optimizing
build removes them.

## Acceptance evidence

| Issue bullet | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Minimum and maximum knots accepted exactly | `both_endpoint_knots_resolve_exactly` over all seven axis fixtures, plus `endpoints_are_accepted_under_every_policy` across all sixteen selections — a boundary policy never touches an in-domain coordinate |
| Every exact interior knot resolves without changing its coordinate | `every_exact_knot_keeps_its_coordinate_and_names_its_own_cell` over every knot of every fixture, including all 1024 of the big axis; `an_exact_knot_cell_reproduces_the_stored_knot_value` feeds the cell to `interpolate_segment` and gets the stored value back, which proves the cell rule is *right* rather than merely in range |
| Values immediately below/above every boundary, Error and Clamp, both axes | eight tests (`x_below_error_reports_the_x_minimum` … `y_above_clamp_resolves_to_the_last_cell`) asserting the **whole** `SurfaceError` variant, so an X/Y or below/above mix-up fails |
| Four sides applied independently | `each_side_selects_its_own_policy` — sixteen policies x four probes, each outcome Err-vs-Ok strictly per its own bit; plus `an_x_policy_never_changes_a_y_outcome` |
| Nonuniform axes | `nonuniform_axes_bracket_each_unequal_segment` on `[3, 4, 5, 1_000, 40_000, 65_000]` and `[100, 101, 500, 30_000]`, including unit-span segments next to a 25 000-unit one |
| Full `0..=u16::MAX` span | `a_full_span_axis_has_no_out_of_domain_coordinate` — a strided sweep of the entire `u16` range where every probe must be `Ok`; `the_widest_and_narrowest_segments_both_resolve` |
| A clamped coordinate resolves to the endpoint cell and cannot underflow or index past the table | `clamped_cells_stay_inside_the_axis_and_the_value_grid` indexes the real `values()[y][x]` corners for six fixtures, including `TINY` where `len - 2 == 0` on both axes; `clamping_never_extrapolates` shows the clamped coordinate interpolates to the stored boundary value |
| Focused tests distinguish binary lookup from a full scan | `the_probe_bound_matches_the_documented_formula` (against an independent halving reference), `the_search_probe_count_is_exact_and_data_independent`, `binary_lookup_costs_far_fewer_comparisons_than_a_scan`, `a_full_lookup_costs_two_endpoint_comparisons_plus_the_probes`, `an_out_of_domain_coordinate_never_searches` |

Twenty-six unit tests, run in **debug and release**. Release matters: every
internal invariant here is a `debug_assert!`, and a bug that only the assertions
catch would otherwise hide behind them.

## `src/interp.rs` is untouched on purpose

Its `expect(dead_code)` goes unfulfilled — a CI failure under `-D warnings` —
the moment non-test code calls `interpolate_segment`. This issue performs no
interpolation, so it stays fulfilled; the tests call the helper freely because
`cfg(test)` removes the attribute entirely. `lookup.rs` carries the same
self-destructing expectation for #6 to delete.

## Coupled edits

- `scripts/ci.sh` — `src/lookup.rs` added to the packaged-file allowlist.
  `Cargo.toml` needs no change (`include` already globs `src/**/*.rs`), but the
  allowlist is the ratchet the repo asked for.
- `AGENTS.md` — now on issue #5, and gains the rule that `src/lookup.rs` owns
  the only axis search in the crate: no second search, no early exit, no
  extrapolation path.
- `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` — the claim that no axis lookup exists is now
  false and is corrected. `BilinearSurface::evaluate` still does not exist.

No dependency, version, `publish`, or workspace change. All three dependency
tables remain empty, and the public API is byte-for-byte unchanged.

## Verification

`./scripts/ci.sh` — every runnable check PASS, including `clippy --all-targets
-- -D warnings`, `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc`, the `integer only` and
`no_std unconditional` greps, `cargo +nightly build --target thumbv7em-none-eabi
-Z build-std=core`, both embedded target checks, `cargo deny`, and `package
list` with the new file.

One `SKIP`: `github metadata`, because the repository's GitHub topics are unset.
Pre-existing, not introduced here — but per the repo's own rule, a skip is not a
pass.

body:
Targets the highest average-duration tests reported by Codecov.

**CPU-reference utility tests removed.** The CPU reference implementations under `tests/integrators/cpu_reference/` are the oracle the device functions are checked against; asserting on those utilities in isolation is a second layer of tests testing the tests. `tests/integrators/cpu_reference/test_cpu_utils.py` is deleted (`test_cpu_krylov_reduction_measures_entry_rhs`, `test_cpu_krylov_default_floor_derives_sqrt_eps`, `test_cpu_newton_convergence_edges`, `test_cpu_driver_evaluator_matches_gpu_time_alignment`).

**The bicgstab step case runs on radau_iia_5.** `BICGSTAB_STEP_CASES` asks whether bicgstab with a chained Neumann/Jacobi preconditioner works inside a Newton-solving family. A FIRK reaches the same linear-solver code as a DIRK for less device time, so `dirk-bicgstab-chained` becomes `firk-bicgstab-chained`.

**Zero-Jacobian smoothing tests dropped.** `test_dirk_zero_jacobian_smoothing_splits_by_mass_row` and `test_firk_zero_jacobian_smoothing_matches_closed_form` assert the zero-differential-row special case of the estimator that `test_dirk_step_smoothed_error_matches_dense_oracle` and `test_firk_step_smoothed_error_matches_dense_oracle` already assert against a dense Newton oracle with a general nonzero Jacobian, and the unsmoothed estimate they compare against is covered by the CPU-reference comparison in `test_step_algorithms.py`. The DIRK pair also built two steps for one assertion. Their `torn_zero_j` system and constants are removed with them. On main those two tests cost 4.6-6.7 s and 2.5-2.9 s of call time in a warm solo run.

**The dense-oracle steps use the shared session chain.** `_oracle_step` and `TIGHT_SOLVES` are replaced by `DIRK_ORACLE_SETTINGS`/`FIRK_ORACLE_SETTINGS` driving `solver_settings_override`, so both tests take `step_object` and read the tableau off the step.

`tests/integrators/algorithms/test_smoothed_error.py` solo warm run, five ABBA pairs against main on a real GPU: median paired delta -1.6 s on a ~12 s file, negative in all five pairs.

## Verification

Real GPU, `pytest -m "not specific_algos and not sim_only" -n 8`: 3291 passed in 79.81 s.
CUDASIM, `pytest -m "not nocudasim and not cupy and not specific_algos" -n 8`: 3240 passed in 21.22 s.
`flake8 . --select=E9,F63,F7,F82 --show-source`: clean. `ruff check` on the touched files: clean.

No `src/` change, so no `ab_gate.py` run.

body: ## Problem User reported (via live DOM inspection of `/pesan/01`) that the self-order item detail/condiment modal's food photo still looked too small/cropped, and the surrounding panels weren't compact enough, causing excess scrolling for customers. ## Root cause The photo header container was tall (210px/232px) but the `` used `object-contain` with large horizontal/vertical padding (`px-6 py-3 sm:px-8`), so the actual photo rendered small and letterboxed inside a tall, mostly-empty panel — the opposite of what was wanted (bigger photo, smaller panel). ## Fix - Photo container height reduced (210/232px → 152/168px) and switched to `object-cover` with no padding, so the image fills the panel edge-to-edge and reads as larger/more prominent while taking less vertical space overall. - Added a subtle bottom gradient behind the close button for legibility over photos. - Tightened header title padding, scroll-area spacing, quick-preset card, and notes card paddings to further reduce scroll depth. ## Validation - `npm run lint` (tsc --noEmit) — pass - `npm run build` — pass - `git diff --check` — clean Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

Adds the first bounded, read-only Domain Handle Work surface under `familiar/domain_handle/`.

The resolver composes three distinct inputs without flattening them:

Context
+ Domain Familiarity

author: pmatos
body:
## Refactoring goal

Audit of the codebase (via the `improve-codebase-architecture` skill) surfaced `vow-runtime/src/lib.rs` as a ~6,000-line god-file holding ~17 distinct concerns. The sharpest **deepening opportunity** in it: `__vow_violation` welded the `VowViolation` diagnostic *formatting* — the documented JSON envelope (`skills/vow/schemas/vow-violation.schema.json`, `docs/spec/cli.md`) plus its human-readable twin — directly onto the C-ABI decode and `process::exit`.

The result was a **shallow FFI wrapper hiding untested formatting logic**: a documented runtime contract that could only be exercised end-to-end through compiled debug binaries, with **zero unit coverage**. This is exactly the "the real bug hides in how a pure function is called" smell the audit looks for.

## What changed

A new `violation` module holds the pure formatting behind a narrow interface — no `unsafe`, no globals, no exit:

- `format_value(tag, payload) -> String` (renamed from the private `fmt_payload`)
- `render_violation(...) -> RenderedViolation` — a **named-field** struct (`json`, `human`) so callers never guess a tuple order, taking a plain-`&str` `ValueBinding` slice as input.

`__vow_violation` becomes a thin **adapter**: decode the C ABI, delegate to `render_violation`, write both lines, abort. Net `lib.rs`: **−60 / +31 lines**; the deep formatting core now lives with its own tests.

The formatting is **byte-identical** — the `format!` templates and `writeln!` calls are unchanged.

## Tests that validate it (TDD)

Built test-first (red → green): tests were written against the intended interface with `todo!()` bodies (observed red — 5 failing), then the bodies were implemented (green). The tests live in the new module (locality), and their expected values are **copy-pasted from independent sources of truth** — `docs/spec/cli.md:511` and `docs/level5-test-trace.md:373-374` — not re-derived from the code:

- `format_value_renders_each_tag` — every value tag (i32/i64/f32/f64/bool/u64/u8 + unknown-tag hex fallback)
- `render_violation_matches_documented_json_with_binding` — anchored on `docs/spec/cli.md`
- `render_violation_matches_trace_doc_json_and_human` — matched JSON+human pair from the trace doc
- `render_violation_omits_values_when_no_bindings_and_maps_callee`
- `render_violation_joins_multiple_bindings`

## Verification

- `cargo test -p vow-runtime` → **102 passed** (97 pre-existing + 5 new)
- `cargo clippy -p vow-runtime --lib -- -D warnings` → clean
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` → clean
- FFI symbol integrity: `__vow_violation` still `#[unsafe(no_mangle)]` with an identical signature; `nm` confirms `T __vow_violation` is exported.

## Scope notes

- **Rust-only, no self-hosted mirror.** `vow-runtime` is a standalone staticlib the compiler links; the self-hosted compiler *emits calls to* the unchanged `__vow_violation` symbol rather than reimplementing it. No `compiler/*.vow` change is required.
- **Discovered but deferred (not fixed here):** the `description`/`file` JSON fields are not escaped, so a violated predicate containing a string literal (e.g. `tests/verify/string_matches_literal_at.vow`, `requires: ... "ab" ...`) would emit invalid JSON. Fixing that is a **behavior change** and belongs in its own PR — kept out to keep this a behavior-preserving extraction. Tracked separately.
